title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
維弘治壬子適
皇上在位之五年天下又當大比
之期總督兩廣右都御史閔
珪祗若
德意先期會巡按廣西監察御史
鄭惟桓朱文暨藩臬二司布
===
政使李孟暘黎福參政程廷珙
洪漢楊守隨參議吳昭按察
使傅希說副使周孟中陳寓
徐瑁僉事劉信黎鼎陳烓禮
聘麒與教諭趙堦司考校學
正陳琬教諭林光重謝愷訓
導熊縝余黙同考校于時總
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序

維弘治壬子，適皇上在位之五年，天下又當大比之期。總督兩廣右都御史閔珪祗若德意，先期會巡按廣西監察御史鄭惟桓、朱文暨藩臬二司布政使李孟暘、黎福，參政程廷珙、洪漢、楊守隨，參議吳昭，按察使傅希說，副使周孟中、陳寓、徐瑁，僉事劉信、黎鼎、陳烓，禮聘麒與教諭趙堦司考校，學正陳琬、教諭林光重、謝愷、訓導熊縝、余黙同考校。于時總
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the renzi year of the Hongzhi reign, the fifth year of His Majesty’s rule [1492], the time had again come for the triennial examinations throughout the realm. Min Gui, Governor-general of Liangguang and Right Censor-in-chief, reverently following the imperial intent, conferred in advance with Zheng Weihuan and Zhu Wen, Investigating Censors serving as Regional Inspectors of Guangxi, and with the officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions: Provincial Administration Commissioners Li Mengyang and Li Fu; Administration Vice Commissioners Cheng Tinggong, Hong Han, and Yang Shousui; Administration Assistant Commissioner Wu Zhao; Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Fu Xishuo; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhou Mengzhong, Chen Yu, and Xu Mao; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Liu Xin, Li Ding, and Chen Wei. They formally invited Qi [the writer, referring to himself by his given name] and Instructor Zhao Jie to serve as Examiners, and Instructor Chen Wan, Instructors Lin Guangzhong and Xie Kai, and Assistant Instructors Xiong Zhen and Yu Mo to serve as Associate Examiners. title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
鎮太監王敬總兵伏羌伯毛
銳同涖玆土武功既成文事
攸舉至期巡按監察御史祁
司員乃合孟中所提督之士
而覆閱之凡七百有竒鎖院
圍棘以就三試則福昭司提
調希說烓司監試而廷珙漢
===
信又皆贊襄防範於外與凡
中外百司皆遴選以充至於
秉公殫慮而始終監臨之者
寔御史祁司員也試已得中
式者五十有五人爰録其氏
名并其文之合程度者以
獻麒謬忝校文宜序諸首竊謂
punctuated: 鎮太監王敬、總兵伏羌伯毛銳同涖玆土，武功既成，文事攸舉。至期，巡按監察御史祁司員乃合孟中所提督之士而覆閱之，凡七百有竒。鎖院圍棘，以就三試，則福、昭司提調，希說、烓司監試，而廷珙、漢、信又皆贊襄防範於外，與凡中外百司，皆遴選以充。至於秉公殫慮而始終監臨之者，寔御史祁司員也。試已，得中式者五十有五人，爰録其氏名，并其文之合程度者以獻。麒謬忝校文，宜序諸首，竊謂……
translation_en: …the eunuch Grand Defender Wang Jing and the Regional Commander Mao Rui, Earl of Fuqiang, jointly presided over this territory. Military achievements having been secured, literary undertakings were now pursued. At the appointed time, the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Qi Siyuan, assembled the scholars under Mengzhong’s supervision and examined them again. They numbered more than seven hundred. The examination compound was locked and enclosed with thorn barriers for the three examination sessions. Li Fu and Wu Zhao served as Proctors; Fu Xishuo and Chen Wei supervised the examinations; and Cheng Tinggong, Hong Han, and Liu Xin all assisted with security outside. Personnel for the various offices within and outside the compound were all carefully selected. As for the man who upheld impartiality, devoted his utmost attention, and served as Supervising Official from beginning to end, this was indeed Censor Qi Siyuan. When the examinations were over, fifty-five candidates had qualified. Their names, together with those of their compositions that met the prescribed standards, were accordingly recorded for presentation to the throne. I, Qi, having undeservedly been entrusted with evaluating the compositions, ought to supply a preface at the beginning. I venture to suggest that …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天地之化其開也有漸聖人
之化其成也亦有漸廣右去
京師萬里古百粤地也自秦
漢迄今更數千百年我
祖宗開基誕敷文德無遠弗届
列聖相承延及
皇上薫蒸融液聲敎益覃然後學
===
校之設詩書之化徧舉漸摩
殆駸駸然與中州齒而深山
大谷猶有怙終而迷復者何
哉譬之陰崖寒谷陽和之所
不及豈理然耶然觀泰伯逃
吳至德之聲漸被無窮子游
北學中國遂爲聖門高弟常
punctuated: 天地之化，其開也有漸；聖人之化，其成也亦有漸。廣右去京師萬里，古百粤地也。自秦漢迄今，更數千百年。我祖宗開基，誕敷文德，無遠弗届。列聖相承，延及皇上，薫蒸融液，聲敎益覃。然後學校之設、詩書之化徧舉，漸摩殆駸駸然與中州齒，而深山大谷猶有怙終而迷復者，何哉？譬之陰崖寒谷，陽和之所不及，豈理然耶？然觀泰伯逃吳，至德之聲漸被無窮；子游北學中國，遂爲聖門高弟。常
translation_en: … The transforming work of Heaven and Earth unfolds gradually; the transforming influence of sages likewise achieves its results gradually. Guangyou lies ten thousand li from the capital and was anciently the land of the Hundred Yue. From the Qin and Han dynasties to the present, thousands of years have passed. Our imperial ancestors established the dynasty’s foundations and broadly spread civil virtue, reaching even the most distant places. Successive sage sovereigns carried on this work down to His Majesty, whose influence permeates and transforms, spreading imperial teaching ever more widely. Thus schools have been established everywhere, and the transforming teachings of the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents have spread throughout the region. Through gradual cultivation, it has advanced swiftly toward parity with the Central Plains. Yet in the deep mountains and great valleys there are still those who persist in wrongdoing and lose their way back. Why is this? They may be compared to shaded cliffs and cold valleys that the warmth of spring does not reach. Can this be the natural order of things? Yet consider how Taibo withdrew to Wu: the renown of his consummate virtue gradually spread, its influence without end. Ziyou went north to study in the central states and became an outstanding disciple in the sage’s school. Often …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
袞亷閩親與諸生為主客之
禮閩人始知文學而歐陽詹
遂登龍虎榜吳與閩皆昔粤
地也自泰伯常袞之風化子
游歐陽詹之倡先遂為詩書
上國隱然海濱之鄒魯矣廣
右在宋時張栻出守靜江民
===
知向化流風餘韻至今猶存
馮京崛起慶遠解省廷對名
皆第一卒膺大拜史稱其有
中立不倚之操則風化之倡
先之未必無其人也詩書士
迨今亦且多矣獨其間頑悍
之習猶使人不能無憾焉者
punctuated: 袞亷閩，親與諸生為主客之禮，閩人始知文學，而歐陽詹遂登龍虎榜。吳與閩皆昔粤地也，自泰伯、常袞之風化，子游、歐陽詹之倡先，遂為詩書上國，隱然海濱之鄒魯矣。廣右在宋時，張栻出守靜江，民知向化，流風餘韻至今猶存。馮京崛起慶遠，解、省、廷對，名皆第一，卒膺大拜。史稱其有中立不倚之操，則風化之、倡先之，未必無其人也。詩書士迨今亦且多矣，獨其間頑悍之習猶使人不能無憾焉者，
translation_en: …[Chang] Gun, while overseeing Min, personally observed the courtesies of host and guest with the students. Only then did the people of Min come to appreciate literary learning, and Ouyang Zhan subsequently gained a place on the “Dragon and Tiger List” of successful examination candidates. Wu and Min were both formerly lands of Yue. Through the transforming influence of Taibo and Chang Gun, and the pioneering examples of Ziyou and Ouyang Zhan, they became eminent regions of classical learning, recognizably a Zou and Lu by the sea—the homeland of the Confucian tradition. In Guangyou, during the Song dynasty, Zhang Shi went out to serve as prefect of Jingjiang, and the people learned to embrace moral transformation. The enduring influence of his example survives to this day. Feng Jing rose to prominence from Qingyuan, placing first in the prefectural qualifying examination, the departmental examination, and the court examination alike, and ultimately received appointment as chief councillor. The histories praise his integrity in standing firm and impartial. Thus, this region has certainly not lacked men to exert a transforming influence and lead by example. By now, scholars versed in the classics have also become numerous. Yet the stubborn and fierce habits that persist among them still leave one unable to feel entirely satisfied…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
衮撫閩親與諸生為主客之
禮閩人始知文學而歐陽詹
遂登龍虎榜吳與閩皆昔粤
地也自泰伯常衮之風化子
游歐陽詹之倡先遂為詩書
上國隱然海濱之鄒魯矣廣
右在宋時張栻出守靜江民
===
知向化流風餘韻至今猶存
馮京崛起慶遠解省廷對名
皆第一卒膺大拜史稱其有
中立不倚之操則風化之倡
先之未必無其人也詩書士
迨今亦且多矣獨其間頑悍
之習猶使人不能無憾焉者

translation_en: …Gun, while governing Min, personally observed the courtesies of host and guest with the students. The people of Min then began to appreciate literary learning, and Ouyang Zhan subsequently gained a place on the “Dragon and Tiger List” of successful examination candidates. Wu and Min were both formerly lands of Yue. Through the moral influence of Taibo and Chang Gun, and the pioneering examples of Ziyou and Ouyang Zhan, they became eminent regions of learning in the Odes and Documents, veritable counterparts of Zou and Lu by the sea. In Guangyou, during the Song dynasty, Zhang Shi went out to serve as prefect of Jingjiang. The people learned to embrace moral transformation, and the lingering influence of his example survives to this day. Feng Jing rose to prominence from Qingyuan, ranking first in the prefectural qualifying examination, the metropolitan examination, and the palace examination alike, and ultimately receiving appointment as chief councilor. The histories praise his integrity in standing upright and inclining to neither side. Thus this region has certainly not lacked men to exert a civilizing influence and take the lead by example. By now, scholars versed in the Odes and Documents are also numerous. Yet the stubborn and fierce habits that persist among them still leave one with cause for regret…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
豈以風化倡先之者吳閩則
肇自周唐之遠廣右僅啓於
有宋之近而其入人不能無
淺深之間也耶雖然以數與
時考之將必有裒然出而先
天下者矣諸士子果能脩於
身化於家推之鄉達之天下
===
由近而遠自易而難易異俗
而歸大同使我
聖朝之化如天之覆如地之載如
日月之照臨陰崖寒谷陽和
遍及頑悍之習罔有不率俾
不愧於同一古粤之區則人
必將稱之曰廣右有此人物
punctuated: 豈以風化倡先之者，吳閩則肇自周唐之遠，廣右僅啓於有宋之近，而其入人不能無淺深之間也耶？雖然，以數與時考之，將必有裒然出而先天下者矣。諸士子果能脩於身，化於家，推之鄉，達之天下，由近而遠，自易而難，易異俗而歸大同，使我聖朝之化如天之覆，如地之載，如日月之照臨，陰崖寒谷，陽和遍及，頑悍之習罔有不率，俾不愧於同一古粤之區，則人必將稱之曰：「廣右有此人物」
translation_en: …Could it be because those who first promoted moral transformation in Wu and Min began as far back as the Zhou and Tang, whereas in Guangyou this began only as recently as the Song, so that its influence upon the people inevitably differs in depth? Even so, judging by the workings of destiny and the times, there will surely be men who rise to distinction [?] and take the lead throughout the realm. If you students can indeed cultivate yourselves, transform your households, extend this influence to your home communities, and carry it throughout the realm—proceeding from near to far and from easy to difficult, changing divergent customs and bringing them into a great unity—then the transforming influence of our sage dynasty will shelter all like heaven, sustain all like earth, and shine upon all like the sun and moon. Its genial warmth will reach even shaded cliffs and cold valleys; all those with stubborn and unruly habits will conform. Thus this region will bring no shame upon its place within the same ancient land of Yue, and people will surely praise it, saying: “Guangyou has men such as these…”

text:

時考之將必有裒然出而先
天下者矣諸士子果能脩於

===
由近而遠自易而難易異俗
而歸大同使我
聖朝之化如天之覆如地之載如
日月之照臨陰崖寒谷陽和
遍及頑悍之習罔有不率俾
不愧於同一古粤之區則人
必將稱之曰廣右有此人物
punctuated: 豈以風化倡先之者，吳閩則肇自周唐之遠，廣右僅啓於有宋之近，而其入人不能無淺深之間也耶？雖然，以數與時考之，將必有裒然出而先天下者矣。諸士子果能脩於身，化於家，推之鄉，達之天下，由近而遠，自易而難，易異俗而歸大同，使我聖朝之化如天之覆，如地之載，如日月之照臨，陰崖寒谷，陽和遍及，頑悍之習罔有不率，俾不愧於同一古粤之區，則人必將稱之曰：「廣右有此人物
translation_en: … Could it be because, among those who first promoted moral transformation, Wu and Min began as far back as the Zhou and Tang, whereas Guangyou began only as recently as the Song, so that its influence upon people necessarily differs in depth? Even so, judging by the course of destiny and the times, there will surely be those who emerge conspicuously [?] and take the lead throughout the realm. If you examination candidates can indeed cultivate yourselves, transform your households, extend this influence to your communities, and spread it throughout the realm, proceeding from near to far and from easy to difficult, changing divergent customs and bringing them into a great unity, then the transforming influence of our sagely dynasty will shelter like Heaven, sustain like Earth, and illuminate like the sun and moon. Its warmth will reach everywhere, even shaded cliffs and cold valleys; none accustomed to obstinacy and unruliness will fail to conform. Thus you will bring no shame upon this region, which likewise belongs to ancient Yue, and people will surely praise you, saying: “Guangyou has such outstanding people …”

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
如此無忝於古昔第一流人
物矣顧不偉歟諸士子幸相
與勉之
浙江衢州府龍游縣儒學教
諭朱麒謹序
punctuated:
如此，無忝於古昔第一流人物矣，顧不偉歟？諸士子幸相與勉之。
浙江衢州府龍游縣儒學教諭朱麒謹序。
translation_en:
…such as these, worthy of the foremost figures of antiquity. Would this not be splendid? May you examination candidates encourage one another in this endeavor.
This preface is respectfully written by Zhu Qi, Instructor of the Confucian School of Longyou County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
發憤忘食樂以忘憂
溥博如天淵泉如淵見而民莫不敬言而
民莫不信行而民莫不說
文王視民如傷望道而未之見武王不泄
邇不忘遠
易
大觀在上順而巽中正以觀天下
===
出可以守宗廟社稷以為祭主也
顯諸仁藏諸用
君子藏器於身待時而動何不利之有動
而不括是以出而有獲語成器而動
者也
書
詢于四岳闢四門明四目達四聰咨十有
二牧曰食哉惟時柔遠能邇惇德允
元而難任人
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

發憤忘食，樂以忘憂。

溥博如天，淵泉如淵，見而民莫不敬，言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。

文王視民如傷，望道而未之見。武王不泄邇，不忘遠。

易

大觀在上，順而巽，中正以觀天下。

出可以守宗廟社稷，以為祭主也。

顯諸仁，藏諸用。

君子藏器於身，待時而動，何不利之有？動而不括，是以出而有獲，語成器而動者也。

書

詢于四岳，闢四門，明四目，達四聰。咨十有二牧，曰：「食哉惟時！柔遠能邇，惇德允元，而難任人。」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

In his earnest striving he forgets to eat; in his joy he forgets his cares.

Vast and all-embracing like Heaven, deep and inexhaustible like the abyss: when he appears, none among the people fails to respect him; when he speaks, none fails to trust him; when he acts, none fails to take delight in him.

King Wen regarded the people as though they were wounded, and gazed toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it. King Wu did not neglect those nearby or forget those far away.

Book of Changes

The great exemplar is on high. Receptive and yielding, central and correct, he presents himself as an example to all under Heaven.

Going forth, he can safeguard the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain, and thus preside over the sacrifices.

It is manifest in benevolence and concealed in its workings.

The gentleman keeps his capacities within himself and waits for the proper time to act. What could fail to be advantageous? He acts without obstruction; thus, when he goes forth, he gains results. This speaks of one who acts only after his capacities have been fully developed.

Book of Documents

He consulted the Four Peaks, opened the gates on all four sides, extended his vision in all four directions, and opened his hearing to all four quarters. He consulted the twelve regional governors, saying: “Food—let this be your timely concern! Deal gently with those far away and cultivate harmony with those nearby. Esteem the virtuous, trust the good, and keep glib flatterers at a distance.”

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
三百里揆文教二百里奮武衛
月之從星則以風雨
天明畏弼我丕丕基
詩
赳赳武夫公侯腹心
我車旣攻我馬旣同四牡龐龐駕言徂東
赫赫明明王命卿士南仲大祖大師皇父
整我六師以脩我戎旣敬旣戒惠此
南國王謂尹氏命程伯休父左右陳
===
行戒我師旅率彼淮浦省此徐土不
留不處三事就緒
有飶其香邦家之光
春秋
元年春王正月天王使宰咺來歸惠
公仲子之賵〔隱公元年〕秋翬帥師王
人子突救衛〔莊公六年〕季子來歸〔閔公元年〕
齊侯衛侯鄭伯來戰于郎〔桓公十年〕齊人衛
人鄭人盟于惡曹〔桓公十一年〕
punctuated:
三百里揆文教，二百里奮武衛。
月之從星，則以風雨。
天明畏，弼我丕丕基。

詩
赳赳武夫，公侯腹心。
我車旣攻，我馬旣同。四牡龐龐，駕言徂東。
赫赫明明，王命卿士，南仲大祖，大師皇父：「整我六師，以脩我戎。」旣敬旣戒，惠此南國。王謂尹氏：「命程伯休父，左右陳行，戒我師旅，率彼淮浦，省此徐土。不留不處，三事就緒。」
有飶其香，邦家之光。

春秋
元年春，王正月，天王使宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵〔隱公元年〕。秋，翬帥師。王人子突救衛〔莊公六年〕。季子來歸〔閔公元年〕。
齊侯、衛侯、鄭伯來戰于郎〔桓公十年〕。齊人、衛人、鄭人盟于惡曹〔桓公十一年〕。
translation_en:
Within the three-hundred-li zone, administer civil instruction; within the two-hundred-li zone, strengthen military defense.
When the moon follows the stars, wind and rain ensue.
Heaven, luminous and awe-inspiring, assists our exceedingly great foundation.

Book of Odes
Valiant warriors are the trusted confidants of dukes and lords.
Our chariots are ready; our horses are matched. The four stallions are mighty; we harness them and journey east.
Majestic and illustrious, the king commanded his high minister, the Grand Preceptor Huangfu, who honored Nanzhong as his great ancestor: “Put our six armies in order, and prepare our forces for war.” Reverent and vigilant, he brought benefit to these southern states. The king addressed the Yin clan official: “Command Chengbo Xiufu to arrange the ranks on the left and right, and put our troops on alert. Follow the banks of the Huai and inspect this territory of Xu. Neither linger nor remain: bring the three tasks to completion.”
Fragrant is its aroma, the glory of the state and ruling house.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In the first year, in spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the Heavenly King sent Administrator Xuan to bring funeral gifts for Duke Hui and Zhongzi. 〔First year of Duke Yin〕 In autumn, Hui led an army. [?] The king’s officer Zitu came to the aid of Wei. 〔Sixth year of Duke Zhuang〕 Jizi returned. 〔First year of Duke Min〕
The Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Zheng came to do battle at Lang. 〔Tenth year of Duke Huan〕 Men of Qi, Wei, and Zheng concluded a covenant at E’cao. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Huan〕

有飶其香，邦家之光。

春秋
元年，春，王正月。天王使宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵。〔隱公元年〕秋，翬帥師。王人子突救衛。〔莊公六年〕季子來歸。〔閔公元年〕齊侯、衛侯、鄭伯來戰于郎。〔桓公十年〕齊人、衛人、鄭人盟于惡曹。〔桓公十一年〕
translation_en:
Within the three-hundred-li zone, oversee civil instruction; within the two-hundred-li zone, strengthen military defenses.
When the moon follows the stars, wind and rain ensue.
Heaven is radiant and awe-inspiring; assist us in greatly enlarging our foundation.

The Odes
Valiant warriors are the trusted confidants of dukes and marquises.
Our chariots are ready; our horses are matched. The four stallions are strong and sturdy; we harness them and go east.
Majestic and illustrious, the king commanded his high minister, the Grand Preceptor Huangfu, whose great ancestor was Nanzhong: “Set our six armies in order and prepare our arms. Be reverent and vigilant, and bring peace to these southern states.” The king told the Yin official to command Chengbo Xiufu: “Arrange the ranks on the left and right. Put our troops on alert; follow the banks of the Huai and inspect this land of Xu. Neither linger nor halt; bring the affairs of the three military divisions into order.”
Fragrant is their aroma, a glory to the state and the royal house.

The Spring and Autumn Annals
In the first year, in spring, in the first month of the royal calendar. The Heavenly King sent Steward Xuan to deliver funeral gifts for Duke Hui and Zhongzi. 〔First year of Duke Yin〕 In autumn, Hui led an army. The king’s officer Zitu came to the aid of Wei. 〔Sixth year of Duke Zhuang〕 Jizi returned. 〔First year of Duke Min〕 The Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Zheng came to fight at Lang. 〔Tenth year of Duke Huan〕 Men of Qi, Wei, and Zheng concluded a covenant at E’cao. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Huan〕

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
元年春王正月公即位〔文公元年〕
晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕
禮記
博聞强識而讓敦善行而不怠謂之君子
司徒脩六禮以節民性明七敎以興民德
齊八政以防淫一道德以同俗養耆
老以致孝恤孤獨以逮不足上賢以
崇德簡不肖以絀惡
古之聖人内之爲尊外之爲樂少之爲貴
===
多之爲美
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣
第貳場
論
孔子之道大而能博
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢諸儒講五經異同於石渠閣詔〔甘露〕
〔三年〕
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕
punctuated:
元年，春，王正月，公即位。〔文公元年〕
晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江。〔文公三年〕

禮記
博聞强識而讓，敦善行而不怠，謂之君子。
司徒脩六禮以節民性，明七敎以興民德，齊八政以防淫，一道德以同俗，養耆老以致孝，恤孤獨以逮不足，上賢以崇德，簡不肖以絀惡。
古之聖人，内之爲尊，外之爲樂，少之爲貴，多之爲美。
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣。

第貳場
論
孔子之道大而能博。

詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢諸儒講五經異同於石渠閣詔。〔甘露〕〔三年〕
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥。〔貞觀十六年〕
translation_en:
In the first year, in spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke assumed his position. 〔First year of Duke Wen〕
Yang Chufu of Jin led an army to attack Chu in order to relieve Jiang. 〔Third year of Duke Wen〕

Book of Rites
One who is widely learned and has a strong memory, yet remains modest, and who earnestly practices good conduct without flagging, is called a gentleman.
The Minister of Education regulates the six rites to restrain the people's dispositions, elucidates the seven teachings to foster their virtue, orders the eight administrative functions to prevent excess, and unifies moral principles to bring their customs into accord. He cares for the aged to promote filial piety, aids orphans and the solitary to reach those in want, elevates the worthy to honor virtue, and singles out the unworthy to reject wickedness.
The sages of antiquity regarded what was inward as worthy of reverence and what was outward as a source of joy; they valued fewness as precious and abundance as beautiful.
Only after attending court audiences do the regional lords understand how to act as subjects.

Second Session
Discourse
The Way of Confucius is great and comprehensive.

Imperial Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?]〕
Compose, in the voice of a Han emperor, an edict directing the scholars to discuss similarities and differences among the Five Classics at the Shiqu Pavilion. 〔Third year of Ganlu〕
Compose, in the voice of a Tang emperor, a proclamation appointing Wei Zheng Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. 〔Sixteenth year of Zhenguan〕

The Way of Confucius is great and all-embracing.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
擬立
皇太子正位東宮
賀表
判語〔五條〕
選用軍職
攬納稅粮
奏對失序
從征違期
干名犯義
===
第叄場
策〔五道〕
問帝王之德莫大於孝而其治天下亦莫
先於孝觀於帝舜以大孝而天下化武
王以達孝而下土式盖可見矣仰惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝御製大誥三編申明五常而首以
父子之親
太宗文皇帝御製孝順事實而首以虞書之克
punctuated:
擬立皇太子正位東宮賀表。
判語〔五條〕：選用軍職；攬納稅粮；奏對失序；從征違期；干名犯義。
第叄場
策〔五道〕
問：帝王之德莫大於孝，而其治天下亦莫先於孝。觀於帝舜以大孝而天下化，武王以達孝而下土式，盖可見矣。仰惟我朝太祖高皇帝御製《大誥》三編，申明五常，而首以父子之親；太宗文皇帝御製《孝順事實》，而首以《虞書》之克
translation_en:
Compose a hypothetical congratulatory memorial on the establishment of the imperial heir apparent and his formal installation in the Eastern Palace.

Legal judgments〔five items〕: selection and appointment of military officers; undertaking to remit tax grain on others’ behalf; failure to observe the proper order when responding to the throne; failure to meet the appointed date for joining a military campaign; violating familial status and moral obligations.

Third Session
Policy questions〔five questions〕

Question: Among the virtues of emperors and kings, none is greater than filial piety; in their governance of All under Heaven, likewise, nothing takes precedence over filial piety. This can be seen in Emperor Shun, whose great filial piety transformed All under Heaven, and King Wu, whose consummate filial piety made him a model for the lands below. We reverently consider how Emperor Taizu Gao of our dynasty personally composed the three compilations of the Great Pronouncement, elucidating the Five Constant Relationships and placing first the affection between father and son; Emperor Taizong Wen personally composed True Accounts of Filial Obedience, beginning with the words in the Documents of Yu, “being able to …”

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諧齊栗
宣宗章皇帝御製五倫書而首以家人之父父
子子是其制作之盛足以為法於天下
可傳於後世
列聖之心盖與舜武同一心也繼惟
皇上曩在春宮仁孝之聲聞于天下嗣登
大寶愛敬之誠洽于
重闈是其德教之至足以加于百姓刑于四海
皇上之心又與
===
列聖同一心也先儒論舜武之孝皆由庸行之
常推之以至其極而所謂極者莫大於
尊養之備稱號之隆而已然以尊養為
孝則後世之君尊養於其親者宜無不
備矣尊養果足以盡孝乎以稱號為孝
則後世之君稱號於其親者宜無不隆
矣稱號果足以盡孝乎夫大孝達孝皆
上聖事業也我
列聖之心既同乎舜武之心
punctuated:
諧、齊栗。宣宗章皇帝御製《五倫書》，而首以《家人》之父父子子。是其制作之盛，足以為法於天下，可傳於後世。列聖之心，盖與舜武同一心也。繼惟皇上曩在春宮，仁孝之聲聞于天下；嗣登大寶，愛敬之誠洽于重闈。是其德教之至，足以加于百姓，刑于四海。皇上之心，又與列聖同一心也。
先儒論舜武之孝，皆由庸行之常，推之以至其極。而所謂極者，莫大於尊養之備、稱號之隆而已。然以尊養為孝，則後世之君尊養於其親者，宜無不備矣。尊養果足以盡孝乎？以稱號為孝，則後世之君稱號於其親者，宜無不隆矣。稱號果足以盡孝乎？夫大孝、達孝，皆上聖事業也。我列聖之心，既同乎舜武之心，
translation_en:
…harmony, and solemn reverence. Emperor Xuanzong, posthumously titled Zhang, composed the Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu), beginning with the words of the Family hexagram: “The father acts as a father, and the son as a son.” Such was the excellence of these imperial writings that they could serve as models throughout the realm and be transmitted to later generations. The hearts of our successive sage emperors were indeed one with those of Shun and King Wu. Furthermore, we respectfully consider how His Majesty, while still in the Eastern Palace as heir apparent, was renowned throughout the realm for benevolence and filial devotion. After succeeding to the imperial throne, his sincere love and reverence suffused the inner palaces of his elders. Such is the perfection of his moral teaching that it can extend to the common people and serve as a model throughout the Four Seas. His Majesty’s heart is likewise one with those of the successive sage emperors.
Earlier Confucian scholars, discussing the filial devotion of Shun and King Wu, held that both began with ordinary daily conduct and extended it to its utmost fulfillment. What they called utmost fulfillment amounted to nothing greater than complete provision of honor and sustenance, and the exaltation of titles. Yet if honoring and supporting one’s parents constitutes filial devotion, then later rulers should all have provided their parents with these things in full. Does honoring and supporting them truly suffice to fulfill filial devotion? If conferring titles constitutes filial devotion, then later rulers should all have conferred the most exalted titles upon their parents. Do titles truly suffice to fulfill filial devotion? Now, “great filial devotion” and “universally acknowledged filial devotion” are both accomplishments of the highest sages. Since the hearts of our successive sage emperors were one with those of Shun and King Wu…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諧齊栗
宣宗章皇帝御製五倫書而首以家人之父父
子子是其制作之盛足以為法於天下
可傳於後世
列聖之心盖與舜武同一心也繼惟
皇上曩在春宫仁孝之聲聞于天下嗣登
大寶愛敬之誠洽于
重闈是其德教之至足以加于百姓刑于四海
皇上之心又與
===
列聖同一心也先儒論舜武之孝皆由庸行之
常推之以至其極而所謂極者莫大於
尊養之備稱號之隆而已然以尊養為
孝則後世之君尊養於其親者宜無不
備矣尊養果足以盡孝乎以稱號為孝
則後世之君稱號於其親者宜無不隆
矣稱號果足以盡孝乎夫大孝達孝皆
上聖事業也我
列聖之心既同乎舜武之心
punctuated:
諧齊栗。
宣宗章皇帝御製《五倫書》，而首以家人之父父子子，是其制作之盛，足以為法於天下，可傳於後世。列聖之心，盖與舜武同一心也。繼惟皇上曩在春宫，仁孝之聲聞于天下；嗣登大寶，愛敬之誠洽于重闈。是其德教之至，足以加于百姓，刑于四海。皇上之心，又與列聖同一心也。
先儒論舜武之孝，皆由庸行之常推之以至其極，而所謂極者，莫大於尊養之備、稱號之隆而已。然以尊養為孝，則後世之君尊養於其親者，宜無不備矣。尊養果足以盡孝乎？以稱號為孝，則後世之君稱號於其親者，宜無不隆矣。稱號果足以盡孝乎？夫大孝、達孝，皆上聖事業也。我列聖之心，既同乎舜武之心，
translation_en:
…harmony, solemnity, and reverence [?].
Emperor Xuanzong Zhang personally composed the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), placing first the principle that, within the family, fathers should fulfill their role as fathers and sons their role as sons. Such was the excellence of his composition that it could serve as a standard throughout the realm and be transmitted to later generations. The hearts of our sagely imperial predecessors were indeed one with those of Shun and King Wu. Turning next to His Majesty: formerly, while he was crown prince, his reputation for benevolence and filial devotion was known throughout the realm. Upon succeeding to the imperial throne, his sincere love and reverence suffused the inner palaces of his imperial elders. Such was the perfection of his moral instruction that it could extend to the common people and serve as a model throughout the Four Seas. His Majesty’s heart, too, is one with those of our sagely imperial predecessors.
Earlier Confucian scholars, discussing the filial devotion of Shun and King Wu, held that both extended ordinary daily conduct to its utmost limit. What they called this utmost limit amounted to nothing greater than completeness in honoring and providing for one’s parents and magnificence in the titles conferred upon them. Yet if honoring and providing for parents constitutes filial devotion, then later rulers should surely have lacked nothing in honoring and providing for their parents. Can honoring and providing for them truly suffice to fulfill filial devotion? If conferring titles constitutes filial devotion, then later rulers should surely have spared no magnificence in the titles bestowed upon their parents. Can such titles truly suffice to fulfill filial devotion? Great filial devotion and universally acknowledged filial devotion are both achievements of the highest sages. Since the hearts of our sagely imperial predecessors were already one with those of Shun and King Wu…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇上之心又同乎
列聖之心而其為孝之極果安在乎夫孝也者
百行之本萬善之原可以動天地感鬼
神化强暴格鳥獸孚草木在匹夫尚然
况天子乎然則
皇上之孝由一念以充塞乎兩間皆諸士子耳
濡而目染必有能鋪張之者矣幸詳陳
以獻
問大學孔氏之遺書而初學入德之門也
===
朱子章句綱舉目張條分縷析無容議
矣然或問一書又所以發明章句未盡
之意學者類多忽而不講是以不能充
然有得今姑撮其大槩與二三子論之
明德新民止至善三綱領也世有不務
明德不屑新民而不求止至善者誰歟
格致誠正脩齊治平八條目也世有不
探其端而驟語其次者誰歟釋明德而
終帝典所言亦有序乎釋新民而先盤
punctuated:
皇上之心又同乎列聖之心，而其為孝之極果安在乎？夫孝也者，百行之本，萬善之原，可以動天地，感鬼神，化强暴，格鳥獸，孚草木。在匹夫尚然，况天子乎？然則皇上之孝，由一念以充塞乎兩間，皆諸士子耳濡而目染，必有能鋪張之者矣。幸詳陳以獻。

問：《大學》，孔氏之遺書，而初學入德之門也。朱子《章句》，綱舉目張，條分縷析，無容議矣。然《或問》一書，又所以發明《章句》未盡之意，學者類多忽而不講，是以不能充然有得。今姑撮其大槩，與二三子論之。明德、新民、止至善，三綱領也。世有不務明德、不屑新民而不求止至善者，誰歟？格、致、誠、正、脩、齊、治、平，八條目也。世有不探其端而驟語其次者，誰歟？釋明德而終《帝典》所言，亦有序乎？釋新民而先盤
translation_en:
…His Majesty’s heart likewise accords with the hearts of the sage emperors before him; wherein, then, does his supreme filial piety truly lie? Filial piety is the root of all conduct and the source of every goodness. It can move Heaven and Earth, stir ghosts and spirits, transform the violent, reach birds and beasts, and extend its influence even to plants and trees. If this holds even for an ordinary man, how much more for the Son of Heaven! His Majesty’s filial piety thus proceeds from a single thought to fill the space between Heaven and Earth. All you candidates have been steeped in it through what you have heard and seen; surely some among you can fully expound it. Please set it forth in detail for presentation to the throne.

Question: The Great Learning is a work handed down from Confucius and the gateway through which beginners enter into virtue. Master Zhu’s Commentary in Chapters and Sentences sets out the guiding principles and unfolds their particulars, distinguishing each item and analyzing every strand; it leaves no room for dispute. Yet his Questions and Answers further elucidates meanings not fully expressed in the Commentary in Chapters and Sentences. Students generally neglect it and fail to study it, and consequently cannot attain a full understanding. Let us now select its main points and discuss them with you.

Illuminating luminous virtue, renewing the people, and resting in the highest good are the three guiding principles. Who are those in the world who do not strive to illuminate luminous virtue, disdain renewing the people, and do not seek to rest in the highest good? Investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world are the eight items. Who are those in the world who fail to investigate their starting point yet hastily discuss the subsequent stages? In explaining the illumination of luminous virtue, the commentary concludes with words from the Canon of the Emperors: is there also a deliberate sequence here? In explaining the renewal of the people, it begins with Pan…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇上之心又同乎
列聖之心而其為孝之極果安在乎夫孝也者
百行之本萬善之原可以動天地感鬼
神化强暴格鳥獸孚草木在匹夫尚然
况天子乎然則
皇上之孝由一念以充塞乎兩間皆諸士子耳
濡而目染必有能鋪張之者矣幸詳陳
以獻
問大學孔氏之遺書而初學入德之門也
===
朱子章句綱舉目張條分縷析無容議
矣然或問一書又所以發明章句未盡
之意學者類多忽而不講是以不能充
然有得今姑撮其大槩與二三子論之
明德新民止至善三綱領也世有不務
明德不屑新民而不求止至善者誰歟
格致誠正脩齊治平八條目也世有不
探其端而驟語其次者誰歟釋明德而
終帝典所言亦有序乎釋新民而先盤
punctuated:
皇上之心又同乎列聖之心，而其為孝之極果安在乎？夫孝也者，百行之本，萬善之原，可以動天地，感鬼神，化强暴，格鳥獸，孚草木。在匹夫尚然，况天子乎？然則皇上之孝，由一念以充塞乎兩間，皆諸士子耳濡而目染，必有能鋪張之者矣。幸詳陳以獻。
問：《大學》，孔氏之遺書，而初學入德之門也。朱子《章句》，綱舉目張，條分縷析，無容議矣。然《或問》一書，又所以發明《章句》未盡之意。學者類多忽而不講，是以不能充然有得。今姑撮其大槩，與二三子論之。明德、新民、止至善，三綱領也。世有不務明德、不屑新民，而不求止至善者，誰歟？格致誠正脩齊治平，八條目也。世有不探其端，而驟語其次者，誰歟？釋明德而終《帝典》，所言亦有序乎？釋新民而先盤
translation_en:
…His Majesty’s heart also accords with the hearts of the successive sage emperors; wherein, then, does his supreme filial piety truly lie? Filial piety is the root of all conduct and the source of all goodness. It can move Heaven and Earth, stir ghosts and spirits, transform the violent, reach birds and beasts, and extend its influence even to plants and trees. If this holds even for an ordinary man, how much more for the Son of Heaven! His Majesty’s filial piety thus proceeds from a single thought to fill the whole space between Heaven and Earth. All you examination candidates have absorbed its influence through what you have heard and seen; surely some among you can set it forth fully. Please present a detailed account.
Question: The Great Learning is a text handed down from Confucius and the gateway through which beginners enter into virtue. Master Zhu’s Commentary in Chapters and Sentences sets out its main principles and particulars, distinguishing its divisions and analyzing its details with nothing left open to dispute. Yet his Questions and Answers further elucidates meanings not fully explained in the Commentary in Chapters and Sentences. Students generally neglect it and fail to study it, and consequently cannot attain a full understanding. Let us now select its main points and discuss them with you.
Manifesting luminous virtue, renewing the people, and resting in the highest good are its three guiding principles. Who are those in the world who do not strive to manifest luminous virtue, disdain renewing the people, and do not seek to rest in the highest good? Investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world are its eight steps. Who are those in the world who, without examining their beginning, abruptly speak of the subsequent steps? In explaining the manifestation of luminous virtue, it concludes with the Canon of the Emperor: is there an order to what is said? In explaining the renewal of the people, it begins with the basin…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
銘所論果有義乎切磋琢磨於學問自
脩之功何所別聽訟無訟於明德新民
之義何所當有言格物致知所當先而
不可後者兩條可指明歟有言涵養本
原之功以為格物致知之本者五條可
歷數歟道有善惡也而誠意者何所先
心有體用也而正心者何所急且意誠
則心宜無不正矣何為有不在之語心
正則身宜無不脩矣何為有好惡之偏
===
仁讓言家貪戾言人而家與人果有別
乎首桃夭次蓼蕭終鳲鳩而三詩之序
亦有意乎至如孝弟慈三者釋齊家治
國既以為言矣而復見於治國平天下
之章不幾於重覆歟自身而家而國而
天下均為推己及人之事矣而釋傳者
一事自為一說若不能相通歟絜矩二
字平天下之要道也後人深得此章之
旨者誰耶敬之一字聖學之所以成始
punctuated: 銘所論，果有義乎？切磋琢磨，於學問自脩之功何所別？聽訟無訟，於明德新民之義何所當？有言格物致知所當先而不可後者，兩條可指明歟？有言涵養本原之功，以為格物致知之本者，五條可歷數歟？道有善惡也，而誠意者何所先？心有體用也，而正心者何所急？且意誠則心宜無不正矣，何為有不在之語？心正則身宜無不脩矣，何為有好惡之偏？仁讓言家，貪戾言人，而家與人果有別乎？首《桃夭》，次《蓼蕭》，終《鳲鳩》，而三詩之序亦有意乎？至如孝弟慈三者，釋齊家治國既以為言矣，而復見於治國平天下之章，不幾於重覆歟？自身而家而國而天下，均為推己及人之事矣，而釋傳者一事自為一說，若不能相通歟？絜矩二字，平天下之要道也，後人深得此章之旨者誰耶？敬之一字，聖學之所以成始
translation_en:
…does what is discussed in the inscription indeed have significance? How do cutting, filing, carving, and polishing differ as forms of effort in learning and self-cultivation? How do hearing lawsuits and bringing about the absence of lawsuits correspond to the meanings of illuminating luminous virtue and renewing the people? Two passages speak of what must come first in investigating things and extending knowledge, and must not be postponed: can you identify them clearly? Five passages speak of nurturing the fundamental source as the foundation for investigating things and extending knowledge: can you enumerate them? The Way has good and evil [?]; what, then, should take precedence in making the intentions sincere? The mind has substance and function; what, then, is most urgent in rectifying it? Moreover, if the intentions are sincere, the mind should invariably be rectified; why, then, is there mention of its being absent? If the mind is rectified, the person should invariably be cultivated; why, then, are there partialities in liking and disliking?

Benevolence and deference are discussed in terms of the family, while greed and perversity are discussed in terms of the individual: is there indeed a distinction between family and individual? First comes “The Peach Tree, Lush and Fair” (Tao yao), next “Tall Southernwood” (Liao xiao) [?], and finally “The Cuckoo” (Shi jiu): is there also an intention behind the sequence of these three poems? As for filial devotion, fraternal respect, and parental kindness, these three have already been mentioned in explaining regulating the family and governing the state, yet they appear again in the chapter on governing the state and bringing peace to All-under-Heaven. Does this not verge on repetition? Proceeding from oneself to the family, to the state, and to All-under-Heaven—all are matters of extending to others what one applies to oneself. Yet those who explicate the Commentary give a separate explanation for each matter, as though they could not be interconnected: is that so? The two characters “applying the measuring square” (xie ju) express the essential way to bring peace to All-under-Heaven. Who among later scholars profoundly grasped the purport of this chapter? The single character “reverence” is that by which the learning of the sages accomplishes its beginning…

translation_en:
…Does what the inscription discusses indeed have significance [?]? How do cutting, filing, chiseling, and polishing differ in their application to the work of learning and self-cultivation? How do hearing lawsuits and bringing about an absence of lawsuits correspond to the principles of manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people? Two passages speak of what must precede the investigation of things and the extension of knowledge and must not be left until afterward: can you identify them clearly? Five passages speak of nurturing the fundamental source as the foundation for investigating things and extending knowledge: can you enumerate them? The Way has good and evil [?]: what, then, should take precedence in making the intentions sincere? The mind has substance and function: what, then, is most urgent in rectifying it? Moreover, if the intentions are sincere, the mind should invariably be rectified; why, then, is there mention of the mind’s being absent? If the mind is rectified, the person should invariably be cultivated; why, then, are there biases in liking and disliking?

In speaking of benevolence and deference, the text says “family”; in speaking of greed and perversity, it says “person.” Is there indeed a distinction between family and person here? It begins with “The Peach Tree Is Tender and Young” (Tao yao), continues with “Tall Southernwood” (Liao xiao), and ends with “The Cuckoo” (Shi jiu): is there also an intention behind the order of these three poems? As for filial devotion, fraternal respect, and parental kindness, these three have already been discussed in explaining the regulation of the family and the government of the state. Yet they appear again in the chapter on governing the state and bringing peace to all under Heaven: does this not verge on repetition? From oneself to the family, to the state, and to all under Heaven, all are matters of extending what pertains to oneself to others. Yet the commentator on the Commentary gives a separate explanation for each matter, as though they could not be interconnected—is this so? The two characters “measuring with the square” express the essential way of bringing peace to all under Heaven. Who among later scholars profoundly grasped the purport of this chapter? The single word “reverence” is that through which the learning of the sages achieves its beginning…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而成終也後學能知用力之方者誰耶
凡此皆讀大學者之所當知而或問中
之所備載者也幸詳言之以觀窮經造
詣之學
問自古國家建立儲貳所以承宗廟之重
繫臣民之心事莫有大焉者也然易曰
蒙以養正聖功也書曰慎厥終惟其始
則教養輔翼之功尤當慎重於厥初焉
古者元子之生接以太牢負以卜士孩
===
提有教輔翼有人或問安於內竪或抗
法於魯公跡其德器治功之所成就卓
乎不可及已漢唐以來英君誼辟亦各
知所用心有委重二傅年甫十二輙通
論語崇尚儒學太子而下莫不受經其
人可指言歟有賜以帝範而極諫責之
羣臣導以師傅而每見必自先拜其人
可詳陳歟作書有法蓋有就學於資善
堂者矣而所輔之人何如師保賓客蓋
punctuated:
而成終也。後學能知用力之方者誰耶？凡此皆讀《大學》者之所當知，而《或問》中之所備載者也。幸詳言之，以觀窮經造詣之學。
問：自古國家建立儲貳，所以承宗廟之重，繫臣民之心，事莫有大焉者也。然《易》曰：「蒙以養正，聖功也。」《書》曰：「慎厥終，惟其始。」則教養輔翼之功，尤當慎重於厥初焉。古者元子之生，接以太牢，負以卜士；孩提有教，輔翼有人。或問安於內竪，或抗法於魯公。跡其德器、治功之所成就，卓乎不可及已。漢唐以來，英君誼辟亦各知所用心。有委重二傅，年甫十二輙通《論語》；崇尚儒學，太子而下莫不受經。其人可指言歟？有賜以《帝範》，而極諫責之羣臣；導以師傅，而每見必自先拜。其人可詳陳歟？作書有法，蓋有就學於資善堂者矣，而所輔之人何如？師保賓客，蓋
translation_en:
…and brings it to completion. Among later students, who understood how to direct their efforts? All these are matters that readers of the Great Learning ought to understand, and that are fully set forth in the Questions and Answers (Huowen). Please discuss them in detail, so that we may assess your scholarly attainments in investigating the classics thoroughly.
Question: Since antiquity, states have established heirs apparent to shoulder the weighty responsibility of the ancestral temples and bind the hearts of officials and people. No matter is more important. Yet the Book of Changes says, “To nurture rectitude in the immature is the work of a sage,” and the Book of Documents says, “To take care over the end, attend to the beginning.” Thus the work of educating, nurturing, assisting, and guiding an heir requires particular care at the very outset. In antiquity, the birth of a principal son was greeted with a full sacrificial offering of ox, sheep, and pig, and he was carried by an officer selected through divination. He received instruction from infancy, with men appointed to assist and guide him. One inquired after his father’s well-being through an attendant of the inner palace; another upheld disciplinary rules against the Duke of Lu [?]. When we trace their achievements in moral character, capacity, and government, they stand far beyond reach. Since the Han and Tang, outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns likewise understood where to devote their attention. There was one who entrusted weighty responsibilities to two preceptors and who, at barely twelve years of age, already understood the Analects; there was another who honored Confucian learning, so that everyone from the heir apparent downward received instruction in the classics. Can you identify these men? There was one who bestowed the Model for Emperors (Difan) upon his heir and charged his assembled ministers with remonstrating to the utmost; another guided his heir through teachers and preceptors and invariably bowed first whenever he met them. Can you give a detailed account of these men? As for writing according to proper models, there was one who studied in the Zishan Hall; what sort of person was it whom his teachers assisted? As for grand preceptors, grand guardians, and guests of the heir apparent, indeed…

translation_en:
…and thus bring it to completion. Who among later students understood how to direct their efforts? All these are matters that readers of the Great Learning ought to know, and they are fully recorded in the Questions and Answers on the Great Learning (Daxue huowen). Please discuss them in detail, so that we may assess the depth of your learning and attainment in investigating the Classics.

Question: Since antiquity, states have established heirs apparent to carry the weighty responsibility of maintaining the ancestral temples and to bind together the hearts of officials and people. No matter is more important. Yet the Book of Changes says, “To nurture rectitude in the inexperienced is the work of a sage,” and the Book of Documents says, “To take care over the end, attend to the beginning.” Thus the work of educating, nurturing, assisting, and guiding an heir demands particular care at the outset. In antiquity, when the principal son was born, he was welcomed with a full sacrificial offering of ox, sheep, and pig, and carried by a gentleman selected through divination. From infancy he received instruction, and there were men to assist and guide him. One inquired of an inner attendant about his father’s well-being; another upheld the rules before the Duke of Lu. Tracing their achievements in moral character, capacity, and government, we find an eminence beyond reach. Can you identify them? There was one who bestowed the Model for Emperors (Difan) and charged his assembled officials with remonstrating to the utmost; another received guidance from his tutors and invariably bowed first whenever he met them. Can you give detailed accounts of these men? There were principles embodied in writings composed for this purpose; indeed, there was one who studied at the Zishan Hall. What sort of person was he whom they assisted? As for grand preceptors, grand guardians, and advisers to the heir apparent, there were…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有處以耆舊老臣者矣而爲教之術安
在究其法意所存德業所就抑果有合
於古人否歟洪惟我
朝
列聖相承儲副之建
宮坊之制盖盡善而盡美矣然所以教之輔
之之道可述其一二乎較諸歷代亦果
有異同否乎諸士子豫養用世之學亦
必有見於此者矣願詳言之吾將以聞
===
于
上
問書曰學古入官易曰君子多識前言往
行以畜其德學固不可以不博也然考
諸往古驗其實用亦有不專於博者如
商周盛時賢才相望體用具備其人不
可尚已下此漢有論過伊管而治安一
策有救時弊學際天人而賢良三策切
中帝心固有可稱然亦有縁飾儒術而
punctuated:
有處以耆舊老臣者矣，而爲教之術安在？究其法意所存、德業所就，抑果有合於古人否歟？洪惟我朝列聖相承，儲副之建、宮坊之制，盖盡善而盡美矣。然所以教之輔之之道，可述其一二乎？較諸歷代，亦果有異同否乎？諸士子豫養用世之學，亦必有見於此者矣。願詳言之，吾將以聞于上。

問：書曰：「學古入官。」易曰：「君子多識前言往行，以畜其德。」學固不可以不博也。然考諸往古，驗其實用，亦有不專於博者。如商周盛時，賢才相望，體用具備，其人不可尚已。下此，漢有論過伊管，而治安一策有救時弊；學際天人，而賢良三策切中帝心，固有可稱。然亦有縁飾儒術而
translation_en:
…some of these posts were filled with venerable senior ministers; but wherein lay their methods of instruction? Examining the intent embodied in their arrangements and their achievements in virtue and public service, did these indeed accord with those of the ancients? We reverently reflect that, under our dynasty’s succession of sage sovereigns, the establishment of the heir apparent and the organization of the Eastern Palace offices have attained complete excellence and perfection. Yet can you recount something of the means by which the heir is instructed and assisted? In comparison with successive earlier dynasties, what similarities or differences are there? You candidates, preparing yourselves through learning for service in the world, must surely have insights into this. Please explain them fully; I shall report them to His Majesty.

Question: The Book of Documents says, “Study antiquity and enter official service.” The Book of Changes says, “The gentleman acquaints himself widely with the words and deeds of the past, thereby nurturing his virtue.” Learning certainly must be broad. Yet if we examine antiquity and test learning by its practical application, there were also those whose strength did not lie exclusively in breadth. At the height of the Shang and Zhou, worthy and talented men appeared in succession, fully equipped in both substance and practical application; they could not be surpassed. Thereafter, under the Han, there was one whose arguments surpassed those of Yi Yin and Guan Zhong, and whose single policy essay on order and security offered remedies for contemporary abuses; another’s learning encompassed Heaven and humanity, and his three policy essays for the examination of Worthy and Good candidates precisely met the emperor’s concerns. These certainly deserve praise. Yet there were also those who used Confucian learning as an embellishment and…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有處以耆舊老臣者矣而爲教之術安
在究其法意所存德業所就抑果有合
於古人否歟洪惟我
朝
列聖相承儲副之建
宮坊之制盖盡善而盡美矣然所以教之輔
之之道可述其一二乎較諸歷代亦果
有異同否乎諸士子豫養用世之學亦
必有見於此者矣願詳言之吾將以聞
===
于
上
問書曰學古入官易曰君子多識前言往
行以畜其德學固不可以不博也然考
諸往古驗其實用亦有不專於博者如
商周盛時賢才相望體用具備其人不
可尚已下此漢有論過伊管而治安一
策有救時弊學際天人而賢良三策切
中帝心固有可稱然亦有緣飾儒術而
punctuated:

translation_en:
…There were also those who appointed venerable senior ministers to these positions; yet wherein lay their methods of instruction? Examining the intentions embodied in their arrangements and their achievements in virtue and service, did these truly accord with the ancients? We reverently reflect that, under our dynasty, sage sovereigns have succeeded one another, and the establishment of the heir apparent and the organization of the Eastern Palace offices have surely attained complete excellence and perfection. Yet can you recount one or two aspects of the methods used to instruct and assist him? Compared with successive earlier dynasties, what similarities or differences are there? You candidates, who have been cultivating the learning needed for service in the world, must have insights into this matter. Please explain them fully; I shall report them to His Majesty.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曲學阿世博極羣書而劇秦美新至於
安社稷輔幼孤者乃在於少文不學之
人可歷指而言之歟唐有文過子房術
密賈誼而有內相之稱抵轢晉魏上軋
周漢而成潮陽之化固不可及然亦有
學比相如而名節蔑聞文學絕倫而才
猷靡邵至於陳十事獻六箴者乃出於
好獵任子之流可悉數而論之歟及宋
有文章名冠天下而著嘉祐之勳有文
===
學無所不通而致元祐之治學博之效
固有可見有如博學强記者疑可取也
而乃怙勢妬賢少習吏事者若可短也
而能定策開基何彼此之不同耶通今
學古者在所與也而乃變法誤國學術
不足者似可少也而能退敵弭兵何彼
此之有異耶夫以其博也而無益於治
以其不博也而有補於時則君子之學
果貴於博否乎雖然天下之理出於一
punctuated:
曲學阿世，博極羣書而劇秦美新。至於安社稷、輔幼孤者，乃在於少文不學之人，可歷指而言之歟？唐有文過子房、術密賈誼而有內相之稱，抵轢晉魏、上軋周漢而成潮陽之化，固不可及。然亦有學比相如而名節蔑聞，文學絕倫而才猷靡邵。至於陳十事、獻六箴者，乃出於好獵任子之流，可悉數而論之歟？

及宋，有文章名冠天下而著嘉祐之勳，有文學無所不通而致元祐之治，學博之效固有可見。有如博學强記者，疑可取也，而乃怙勢妬賢；少習吏事者，若可短也，而能定策開基，何彼此之不同耶？通今學古者，在所與也，而乃變法誤國；學術不足者，似可少也，而能退敵弭兵，何彼此之有異耶？夫以其博也，而無益於治；以其不博也，而有補於時，則君子之學果貴於博否乎？雖然，天下之理出於一
translation_en:
…distorted learning to curry favor with their age, and, despite ranging through the whole wealth of books, wrote Criticizing Qin and Praising Xin. Yet those who secured the state and assisted its orphaned young ruler were men of little literary accomplishment and no learning. Can you identify them individually and discuss them? In the Tang, there were those whose literary ability surpassed Zifang’s and whose statecraft was more meticulous than Jia Yi’s, earning them the designation “inner councilor”; there were those whose writings rivaled those of the Jin and Wei and reached back to compete with those of the Zhou and Han, and who brought about the moral transformation of Chaoyang. Their achievements were indeed beyond compare. Yet there were also those whose learning matched Xiangru’s but whose reputation and integrity scarcely merited mention, and those whose literary learning was unequaled but whose ability and plans achieved no distinction [?]. As for those who presented the ten proposals and submitted the six admonitions, they came from the ranks of men fond of hunting or admitted to office through hereditary privilege. Can you enumerate them all and discuss them?

Coming to the Song, there were those whose literary reputation stood foremost in the empire and who achieved distinguished service during the Jiayou era, and those whose literary learning encompassed everything and who brought about the good government of the Yuanyou era. Here the effects of broad learning can certainly be seen. Someone of extensive learning and strong memory might seem worthy of approval, yet he relied on powerful backing and envied worthy men. Someone who had practiced administrative work from youth might seem open to criticism, yet he settled the plan for founding the dynasty and laid its foundations. Why were the two so different? Someone versed in present affairs and learned in antiquity deserved approval, yet he changed the laws and harmed the state. Someone whose learning was insufficient might seem deserving of scant regard, yet he repelled the enemy and brought warfare to an end. Why were the two so different? If a man’s breadth of learning brings no benefit to government, while another’s lack of broad learning nevertheless enables him to serve the needs of his time, does the learning of a gentleman truly prize breadth or not? Even so, the principles of all under Heaven proceed from one…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
原而何以有取於博古今事物萬有不
齊而何以能致其博諸士子積學待用
有年請詳言之毋畧
問邦本固在於民國事莫大乎戎撫民勵
兵誠國家久安長治之策舍是非可以
言治也姑以廣西論之古號百粤之地
素為難治况邇年以来民敝兵壞莫此
為甚以民言則土曠人稀弱肉强食深
山大澤夷類十占八九窮簷部屋編氓
===
僅得二三師旅迭動其財已窮科差百
出其力已竭民敝若此司民牧者可忍
而不之究心哉兹欲祛除而撫摩之術
果安在以兵言則行伍空虚武備廢弛
粮餉稍緩剽掠遽及於省城勞苦窮年
役占無間於小大蠻寇肆暴而守卒逃
匿主将遇害而麾下坐視兵壞若此司
兵政者可忍而置諸度外哉兹欲飭治
而振起之計将安出夫法敝於今當稽
punctuated:
原，而何以有取於博？古今事物，萬有不齊，而何以能致其博？諸士子積學待用有年，請詳言之，毋畧。

問：邦本固在於民，國事莫大乎戎。撫民勵兵，誠國家久安長治之策，舍是非可以言治也。姑以廣西論之，古號百粤之地，素為難治。况邇年以来，民敝兵壞，莫此為甚。以民言，則土曠人稀，弱肉强食；深山大澤，夷類十占八九；窮簷部屋，編氓僅得二三。師旅迭動，其財已窮；科差百出，其力已竭。民敝若此，司民牧者可忍而不之究心哉？兹欲祛除而撫摩之術，果安在？以兵言，則行伍空虚，武備廢弛；粮餉稍緩，剽掠遽及於省城；勞苦窮年，役占無間於小大；蠻寇肆暴，而守卒逃匿；主将遇害，而麾下坐視。兵壞若此，司兵政者可忍而置諸度外哉？兹欲飭治而振起之計，将安出？夫法敝於今，當稽
translation_en:
…source, yet why should breadth of learning be valued? The affairs and things of past and present differ in countless ways: how can one attain comprehensive knowledge of them? You candidates have spent years accumulating learning while awaiting employment. Please explain this fully, omitting nothing.

Question: The foundation of the state assuredly lies in the people, and among affairs of state none is more important than military affairs. Caring for the people and strengthening the troops are indeed the means of securing lasting peace and enduring good government for the state. Without these, one cannot speak of good government. Take Guangxi as an example. Known in antiquity as the land of the Hundred Yue, it has always been difficult to govern. Moreover, in recent years nowhere has the exhaustion of the people and the deterioration of the troops been more severe. As for the people, the land is extensive but sparsely populated, and the strong prey upon the weak. In the remote mountains and great marshlands, non-Han peoples account for eight or nine out of ten; registered commoners living in impoverished dwellings [?] amount to barely two or three. Repeated military mobilizations have exhausted their wealth; levies and labor requisitions imposed in countless forms have drained their strength. With the people so exhausted, can those charged with governing them bear to refrain from giving this their earnest attention? Where, then, are the methods for removing these afflictions [?] and providing care and relief? As for the troops, the ranks are depleted and military preparedness has fallen into neglect. At the slightest delay in provisions and pay, their plundering immediately reaches the provincial capital. They toil throughout the year, while officials great and small alike appropriate their services for private labor. When non-Han raiders unleash violence, the garrison soldiers flee and hide; when their commanding general is killed, his subordinates stand idly by. With the troops in such disorder, can those responsible for military administration bear to disregard it? From where, then, will come a plan to restore discipline and reinvigorate them? Since the regulations have become defective in our day, one ought to examine…

translation_en:
…their origins; but why should one draw upon extensive knowledge of antiquity? Now, the myriad things and affairs are diverse: how can one attain comprehensive knowledge of them? You candidates have spent years accumulating learning in readiness for service. Please explain in detail, omitting nothing.

Question: The foundation of the state assuredly lies in its people, and among affairs of state none is greater than military affairs. Caring for the people and invigorating the troops are indeed the means to lasting peace and enduring good government. Without these, one cannot speak of governing. Let us consider Guangxi. Known in antiquity as the land of the Hundred Yue, it has always been difficult to govern. Moreover, in recent years, nowhere has the exhaustion of the people and the deterioration of the military been more severe. As for the people, the land is extensive and sparsely populated, and the strong prey upon the weak. In the deep mountains and vast marshlands, non-Han peoples account for eight or nine out of ten; among the humble dwellings [?], registered commoners number only two or three out of ten. With the military so deteriorated, can those responsible for military administration bear to put the matter out of their minds? From where, then, will come a plan to restore order and revive the forces? Since present-day institutions have fallen into decay, one ought to examine…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諸古古之人有為鬱林太守而招降數
萬有為柳州刺史而流逋四歸有攝興
安而餽餉大為民利有知梧州而免稅
以為民便皆善於撫民者也果可施於
今乎有為桂州都督而息轉漕之勞有
為容管經畧使而貽詔答之榮有平邕
州之亂而廣人磨崖紀功有死靜江之
戰而部將自焚無降皆善於勵兵者也
果可用於今乎諸士子生長斯邦目擊
===
而心惟久矣願為我陳之
punctuated: 諸古。古之人有為鬱林太守而招降數萬，有為柳州刺史而流逋四歸，有攝興安而餽餉大為民利，有知梧州而免稅以為民便，皆善於撫民者也，果可施於今乎？有為桂州都督而息轉漕之勞，有為容管經畧使而貽詔答之榮，有平邕州之亂而廣人磨崖紀功，有死靜江之戰而部將自焚無降，皆善於勵兵者也，果可用於今乎？諸士子生長斯邦，目擊而心惟久矣，願為我陳之。
translation_en: …against ancient precedents. Among men of old, one served as governor of Yulin and induced tens of thousands to surrender; another served as prefect of Liuzhou and brought fugitives and displaced people back from all directions; another administered Xing’an in an acting capacity and greatly benefited the people through his arrangements for provisioning the troops; and another governed Wuzhou and exempted the people from taxes for their relief. All were skilled in caring for the people. Can their methods indeed be applied today? One served as area commander-in-chief of Guizhou and relieved the burden of transporting grain; another served as military commissioner of Rongguan and received the honor of an imperial reply [?]; another quelled the rebellion in Yongzhou, and the people of Guangxi engraved a cliff face to commemorate his achievement; and another died in the battle of Jingjiang, while his subordinate commanders burned themselves to death rather than surrender. All were skilled in inspiring their troops. Can their methods indeed be employed today? You candidates were born and raised in this land; you have witnessed its conditions and pondered them for a long time. I ask you to set forth your views for me.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諸古古之人有為鬱林太守而招降數
萬有為柳州刺史而流逋四歸有攝興
安而餽餉大為民利有知梧州而免稅
以為民便皆善於撫民者也果可施於
今乎有為桂州都督而息轉漕之勞有
為容管經畧使而貽詔答之榮有平邕
州之亂而廣人磨崖紀功有死靜江之
戰而部將自焚無降皆善於勵兵者也
果可用於今乎諸士子生長斯邦目擊

而心惟久矣願為我陳之

translation_en: …Those men of antiquity [?]: one served as Governor of Yulin and induced tens of thousands to surrender; one served as Prefect of Liuzhou, and displaced people and fugitives returned from all directions; one served as acting administrator of Xing’an and greatly benefited the people through the provisioning of supplies; and one administered Wuzhou and remitted taxes for the people’s relief. All were skilled at inspiring their soldiers. Can their methods indeed be employed today? title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
發憤忘食樂以忘憂
黃鼒
同考試官訓導余批題似易而難作者多
失之冗泛精緻者僅見此篇
考試官教諭趙批認理明措辭當可取
考試官教諭朱批簡明通暢可嘉
聖人自言其好學求之切而樂之深焉蓋天下
===
之理必學之而後得也然則聖人未得而求之
切已得而樂之深其好學之篤為何如哉想昔
吾夫子因子路不對葉公之問故告之以此若
謂吾之所以為人無他惟篤於好學而已彼其
應事接物之間莫不各有本然一定之理方其
未有所得則理與我若有間也而憤可容已乎
殆必奮發激昂孳孳焉直欲求通夫此事之理
心一於是何食之暇計哉黽勉精進汲汲焉直
欲求達夫此物之理志有所在何食之暇念哉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

發憤忘食，樂以忘憂。

黃鼒

同考試官訓導余批：題似易而難，作者多失之冗泛，精緻者僅見此篇。

考試官教諭趙批：認理明，措辭當，可取。

考試官教諭朱批：簡明通暢，可嘉。

聖人自言其好學，求之切而樂之深焉。蓋天下之理，必學之而後得也。然則聖人未得而求之切，已得而樂之深，其好學之篤為何如哉！想昔吾夫子因子路不對葉公之問，故告之以此。若謂：吾之所以為人，無他，惟篤於好學而已。彼其應事接物之間，莫不各有本然一定之理。方其未有所得，則理與我若有間也，而憤可容已乎？殆必奮發激昂，孳孳焉，直欲求通夫此事之理，心一於是，何食之暇計哉？黽勉精進，汲汲焉，直欲求達夫此物之理，志有所在，何食之暇念哉？
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“In his earnest pursuit he forgets to eat; in his joy he forgets his worries.”

Huang Zi 黃鼒

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: The topic seems easy but is difficult. Most writers err through verbosity and vagueness; this is the only essay I have seen that is finely wrought.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: His understanding of principle is clear, and his wording apt. Worth selecting.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Concise, clear, and fluent. Commendable.

The sage speaks of his own love of learning: the earnestness of his pursuit and the depth of his joy in it. For the principles of all things under Heaven must be studied before they can be grasped. If, then, the sage pursues them earnestly before grasping them, and rejoices deeply in them once he has grasped them, how profound must his devotion to learning be!

I imagine how, long ago, our Master told Zilu this because Zilu had not answered the question posed by the Lord of She. It was as though he were saying: What makes me the person I am is nothing other than steadfast devotion to learning. In responding to affairs and engaging with things, each has its own inherent, fixed principle. While I have not yet grasped it, there seems to be a gap between that principle and myself. How, then, could I allow my earnest striving to cease? Surely I must rouse myself with fervor and work tirelessly, intent only on comprehending the principle of this affair. With my mind wholly absorbed in this, what leisure have I to think of eating? I exert myself and advance diligently, striving urgently, intent only on apprehending the principle of this thing. With my purpose thus engaged, what leisure have I to remember food?

First Session

Four Books

“In his ardent pursuit he forgets to eat; in his joy he forgets his cares.”

Huang Zi

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: “The topic appears easy but is difficult. Most writers err by being verbose and vague; this is the only finely wrought essay I have seen.”

The sage speaks of his own love of learning: how earnestly he seeks and how deeply he delights. For the principles of all things under Heaven can be grasped only through learning. title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
是何耶理無終窮不造其極自有不容於已者
耳及其既有所得則我與理若相契也而樂寧
有既乎殆見天君泰然靜與天游雖宮商相宣
不足以喻之矣外憂豈足以介于懷胷次悠然
動與天合雖律呂相和不足以方之矣外慮豈
足以動于內又何耶心無繫累獨得之妙自有
莫知其然者耳是則惟無憤也憤則自有以忘
乎食惟無樂也樂則自有以忘乎憂一憤一樂
循環代至吾之為人如斯而已矣抑觀聖人猶
===
天然天道有寒有暑而化工之妙以全聖人有
憤有樂而學問之功以備夫豈有所勉强於其
間哉乃若夫子之所自言一則曰好學二則曰
好學蓋亦謙己誨人之意是不以既聖而自居
也然深味之則其全體至極純亦不已之妙有
非聖人不能及者亦在其中矣有志於希聖者
宜致思焉
溥博如天淵泉如淵見而民莫不敬言而
民莫不信行而民莫不說
punctuated:
是何耶？理無終窮，不造其極，自有不容於已者耳。及其既有所得，則我與理若相契也，而樂寧有既乎？殆見天君泰然，靜與天游，雖宮商相宣，不足以喻之矣，外憂豈足以介于懷？胷次悠然，動與天合，雖律呂相和，不足以方之矣，外慮豈足以動于內？又何耶？心無繫累，獨得之妙，自有莫知其然者耳。是則惟無憤也，憤則自有以忘乎食；惟無樂也，樂則自有以忘乎憂。一憤一樂，循環代至，吾之為人如斯而已矣。抑觀聖人猶天，然天道有寒有暑，而化工之妙以全；聖人有憤有樂，而學問之功以備。夫豈有所勉强於其間哉？乃若夫子之所自言，一則曰好學，二則曰好學，蓋亦謙己誨人之意，是不以既聖而自居也。然深味之，則其全體至極、純亦不已之妙，有非聖人不能及者，亦在其中矣。有志於希聖者，宜致思焉。

溥博如天，淵泉如淵，見而民莫不敬，言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。
translation_en:
Why is this? Principle is inexhaustible: until one reaches its utmost extent, there is naturally something that will not allow one to stop. Once I have attained some understanding, however, I seem to accord with principle; how, then, could my joy have an end? The mind, the ruler within, is at ease; in stillness it roams with Heaven. Even the mutually resounding notes of gong and shang cannot convey this state. How could external troubles intrude upon my thoughts? Within my breast all is serene; in activity I accord with Heaven. Even the harmonizing pitch pipes cannot compare with this state. How could external concerns stir me within? Why, again, is this? The mind is free of attachments and burdens, and the marvel of what one has grasped for oneself naturally includes something whose workings no one can explain. Thus, unless there is no fervent striving, that striving naturally makes me forget food; unless there is no joy, that joy naturally makes me forget sorrow. Striving and joy come in turn, in a recurring cycle. This is simply the sort of person I am.

Consider, moreover, how the sage resembles Heaven. The Way of Heaven has cold and heat, through which the marvel of its transforming work is made complete; the sage has striving and joy, through which the work of learning is brought to fulfillment. How could there be any forced effort in this? As for what the Master says of himself, first he speaks of loving learning, and then again he speaks of loving learning. This also expresses his intention to be modest about himself and to instruct others: he does not claim the standing of one who has already become a sage. Yet if we ponder his words deeply, they also contain the marvel of his complete realization of the utmost perfection, his purity and unceasing activity—something none but a sage can attain. Those who aspire to sagehood should reflect upon this.

“Vast and broad as Heaven, deep and ever-flowing as an abyss: when he appears, none among the people fails to respect him; when he speaks, none among the people fails to trust him; when he acts, none among the people fails to be pleased.”

How could external sorrows intrude upon one’s heart? Within the breast all is serene, and in activity one accords with Heaven. Even the harmonious pitch pipes cannot compare with this state. How could external concerns stir one inwardly? Why, again, is this so? With the mind free of attachments and burdens, the wonder of understanding gained for oneself naturally has something whose workings no one can comprehend. Thus, unless there is ardent striving, that is all; once there is such striving, it naturally makes one forget to eat. Unless there is joy, that is all; once there is joy, it naturally makes one forget sorrow. Striving and joy come in alternation, each succeeding the other. This alone is the sort of person I am.

Consider, moreover, how the sage resembles Heaven. The Way of Heaven has cold and heat, through which the wondrous work of transformation is made complete; the sage has striving and joy, through which the work of learning is brought to fulfillment. Could there be anything forced in this? As for what the Master said of himself, first he spoke of loving learning, and again he spoke of loving learning. This, too, expressed his intention to be humble and instruct others: he did not presume upon having already become a sage. Yet, if we ponder these words deeply, they also contain the wonder of his whole being reaching the utmost perfection, pure and unceasing—a state that none but a sage can attain. Those who aspire to sagehood should reflect upon this.

Vast and broad as Heaven, a deep-flowing spring like the depths: when he appears, none among the people fail to respect him; when he speaks, none fail to trust him; when he acts, none fail to delight in him.

text:

Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the language flows smoothly. It deserves inclusion as a model for later students.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Its understanding is precise and pertinent. The author must be deeply versed in the Learning of Principle.”

The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the virtue of the utmost sage: accumulated within, it reaches the greatest fullness; manifested outwardly, it is perfectly appropriate. For what exists within must take form without. Who could say that the perfect appropriateness of sagely virtue’s manifestation does not arise from its accumulation in the greatest fullness? Chapter Thirty-One of the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the Way of Heaven in terms of the lesser virtues flowing like streams. Now, in the utmost sage under Heaven, perceptiveness, discernment, sagacity, and wisdom originate in knowledge possessed from birth; benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom are rooted in what is inherently his. Accumulated within, these are indeed all-embracing and vast, deep and inexhaustible as a wellspring; they manifest outwardly at the proper times. Yet could this amount merely to inward accumulation?

Speaking of its all-embracing vastness: nothing equals Heaven, whose greatness leaves nothing outside it. These five virtues extend everywhere in their breadth, just like the greatness of Heaven; they cannot be apprehended through finite measures. When this all-embracing vastness is described as being like Heaven, we can understand the supreme fullness of their accumulation. Speaking of its depth as a wellspring: nothing equals an abyss, whose depth has no bounds. These five virtues are still and deep, with a firm source, just like the depth of an abyss; they cannot be measured by its shores or banks. Deep and inexhaustible as a wellspring, and …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曰如淵則充積之極其盛也可見夫聖德之盛
如此則其發於外者豈止於以時而已耶是故
見之於身則為德容動容周旋有以聳人之觀
瞻莫不敬之如神明矣形之於言則為德言渙
號宣布有以足人之聽聞莫不信之如蓍龜矣
施之於行則為德行政教覃敷足以感人之心
志而民又豈有不說乎夫聖德之發見而當其
可者如此非充積之盛曷克爾哉大抵莫強於
人心而可以德感莫柔於人心而不可以力服
===
聖人之德既極其盛則外有以正天下之觀内
有以通天下之志其敬信說服自有不期然而
然者矣抑豈止此哉聲名洋溢乎兩間尊親無
間於庶類德之所及直與天道脗合而為一焉
故曰配天
文王視民如傷望道而未之見武王不泄
邇不忘遠
宋澍
同考試官教諭謝批善形容文武憂勤惕
punctuated:
曰如淵，則充積之極，其盛也可見。夫聖德之盛如此，則其發於外者，豈止於以時而已耶？是故見之於身，則為德容，動容周旋，有以聳人之觀瞻，莫不敬之如神明矣；形之於言，則為德言，渙號宣布，有以足人之聽聞，莫不信之如蓍龜矣；施之於行，則為德行，政教覃敷，足以感人之心志，而民又豈有不說乎？夫聖德之發見而當其可者如此，非充積之盛，曷克爾哉？大抵莫強於人心，而可以德感；莫柔於人心，而不可以力服。聖人之德既極其盛，則外有以正天下之觀，内有以通天下之志，其敬信說服，自有不期然而然者矣。抑豈止此哉？聲名洋溢乎兩間，尊親無間於庶類，德之所及，直與天道脗合而為一焉。故曰配天。
文王視民如傷，望道而未之見；武王不泄邇，不忘遠。
宋澍
同考試官教諭謝批：善形容文武憂勤惕
translation_en:
…when it is said to be “like a deep pool,” the fullness of its accumulation and its flourishing abundance can be seen. Since the sage’s virtue flourishes in this way, can its outward expression consist merely in appearing at the proper times? Thus, when manifested in his person, it becomes a virtuous bearing: his every movement and gesture commands people’s attention, and all revere him as they would a divine spirit. When expressed in speech, it becomes virtuous utterance: his proclamations are widely promulgated, fully satisfying those who hear them, and all trust him as they would divining stalks and tortoise shells. When put into practice, it becomes virtuous conduct: his governance and instruction spread far and wide, moving people’s hearts and aspirations. How could the people fail to delight in him? Since the manifestations of the sage’s virtue are thus perfectly appropriate, how could this be achieved without the abundant accumulation within? Nothing, generally speaking, is stronger than the human heart, yet virtue can move it; nothing is softer than the human heart, yet force cannot make it submit. Once the sage’s virtue reaches its fullest flourishing, outwardly it can rectify the outlook of all under Heaven, and inwardly it can bring their aspirations into accord. Their reverence, trust, delight, and submission then arise spontaneously, without being sought. Yet could it stop here? His fame fills the space between Heaven and Earth; all people alike honor and cherish him. Wherever his virtue reaches, it accords perfectly with the Way of Heaven and becomes one with it. Hence it is said that he “matches Heaven.”
“King Wen regarded the people as though they were injured, and gazed toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it; King Wu did not slight those nearby or forget those far away.”
Song Shu 宋澍
Comment by Associate Examiner Xie 謝, Instructor: Skillfully portrays the anxious concern, diligence, and vigilance of Kings Wen and Wu…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
厲之意宛然在目可嘉可嘉
同考試官學正陳批題本正大作者皆蹈
襲陳言令人厭觀此篇融會傳註詞理俱到
真作手也是宜錄出
考試官敎諭趙批文有發越可取
考試官敎諭朱批詞理簡切佳作也
大賢舉二聖之事有不自足其所已足者有不
自忽其所易忽者蓋聖人之心一憂勤惕厲之
心也然則有周二聖之事雖若不同而此心寧
===
有異哉宜孟子並舉而言之也且夫當天下三
分有二之際而以服事殷者文王也文王之心
何心哉彼怙冒西土化行江漢民已安矣而文
也遹求厥寧遹觀厥成視咸和之民尚若瘡痏
之未瘳焉聰明齊聖徽柔懿恭道已至矣而文
也不顯亦臨無射亦保企精一之傳初若堂奧
之未窺焉謹怠荒於已治之餘加緝熈於既聖
之後可謂愛民深而求道切矣其不自足之心
爲何如若夫纘太王王季文王之緒而遂有天
punctuated:
厲之意，宛然在目，可嘉可嘉！

同考試官學正陳批：「題本正大，作者皆蹈襲陳言，令人厭觀。此篇融會傳註，詞理俱到，真作手也，是宜錄出。」

考試官敎諭趙批：「文有發越，可取。」

考試官敎諭朱批：「詞理簡切，佳作也。」

大賢舉二聖之事，有不自足其所已足者，有不自忽其所易忽者。蓋聖人之心，一憂勤惕厲之心也。然則有周二聖之事雖若不同，而此心寧有異哉？宜孟子並舉而言之也。且夫當天下三分有二之際，而以服事殷者，文王也。文王之心，何心哉？彼怙冒西土，化行江漢，民已安矣，而文也遹求厥寧，遹觀厥成，視咸和之民，尚若瘡痏之未瘳焉。聰明齊聖，徽柔懿恭，道已至矣，而文也不顯亦臨，無射亦保，企精一之傳，初若堂奧之未窺焉。謹怠荒於已治之餘，加緝熈於既聖之後，可謂愛民深而求道切矣。其不自足之心爲何如？若夫纘太王王季文王之緒，而遂有天
translation_en:
…their spirit of vigilance and self-discipline appears vividly before our eyes. Admirable, admirable!

Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor, comments: “The topic is inherently upright and grand, but writers all repeat stale expressions, making their work tiresome to read. This essay integrates the commentarial tradition; both its language and its reasoning are fully accomplished. Truly the work of a master hand! It deserves to be selected for inclusion.”

Examiner Zhao, School Instructor, comments: “The writing has expressive vigor and merits selection.”

Examiner Zhu, School Instructor, comments: “Its language and reasoning are concise and pertinent. An excellent composition.”

The great worthy cited the deeds of two sages: one would not rest content with what he had already fully achieved; the other would not allow himself to neglect what he might easily have neglected. For the sage’s heart is wholly a heart of anxious diligence, vigilance, and self-discipline. Thus, although the deeds of the two sages of Zhou may appear different, could their hearts have differed? It was fitting that Mengzi discussed them together.

Consider King Wen: when he possessed two-thirds of the realm, he nevertheless used his position to serve Yin. What sort of heart did King Wen have? He sheltered and protected the western lands, and his transforming influence reached the Jiang and Han rivers. The people were already at peace. Yet Wen continued to seek their tranquility and to attend to its accomplishment. He regarded the people, though all lived in harmony, as if their wounds had yet to heal. Intelligent, discerning, comprehensively wise, admirable in gentleness and excellent in reverence, he had already attained the Way. Yet Wen felt himself watched over even in places unseen, and maintained his virtue without weariness. He aspired to the transmitted teaching of refinement and singleness of purpose, as though he had not yet glimpsed its inner chambers. He guarded against indolence and neglect even after good order had been achieved, and further cultivated luminous virtue even after attaining sagehood. Truly, his love for the people was profound, and his pursuit of the Way earnest. How remarkable was this heart that would never rest content with itself!

As for the one who carried on the legacy of King Tai, Wang Ji, and King Wen, and thus came to possess all under Heaven…

爲何如若夫纘太王王季文王之緒而遂有天
punctuated:
厲之意，宛然在目，可嘉可嘉！
同考試官學正陳批：題本正大，作者皆蹈襲陳言，令人厭觀。此篇融會傳註，詞理俱到，真作手也，是宜錄出。
考試官教諭趙批：文有發越，可取。
考試官教諭朱批：詞理簡切，佳作也。
大賢舉二聖之事，有不自足其所已足者，有不自忽其所易忽者。蓋聖人之心，一憂勤惕厲之心也。然則有周二聖之事，雖若不同，而此心寧有異哉？宜孟子並舉而言之也。且夫當天下三分有二之際，而以服事殷者，文王也。文王之心何心哉？彼怙冒西土，化行江漢，民已安矣，而文也遹求厥寧，遹觀厥成，視咸和之民，尚若瘡痏之未瘳焉。聰明齊聖，徽柔懿恭，道已至矣，而文也不顯亦臨，無射亦保，企精一之傳，初若堂奧之未窺焉。謹怠荒於已治之餘，加緝熈於既聖之後，可謂愛民深而求道切矣。其不自足之心爲何如？若夫纘太王、王季、文王之緒，而遂有天
translation_en:
…the spirit of vigilance is vividly before our eyes. Admirable, admirable!
Associate Examiner Chen, an instructor, comments: The topic itself is upright and substantial, but writers all repeat stale expressions, making their work tiresome to read. This essay integrates the commentaries, achieving excellence in both expression and reasoning. Its author is truly accomplished; it deserves to be recorded here.
Examiner Zhao, an instructor, comments: The writing displays expressive vigor and merits acceptance.
Examiner Zhu, an instructor, comments: Concise and pertinent in both expression and reasoning—a fine composition.
The great worthy cited the deeds of two sages: one did not rest content with what he had already sufficiently achieved; the other did not allow himself to neglect what could easily be neglected. The sage’s heart is wholly a heart of anxious diligence and vigilant self-discipline. Thus, although the deeds of the two sages of Zhou might seem different, could their hearts have differed? It was fitting that Mengzi discussed them together.
Consider King Wen: when he possessed two-thirds of the realm, he nevertheless served Yin. What sort of heart was King Wen’s? He sheltered the western lands, and his transforming influence spread through the regions of the Jiang and Han rivers. The people were already at peace, yet Wen continued to seek their tranquility and attend to their fulfillment. He regarded the people, though all lived in harmony, as if their wounds had still not healed. Intelligent, perceptive, sagacious, wise, gracious, gentle, admirable, and reverent, he had already attained the utmost in the Way. Yet Wen felt himself watched over even where nothing was manifest, and maintained his devotion without weariness. He aspired to the transmitted teaching of refinement and single-mindedness, as though he had yet to glimpse its inner chambers. He guarded against indolence and neglect after order had already been established, and further cultivated luminous virtue after he had already become a sage. Truly, his love for the people was profound and his pursuit of the Way earnest. How remarkable was his refusal to rest content! As for the one who continued the legacy of King Tai, Wang Ji, and King Wen, and thus came to possess all under Heaven…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
下者武王也武王之心何心哉彼邇者耳目之
所常接人易狎也武則聽微言如大政對僕御
如嚴賓初不以其邇而或泄焉遠者耳目之所
不及人易忘也武則視疎逺如左右慮千里於
几席初不以其遠而或遺焉存一敬於易泄之
時持一誠於易忘之頃可謂德之盛而仁之至
矣其不自忽之心又何如噫文武之事不同而
所以為憂勤惕厲則一此天理之所以常存而
人心之所以不死也歟抑不特此惡旨酒好善
===
言者禹此心也執中而立賢無方者湯此心也
思兼三王以施四事者周公亦此心也然文武
之聖上有以接禹湯之統下有以啓周公之傳
先後一揆父子一心此其所以開八百年之洪
基超二代而獨盛歟
易
出可以守宗廟社稷以為祭主也
黃鼒
同考試官訓導余批題本平易作者多不
punctuated:
下者，武王也。武王之心何心哉？彼邇者，耳目之所常接，人易狎也；武則聽微言如大政，對僕御如嚴賓，初不以其邇而或泄焉。遠者，耳目之所不及，人易忘也；武則視疎逺如左右，慮千里於几席，初不以其遠而或遺焉。存一敬於易泄之時，持一誠於易忘之頃，可謂德之盛而仁之至矣。其不自忽之心又何如？噫！文武之事不同，而所以為憂勤惕厲則一。此天理之所以常存，而人心之所以不死也歟？抑不特此，惡旨酒、好善言者，禹此心也；執中而立賢無方者，湯此心也；思兼三王以施四事者，周公亦此心也。然文武之聖，上有以接禹湯之統，下有以啓周公之傳，先後一揆，父子一心。此其所以開八百年之洪基，超二代而獨盛歟？

易
出可以守宗廟社稷，以為祭主也。
黃鼒

同考試官訓導余批：題本平易，作者多不
translation_en:
…the one who came to possess all under Heaven was King Wu. What sort of heart did King Wu have? People easily grow overly familiar with those nearby, whom their eyes and ears constantly encounter. Yet King Wu listened to even minor remarks as he would to great affairs of government, and treated servants and charioteers as he would honored guests. Never did he allow their proximity to make him lax. People easily forget those far away, beyond the reach of their eyes and ears. Yet King Wu regarded those distant from him as though they were at his side, and, seated at his table, gave thought to those a thousand li away. Never did he allow their distance to make him neglect them. He preserved undivided reverence when it was easy to grow lax and maintained undivided sincerity when it was easy to forget. This may truly be called fullness of virtue and the utmost benevolence. What, then, was this heart that never allowed itself to become heedless? Ah! The affairs of Kings Wen and Wu differed, but their anxious diligence and vigilant self-discipline were one. Was this not why Heaven’s principle constantly endured and the human heart did not become deadened? Nor was this all. Yu, who disliked fine wine and delighted in good words, had this same heart. Tang, who held fast to the mean and appointed worthy men without restriction, had this same heart. The Duke of Zhou, who sought to combine the achievements of the Three Kings in carrying out four undertakings, also had this same heart. Yet the sagehood of Wen and Wu enabled them to continue the line of Yu and Tang before them and to open the way for the Duke of Zhou’s transmission after them. Earlier and later sages followed one standard; father and son shared one heart. Was this not how they laid the vast foundations of an eight-hundred-year dynasty, surpassing the two preceding dynasties in their singular flourishing?

Book of Changes
“When he goes forth, he can safeguard the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain, and serve as master of the sacrifices.”
Huang Zi 黃鼒

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
原上文立說且分守宗社主祭作兩段殊失
本旨此作見理明措辭當宜錄以為後學式
考試官教諭趙批說出長子之義可嘉
考試官教諭朱批簡明雄健宜冠本房
彖傳論儲君繼世足以承祀事之重焉盖儲君
天下本也自非震之長子曷克以繼世而承此
祀事之重也哉昔吾夫子傳震之彖至此推言
不喪匕鬯之義謂夫當震驚百里之時正驚遠
懼邇之日而震之長子恐懼為心而所執之匕
===
鬯不喪誠敬為念而所持之重器不失天命與
之人心歸之由是出而繼先世之統皇皇穆穆
于以宰制乎六合進而纘前人之緒赫赫明明
于以統御乎萬方彼宗廟之重未易守也今能
恐懼如此則可以守之而享祖宗於不已延國
祚於無疆而宗廟之神莫不依之而立矣豈不
可為宗廟之祭主乎社稷之大未易保也今能
誠敬如此則可以保之而享神明於无穷壯基
圖於不拔而社稷之神莫不由之而安矣豈不
punctuated:
原上文立說，且分守宗社、主祭作兩段，殊失本旨。此作見理明，措辭當，宜錄以為後學式。
考試官教諭趙批：說出長子之義，可嘉。
考試官教諭朱批：簡明雄健，宜冠本房。
《彖傳》論儲君繼世，足以承祀事之重焉。盖儲君，天下本也。自非震之長子，曷克以繼世而承此祀事之重也哉？昔吾夫子傳震之彖，至此推言不喪匕鬯之義，謂夫當震驚百里之時，正驚遠懼邇之日，而震之長子恐懼為心，而所執之匕鬯不喪；誠敬為念，而所持之重器不失。天命與之，人心歸之。由是出而繼先世之統，皇皇穆穆，于以宰制乎六合；進而纘前人之緒，赫赫明明，于以統御乎萬方。彼宗廟之重，未易守也。今能恐懼如此，則可以守之，而享祖宗於不已，延國祚於無疆，而宗廟之神莫不依之而立矣。豈不可為宗廟之祭主乎？社稷之大，未易保也。今能誠敬如此，則可以保之，而享神明於无穷，壯基圖於不拔，而社稷之神莫不由之而安矣。豈不
translation_en:
…[fail to] ground their arguments in the preceding text, and moreover treat safeguarding the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain and presiding over sacrifices as two separate sections, thereby seriously missing the original meaning. This composition understands the principle clearly and expresses it aptly. It should be recorded as a model for later students.
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “It brings out the significance of the eldest son: commendable.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Concise, clear, vigorous, and forceful. It should rank first in this grading room.”
The Commentary on the Judgments discusses how the heir apparent, in succeeding to the throne, is fully capable of bearing the weighty responsibility of sacrificial service. The heir apparent is indeed the foundation of all under Heaven. Unless he were the eldest son represented by Zhen, how could he succeed to the throne and bear this weighty responsibility? In former times, when our Master explained the judgment of Zhen, the hexagram of Thunder, he elaborated at this point on the meaning of “not losing the sacrificial ladle and aromatic wine.” He meant that when thunder startles those a hundred li away—precisely when it alarms those far off and frightens those nearby—the eldest son represented by Zhen keeps fear and apprehension in his heart and does not lose the sacrificial ladle and aromatic wine he holds. He keeps sincerity and reverence in his thoughts and does not let slip the precious vessels entrusted to him. Heaven’s Mandate is bestowed upon him, and the people’s hearts turn to him. Thus he comes forth to succeed to the dynastic succession of his forebears: august and reverent, he governs all within the six directions. He advances to carry on his predecessors’ enterprise: illustrious and enlightened, he rules the myriad regions.
The weighty charge of the ancestral temple is not easily safeguarded. Yet if he can be fearful and apprehensive in this way, he can safeguard it, make offerings to his ancestors without cease, and prolong the dynasty’s allotted span without limit. The spirits of the ancestral temple will all depend upon him for their continued establishment. Could he not then preside over the ancestral temple’s sacrifices? The great charge of the altars of soil and grain is not easily preserved. Yet if he can be sincere and reverent in this way, he can preserve them, make offerings to the spirits forever, and strengthen the foundations of his rule so that they cannot be uprooted. The spirits of the altars of soil and grain will all thereby rest secure. Could he not…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
可爲社稷之祭主乎吁極敬懼之心承祀事之
重震之長子其優於負荷也歟大抵莫爲之前
雖美弗彰莫爲之後雖盛弗傳君子創業垂統
固有光於家國矣不有儲君出而繼之則宗社
孰爲之守而祀事孰爲之主乎然則震之長子
其殆光前而裕後者歟
顯諸仁藏諸用
許紀
同考試官訓導余批本義顯藏二字作表
===
裏說場中多襲陳言體認不切令人厭觀是
篇發明顯仁藏用深得本旨宜錄
考試官教諭趙批辭達而已此篇庶乎
考試官教諭朱批發明顯藏二字得旨
著於外者造化之功斂於內者機緘之妙一道
之所寓也夫仁乃造化之功用乃機緘之妙也
然而所以顯之藏之何莫非斯道之所寓哉大
傳聖人論一陰一陽之道至此謂夫天地之間
莫非陰陽陰陽之道无非動靜是故自道之動
punctuated:
可爲社稷之祭主乎？吁！極敬懼之心，承祀事之重，震之長子，其優於負荷也歟！大抵莫爲之前，雖美弗彰；莫爲之後，雖盛弗傳。君子創業垂統，固有光於家國矣。不有儲君出而繼之，則宗社孰爲之守，而祀事孰爲之主乎？然則震之長子，其殆光前而裕後者歟！
