title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而行乎陽者言之則爲顯諸仁焉蓋必自内而
外自裏而表續生意於幾息之餘著貞性於幾
泯之後勾者萌甲者拆煥乎品物之咸章卵者
形胎者息蔚乎庶類之咸美凡其流動充滿而
不可掩者何莫非此造化之功乎此顯諸仁所
以爲用之迹德之發也自道之靜而具於陰者
言之則爲藏諸用焉蓋必自外而内由表而裏
歸已續之生意於中固既著之貞性於内脆者
堅華者實充然性命之各正大成大小成小翕
===
然大和之保合凡其凝靜收斂而不可見者何
莫非此機緘之妙乎此藏諸用所以爲仁之心
業之本也吁一顯一藏而顯微無間曰仁曰用
而體用一源斯道運行於天地間曷嘗一息之
或停哉大抵此章論道之體用皆不外乎陰陽
也上文曰繼之者善成之者性蓋以賦受言此
曰顯諸仁藏諸用鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂蓋
以表裏言皆兼人物而通論之也若以流行不
息言之則繼而成成而復繼顯而藏藏而復顯
punctuated: 而行乎陽者言之，則爲顯諸仁焉。蓋必自内而外，自裏而表，續生意於幾息之餘，著貞性於幾泯之後。勾者萌，甲者拆，煥乎品物之咸章；卵者形，胎者息，蔚乎庶類之咸美。凡其流動充滿而不可掩者，何莫非此造化之功乎？此顯諸仁所以爲用之迹、德之發也。自道之靜而具於陰者言之，則爲藏諸用焉。蓋必自外而内，由表而裏，歸已續之生意於中，固既著之貞性於内。脆者堅，華者實，充然性命之各正；大成大，小成小，翕然大和之保合。凡其凝靜收斂而不可見者，何莫非此機緘之妙乎？此藏諸用所以爲仁之心、業之本也。吁！一顯一藏，而顯微無間；曰仁曰用，而體用一源。斯道運行於天地間，曷嘗一息之或停哉？大抵此章論道之體用，皆不外乎陰陽也。上文曰：「繼之者善，成之者性。」蓋以賦受言。此曰：「顯諸仁，藏諸用，鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂。」蓋以表裏言。皆兼人物而通論之也。若以流行不息言之，則繼而成，成而復繼，顯而藏，藏而復顯。
translation_en:
…and operates through yang, it is said to be “manifested in benevolence.” For it must proceed from within to without, from the interior to the exterior, renewing the impulse of life after it has nearly ceased and revealing the enduring nature after it has nearly disappeared. Curled shoots sprout and seed casings split: how brilliantly the myriad things all display themselves! Creatures born from eggs take form, and those born from wombs grow: how luxuriantly the many kinds all attain their beauty! Of all that flows forth and fills the world, incapable of being concealed, what is not the achievement of this creative transformation? This is why “manifested in benevolence” constitutes the trace of functioning and the unfolding of virtue.

Speaking of the Way in its stillness, fully present in yin, it is said to be “concealed in functioning.” For it must proceed from without to within, from the exterior to the interior, returning the renewed impulse of life to the center and securing within the enduring nature already manifested. The tender becomes firm, and blossoms become fruit: each fully attains its proper nature and allotted existence. The great is perfected as great, the small as small: in their gathering together, supreme harmony is preserved and united. Of all that becomes still and draws inward, remaining invisible, what is not the subtle working of this hidden mechanism? This is why “concealed in functioning” constitutes the heart of benevolence and the foundation of achievement.

Ah! Now manifest, now concealed, yet there is no gap between the evident and the subtle. We speak of benevolence and of functioning, yet substance and function have a single source. As this Way moves through Heaven and Earth, when has it ever stopped for even a single breath? In general, this chapter’s discussion of the substance and function of the Way never goes beyond yin and yang. The preceding passage says: “What continues it is goodness; what brings it to completion is nature.” This speaks in terms of endowment and reception. Here it says: “Manifested in benevolence and concealed in functioning, it quickens the myriad things without sharing the sage’s anxieties.” This speaks in terms of exterior and interior. Both passages discuss human beings and other things together in a comprehensive account. If we speak in terms of its ceaseless flow, then continuation leads to completion, completion again to continuation, manifestation to concealment, and concealment again to manifestation…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
循環无端一生生而无窮矣故下文又曰生生
之謂易聖人之言各有攸當讀易者此又不可
不知
書
三百里揆文教二百里奮武衛
龍竒
同考試官教諭林批作此題者多不以禹
制服為重獨此得之且一結尤佳宜錄以冠
本房
===
考試官教諭趙批文簡意足錄之
考試官教諭朱批詞能達意可取
內治用乎文外治用乎武此聖人定綏服之制
也盖地有內外而治有文武勢固然也禹定綏
服而分為二等者如此其嚴華夏之辨何如哉
且夫水土既平法制斯定侯服之外有綏服焉
內取王城千里外取荒服千里以五百里之地
介乎內外之間聖人制治方畧能無異耶是故
內三百里密邇侯甸而安中國之治在所重也
punctuated:

書
三百里揆文教，二百里奮武衛。

同考試官教諭林批：作此題者，多不以禹制服為重，獨此得之。且一結尤佳，宜錄以冠本房。
考試官教諭趙批：文簡意足，錄之。
考試官教諭朱批：詞能達意，可取。
內治用乎文，外治用乎武，此聖人定綏服之制也。盖地有內外，而治有文武，勢固然也。禹定綏服而分為二等者如此，其嚴華夏之辨何如哉！且夫水土既平，法制斯定。侯服之外，有綏服焉。內取王城千里，外取荒服千里，以五百里之地介乎內外之間，聖人制治方畧能無異耶？是故內三百里，密邇侯甸，而安中國之治在所重也。
translation_en:
…cycling without beginning or end, in a single inexhaustible process of generation and regeneration. Thus the text below also says: “Generation upon generation is called change.” Each statement of the sage has its appropriate application; this too is something readers of the Book of Changes must understand.
Book of Documents
“For three hundred li, oversee civil instruction; for two hundred li, strengthen military defenses.”
Long Qi
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Most who wrote on this topic failed to give due weight to Yu’s establishment of the territorial zones. This essay alone grasps it. Moreover, its conclusion is particularly fine. It should be selected and ranked first in this examining section.
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: The writing is concise and the meaning fully expressed. Select it.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The wording conveys the meaning effectively. Worth selecting.
Civil means are employed in governing the inner territory, and military means in governing the outer territory: this was the sage’s arrangement in establishing the Pacification Zone. Territory has its inner and outer divisions, and government has its civil and military means; circumstances naturally require this. Yu established the Pacification Zone and divided it into two sections in this way. How strictly he maintained the distinction concerning the Hua-Xia realm [?]!
Once the waters and lands had been put in order, laws and institutions were established. Beyond the Feudatory Zone lay the Pacification Zone. Inward lay the thousand li of the royal capital’s territory, and outward the thousand li of the Wild Zone [?]; a tract five hundred li wide stood between the inner and outer territories. Could the sage’s methods of establishing government have been identical throughout? Thus, the inner three hundred li closely adjoined the Feudatory and Royal Domain Zones, and priority there lay in securing orderly government in the central lands.…

How strictly he maintained the distinction separating the Chinese realm from what lay beyond!

Once the waters and lands had been brought into order, laws and institutions were established. Beyond the Lords’ Domain lay the Pacification Domain. With a thousand li inward toward the royal capital and a thousand li outward toward the Wild Domain, its five hundred li of territory stood between the inner and outer regions. Could the sage’s methods of government fail to differ between them? Thus the inner three hundred li closely adjoined the Lords’ and Royal Domains, and the government needed to secure peace in the central lands was the chief concern…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
禹於是而有揆文教之制焉揆之何如殆必學
校立焉人倫明焉而施為有其序五典敷焉民
則和焉而詳畧有其宜勞來匡直之政恒修禮
義仁讓之化有漸則所以治乎内者於是矣外
二百里聯屬要荒而安邊疆之治在所急也禹
於是而有奮武衛之制焉奮之何如殆必修車
馬也備器械也而嚴禦戎之具比什伍也時簡
教也而精練兵之方王靈布昭於遐服武備保
障乎群黎則所以治乎外者於是矣吁文武之
===
治既異華夏之辨自嚴聖人經理之周密有如
是哉雖然文武並用國家長久之道也史臣叙
禹定服似乃岐而二之何歟盖聖人之治各有
所主内治非無武也而以文為主外治非無文
也而以武為主初非各一其用而有所遺也其
視後世彼此偏廢卒以貽窮兵黷武之譏致夷
狄侵陵之患者詎可同日語哉此其制治之微
意讀者自當於書法之外求焉
天明畏弼我丕丕基
punctuated:
禹於是而有揆文教之制焉。揆之何如？殆必學校立焉，人倫明焉，而施為有其序；五典敷焉，民則和焉，而詳畧有其宜。勞來匡直之政恒修，禮義仁讓之化有漸，則所以治乎内者於是矣。外二百里，聯屬要荒，而安邊疆之治在所急也。禹於是而有奮武衛之制焉。奮之何如？殆必修車馬也，備器械也，而嚴禦戎之具；比什伍也，時簡教也，而精練兵之方。王靈布昭於遐服，武備保障乎群黎，則所以治乎外者於是矣。吁！文武之治既異，華夏之辨自嚴，聖人經理之周密有如是哉！雖然，文武並用，國家長久之道也。史臣叙禹定服，似乃岐而二之，何歟？盖聖人之治，各有所主。内治非無武也，而以文為主；外治非無文也，而以武為主。初非各一其用而有所遺也。其視後世彼此偏廢，卒以貽窮兵黷武之譏、致夷狄侵陵之患者，詎可同日語哉！此其制治之微意，讀者自當於書法之外求焉。

天明畏，弼我丕丕基。
translation_en:
…Yu therefore established a system for ordering civil instruction here. How was it ordered? Surely schools were established and human relationships clarified, so that measures were carried out in their proper sequence; the teachings concerning the five relationships were disseminated and the people brought into harmony, with due judgment as to what required detail and what could be treated briefly. Policies of encouraging and attracting the people, correcting and setting them upright, were constantly maintained, while the transforming influence of ritual propriety, righteousness, benevolence, and deference gradually took effect. Such were the means of governing the inner area.

The outer two hundred li adjoined the Yao and Huang domains, where the urgent task of government was to secure the frontiers. Yu therefore established a system for strengthening military defense here. How was it strengthened? Surely chariots and horses were put in order and weapons and equipment made ready, ensuring rigorous preparations for resisting hostile incursions; men were organized into groups of ten and five, and inspected and instructed at the proper times, perfecting the methods of training troops. The king’s awe-inspiring power shone throughout the distant domains, and military preparedness safeguarded the common people. Such were the means of governing the outer area.

Ah! Once civil and military governance were differentiated, the distinction between Hua and Xia [?] was naturally strict. How thorough and meticulous was the sage’s ordering of affairs! Nevertheless, employing civil and military means together is the way to secure the state’s enduring existence. In recounting Yu’s establishment of the domains, the court historian seems to divide these means into two separate courses. Why is this? In the sage’s governance, each area had its principal emphasis. Government of the inner area did not lack military measures, but gave primacy to civil means; government of the outer area did not lack civil measures, but gave primacy to military means. It was never a matter of employing only one in each area and leaving something neglected. How could this be spoken of in the same breath as later ages, when partiality toward one meant neglect of the other, ultimately inviting criticism for exhausting military resources and recklessly resorting to war, or bringing about the calamity of incursions and encroachments by the Yi and Di? Such was the subtle intent behind his system of governance. Readers should seek it beyond the manner in which the account was written.

Heaven’s manifest majesty aids our exceedingly great foundation.

Yu accordingly instituted measures for ordering civil instruction. How was this ordering carried out? Surely schools had to be established and human relationships clarified, so that action proceeded in its proper sequence; the teachings concerning the five relationships had to be disseminated and the people brought into harmony, with due consideration for what required detail and what could be treated briefly. title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
徐淮
同考試官教諭林批天明畏主今日卜吉
而言作者往往將預告之卜混講此篇體認
真切詞理俱優故錄之
考試官教諭趙批詞贍理明可嘉
考試官教諭朱批說出成王諭臣之意
宛然
賢王原天命之可畏實天眷之所存以見卜之
不可違也夫卜伐有殷而吉是明命可畏而天
===
眷周之意有在也成王原此以示邦君御事則
卜之不可違者可見矣且王之意若曰國有大
事當稽于天天有明命一寓於卜則卜之所在
天命之所在也彼夫往伐武庚蓋嘗求之卜矣
而朕卜有并吉之祥是上帝討罪之意昭告於
鑽灼之間凛乎其無赦可畏孰加焉徂征四國
我嘗决之龜矣而三龜有并吉之兆是上天禍
淫之命顯示於墨食之頃赫然其不僭可畏孰
甚焉然天之意果安在哉誠以今日之歷數即
punctuated:
徐淮

同考試官教諭林批：「天明畏，主今日卜吉而言。作者往往將預告之卜混講。此篇體認真切，詞理俱優，故錄之。」

考試官教諭趙批：「詞贍理明，可嘉。」

考試官教諭朱批：「說出成王諭臣之意，宛然。」

賢王原天命之可畏，實天眷之所存，以見卜之不可違也。夫卜伐有殷而吉，是明命可畏，而天眷周之意有在也。成王原此以示邦君御事，則卜之不可違者可見矣。且王之意若曰：「國有大事，當稽于天。天有明命，一寓於卜，則卜之所在，天命之所在也。彼夫往伐武庚，蓋嘗求之卜矣，而朕卜有并吉之祥，是上帝討罪之意，昭告於鑽灼之間，凛乎其無赦，可畏孰加焉？徂征四國，我嘗决之龜矣，而三龜有并吉之兆，是上天禍淫之命，顯示於墨食之頃，赫然其不僭，可畏孰甚焉？然天之意果安在哉？誠以今日之歷數即
translation_en:
Xu Huai

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “‘Heaven’s manifest awesomeness’ refers chiefly to the auspicious divination on the present occasion. Writers often confuse this with the earlier divination that foretold events. This essay grasps the meaning accurately and deeply, and excels in both expression and reasoning; hence its inclusion.”

Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “Ample expression and clear reasoning: commendable.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “It vividly conveys King Cheng’s intention in admonishing his ministers.”

The worthy king examined why Heaven’s mandate was to be feared and established wherein Heaven’s favor lay, thereby showing that the divination could not be defied. The divination concerning an attack upon Yin was auspicious: this meant that Heaven’s manifest mandate was awe-inspiring, and that Heaven had a purpose in favoring Zhou. King Cheng examined this and made it known to the lords of the states and the officials conducting affairs; thus it became evident that the divination could not be defied. The king’s meaning was, in effect:

“When the state faces a great undertaking, it must consult Heaven. Heaven has a manifest mandate, embodied entirely in divination; wherever the divination points, there lies Heaven’s mandate. As for setting out to attack Wu Geng, we have already sought guidance through divination, and my divinations have yielded uniformly auspicious signs. Thus the Supreme Lord’s intention to punish the guilty has been clearly proclaimed through the drilling and scorching of the tortoise shells. Sternly allowing no pardon, what could inspire greater fear? Before marching against the four states, I sought a decision through the tortoise shells, and all three shells yielded auspicious omens. Thus Heaven’s command to bring calamity upon the wicked was revealed as the cracks formed along the ink markings. Majestic and unerring, what could inspire greater awe? Yet wherein, indeed, lies Heaven’s intention? Truly, it is because the divinely allotted succession of the present day is precisely …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
武王之歷數基莫有大焉者也苟武庚不靖王
基不幾於危乎茲盖使我肅將天威戡彼禍亂
于以奠安宗社而綿歷數於無疆也非弼成我
之丕基而何今日之五服卽武王之五服業莫
有大焉者也苟四國靡寧王業不幾於衰乎茲
盖使我奉行天討推彼敗亡于以指定疆土而
嗣五服於無窮也非輔成我之大業而何夫天
之眷周驗諸卜而可見我之伐殷質諸天而無
疑爾邦君御事何乃欲違卜而勿征乎抑考武
===
王集大統而有天下凡以順天而應人也不期
而會者八百國人心從周可知矣夫何一傳而
至成王蠢爾四國乃敢動摇其間豈不以三監
有隙實有以啟之耶是以成王上原天命下憫
人窮而反覆終始乎卜之一言盖所以斷天下
之疑定天下之業而求匹休於前人也卒致罪
人黜服而為繼世之令主也宜哉
詩
赳赳武夫公侯腹心
punctuated:
武王之歷數，基莫有大焉者也。苟武庚不靖，王基不幾於危乎？茲盖使我肅將天威，戡彼禍亂，于以奠安宗社，而綿歷數於無疆也，非弼成我之丕基而何？今日之五服，卽武王之五服，業莫有大焉者也。苟四國靡寧，王業不幾於衰乎？茲盖使我奉行天討，推彼敗亡，于以指定疆土，而嗣五服於無窮也，非輔成我之大業而何？夫天之眷周，驗諸卜而可見；我之伐殷，質諸天而無疑。爾邦君御事，何乃欲違卜而勿征乎？抑考武王集大統而有天下，凡以順天而應人也。不期而會者八百國，人心從周可知矣。夫何一傳而至成王，蠢爾四國乃敢動摇其間？豈不以三監有隙，實有以啟之耶？是以成王上原天命，下憫人窮，而反覆終始乎卜之一言，盖所以斷天下之疑，定天下之業，而求匹休於前人也。卒致罪人黜服，而為繼世之令主也，宜哉！

詩
赳赳武夫，公侯腹心。
translation_en:
…the succession ordained for King Wu: no foundation could be greater. If Wu Geng were not subdued, would not the royal foundation approach peril? Heaven thus bids me reverently wield its might and quell those disastrous disorders, thereby securing the ancestral temples and altars of state and perpetuating the ordained succession without limit. What is this if not helping establish my great foundation? The five domains of service today are precisely those of King Wu: no undertaking could be greater. If the four states were not pacified, would not the royal enterprise approach decline? Heaven thus bids me carry out its punishment and bring about their defeat and destruction, thereby settling the boundaries of the realm and perpetuating the five domains of service without end. What is this if not helping complete my great undertaking? Heaven’s favor toward Zhou can be seen by examining the divinations; my campaign against Yin admits of no doubt when tested against Heaven. Why, then, do you lords of states and officials wish to defy the divinations and refrain from campaigning?

Now consider how King Wu united the great succession and possessed All-under-Heaven: it was entirely through obeying Heaven and responding to the people. Eight hundred states assembled without prior arrangement; from this we can know that the people’s hearts followed Zhou. How, then, after just one succession, when the throne passed to King Cheng, did those rebellious four states dare to stir up turmoil? Was it not because discord involving the Three Supervisors gave them an opening? Thus King Cheng sought above to fathom Heaven’s mandate and, below, pitied the people’s distress. From beginning to end, he returned repeatedly to the single matter of divination, thereby resolving the doubts of All-under-Heaven, securing its great enterprise, and seeking to equal the glory of his predecessor. That he ultimately brought the guilty to submission through punishment and became an excellent ruler who continued the dynasty was fitting indeed!

Book of Odes
“Valiant are the warriors, the trusted confidants of dukes and lords.”

有隙實有以啟之耶是以成王上原天命下憫
人窮而反覆終始乎卜之一言盖所以斷天下
之疑定天下之業而求匹休於前人也卒致罪
人黜服而為繼世之令主也宜哉
詩
赳赳武夫公侯腹心
punctuated:
武王之歷數，基莫有大焉者也。苟武庚不靖，王基不幾於危乎？兹盖使我肅將天威，戡彼禍亂，于以奠安宗社，而綿歷數於無疆也，非弼成我之丕基而何？今日之五服，即武王之五服，業莫有大焉者也。苟四國靡寧，王業不幾於衰乎？兹盖使我奉行天討，推彼敗亡，于以指定疆土，而嗣五服於無窮也，非輔成我之大業而何？夫天之眷周，驗諸卜而可見；我之伐殷，質諸天而無疑。爾邦君御事，何乃欲違卜而勿征乎？抑考武王集大統而有天下，允以順天而應人也。不期而會者八百國，人心從周可知矣。夫何一傳而至成王，蠢爾四國乃敢動摇其間，豈不以三監有隙，實有以啟之耶？是以成王上原天命，下憫人窮，而反覆終始乎卜之一言，盖所以斷天下之疑，定天下之業，而求匹休於前人也。卒致罪人黜服，而為繼世之令主也，宜哉！

詩
赳赳武夫，公侯腹心。
translation_en:
…King Wu’s Heaven-allotted succession—no foundation could be greater. If Wu Geng were not pacified, would the royal foundation not approach peril? This surely bids me reverently wield Heaven’s might and quell that disastrous unrest, thereby securing the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain and extending the allotted succession without limit. What is this but helping me complete my great foundation? Today’s five zones of submission are precisely King Wu’s five zones: no undertaking could be greater. If the four states were not at peace, would the royal enterprise not approach decline? This surely bids me carry out Heaven’s punishment and bring them to ruin, thereby fixing the boundaries of the realm and perpetuating rule over the five zones without end. What is this but assisting me in completing my great enterprise? Heaven’s favor toward Zhou can be seen by examining the divination; my campaign against Yin, tested against Heaven’s will, admits of no doubt. You lords of states and officers, why would you defy the divination and refrain from campaigning?

Consider, moreover, how King Wu united the supreme succession and possessed all under Heaven: truly, he followed Heaven and responded to the people. Eight hundred states assembled without prior arrangement; from this we can see that the people’s hearts followed Zhou. Why, then, after only one succession, when the throne passed to King Cheng, did those rebellious four states dare to stir up disorder within the realm? Was it not because the Three Supervisors had a breach in their relations, which indeed gave an opening for this? Thus King Cheng looked upward to seek the source of Heaven’s mandate and downward in compassion for the people’s distress. From beginning to end, he returned repeatedly to the single word ‘divination.’ This was how he resolved the doubts of all under Heaven, secured the royal enterprise, and sought to equal his predecessor’s glory. That he finally brought the guilty to punishment and submission, becoming an excellent ruler who inherited the throne, was fitting indeed!

The Book of Odes
‘The valiant warriors are the trusted confidants of dukes and lords.’

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
宋澍
同考試官教諭謝批題本冠冕塲中臆說
紛紛多以赳赳作才甚戾本㫖此篇不惑衆
見察理詳明蓋嘗用心於詩者高薦何忝
同考試官學正陳批作此題者不泛則畧
求其認理精切措詞溫厚無踰此篇健羨健羨
考試官教諭趙批詞理豐贍
考試官教諭朱批以才立說得㫖
詩人美武勇之賤者而同體於貴者此其才之
===
可用也夫以武勇野人而與公侯同心德則人
才之盛可見矣非蒙聖化其能然乎昔文王化
行俗美賢才衆多雖罝兎之野人而其才之可
用猶如此故詩人因其所事而美之及此意謂
當岐周興王之始適賢才輩出之時彼其肅肅
以罝兎者一田野之民耳設罝之間但見其如
熊如羆而有以振果敢之氣其武何赳赳也罝
兎於中林者一獵者之儔耳施罝之頃惟見其
如虎如貔而有以奮强壯之威其勇何赳赳也
punctuated:
宋澍

同考試官教諭謝批：題本冠冕，塲中臆說紛紛，多以赳赳作才，甚戾本㫖。此篇不惑衆見，察理詳明，蓋嘗用心於詩者，高薦何忝！

同考試官學正陳批：作此題者，不泛則畧。求其認理精切、措詞溫厚，無踰此篇。健羨，健羨！

考試官教諭趙批：詞理豐贍。

考試官教諭朱批：以才立說，得㫖。

詩人美武勇之賤者而同體於貴者，此其才之可用也。夫以武勇野人而與公侯同心德，則人才之盛可見矣。非蒙聖化，其能然乎？昔文王化行俗美，賢才衆多，雖罝兎之野人，而其才之可用猶如此，故詩人因其所事而美之及此。意謂當岐周興王之始，適賢才輩出之時，彼其肅肅以罝兎者，一田野之民耳。設罝之間，但見其如熊如羆，而有以振果敢之氣，其武何赳赳也！罝兎於中林者，一獵者之儔耳。施罝之頃，惟見其如虎如貔，而有以奮强壯之威，其勇何赳赳也！
translation_en:
Song Shu 宋澍

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: The topic itself is of the highest distinction. Yet conjectural interpretations abound in the examination hall, most treating “martial and valiant” as referring to talent, greatly at odds with the original meaning. This essay is not misled by prevailing views; its examination of principle is thorough and clear. Its author has evidently devoted attention to the Book of Odes. How could recommending him highly be undeserved?

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Those who write on this topic are either vague or cursory. For a precise and incisive grasp of principle and language that is gentle and generous, none surpasses this essay. Most admirable, most admirable!

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: Rich and ample in both expression and reasoning.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: By grounding its argument in talent, it captures the meaning.

The poet praises a man of low station for his martial courage and for being as one body with those of high rank: this shows that his talent can be put to use. When a rustic of martial courage shares the purposes and virtue of dukes and lords, the abundance of talented men becomes apparent. Could this have happened without his receiving the transforming influence of a sage?

In former times, King Wen’s transforming influence spread, customs were fine, and worthy and talented men were numerous. Even a rustic who set nets for rabbits possessed talent as serviceable as this. Thus the poet, taking the man’s occupation as his starting point, carried his praise to such lengths. His meaning is that, at the beginning of Zhou’s rise to kingship in Qi, it was precisely a time when worthy and talented men emerged in succession. That man busily setting rabbit nets was merely one of the people of the fields. Yet as he set his nets, one could see him resembling a bear or a brown bear, displaying a spirit of resolve and daring. How martial and valiant his prowess was! That man netting rabbits in the forest was merely one among the hunters. Yet as he spread his nets, one could see him resembling a tiger or a leopard, displaying the formidable might of his strength. How martial and valiant his courage was!

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: “The topic itself is dignified and distinguished. title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
是武夫也沐聖德於綱紀之中沾神化於振作
之下其可用之才不與公侯同心德乎是故人
雖微也才則公侯之貴如輔相朝廷之政公侯
為國武夫亦為國其心與之同焉心之同者才
之同也豈特好仇而已哉事雖小也才則公侯
之大如參贊國家之務公侯為民武夫亦為民
其德與之同焉德之同者才之同也豈特善匹
而已哉吁野人有可用之才如此而文王德化
之盛因可見矣大抵天下之事有所為者必有
===
所益故勤於菑田者則以自養樂於植材者則
以自庇况善於作人者豈不得人以為用哉詩
人稱文王之作人則曰勉勉我王綱紀四方稱
文王之得人則曰濟濟多士文王以寧如此詩
之武夫則亦在其綱紀之中者矣易曰雲從龍
風從虎聖人作而萬物覩其文王之謂歟
赫赫明明王命卿士南仲大祖大師皇父
整我六師以脩我戎既敬既戒惠此南國
王謂尹氏命程伯休父左右陳行戒我師
punctuated:
是武夫也，沐聖德於綱紀之中，沾神化於振作之下，其可用之才不與公侯同心德乎？是故人雖微也，才則公侯之貴，如輔相朝廷之政，公侯為國，武夫亦為國，其心與之同焉。心之同者，才之同也，豈特好仇而已哉？事雖小也，才則公侯之大，如參贊國家之務，公侯為民，武夫亦為民，其德與之同焉。德之同者，才之同也，豈特善匹而已哉？吁！野人有可用之才如此，而文王德化之盛因可見矣。大抵天下之事，有所為者必有所益，故勤於菑田者則以自養，樂於植材者則以自庇，况善於作人者，豈不得人以為用哉？詩人稱文王之作人，則曰：「勉勉我王，綱紀四方。」稱文王之得人，則曰：「濟濟多士，文王以寧。」如此詩之武夫，則亦在其綱紀之中者矣。《易》曰：「雲從龍，風從虎，聖人作而萬物覩。」其文王之謂歟？

赫赫明明，王命卿士，南仲大祖，大師皇父：「整我六師，以脩我戎。既敬既戒，惠此南國。」王謂尹氏：「命程伯休父，左右陳行，戒我師
translation_en:
These warriors have been bathed in the sage’s virtue within the ordering of his rule and touched by his wondrous transforming influence through his efforts to rouse them. Do not their useful talents reflect a shared purpose and virtue with the dukes and lords? Thus, although their standing is humble, their talents possess the nobility of those of dukes and lords. In assisting with the government of the court, for example, dukes and lords serve the state, and warriors likewise serve the state: their purposes are the same. To share the same purpose is to share the same talent. How could they be merely good companions? Although their tasks are small, their talents possess the greatness of those of dukes and lords. In assisting with the affairs of the state, for example, dukes and lords act for the people, and warriors likewise act for the people: their virtue is the same. To share the same virtue is to share the same talent. How could they be merely suitable partners? Ah! That countrymen possessed useful talents such as these reveals the flourishing power of King Wen’s moral transformation. Generally, in the affairs of the world, effort necessarily brings benefit. Thus those who diligently clear and cultivate fields thereby feed themselves, and those who delight in planting timber trees thereby provide themselves with shelter. How much more must one skilled in cultivating people obtain men whose talents he can employ! Praising King Wen’s cultivation of men, the poet says: “Diligently our king orders the four quarters.” Praising King Wen’s success in obtaining men, he says: “Numerous were the worthy men; through them King Wen enjoyed peace.” Warriors such as those in this poem were likewise included within the ordering of his rule. The Book of Changes says: “Clouds follow the dragon; winds follow the tiger. The sage arises, and all beings behold him.” Does this not speak of King Wen?

Illustrious and radiant, the king commanded his high minister, Grand Preceptor Huangfu, whose great ancestor was Nanzhong: “Put our six armies in order and prepare our arms. Be reverent and vigilant, and bring beneficence to these southern states.” The king addressed the Yin clan official: “Command Chengbo Xiufu to arrange the ranks on the left and right and admonish our armies …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
旅率彼淮浦省此徐土不留不處三事就
緒
陳堯道
同考試官教諭謝批見理明白行文條暢
宜置優列
同考試官學正陳批此題宣王自將以征
不庭命皇父休父治其軍事場中作者往往
認理不真立說穿鑿惟晚得此作理明詞順
非精於葩經者不能也宜錄出
===
考試官教諭趙批作大雅義當齊莊嚴
重此作得之
考試官教諭朱批歛繁就簡可佳
王者自將以伐遠既親命世臣以治其事復傳
命大臣以副其事盖軍事至重不可忽也今王
者既親命世臣以治之而又傳命大臣以副之
慎重其事也為何如哉昔宣王自將以伐淮北
之夷詩人作此以美之謂夫吾王當徐方不庭
之時動萬乘自將之舉故玉音渙發赫赫明明
punctuated:
旅，率彼淮浦，省此徐土，不留不處，三事就緒。
陳堯道。
同考試官教諭謝批：「見理明白，行文條暢，宜置優列。」
同考試官學正陳批：「此題宣王自將以征不庭，命皇父、休父治其軍事。場中作者往往認理不真，立說穿鑿。惟晚得此作，理明詞順，非精於葩經者不能也，宜錄出。」
考試官教諭趙批：「作《大雅》義，當齊莊嚴重，此作得之。」
考試官教諭朱批：「歛繁就簡，可佳。」
王者自將以伐遠，既親命世臣以治其事，復傳命大臣以副其事，盖軍事至重，不可忽也。今王者既親命世臣以治之，而又傳命大臣以副之，慎重其事也為何如哉！昔宣王自將以伐淮北之夷，詩人作此以美之，謂夫吾王當徐方不庭之時，動萬乘自將之舉，故玉音渙發，赫赫明明。
translation_en:
…the troops; follow the banks of the Huai and inspect these lands of Xu. Neither linger nor remain: bring the three affairs into order.

Chen Yaodao.

Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: “His understanding of the principles is clear, and his writing orderly and fluent. This should be placed among the superior answers.”

Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor, comments: “This topic concerns King Xuan personally leading a campaign against those who would not attend his court, and ordering Huangfu and Xiufu to manage his military affairs. Candidates in the examination hall often failed to grasp the principles correctly and advanced strained interpretations. Only late did I obtain this answer, with its clear reasoning and fluent language. None but someone deeply versed in the Classic of Poetry could have achieved this. It should be selected for inclusion in the record.”

Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “An exposition on the Greater Odes should be reverent, dignified, solemn, and weighty. This answer achieves that.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “It trims elaboration to achieve simplicity. Admirable.”

When the king personally led his forces to campaign against distant peoples, he first personally commanded a hereditary minister to manage the undertaking, then also conveyed orders to a high minister to assist in it. For military affairs are of the utmost importance and cannot be treated lightly. Now, having personally commanded a hereditary minister to manage them, the king further conveyed orders to a high minister to assist: how great was the care and gravity with which he treated this undertaking! Formerly, King Xuan personally led a campaign against the Yi peoples north of the Huai. The poet composed this poem to praise him, saying that when the people of Xu would not attend court, our king, lord of ten thousand chariots, undertook to lead the campaign himself. Thus his august words issued forth abundantly, majestic and resplendent…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
旅率彼淮浦省此徐土不留不處三事就
緒
陳堯道
同考試官教諭謝批見理明白行文條暢
宜置優列
同考試官學正陳批此題宣王自將以征
不庭命皇父休父治其軍事場中作者往往
認理不真立說穿鑿惟晚得此作理明詞順
非精於葩經者不能也宜錄出
===
考試官教諭趙批作大雅義當辭莊嚴
重此作得之
考試官教諭朱批斂繁就簡可佳
王者自將以伐遠既親命世臣以治其事復傳
命大臣以副其事盖軍事至重不可忽也今王
者既親命世臣以治之而又傳命大臣以副之
慎重其事也為何如哉昔宣王自將以伐淮北
之夷詩人作此以美之謂夫吾王當徐方不庭
之時動萬乘自將之舉故玉音渙發赫赫明明
punctuated:
旅率彼淮浦，省此徐土，不留不處，三事就緒。
陳堯道。

同考試官學正陳批：此題宣王自將以征不庭，命皇父、休父治其軍事。場中作者往往認理不真，立說穿鑿，惟晚得此作，理明詞順，非精於葩經者不能也，宜錄出。

考試官教諭朱批：斂繁就簡，可佳。

…the army followed the banks of the Huai, inspected this land of Xu, neither lingering nor remaining; the three affairs were brought into order.

Chen Yaodao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: “The principles are understood clearly, and the writing is orderly and fluent. This should be placed among the superior papers.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor: “This topic concerns King Xuan personally leading a campaign against those who would not submit to his court, and ordering Huangfu and Xiufu to manage his military affairs. Writers in the examination hall frequently misunderstand the principles and advance strained interpretations. When a king personally leads a campaign against distant peoples, after himself commanding a hereditary minister to manage its affairs, he further transmits orders to a high minister to assist in them. title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而命卿士之謂南仲爲大祖兼大師而字皇父
者盖以文事武備而籌策素習也命之何如整
我從行之六軍而上下同心脩我敵愾之戎事
而器械精好師嚴器備而有制勝之勢所以然
者淮夷爲患南國爲之不寧當旣敬旣戒執訊
獲醜而惠此南方之國無擾攘之患焉有嚴有
翼聲罪致討而安此南土之人無侵凌之害焉
夫軍旅之事既有大師以治之可無司馬以副
之乎於是王命肅肅如絲如綸而詔尹氏策命
===
程伯休父而授以司馬之職者盖以料敵制勝
而計出萬全也命之何如使之左右陳行而無
愆於六步七步之法戒我師旅而無爽於六伐
七伐之律循彼淮浦而省徐州之土所以然者
師之久處農事爲之荒廢當式遄其歸無久留
於彼令三事得以就緒而俶載南畝也早畢其
事不久處於外令三農得以就業而有事西疇
也吁王者行師命臣分任其事如此則成自將
之功也可必矣雖然宣王之服淮夷豈特分命
punctuated: 而命卿士之謂南仲爲大祖、兼大師而字皇父者，盖以文事武備而籌策素習也。命之何如？整我從行之六軍，而上下同心；脩我敵愾之戎事，而器械精好。師嚴器備，而有制勝之勢。所以然者，淮夷爲患，南國爲之不寧。當旣敬旣戒，執訊獲醜，而惠此南方之國，無擾攘之患焉；有嚴有翼，聲罪致討，而安此南土之人，無侵凌之害焉。夫軍旅之事，既有大師以治之，可無司馬以副之乎？於是王命肅肅，如絲如綸，而詔尹氏策命程伯休父，而授以司馬之職者，盖以料敵制勝而計出萬全也。命之何如？使之左右陳行，而無愆於六步七步之法；戒我師旅，而無爽於六伐七伐之律；循彼淮浦，而省徐州之土。所以然者，師之久處，農事爲之荒廢。當式遄其歸，無久留於彼，令三事得以就緒，而俶載南畝也；早畢其事，不久處於外，令三農得以就業，而有事西疇也。吁！王者行師，命臣分任其事如此，則成自將之功也可必矣。雖然，宣王之服淮夷，豈特分命
translation_en:
…and he commanded the high minister who took Nanzhong as his great ancestor, concurrently held the office of Grand Preceptor, and bore the courtesy name Huangfu. This was because he was thoroughly practiced in planning for both civil affairs and military preparations. What did the king command him to do? To put in order the six armies accompanying him, so that superiors and subordinates would be of one mind; and to prepare the military operations against the enemy, ensuring that weapons and equipment were excellent. With disciplined troops and equipment ready, they would be positioned to secure victory. The reason was that the Huai Yi were causing trouble, disturbing the peace of the southern states. They must therefore be reverent and vigilant, seize prisoners for interrogation and capture the enemy multitude, bringing relief to these southern states and freeing them from turmoil. With stern discipline and circumspection, they must proclaim the enemy’s offenses and undertake a punitive campaign, securing peace for the people of these southern lands and freeing them from invasion and oppression.

Now that there was a Grand Preceptor to direct military affairs, could there be no Minister of War to assist him? Thus the king’s commands issued solemnly, like threads of silk becoming stout cords, and he instructed Yin to formally commission Chengbo Xiufu and appoint him Minister of War. This was because Xiufu could assess the enemy and secure victory, devising plans that left nothing to chance. What did the king command him to do? To arrange the ranks to the left and right, without departing from the rule of advancing six or seven paces; to admonish our troops, without deviating from the regulation of striking six or seven times; and to follow the banks of the Huai and inspect the territory of Xuzhou. The reason was that a prolonged military presence caused agricultural work to fall into neglect. They must therefore hasten their return, without lingering there, so that the three undertakings could be put in order and work begun in the southern fields. They must finish their business early, without remaining long abroad, so that the farmers of the three kinds of land could pursue their livelihoods and work in the western fields.

Ah! When a king leads an army and commands his ministers to divide responsibility in this way, success in his personal command can surely be assured. Nevertheless, was King Xuan’s subjugation of the Huai Yi due merely to his assigning separate commands…

也吁王者行師命臣分任其事如此則成自將
之功也可必矣雖然宣王之服淮夷豈特分命
punctuated: 而命卿士之謂？南仲爲大祖，兼大師而字皇父者，盖以文事武備而籌策素習也。命之何如？整我從行之六軍而上下同心，脩我敵愾之戎事而器械精好，師嚴器備而有制勝之勢。所以然者，淮夷爲患，南國爲之不寧。當旣敬旣戒，執訊獲醜，而惠此南方之國，無擾攘之患焉；有嚴有翼，聲罪致討，而安此南土之人，無侵凌之害焉。夫軍旅之事，既有大師以治之，可無司馬以副之乎？於是王命肅肅，如絲如綸，而詔尹氏策命程伯休父而授以司馬之職者，盖以料敵制勝而計出萬全也。命之何如？使之左右陳行，而無愆於六步七步之法；戒我師旅，而無爽於六伐七伐之律；循彼淮浦，而省徐州之土。所以然者，師之久處，農事爲之荒廢。當式遄其歸，無久留於彼，令三事得以就緒而俶載南畝也；早畢其事，不久處於外，令三農得以就業而有事西疇也。吁！王者行師，命臣分任其事如此，則成自將之功也可必矣。雖然，宣王之服淮夷，豈特分命
translation_en:
…and appointing his high ministers? The man who had Nanzhong as his great ancestor, concurrently held the office of Grand Preceptor, and bore the courtesy name Huangfu was chosen because he was thoroughly practiced in planning for both civil affairs and military preparations. What commands did the king give him? To put in order the six armies accompanying the king, so that superiors and subordinates shared one purpose; and to prepare our military forces against the enemy, ensuring that their weapons and equipment were excellent. With disciplined troops and equipment ready, they would be positioned to secure victory. The reason was that the Huai Yi were causing trouble and disturbing the southern states. He must be both vigilant and cautious, take prisoners for interrogation and capture the enemy host, thereby benefiting these southern states and freeing them from turmoil. With strict discipline and care, he must proclaim the enemy’s offenses and punish them, thereby bringing peace to the people of these southern lands and freeing them from the harm of aggression.

Now that there was a Grand Preceptor to direct military affairs, could there be no Minister of War to assist him? Thus the king’s commands were solemn, like silken threads and cords, and he ordered the Yin officer to formally invest Chengbo Xiufu with the office of Minister of War. This was because Xiufu could assess the enemy and secure victory, devising plans that ensured success. What commands did the king give him? To array the ranks to left and right, without violating the rule of advancing six or seven paces; to admonish our troops, without departing from the rule of striking six or seven times; and to follow the banks of the Huai and inspect the territory of Xuzhou. The reason was that a prolonged military presence would leave farming neglected. He must therefore hasten the army’s return and not linger there, allowing the three agricultural tasks to proceed in due order and work to begin in the southern fields. He must finish his business early and not remain long away, allowing the three classes of farmers to resume their occupations and work in the western fields.

Ah! When a king campaigns and commands his ministers to share responsibility in this way, success in personally leading the army can assuredly be expected. Nevertheless, was King Xuan’s subjugation of the Huai Yi due merely to his separately commissioning…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
二臣指授方畧之得其宜而已盖由推赤心以
置其腹中耳故卒章曰王猶允塞徐方旣來徐
方旣同天子之功不然書何以曰至誠感神矧
兹有苗後之治夷者可以鑒夫
春秋
齊侯衛侯鄭伯來戰于郎〔桓公十年〕齊人衛
人鄭人盟于惡曹〔桓公十一年〕
李鑾
同考試官訓導熊批題目平易作者浮泛
不切惟此篇一本傳意而文足以發之殆行
空天馬自不羣也錄之
考試官教諭趙批融會傳註成文可取
考試官教諭朱批有斷制
列國兵舉於逞忿春秋旣著其罪信講於固黨
春秋尤示其責此于郎書爵以來戰為罪惡曹
書盟以奪爵為貶觀春秋之書法而三國之罪
自見矣且魯桓非義得國而甞結援於諸侯齊
鄭投間濟私而因納交於我魯今何為而有郎
punctuated:
二臣指授方畧之得其宜而已，盖由推赤心以置其腹中耳。故卒章曰：「王猶允塞，徐方旣來；徐方旣同，天子之功。」不然，《書》何以曰：「至誠感神，矧兹有苗。」後之治夷者可以鑒夫！
《春秋》
齊侯、衛侯、鄭伯來戰于郎〔桓公十年〕。齊人、衛人、鄭人盟于惡曹〔桓公十一年〕。
李鑾
同考試官訓導熊批：「題目平易，作者浮泛不切。惟此篇一本傳意，而文足以發之，殆行空天馬，自不羣也。錄之。」
考試官教諭趙批：「融會傳註，成文可取。」
考試官教諭朱批：「有斷制。」
列國兵舉於逞忿，《春秋》旣著其罪；信講於固黨，《春秋》尤示其責。此于郎書爵，以來戰為罪；惡曹書盟，以奪爵為貶。觀《春秋》之書法，而三國之罪自見矣。且魯桓非義得國，而甞結援於諸侯；齊、鄭投間濟私，而因納交於我魯。今何為而有郎
translation_en:
…merely because he assigned duties to the two ministers and appropriately instructed them in strategy. Rather, it was because he laid bare his sincere heart, placing it within their very breasts. Thus the final stanza says: “The king’s plans were truly thorough; the regions of Xu have submitted. The regions of Xu are now united: this is the Son of Heaven’s achievement.” Otherwise, why would the Book of Documents say, “Utmost sincerity moves the spirits; how much more these Miao”? Those who govern the non-Chinese peoples in later ages may take this as a lesson!
Spring and Autumn Annals
“The marquises of Qi and Wei and the earl of Zheng came to do battle at Lang.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Huan〕 “Men of Qi, Wei, and Zheng made a covenant at E’cao.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Huan〕
Li Luan
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiong, Assistant Instructor: “The topic is straightforward, but writers have treated it superficially and failed to address it closely. This essay alone takes the commentary’s meaning as its sole foundation, and its prose adequately develops that meaning. Like a heavenly steed coursing through the sky, it stands apart from the common herd. Selected for inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “It integrates the commentaries and annotations into a commendable composition.”
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “It shows decisive judgment.”
When the states raised armies to vent their anger, the Spring and Autumn Annals made their guilt manifest; when they pledged good faith to consolidate their faction, the Spring and Autumn Annals made their culpability still clearer. Here, in the entry concerning Lang, it records their ranks and treats their coming to do battle as their offense; at E’cao, it records their covenant and censures them by stripping away their ranks. Examining the recording conventions of the Spring and Autumn Annals makes the guilt of the three states evident of itself. Now Duke Huan of Lu had acquired his state unrighteously and had sought support among the feudal lords. Qi and Zheng seized an opening to advance their private interests and accordingly established relations with our state of Lu. Why, then, did the affair at Lang occur…

…merely that the two ministers gave appropriate strategic directions; this was surely because he laid bare his sincere heart, placing it within their own breasts. Thus the final stanza says: “The king’s plans were truly fulfilled; the people of Xu have come to submit. The people of Xu are now united with us: this is the achievement of the Son of Heaven.” Otherwise, why would the Book of Documents say, “Utmost sincerity moves the spirits—how much more these people of Miao”? Those who govern the non-Chinese peoples in later ages may take this as a lesson!

Spring and Autumn Annals
“The Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Zheng came to fight at Lang.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Huan.〕 “Men of Qi, Wei, and Zheng made a covenant at E’cao.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Huan.〕
Li Luan

It is almost like a heavenly horse traversing〕〔the skies, naturally standing apart from the herd. Accept it.〕

When the states raised troops to vent their anger, the Spring and Autumn Annals already made their guilt manifest; when they pledged good faith to consolidate their faction, the Spring and Autumn Annals made their culpability still clearer. Thus, in the entry concerning Lang, it records their ranks, treating their coming to fight as their offense; in the entry concerning E’cao, it records their covenant, expressing censure by stripping them of their ranks. Examine the recording conventions of the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the guilt of the three states becomes evident of itself. Moreover, Duke Huan of Lu had acquired his state unrighteously and had previously sought support among the feudal lords. Qi and Zheng seized an opportunity to advance their private interests and accordingly established friendly relations with our state of Lu. Why, then, was there the campaign at Lang…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之師乎蓋鄭忽因救齊之有功怒魯以周班而
後已故要齊衛之兵特戰于郎之地聲威大奮
勢云強矣初非誅暴禁亂之舉甲冑長驅忿固
泄矣寧免悖道縱欲之譏夫兵凶戰危聖人所
慎也使其以道興師而伸討逆之義尚有可言
乃以私忿小怨親帥其師而戰于魯境尚為知
類也哉故春秋紀兵以受伐者為主此特列齊
衛鄭之爵而以來戰書者是主三國而罪之也
夫戰郎之師既克而怒魯之氣當舒又何為而
===
有惡曹之盟乎蓋三君既思啓釁於魯恐其尚
懷報復之心即惡曹而為盟植私黨以自固詔
於鬼神惟圖以仇魯也而懲忿窒慾之義罔聞
誓於牲歃惟務以樹黨也而處已息爭之道安
在夫盟以長亂聖人所惡也使其講信脩睦以
公天下為事猶有可取顧乃私相要誓謀以敵
人而愈陷於惡尚為知義也哉故微者盟會不
志於春秋此盟實齊衛鄭之君而以人書者是
微三國而貶之也吁惡曹之三人即戰郎之三
punctuated: 之師乎？蓋鄭忽因救齊之有功，怒魯以周班而後已，故要齊衛之兵，特戰于郎之地。聲威大奮，勢云強矣，初非誅暴禁亂之舉；甲冑長驅，忿固泄矣，寧免悖道縱欲之譏？夫兵凶戰危，聖人所慎也。使其以道興師，而伸討逆之義，尚有可言；乃以私忿小怨，親帥其師而戰于魯境，尚為知類也哉？故春秋紀兵，以受伐者為主。此特列齊衛鄭之爵，而以來戰書者，是主三國而罪之也。夫戰郎之師既克，而怒魯之氣當舒，又何為而有惡曹之盟乎？蓋三君既思啓釁於魯，恐其尚懷報復之心，即惡曹而為盟，植私黨以自固。詔於鬼神，惟圖以仇魯也，而懲忿窒慾之義罔聞；誓於牲歃，惟務以樹黨也，而處已息爭之道安在？夫盟以長亂，聖人所惡也。使其講信脩睦，以公天下為事，猶有可取；顧乃私相要誓，謀以敵人，而愈陷於惡，尚為知義也哉？故微者盟會，不志於春秋。此盟實齊衛鄭之君，而以人書者，是微三國而貶之也。吁！惡曹之三人，即戰郎之三
translation_en: …the military expedition to Lang? Hu of Zheng, having earned merit by rescuing Qi, resented Lu for placing him behind others according to the Zhou order of precedence [?]. He therefore enlisted the troops of Qi and Wei expressly to fight at Lang. Their martial renown rose mightily, and their power could indeed be called strong; yet this was never an undertaking to punish violence and suppress disorder. Their armored troops swept forward, and their anger was certainly vented; but could they escape criticism for violating the Way and indulging their desires? Arms are instruments of ill omen, and warfare is perilous: these are matters about which the Sage exercised caution. Had they raised troops in accordance with the Way and upheld the righteousness of punishing rebels, something might still have been said in their defense. Instead, out of private anger and petty resentment, they personally led their armies into battle within Lu’s borders. Could they still be said to understand the proper distinctions? Thus, when the Spring and Autumn Annals records warfare, it takes the state under attack as its principal subject. Here, however, it specifically lists the ranks of the rulers of Qi, Wei, and Zheng and writes that they “came to fight”: it thereby makes the three states the principal subjects and condemns them. Once the army that fought at Lang had prevailed, their anger toward Lu ought to have subsided. Why, then, was there also the covenant at E’cao? The three rulers, having intended to provoke hostilities against Lu, feared that Lu might still harbor thoughts of revenge. They therefore concluded a covenant at E’cao, establishing a private faction to secure themselves. In their declarations to the spirits, they sought only to make an enemy of Lu; nothing was heard of the principle of restraining anger and curbing desire. In their oaths, sworn with sacrificial blood, they strove only to establish a faction; where was the way of conducting oneself [?] and ending contention? Covenants that foster disorder are what the Sage abhors. Had they cultivated trust and harmony, making impartial concern for all under Heaven their purpose, there might still have been something commendable in their conduct. Instead, they privately bound one another by oaths, plotting to oppose others and sinking ever deeper into wrongdoing. Could they still be said to understand righteousness? Thus, covenant meetings involving persons of low standing are not recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals. This covenant actually involved the rulers of Qi, Wei, and Zheng, yet the text calls them merely “men”: it thereby lowers the standing of the three states and censures them. Alas! The three “men” of E’cao were precisely the three who fought at Lang…

punctuated:

He therefore enlisted the troops of Qi and Wei and fought at Lang. Their martial prestige surged and their strength could indeed be called great, yet this was never an undertaking to punish violence and suppress disorder. Their armored forces drove far forward, and their anger was certainly vented; but could they escape the charge of flouting the Way and indulging their desires? Arms are inauspicious and warfare perilous: these are matters about which the Sage exercised caution. Instead, out of private anger and petty resentment, they personally led their armies into battle within Lu’s borders. Could they still be said to understand how to distinguish like cases? title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
君也一戰一盟而均失於義一爵一人而各致
其誅春秋之意夫豈苟然哉大抵春秋孔子之
刑書也褒善貶惡錙銖不爽随事立義其變無
窮一人之身俄而進退焉豈特於此見之哉前
伐山戎書齊人後獻戎捷書齊侯則知伐戎者
即齊侯也上之會蜀書公子嬰齊下之盟蜀書
楚人則知盟蜀者即嬰齊也比事求之春秋懲
惡之義思過半矣先儒謂通於春秋然後能權
天下之事信哉
===
晋陽處父帥師伐楚以救江文公三年
歐一清

遣詞作者率多遺之惟此篇組織傳註發明

考試官教諭趙 批發明傳意殆無餘蘊
考試官教諭朱 批此篇深得本旨佳作也
伯國失恤患之道春秋紀用兵之法夫用兵貴
乎得宜也處父救江有愧於人多矣春秋得不
punctuated:
君也。一戰一盟，而均失於義；一爵一人，而各致其誅。《春秋》之意，夫豈苟然哉？大抵《春秋》，孔子之刑書也。褒善貶惡，錙銖不爽；随事立義，其變無窮。一人之身，俄而進退焉，豈特於此見之哉？前伐山戎書齊人，後獻戎捷書齊侯，則知伐戎者即齊侯也。上之會蜀書公子嬰齊，下之盟蜀書楚人，則知盟蜀者即嬰齊也。比事求之，《春秋》懲惡之義，思過半矣。先儒謂通於《春秋》，然後能權天下之事，信哉！

歐一清

translation_en:
…rulers. In the one battle and the one covenant alike, they violated righteousness; whether designated by noble title or simply as “men,” each received his due condemnation. Could the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals possibly be arbitrary? Broadly speaking, the Spring and Autumn Annals is Confucius’s book of penal judgments. In praising good and censuring evil, it errs not by the slightest measure; in establishing moral judgments according to events, its variations are inexhaustible. The same person may in quick succession be advanced or degraded in its wording: is this the only instance? Earlier, in recording the attack on the Shanrong, it writes “men of Qi”; later, in recording the presentation of spoils from the Rong, it writes “the Marquis of Qi.” Thus we know that the attacker of the Rong was the Marquis of Qi himself. In the earlier entry for the meeting at Shu, it writes “Prince Yingqi”; in the later entry for the covenant at Shu, it writes “a man of Chu.” Thus we know that the participant in the covenant at Shu was Yingqi himself. By comparing events and investigating them, one has already gone more than halfway toward understanding the principle by which the Spring and Autumn Annals chastises evil. Earlier scholars said that only after comprehending the Spring and Autumn Annals could one weigh the affairs of the world. How true!

“Yang Chufu of Jin led an army to attack Chu in order to rescue Jiang.” Third year of Duke Wen.
Ou Yiqing

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
致意於書法間哉昔者楚窺晋政挑釁圍江處
父先事而伐楚欲其引兵以自救其謀未為失
也胡為不足於春秋而書以耶盖嘗考諸經矣
楚始伐鄭齊桓合召陵之師而鄭患自弭又嘗
圍宋晋文角城濮之戰而宋禍以紓今江國小
而弱楚人圍之必不待舉國甲兵之眾以勢易
為力也楚當是時負覆載不容之罪以義所當
討也使晋襄果能謀如桓文命齊秦諸兵以剪
其羽翼率曲沃大眾直擣其腹心伸我王法問
===
彼悖逆楚必震恐而江圍自解矣豈不得用兵
之法哉何乃君怠臣昏計不出此獨遣處父之
孤軍遠攻陸梁之強國友邦未見其從征元惡
不聞其致討意者晋人於此豈誠心於伐楚哉
特恐失諸侯之好而姑以塞其責耳是以門于
方城而建旗未斾一遇息公而卷甲遂還一矢
莫加於楚秋毫無補於江既不如召陵之盟有
以服其心又不如城濮之戰有以讋其氣楚益
猖獗江竟滅亡晋實為之也善用兵者果如是
punctuated: 致意於書法間哉？昔者楚窺晋政，挑釁圍江，處父先事而伐楚，欲其引兵以自救，其謀未為失也。胡為不足於春秋而書以耶？盖嘗考諸經矣。楚始伐鄭，齊桓合召陵之師，而鄭患自弭；又嘗圍宋，晋文角城濮之戰，而宋禍以紓。今江國小而弱，楚人圍之，必不待舉國甲兵之眾，以勢易為力也。楚當是時，負覆載不容之罪，以義所當討也。使晋襄果能謀如桓、文，命齊、秦諸兵以剪其羽翼，率曲沃大眾直擣其腹心，伸我王法，問彼悖逆，楚必震恐，而江圍自解矣。豈不得用兵之法哉？何乃君怠臣昏，計不出此，獨遣處父之孤軍，遠攻陸梁之強國？友邦未見其從征，元惡不聞其致討。意者晋人於此，豈誠心於伐楚哉？特恐失諸侯之好，而姑以塞其責耳。是以門于方城，而建旗未斾；一遇息公，而卷甲遂還。一矢莫加於楚，秋毫無補於江。既不如召陵之盟，有以服其心；又不如城濮之戰，有以讋其氣。楚益猖獗，江竟滅亡，晋實為之也。善用兵者，果如是
translation_en:
…give particular attention to its wording? Formerly, Chu watched for an opening in Jin’s government, provoked hostilities, and besieged Jiang. Chufu took the initiative and attacked Chu, intending to make it withdraw its troops to defend itself. His plan was not in itself mistaken. Why, then, did the Spring and Autumn Annals find him wanting and record the action using the word yi (以, “with”)? I have examined this in the Classic. When Chu first attacked Zheng, Duke Huan of Qi assembled the army at Shaoling, and Zheng’s troubles subsided of themselves. When Chu later besieged Song, Duke Wen of Jin fought the battle of Chengpu, and Song’s calamity was relieved.

Now Jiang was a small and weak state. To besiege it, the men of Chu surely did not need to mobilize their entire country’s armed forces: the balance of power made the undertaking easy. At that time, Chu bore guilt that Heaven and Earth could not tolerate, and righteousness demanded that it be punished. Had Duke Xiang of Jin truly been able to plan as Dukes Huan and Wen had done, he would have ordered the forces of Qi, Qin, and the other states to clip Chu’s wings, led the great host of Quwo straight into its heartland, upheld our royal law, and called Chu to account for its defiance. Chu would surely have trembled in fear, and the siege of Jiang would have lifted of itself. Would this not have accorded with the proper methods of warfare?

Why, instead, were the ruler negligent and his minister benighted, unable to devise such a plan, sending only Chufu’s isolated army to attack a powerful and unruly state far away? No friendly states were seen joining the expedition, and nothing was heard of punishment being brought upon the chief offender. One wonders: were the men of Jin really sincere in attacking Chu? They merely feared losing the goodwill of the other lords and acted simply to discharge their responsibility. Thus they approached the gates of Fangcheng, but their raised banners had scarcely unfurled; as soon as they encountered the Lord of Xi, they packed up their armor and returned. Not one arrow struck Chu; not the slightest help reached Jiang. They neither secured its submission, as at the covenant of Shaoling, nor cowed its spirit, as at the battle of Chengpu. Chu grew ever more unrestrained, and Jiang was ultimately destroyed. Jin was truly responsible for this. Do those skilled in warfare really act like this…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
致意於書法間哉昔者楚窺晋政挑釁圍江處
父先事而伐楚欲其引兵以自救其謀未為失
也胡為不足於春秋而書以耶盖嘗考諸經矣
楚始伐鄭齊桓合召陵之師而鄭患自弭又嘗
圍宋晋文角城濮之戰而宋禍以紓今江國小
而弱楚人圍之必不待舉國甲兵之眾以勢易
為力也楚當是時負覆載不容之罪以義所當
討也使晋襄果能謀如桓文命齊秦諸兵以剪
其羽翼率曲沃大眾直擣其腹心伸我王法問
===
彼悖逆楚必震恐而江圍自解矣豈不得用兵
之法哉何乃君怠臣昏計不出此獨遣處父之
孤軍遠攻陸梁之強國友邦未見其從征元惡
不聞其致討意者晋人於此豈誠心於伐楚哉

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
乎故春秋於侵伐多不言所事此特書伐楚以
救江傳云以者不以者也言救江雖善而所以
救之者非其道矣其紀用兵之法為何如哉嗟
夫王風不競荆蠻暴横其為患於中國乆矣然
中國加兵於楚者僅有三處父救江有伐楚之
名而無討楚之實晋定召陵有伐楚之勢而僅
為侵楚之陋所謂彼善於此者其惟齊桓召陵
之師乎管仲相桓屈完受盟固其所也噫賢如
管仲乃能相君而成安攘之績彼處父者何以
===
為哉
禮記
司徒脩六禮以節民性明七教以興民德
齊八政以防淫一道德以同俗養耆老以
致孝恤孤獨以逮不足上賢以崇德簡不
肖以絀惡
蔣曙
考試官教諭趙 批 詞暢理明可取
考試官教諭朱 批 題本正大而組織傅
punctuated:
乎？故《春秋》於侵伐多不言所事，此特書「伐楚以救江」。傳云：「以者，不以者也。」言救江雖善，而所以救之者非其道矣。其紀用兵之法為何如哉？嗟夫！王風不競，荆蠻暴横，其為患於中國乆矣。然中國加兵於楚者僅有三：處父救江，有伐楚之名而無討楚之實；晋定召陵，有伐楚之勢而僅為侵楚之陋。所謂彼善於此者，其惟齊桓召陵之師乎？管仲相桓，屈完受盟，固其所也。噫！賢如管仲，乃能相君而成安攘之績，彼處父者何以為哉？
《禮記》
司徒脩六禮以節民性，明七教以興民德，齊八政以防淫，一道德以同俗，養耆老以致孝，恤孤獨以逮不足，上賢以崇德，簡不肖以絀惡。
蔣曙
考試官教諭趙批：「詞暢理明，可取。」
考試官教諭朱批：「題本正大，而組織傅」
translation_en:
…could this be so? Thus, when recording incursions and punitive expeditions, the Spring and Autumn Annals generally does not state their purpose. Here alone it specifically records, “attacked Chu in order to rescue Jiang.” The commentary says, “‘In order to’ signifies that the means were inappropriate.” This means that although rescuing Jiang was good, the means employed to rescue it were improper. How, then, does this record set forth the proper principles for employing troops? Alas! The influence of the royal house had waned, and the Man peoples of Jing acted with violence and insolence; they had long afflicted the central states. Yet there were only three occasions on which the central states took up arms against Chu. Chufu’s rescue of Jiang bore the name of an attack on Chu but lacked the substance of a punitive expedition. Duke Ding of Jin’s undertaking at Shaoling had the potential for a punitive attack on Chu, but amounted merely to an ignoble incursion. Of those that might be called “better than this,” surely only Duke Huan of Qi’s campaign at Shaoling qualifies? With Guan Zhong assisting Duke Huan, Qu Wan’s acceptance of the covenant was indeed the fitting outcome. Ah! Only someone as worthy as Guan Zhong could assist his ruler and achieve the pacification of the realm and the repulsion of outsiders. What could that Chufu accomplish?
Record of Rites
“The Minister of Education regulates the six rites to restrain the people’s dispositions, clarifies the seven teachings to promote the people’s virtue, orders the eight branches of government to prevent excess, and unifies moral principles to bring customs into agreement. He cares for the aged to foster filial devotion, shows compassion for orphans and the solitary to provide for those in want, elevates the worthy to honor virtue, and distinguishes the unworthy to reject wickedness.”
Jiang Shu
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “The language flows smoothly and the reasoning is clear. Worth accepting.”
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The topic itself is upright and grand, and the composition’s arrangement [?]…”

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
註措詞莊重無如此篇是用録出
大臣於鄉學必詳其教民取士之法也盖教民
取士鄉學之政令也大臣於此烏可不詳其法
而總其政令哉且夫先王立鄉學之教必設大
司徒以總其政令然其教民取士之法當何如
哉彼民性非禮節之則易以流必脩冠昏喪祭
鄉相見之六禮以節民性使不至於流焉民德
非教興之則易以廢必明父子兄弟夫婦君臣
長幼朋友賓客之七教以興民德使不至於廢
===
焉八政不齊則亦禮教之害又必齊其飲食衣
服事為異别度量數制之八政以防民淫所以
使之無過行也道德異尚則其體不一又必一
其人所共由之道衆所同得之德以同民俗所
以使之無異習也六十曰耆七十曰老養耆老以
享食之禮則推愛親之心於是為至矣無父曰
孤無子曰獨恤孤獨以常餼之養則損有餘之
心無所不及矣至於能帥教而才德穎出者為
賢於賢者上之則命鄉論秀或升於司徒而名
punctuated:
註，措詞莊重，無如此篇，是用録出。

大臣於鄉學，必詳其教民取士之法也。盖教民取士，鄉學之政令也。大臣於此，烏可不詳其法而總其政令哉？且夫先王立鄉學之教，必設大司徒以總其政令。然其教民取士之法，當何如哉？彼民性非禮節之，則易以流，必脩冠、昏、喪、祭、鄉、相見之六禮以節民性，使不至於流焉。民德非教興之，則易以廢，必明父子、兄弟、夫婦、君臣、長幼、朋友、賓客之七教以興民德，使不至於廢焉。八政不齊，則亦禮教之害，又必齊其飲食、衣服、事為、異别、度、量、數、制之八政以防民淫，所以使之無過行也。道德異尚，則其體不一，又必一其人所共由之道、衆所同得之德以同民俗，所以使之無異習也。六十曰耆，七十曰老。養耆老以享食之禮，則推愛親之心於是為至矣。無父曰孤，無子曰獨。恤孤獨以常餼之養，則損有餘之心無所不及矣。至於能帥教而才德穎出者為賢，於賢者上之，則命鄉論秀，或升於司徒而名
translation_en:
…the commentary. In its dignified wording, none equals this essay; it has therefore been selected for inclusion.

In overseeing the local schools, a high minister must thoroughly understand the methods for educating the people and selecting worthy men. Educating the people and selecting worthy men constitute the administrative business of the local schools. How could a high minister direct that business without thoroughly understanding its methods? When the former kings established instruction in the local schools, they invariably appointed a Minister of Education to oversee their administration. But what should their methods for educating the people and selecting worthy men be?

Unless restrained by ritual, the people's dispositions readily go astray. The six rites—capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice, the village drinking ceremony, and formal meetings—must therefore be cultivated to regulate their dispositions and keep them from going astray. Unless fostered through instruction, the people's virtue readily falls into neglect. The seven teachings concerning fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers, husbands and wives, rulers and ministers, seniors and juniors, friends, and hosts and guests must therefore be elucidated to foster the people's virtue and keep it from falling into neglect.

If the eight branches of regulation are not made uniform, they too will undermine ritual instruction. The eight branches governing food and drink, clothing, activities, distinctions, linear measures, measures of capacity, numerical reckoning, and prescribed standards must therefore be made uniform to guard against excess among the people and prevent improper conduct. If different ways and virtues are esteemed, the social body will lack unity. The Way that all people follow and the virtue that all alike possess must therefore be unified to make popular customs uniform and prevent divergent practices.

Those aged sixty are called elders; those aged seventy are called the aged. Providing for elders and the aged through the rites of feasting and feeding brings the extension of one's love for one's parents to its fullest expression. Those without fathers are called orphans; those without children are called the solitary. Caring for orphans and the solitary through regular provisions extends everywhere the intention to give from one's surplus.

Those who can follow the teachings and whose ability and virtue stand out are deemed worthy. To exalt the worthy, the local communities are ordered to assess their outstanding men; some are advanced to the Minister of Education and their names…

孤無子曰獨恤孤獨以常餼之養則損有餘之
心無所不及矣至於能帥教而才德穎出者為
賢於賢者上之則命鄉論秀或升於司徒而名
punctuated:
註：措詞莊重，無如此篇，是用録出。

大臣於鄉學，必詳其教民取士之法也。蓋教民取士，鄉學之政令也。大臣於此，烏可不詳其法而總其政令哉？且夫先王立鄉學之教，必設大司徒以總其政令，然其教民取士之法當何如哉？彼民性非禮節之則易以流，必脩冠、昏、喪、祭、鄉、相見之六禮，以節民性，使不至於流焉。民德非教興之則易以廢，必明父子、兄弟、夫婦、君臣、長幼、朋友、賓客之七教，以興民德，使不至於廢焉。八政不齊，則亦禮教之害，又必齊其飲食、衣服、事為、異别、度、量、數、制之八政，以防民淫，所以使之無過行也。道德異尚，則其體不一，又必一其人所共由之道、衆所同得之德，以同民俗，所以使之無異習也。六十曰耆，七十曰老，養耆老以享食之禮，則推愛親之心，於是為至矣。無父曰孤，無子曰獨，恤孤獨以常餼之養，則損有餘之心，無所不及矣。至於能帥教而才德穎出者為賢，於賢者上之，則命鄉論秀，或升於司徒而名
translation_en:
Note: No other piece matches this one in the gravity of its wording; it is therefore transcribed here.

A high minister must thoroughly understand the methods by which the district schools instruct the people and select scholars. For instructing the people and selecting scholars constitute the administrative duties of the district schools. How could a high minister oversee their administration without thoroughly understanding these methods? When the former kings established instruction in the district schools, they invariably appointed a Minister of Education to oversee their administration. What, then, should their methods of instructing the people and selecting scholars be?

The people's natural dispositions readily go astray unless restrained by ritual. Thus the six rites—capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice, district drinking ceremonies, and formal meetings—must be cultivated to regulate the people's dispositions and keep them from going astray. The people's virtue readily falls into neglect unless fostered through instruction. Thus the seven teachings concerning fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers, husbands and wives, rulers and ministers, seniors and juniors, friends, and hosts and guests must be clarified to foster the people's virtue and keep it from falling into neglect.

If the eight domains of governance are not regulated uniformly, this too harms ritual instruction. Thus uniform regulation must be imposed on food and drink, clothing, activities, distinctions, measures of length, measures of capacity, numbers, and standards, to guard against the people's excesses and keep their conduct from overstepping proper bounds. If people esteem different ways and virtues, their underlying principles will lack unity. Thus the Way that all follow and the virtue that all acquire must be unified, to bring the people's customs into agreement and prevent divergent practices.

Those aged sixty are called elders, and those aged seventy are called the aged. Supporting them through the rites of feasting and feeding extends the love one bears one's parents to its fullest reach. Those without fathers are called orphans, and those without sons are called the solitary. Caring for them through regular provisions extends everywhere the resolve to give up one's surplus. As for those who follow the teachings and excel in talent and virtue, they are deemed worthy. To elevate the worthy, the districts are ordered to assess their outstanding men; some are advanced to the Minister of Education and designated …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
選士或升於國學而名俊士其崇德也可見不
帥教而無善可録者爲不肖於不肖者簡之則
命鄉習禮或移郊遂以示其不變或屏遠方而
示以不齒其絀惡也可知噫教民取士之法其
詳如此非大司徒總其政令孰能然哉雖然此
特鄉學教民取士之法耳下章有曰樂正崇四
術立四教順先王詩書禮樂以造士至於大樂
正論造士之秀者以告于王而升之司馬曰進
士此又言國學教國子民俊及取賢才之法也
===
盖古者鄉學教庶人國學教國子及庶人之俊
而皆升其秀者而爵禄之此所以人無不學野
無遺賢治隆俗美而爲王道之成也歟
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣
藍貴
考試官教諭趙批簡明
考試官教諭朱批辭理俱到發明武王〔大教之意殆盡録之〕
聖王始制尊君之禮群臣自效尊君之誠夫禮
punctuated:
選士，或升於國學而名俊士，其崇德也可見。不帥教而無善可録者爲不肖，於不肖者簡之，則命鄉習禮，或移郊遂以示其不變，或屏遠方而示以不齒，其絀惡也可知。噫！教民取士之法，其詳如此，非大司徒總其政令，孰能然哉？雖然，此特鄉學教民取士之法耳。下章有曰：「樂正崇四術，立四教，順先王詩書禮樂以造士。」至於大樂正論造士之秀者，以告于王，而升之司馬，曰進士，此又言國學教國子、民俊及取賢才之法也。盖古者鄉學教庶人，國學教國子及庶人之俊，而皆升其秀者而爵禄之。此所以人無不學，野無遺賢，治隆俗美，而爲王道之成也歟！
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣
藍貴
考試官教諭趙批：「簡明。」
考試官教諭朱批：「辭理俱到，發明武王〔大教之意殆盡，録之〕。」
聖王始制尊君之禮，群臣自效尊君之誠。夫禮
translation_en:
…“selected scholars”; others are advanced to the state school and called “outstanding scholars.” Its honoring of virtue is thus evident. Those who do not follow the instruction and have no goodness worth recording are deemed unworthy. The unworthy are distinguished and ordered to practice ritual in their home districts; some are moved to the outer suburban districts to mark their failure to reform, while others are banished to distant regions to show that they are excluded from the community. Its rejection of wickedness can thus be understood. Ah! The methods for instructing the people and selecting scholars were so detailed: without the Grand Minister of Education directing their administrative commands, who could have achieved this? Nevertheless, these are only the methods by which district schools instructed the people and selected scholars. The following chapter says: “The Director of Music promotes the four arts and establishes the four teachings, following the former kings’ Poetry, Documents, Rites, and Music to train scholars.” It goes on to describe how the Grand Director of Music assesses the outstanding scholars so trained, reports them to the king, and advances them to the Minister of War, calling them “advanced scholars” (jinshi). This, in turn, describes how the state school instructed the sons of the nobility and outstanding commoners, and selected worthy talent.
In antiquity, district schools instructed commoners, while the state school instructed the sons of the nobility and outstanding commoners. In both cases, the most distinguished were promoted and granted rank and emoluments. Was this not why no one failed to study, no worthy person remained overlooked in the countryside, government flourished, customs were admirable, and the Kingly Way was brought to fulfillment?
“Only after attending court audiences do the feudal lords understand how to act as subjects.”
Lan Gui
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “Concise and clear.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished. It elucidates King Wu’s 〔intent in his great teaching almost exhaustively. Include it.〕”
The sage king first instituted the rites for honoring the ruler, and his assembled ministers themselves demonstrated their sincerity in honoring him. Now, ritual…

聖王始制尊君之禮，群臣自效尊君之誠。夫禮
translation_en:
…selected scholars; some were promoted to the state school and called outstanding scholars. Here one can see how virtue was honored. Those who did not follow the instruction and had no goodness worth recording were deemed unworthy. After distinguishing among the unworthy, the authorities ordered them to practice ritual in the local district; some were transferred to the outer suburbs and outlying districts to make their failure to reform manifest, while others were banished to distant regions to show that they were excluded from the community. Here one can understand how wrongdoing was rejected. Ah! The methods for instructing the people and selecting scholars were so detailed: who could have accomplished this unless the Minister of Education oversaw their ordinances? Yet these were merely the methods by which local schools instructed the people and selected scholars. The following chapter says: “The Director of Music upholds the four arts and establishes the four teachings, following the former kings’ Poetry, Documents, Rites, and Music to train scholars.” Then the Grand Director of Music assesses the outstanding scholars thus trained, reports them to the king, and advances them to the Minister of War; they are called “advanced scholars” (jinshi). In antiquity, local schools instructed commoners, while the state school instructed the sons of the nobility and outstanding commoners. Both advanced their outstanding scholars and bestowed rank and emoluments upon them. Was this not why everyone studied, no worthy man remained overlooked in the countryside, government flourished, customs were admirable, and the Kingly Way reached fulfillment?

“Only after attending court audiences do the feudal lords understand how to act as subjects.”
Lan Gui.
Examiner Zhao, School Instructor, comments: “Concise and clear.”
Examiner Zhu, School Instructor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully developed. It elucidates almost exhaustively the intent of the great teaching of the ‘martial ruler’ [?]. Include it.”

The sage king first established the rites for honoring the ruler, and his ministers of their own accord demonstrated their sincerity in honoring him. As for ritual…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
莫尊於朝覲也然則群臣知自效其尊君之誠
者豈無所由來哉樂記論武王克商之後武功
告成而文教之誕敷封賞既行而禮制之當舉
彼其春見曰朝諸侯敬君之大禮也武王即位
之初遂制為朝禮以嚴上下之分所謂天子當
宁而立諸公東面諸侯西面之禮於是乎定矣
秋見曰覲諸侯尊君之大典也武王踐祚之始
即制為覲禮以明君臣之義所謂天子當依而
立諸侯北面而見之禮於是乎舉矣夫朝覲之
===
禮既有定制由是析圭儋爵而為公為侯者非
一臣也今則莫不再拜稽首於冕旒之前功罪
舉焉黜陟行焉而知所以臣者一天冠地屨之
截然也尊君之誠容有已乎分茅胙土而曰伯
曰子男者非一國也今則靡不對揚休命於阼
階之下賞罰明焉予奪加焉而知所以臣者一
山高澤卑之自如也敬君之心容有間乎此朝
覲所以為大禮武王所以為大教也歟抑論武
王當商家之季興牧野之師救民於水火之中
punctuated: 莫尊於朝覲也。然則群臣知自效其尊君之誠者，豈無所由來哉？《樂記》論武王克商之後，武功告成而文教之誕敷，封賞既行而禮制之當舉。彼其春見曰朝，諸侯敬君之大禮也。武王即位之初，遂制為朝禮，以嚴上下之分。所謂天子當宁而立，諸公東面，諸侯西面之禮，於是乎定矣。秋見曰覲，諸侯尊君之大典也。武王踐祚之始，即制為覲禮，以明君臣之義。所謂天子當依而立，諸侯北面而見之禮，於是乎舉矣。夫朝覲之禮既有定制，由是析圭儋爵而為公為侯者，非一臣也。今則莫不再拜稽首於冕旒之前，功罪舉焉，黜陟行焉，而知所以臣者一。天冠地屨之截然也，尊君之誠容有已乎？分茅胙土而曰伯曰子男者，非一國也。今則靡不對揚休命於阼階之下，賞罰明焉，予奪加焉，而知所以臣者一。山高澤卑之自如也，敬君之心容有間乎？此朝覲所以為大禮，武王所以為大教也歟？抑論武王當商家之季，興牧野之師，救民於水火之中
translation_en:
…none is more exalted than the spring and autumn audiences. If so, surely there is a reason why the assembled ministers knew to demonstrate for themselves their sincerity in honoring their ruler? The Record of Music (Yueji) discusses how, after King Wu conquered Shang, his military achievements were complete and civil instruction was spread far and wide; enfeoffments and rewards having been bestowed, ritual institutions were then to be established. An audience in spring was called chao: this was the great rite through which the regional lords showed reverence for their ruler. At the beginning of his reign, King Wu accordingly instituted the spring audience to enforce the distinction between superior and inferior. Thus was established the rite described as the Son of Heaven standing in the space before the hall, with the dukes facing east and the marquises facing west. An audience in autumn was called jin: this was the great ceremony through which the regional lords honored their ruler. Upon ascending the throne, King Wu instituted the autumn audience to clarify the proper relationship between ruler and minister. Thus was put into practice the rite described as the Son of Heaven standing before the screen, with the regional lords facing north to appear before him.

Once fixed regulations had been established for the spring and autumn audiences, the ministers who received jade tablets and bore noble rank as dukes and marquises were many. Now all bowed twice and touched their foreheads to the ground before the ruler in his tasseled crown. Their merits and offenses were brought forward, and demotions and promotions were carried out; all alike understood how to conduct themselves as subjects. With the distinction as clear-cut as heaven above, like a cap, and earth below, like shoes, could their sincerity in honoring the ruler ever cease? There were many states whose rulers, receiving the ceremonial thatch and grants of territory, were styled earls, viscounts, and barons. Now all acknowledged and extolled the gracious commands below the eastern steps. Rewards and punishments were made clear, and grants and deprivations were imposed; all alike understood how to conduct themselves as subjects. With their stations as naturally ordered as the height of mountains and the lowliness of marshes, could their reverence for the ruler ever lapse? Is this not why the spring and autumn audiences constituted great rites, and why King Wu made them a great instrument of instruction? Furthermore, consider how King Wu, in the closing years of the Shang house, raised the army that fought at Muye and rescued the people from fire and flood…

text:

王當商家之季興牧野之師救民於水火之中
punctuated: 莫尊於朝覲也。然則群臣知自效其尊君之誠者，豈無所由来哉？《樂記》論武王克商之後，武功告成而文教之誕敷，封賞既行而禮制之當舉。彼其春見曰朝，諸侯敬君之大禮也。武王即位之初，遂制為朝禮，以嚴上下之分，所謂天子當宁而立，諸公東面、諸侯西面之禮，於是乎定矣。秋見曰覲，諸侯尊君之大典也。武王踐阼之始，即制為覲禮，以明君臣之義，所謂天子當依而立，諸侯北面而見之禮，於是乎舉矣。夫朝覲之禮既有定制，由是析圭儋爵而為公為侯者，非一臣也。今則莫不再拜稽首於冕旒之前，功罪舉焉，黜陟行焉，而知所以臣者一，天冠地屨之截然也。尊君之誠容有已乎？分茅胙土而曰伯曰子男者，非一國也。今則靡不對揚休命於黼陛之下，賞罰明焉，予奪加焉，而知所以臣者一，山高澤卑之自如也。敬君之心容有間乎？此朝覲所以為大禮，武王所以為大教也歟！抑論武王當商家之季，興牧野之師，救民於水火之中
translation_en:
…None is more exalted than the rites of court audience. Thus, could the assembled ministers’ understanding that they must themselves demonstrate their sincerity in honoring their ruler have arisen without a cause? The Record of Music discusses how, after King Wu conquered Shang, his military achievement was complete and civil instruction was widely disseminated; enfeoffments and rewards had been granted, and ritual institutions were due to be established. An audience in spring was called chao: it was the great rite through which the regional lords showed reverence for their ruler. At the beginning of his reign, King Wu accordingly instituted the spring audience rites to enforce the distinction between superior and inferior. Thus was established the rite in which the Son of Heaven stood in the space between the palace gate and the screen, with the dukes facing east and the marquises facing west. An audience in autumn was called jin: it was the great ceremony through which the regional lords honored their ruler. Upon ascending the throne, King Wu instituted the autumn audience rites to clarify the proper relationship between ruler and subject. Thus was enacted the rite in which the Son of Heaven stood before the ceremonial screen and the regional lords faced north to appear before him.

Once fixed regulations existed for the rites of court audience, the ministers who received allotted jade tablets and bore noble rank as dukes and marquises were many. Now, however, all bowed twice and knocked their heads to the ground before the ruler in his pendant-strung ceremonial crown. Merits and offenses were brought forward, and demotions and promotions were carried out. They understood that the sovereign whom they served was one, with the distinction between ruler and subject as absolute as that between Heaven above, like a cap, and Earth below, like shoes. Could their sincerity in honoring their ruler ever cease? Those granted thatch and invested with lands as earls, viscounts, and barons ruled more than a single domain. Now, however, all acknowledged and extolled the gracious commands below the ornamented throne steps. Rewards and punishments were made clear, and grants and deprivations were imposed. They understood that the sovereign whom they served was one, with the relationship as natural as mountains being high and marshes low. Could their reverence for their ruler ever lapse? Is this not why court audiences constituted a great rite, and why King Wu made them a great instrument of instruction? Furthermore, consider how King Wu, in the last days of the Shang house, raised the army that fought at Muye and rescued the people from fire and flood…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
撥亂而歸之正大敎之舉豈止此哉觀其習射
以貍首騶虞為節諸侯以裨冕搢笏為容明堂
耕籍養老之禮以次而行皆以一天下之制度
新天下之觀聽所以周道四達而禮樂交通也
孔子語賓牟賈武樂之遲而又久者其以此夫
第貳塲
論
孔子之道大而能博
徐淮
同考試官敎諭林批作者多於大博二字
分別不精理明詞暢者僅見是篇宜錄
考試官敎諭趙批議論疊出詞理渾成
非筆端有造化者安能辦此
考試官敎諭朱批論有抑揚有歸宿且
辭氣舂容真佳士也
舉斯道之全體而獨歸於聖人善言聖人
者也夫道原于天而畀于人本至大而且
博也顧見之小者自失其大局於偏者自
punctuated:

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
狹其博而道之全體虧矣然則大以該其
博博以成其大舉全體而咸備於一身不
於聖人之歸而誰歸哉是其一理純全渾
淪而無外萬善畢具該貫而無遺無惑乎
門弟子不能徧觀而盡識也韓愈氏有見
于此而獨言之可謂善言聖人者矣請畢
其說天地生物而厚於人天地生人而厚
於聖人人也者道之寓也聖人者人之至
而斯道所由以傳者也然群聖相承至孔
===
子而獨盛聖道相傳至孔子而獨全道全
於孔子則其集群聖之大成而既大且博
也固宜且孔子之道何道也堯舜禹湯文
武周公之道也亦天下古今所共由之道
也然知之而不能有有之而不能咸者衆
矣道之全體惡乎備彼夷之清尹之任惠
之和幾于大矣而所就各倚於一偏何有
於博聃之禮弘之樂郯之官似乎博矣而
所知各局於一善何有於大下此則愈小
punctuated:
狹其博，而道之全體虧矣。然則大以該其博，博以成其大，舉全體而咸備於一身，不於聖人之歸而誰歸哉？是其一理純全，渾淪而無外；萬善畢具，該貫而無遺。無惑乎門弟子不能徧觀而盡識也。韓愈氏有見于此而獨言之，可謂善言聖人者矣。請畢其說。
天地生物而厚於人，天地生人而厚於聖人。人也者，道之寓也；聖人者，人之至，而斯道所由以傳者也。然群聖相承，至孔子而獨盛；聖道相傳，至孔子而獨全。道全於孔子，則其集群聖之大成而既大且博也，固宜。且孔子之道何道也？堯舜禹湯文武周公之道也，亦天下古今所共由之道也。然知之而不能有，有之而不能咸者衆矣，道之全體惡乎備？彼夷之清、尹之任、惠之和，幾于大矣，而所就各倚於一偏，何有於博？聃之禮、弘之樂、郯之官，似乎博矣，而所知各局於一善，何有於大？下此則愈小
translation_en:
…constrict its breadth, and thus impair the Way in its entirety. Greatness, then, embraces its breadth, and breadth completes its greatness. If the embodiment of its entirety, fully present in a single person, is not to be attributed to the sage, to whom can it be attributed? In him, the single principle is pure and complete, an undivided whole with nothing outside it; all forms of goodness are fully present, comprehensively united with nothing omitted. No wonder his disciples could not survey it everywhere and comprehend it completely. Han Yu perceived this and gave it distinctive expression: he may indeed be called one who spoke well of the sage. Let me complete this explanation.
Heaven and Earth produce the myriad beings, but endow human beings most generously; they produce human beings, but endow sages most generously. Human beings are where the Way resides; sages represent the highest attainment of humanity and are those through whom this Way is transmitted. Yet, as successive sages continued one another’s work, it was only with Kongzi that this reached its fullest flourishing; as the sages’ Way was handed down, it was only with Kongzi that it reached completeness. Since the Way was complete in Kongzi, it was fitting that he brought together the achievements of all the sages into a grand consummation, both great and broad. And what Way was Kongzi’s Way? It was the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and Zhou Gong, and also the Way followed in common throughout the world, in antiquity and today. Yet many know it without being able to embody it, or embody it without being able to encompass it all. Where, then, is the Way present in its entirety? The purity of Bo Yi, the readiness of Yi Yin to shoulder responsibility, and the harmony of Liuxia Hui came close to greatness; yet each one’s attainment inclined toward a single aspect. How could they possess breadth? Lao Dan’s knowledge of ritual, Chang Hong’s knowledge of music, and Tan Zi’s knowledge of official institutions seem broad; yet each one’s knowledge was confined to a single excellence. How could they possess greatness? Below these, attainments grow still smaller…

translation_en: …constrict its breadth [?], and the Way in its entirety is impaired. Thus, greatness encompasses breadth, and breadth completes greatness. In him, the single principle is pure and complete, an undivided whole with nothing outside it; every goodness is fully present, comprehensively integrated, with nothing omitted. title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
愈狹初不足以企吾道之彷彿其視所謂
大者博者何物耶學者欲識斯道之全曷
不於孔子而觀之乎是故仁義禮智其性
也而一由於天縱親義序別信其用也而
一出於安行仰之彌高鑽之彌堅何窮盡
也瞻之在前忽焉在後何方體也語其所
至渾然如元氣流行而諸子之清之任之
和直道中之一端耳曾足以方其大耶古
今事變貫徹於敏求之餘物理精粗昭融
===
於默識之表釣弋獵較事至微也而無乎
不能乘田委吏職至卑也而無乎不稱究
其所有充然如萬象森列而諸子之禮之
樂之官僅道中之一藝耳曾足以擬其博
耶譬諸天輕清在上穹然其形也而日月
行焉星辰繫焉舉萬物而無不覆譬諸地
重濁在下隤然其質也而華岳峙焉河海
振焉舉萬物而無不載聖人之道天地之
道也知天地則知聖人矣是則非大無以
punctuated: 愈狹，初不足以企吾道之彷彿，其視所謂大者博者何物耶？學者欲識斯道之全，曷不於孔子而觀之乎？是故仁義禮智，其性也，而一由於天縱；親義序別信，其用也，而一出於安行。仰之彌高，鑽之彌堅，何窮盡也？瞻之在前，忽焉在後，何方體也？語其所至，渾然如元氣流行，而諸子之清之任之和，直道中之一端耳，曾足以方其大耶？古今事變，貫徹於敏求之餘；物理精粗，昭融於默識之表。釣弋獵較，事至微也，而無乎不能；乘田委吏，職至卑也，而無乎不稱。究其所有，充然如萬象森列，而諸子之禮之樂之官，僅道中之一藝耳，曾足以擬其博耶？譬諸天，輕清在上，穹然其形也，而日月行焉，星辰繫焉，舉萬物而無不覆；譬諸地，重濁在下，隤然其質也，而華岳峙焉，河海振焉，舉萬物而無不載。聖人之道，天地之道也。知天地，則知聖人矣。是則非大無以
translation_en:
…and ever narrower, utterly unable even to approach a semblance of our Way. What do they amount to when measured against what is called greatness and breadth? If students wish to understand this Way in its entirety, why do they not look to Confucius? Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom constituted his nature, all arising from Heaven’s endowment. Affection, righteousness, precedence, distinction, and trustworthiness constituted its practical workings, all proceeding from effortless conduct. Look up to it, and it grows ever higher; bore into it, and it grows ever harder: how could it be exhausted? Behold it ahead, and suddenly it is behind: what fixed location or form could it have? Speaking of his attainment, it was an integrated whole, like the primal vital force flowing everywhere. The purity, responsibility, and harmony of those other masters were merely single aspects of the Way. How could they possibly compare with his greatness?

The affairs and changes of past and present he comprehended through his diligent pursuit of knowledge; the principles of things, subtle and coarse alike, he understood with luminous clarity beyond what he silently retained. Angling, shooting birds with corded arrows, and competing in the hunt were exceedingly minor activities, yet there was none in which he lacked ability. Keeper of livestock and keeper of stores were exceedingly humble posts, yet in each he discharged his duties fittingly. Examining all that he possessed, one finds it abundant, like the myriad phenomena arrayed in their profusion. The ritual, music, and official institutions known by those other masters were merely individual accomplishments within the Way. How could they possibly match his breadth?

Compare it to Heaven: light and clear above, vaulted in form, with the sun and moon moving through it and the stars and constellations attached to it—of all the myriad things, there is none it does not cover. Compare it to Earth: heavy and turbid below, solid and settled in substance, with Mount Hua and the other great peaks towering upon it, and rivers and seas surging through it—of all the myriad things, there is none it does not bear. The Way of the sage is the Way of Heaven and Earth. Understand Heaven and Earth, and one understands the sage. Thus, without greatness there is no means to…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
該乎博而大者博之所寓也非博無以成
其大而博者大之所包也具其大而不遺
於博孔子之道如之何其可及乎夷考當
時七十之徒相與受學亦皆得其性之所
近如淵騫之德行予賜之言語初非無所
得也而各一其善由求之政事游夏之文
學亦非無所得也而各一其長何也道大
而博不能徧觀而盡識也及門之徒尚然
則夫授受於列國源遠而末益分者可知
===
矣宜乎百有餘歲之後僅一孟軻氏上接
其傳而得其宗也噫至哉孔子之道乎其
備全體而獨盛亘古今而一人者乎愈也後
孟軻而生乃復遠窺而特稱之謂非善言
聖人者能之歟抑愈於此既稱夫子之道
而謂得其傳者在於軻矣至於原道復歷
叙列聖相傳之統而歎軻死不得其傳焉
其意豈不以軻之所自任者自期耶惜其
志雖有在而大道未聞閎中肆外之文尚
punctuated: 該乎博，而大者博之所寓也；非博無以成其大，而博者大之所包也。具其大而不遺於博，孔子之道如之何其可及乎？夷考當時，七十之徒相與受學，亦皆得其性之所近。如淵騫之德行，予賜之言語，初非無所得也，而各一其善；由求之政事，游夏之文學，亦非無所得也，而各一其長。何也？道大而博，不能徧觀而盡識也。及門之徒尚然，則夫授受於列國，源遠而末益分者可知矣。宜乎百有餘歲之後，僅一孟軻氏上接其傳而得其宗也。噫！至哉，孔子之道乎！其備全體而獨盛，亘古今而一人者乎！愈也後孟軻而生，乃復遠窺而特稱之，謂非善言聖人者能之歟？抑愈於此既稱夫子之道，而謂得其傳者在於軻矣。至於《原道》，復歷叙列聖相傳之統，而歎軻死不得其傳焉。其意豈不以軻之所自任者自期耶？惜其志雖有在，而大道未聞，閎中肆外之文尚
translation_en:
…encompass its breadth; greatness is that in which breadth resides. Without breadth, its greatness cannot be achieved; breadth is what greatness embraces. Possessing such greatness while omitting nothing in breadth, how could Confucius’s Way ever be equaled? Examining the circumstances of his time, we find that the seventy disciples who studied together under him each attained what accorded with their natural dispositions. Thus Yan Yuan and Min Qian excelled in virtuous conduct, and Zai Yu and Duanmu Ci in speech. It was certainly not that they attained nothing, but each excelled in one particular respect. Zhong You and Ran Qiu excelled in government, and Ziyou and Zixia in literary learning. They too certainly attained something, but each had his particular strength. Why was this? The Way was so great and broad that they could not survey it everywhere and comprehend it entirely. If even the disciples who entered his gate were like this, we can understand how, as his teaching was transmitted and received throughout the various states, its branches became ever more divided as they grew farther from their source. It is fitting, then, that more than a hundred years later, Meng Ke alone should have reached back to continue its transmission and grasped its essential teaching.

Ah, how consummate was the Way of Confucius! Did he not possess its complete substance and flourish without equal, standing alone throughout past and present? Han Yu was born after Meng Ke, yet he could discern it across that distance and single it out for praise. Could anyone who was not adept at speaking of the sage have accomplished this? Moreover, here Han Yu praises the Master’s Way and declares that it was Meng Ke who received its transmission. In his Inquiry into the Way, he again recounts in sequence the lineage transmitted from sage to sage, and laments that after Meng Ke’s death no one received that transmission. Was his intention not to aspire to the responsibility that Meng Ke had taken upon himself? Regrettably, although his aspirations had their object, he had not yet apprehended the Great Way, and his writing, expansive within and unrestrained in outward expression, still…

…encompasses breadth. Greatness is that in which breadth resides: without breadth, its greatness could not be realized. Breadth, in turn, is what greatness embraces: possessing that greatness, it leaves nothing out of its breadth. How could the Way of Kongzi be equaled? If we examine the circumstances of his time, the seventy disciples who studied together under him each grasped what was closest to his own nature. Yuan and Qian excelled in virtuous conduct, and Yu and Ci in speech. They certainly attained something, yet each possessed only his particular excellence.
