Regrettably, although his aspirations were directed toward this, he had not heard the Great Way, and his writing, capacious within and unrestrained in its outward expression, still …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
未敢上擬夫子之所謂傳者而況於其大
乎雖然道具於心者也道有顯晦而心無
存亡又安知千載之下不有以心感心而
契此道之傳者哉
表
擬立
皇太子正位東宮
賀表
楊樌
===
同考試官教諭謝批駢驪有則
同考試官學正陳批詞氣渾厚而忠愛之
心見於言外可謂善
頌禱者矣
考試官教諭趙批表有忠惓之誠非區
區騁浮詞者
考試官教諭朱批得體
弘治五年三月初八日伏遇
皇上冊立
punctuated:
未敢上擬夫子之所謂傳者，而況於其大乎？雖然，道具於心者也。道有顯晦，而心無存亡，又安知千載之下，不有以心感心而契此道之傳者哉？

表
擬立皇太子正位東宮賀表
楊樌

同考試官教諭謝批：駢驪有則。
同考試官學正陳批：詞氣渾厚，而忠愛之心見於言外，可謂善頌禱者矣。
考試官教諭趙批：表有忠惓之誠，非區區騁浮詞者。
考試官教諭朱批：得體。

弘治五年三月初八日，伏遇皇上冊立
translation_en:
…one would not yet dare compare it with what the Master called the transmission, much less with the greatness of his Way! Nevertheless, the Way is fully present in the heart. The Way may become manifest or obscure, but the heart neither comes into being nor perishes. How, then, can we know that a thousand years later there will not be someone whose heart responds to another heart and accords with the transmission of this Way?

Memorial
A model congratulatory memorial on the establishment of the Imperial Heir Apparent and his assumption of his rightful position in the Eastern Palace
By Yang Guan

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: The parallel prose [?] observes proper rules.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The language and spirit are full and substantial, while a heart of loyalty and love is evident beyond the words. He may indeed be called skilled in offering praise and prayers.
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: This memorial conveys sincere loyalty and devoted concern; it is no mere display of empty phrases.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Appropriate in form and tone.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇太子正位東宮率四方群臣賀者〔臣〕等誠惶
誠恐稽首頓首上言
伏以
紫極穹窿光映
前星之煥
青宮突兀高依
北闕之尊開萬年不拔之洪基成一代非常之
盛事光生宇宙懽動華夷恭惟
〇〇〇〇
===
至誠至聖
允武允文篤孝
重闈循大舜克諧之道
丕承
列聖同武王善述之心
帝德罔愆
天心攸格熊羆夢叶肇嫡派於
天潢麟趾化行植本宗於
帝胄
punctuated:
皇太子正位東宮，率四方群臣賀者，〔臣〕等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：
伏以紫極穹窿，光映前星之煥；青宮突兀，高依北闕之尊。開萬年不拔之洪基，成一代非常之盛事。光生宇宙，懽動華夷。恭惟〇〇〇〇，至誠至聖，允武允文。篤孝重闈，循大舜克諧之道；丕承列聖，同武王善述之心。帝德罔愆，天心攸格。熊羆夢叶，肇嫡派於天潢；麟趾化行，植本宗於帝胄。
translation_en:
…the Crown Prince, duly established in the Eastern Palace, on which occasion the assembled officials from all quarters offer congratulations. We, your servants, in profound awe and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground and kowtow, submitting these words:
We humbly consider: the lofty vault of the Purple Pole shines upon the brilliance of the Foremost Star, emblem of the heir apparent; the towering Azure Palace of the heir rests upon the exalted dignity of the Northern Palace Gate. An immense foundation, unshakable for ten thousand years, has been laid; an extraordinary and glorious undertaking of this dynasty has been accomplished. Radiance fills the universe; joy stirs both the Chinese and the peoples beyond.
We respectfully consider that [〇〇〇〇: unclear honorific text?] is supremely sincere and supremely sagely, truly martial and truly cultured. With profound filial devotion toward the senior palace generations, you follow the way of the great Shun, who brought his family into harmony. In grandly carrying forward the legacy of successive sage sovereigns, you share King Wu’s resolve to continue his predecessors’ undertakings faithfully. Your imperial virtue is without fault; it reaches the heart of Heaven. The dream of bears has been fulfilled, inaugurating the legitimate line within the celestial stream of the imperial house. The transforming influence celebrated in “The Qilin’s Hooves” spreads, establishing the main ancestral line among the imperial descendants…

伏以紫極穹窿，光映前星之煥；青宮突兀，高依北闕之尊。開萬年不拔之洪基，成一代非常之盛事。光生宇宙，懽動華夷。恭惟〇〇〇〇，至誠至聖，允武允文。篤孝重闈，循大舜克諧之道；丕承列聖，同武王善述之心。帝德罔愆，天心攸格。熊羆夢叶，肇嫡派於天潢；麟趾化行，植本宗於帝胄。
translation_en:
The Imperial Crown Prince having formally assumed his position in the Eastern Palace, [we] lead the assembled officials from the four quarters in offering congratulations [?]. We, your servants, in deepest awe and fear, bow our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtow, submitting these words:
We humbly consider: the Purple Pole, lofty and overarching, casts its radiance upon the brilliance of the Foremost Star—the Crown Prince. The Azure Palace towers aloft, resting upon the majesty of the Northern Palace Gates. A vast foundation has been established, unshakable for ten thousand years; an extraordinary achievement of this dynasty has been accomplished. Radiance fills the universe, and joy stirs Chinese and foreign peoples alike. Reverently considering 〇〇〇〇 [imperial designation unclear]: utmost in sincerity and sagacity, truly accomplished in arms and letters. Profoundly filial toward the senior palace households, you follow the way of the great Shun in bringing harmony to his family; magnificently continuing the legacy of the imperial ancestors, you share King Wu’s resolve to carry forward his forebears’ purposes. Your imperial virtue is without fault, and has moved the heart of Heaven. The dream of bears has been fulfilled—a favorable portent of a son—establishing the legitimate line within the celestial stream of imperial kinship. The transforming influence celebrated in “The Qilin’s Hoof” spreads, securing the principal line among the imperial descendants…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
方幼冲而岐嶷
即睿智而聰明福慶攸鍾人心均戴臣工懇
請謂主器不宜以久虛
聖意允從謂輿情不可以固拒光凝赫赫之命
敬展煌煌之儀授
冊寶而正位東儲渙
綸音而敷恩下土此誠自古帝王欲求而未
得欲遂而未能者也臣等職忝百司班參
群辟咸樂鳶飛之化盛事幸逢式勤燕賀
===
之心名言莫罄伏願
君謨協贊昭彰日月之明
國本滋培磅礴乾坤之大
皇圖有永
聖壽無疆臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
punctuated:
方幼冲而岐嶷，即睿智而聰明，福慶攸鍾，人心均戴。臣工懇請，謂主器不宜以久虛；聖意允從，謂輿情不可以固拒。光凝赫赫之命，敬展煌煌之儀，授冊寶而正位東儲，渙綸音而敷恩下土。此誠自古帝王欲求而未得、欲遂而未能者也。臣等職忝百司，班參群辟，咸樂鳶飛之化，盛事幸逢；式勤燕賀之心，名言莫罄。
伏願君謨協贊，昭彰日月之明；國本滋培，磅礴乾坤之大；皇圖有永，聖壽無疆。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱賀以
translation_en:
Though still of tender years, he already displays exceptional discernment; even now he is sagacious, intelligent, and perceptive. Blessings and good fortune converge upon him, and all hearts alike uphold him. Your officials earnestly petitioned, declaring that the position of heir to the ancestral vessels should not long remain vacant. Your Majesty graciously consented, considering that the wishes of the people could not be persistently refused. Your resplendent command was gloriously confirmed, and the magnificent ceremony reverently performed. Investiture documents and a seal were bestowed, establishing him in his rightful position as Crown Prince; imperial pronouncements were issued far and wide, extending grace throughout the realm. This is truly what emperors and kings since antiquity have sought without obtaining, and wished to accomplish without being able to do so. We, your servants, unworthily hold posts among the many offices and take our places among the assembled dignitaries. All rejoice in the transforming influence under which even kites soar freely, fortunate to witness this splendid event. Earnestly cherishing the congratulatory joy of nesting swallows, we cannot fully express our feelings in words [?].
We humbly wish that Your Majesty’s plans may receive united support, making manifest a brilliance like that of the sun and moon; that the foundation of the state may be nourished and strengthened, attaining the all-encompassing greatness of Heaven and Earth; that the imperial enterprise may endure forever; and that Your Majesty’s longevity may know no bounds. Gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, we, your servants, are overcome with fervent emotion and reverent awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to offer congratulations, thereby …

Blessings and good fortune converge upon him, and all hearts accord him their allegiance. Your Majesty graciously consented, judging that the wishes of the people could not firmly be refused. 帝王之制先於孝，而足以垂立教之典；帝王之孝本於誠，而有以弘化民之功。蓋孝也者，百行之本，萬善之原，古今人心所同然也。帝王垂世立教之典，化民成俗之功，固不外此，而要其所極，實本於此心之一誠耳。此我朝列聖之制作暨

…for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session. Policy Essay. First Question. Huang Zhifei 黃直奜.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: He amply expounds the filial piety of the successive sage emperors, matching it against the excellence of antiquity, and traces its source to undivided sincerity. Is he perhaps one who cherishes these principles and awaits an opportunity to put them into practice [?]?

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: He has a skilled hand for policy essays.

The institutions of emperors and kings give precedence to filial piety and thus suffice to bequeath standards for establishing moral instruction. The filial piety of emperors and kings is rooted in sincerity and thus serves to extend their achievement in transforming the people. The standards that emperors and kings bequeath to posterity for establishing moral instruction, and their achievements in transforming the people and shaping customs, assuredly do not go beyond this. title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇上之德教盖與虞帝之大孝武王之達孝同
一揆矣是豈後世所能及哉請因明問而
敷陳之天經地義莫尊乎親降衷秉彝莫
先於孝一自然而然初非有所勉強而為
者也肆我
太祖高皇帝創業垂統追
帝其先推而製夫大誥三編申明五常首以父
子之親
太宗文皇帝肅靖邦家推而製夫孝順事實首
===
以虞帝之克諧齊栗
宣宗章皇帝繼體守成推而製夫五倫一書首
以家人之父父子子大哉
三聖之制乎至哉
三聖之心乎是皆欲以一人之孝而為天下之
孝以一家之孝而為萬世之孝豈不與舜
武異世而同符哉且舜盡事親之道而瞽
瞍厎豫武王盡繼述之道而王業始成一
則備大德而尊富保饗之具全受天眷而
punctuated:
皇上之德教，盖與虞帝之大孝、武王之達孝同一揆矣。是豈後世所能及哉？請因明問而敷陳之。天經地義，莫尊乎親；降衷秉彝，莫先於孝。一自然而然，初非有所勉強而為者也。
肆我太祖高皇帝創業垂統，追帝其先，推而製夫《大誥》三編，申明五常，首以父子之親。太宗文皇帝肅靖邦家，推而製夫《孝順事實》，首以虞帝之克諧齊栗。宣宗章皇帝繼體守成，推而製夫《五倫》一書，首以家人之父父子子。大哉，三聖之制乎！至哉，三聖之心乎！是皆欲以一人之孝而為天下之孝，以一家之孝而為萬世之孝，豈不與舜、武異世而同符哉？
且舜盡事親之道，而瞽瞍厎豫；武王盡繼述之道，而王業始成。一則備大德，而尊富保饗之具全，受天眷而
translation_en:
…His Majesty’s moral instruction surely accords with the great filial piety of the Emperor of Yu and the universally acknowledged filial piety of King Wu. How could later ages have equaled this? Allow me to elaborate in response to your illuminating question. In the constant principles of Heaven and the proper order of Earth, none merits greater reverence than one’s parents; among the moral dispositions bestowed by Heaven and the enduring norms people uphold, none takes precedence over filial piety. This comes entirely of itself, never through forced effort.
Thus our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty and established its succession, posthumously conferring imperial status upon his ancestors. Extending this purpose, he composed the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao), expounding the five constant relationships and placing first the affection between father and son. Emperor Taizong Wen pacified the realm and, extending this purpose, composed True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi), beginning with the Emperor of Yu’s ability to bring harmony through reverence and circumspection [?]. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang inherited the throne and preserved the achievements of his predecessors. Extending this purpose, he composed the book Five Relationships (Wulun), beginning with fathers acting as fathers and sons as sons within the family. Great indeed were the works of these three sages! Perfect indeed were their intentions! They all wished to make the filial piety of one man the filial piety of all under Heaven, and the filial piety of one family the filial piety of all generations. Though they lived in different ages from Shun and King Wu, did they not accord with them exactly?
Moreover, Shun fulfilled the way of serving his parents, and Gusou was brought to contentment; King Wu fulfilled the way of carrying forward his predecessors’ purposes and undertakings, and the royal enterprise was at last accomplished. The one possessed great virtue in full, with every provision for honor and wealth, their preservation, and the enjoyment of sacrificial offerings; he received Heaven’s favor and…

His Majesty’s moral instruction surely accords with the same standard as the great filial piety of the Emperor of Yu and the universally recognized filial piety of King Wu. How could later ages equal this? Allow me to elaborate in response to your discerning question. In the constant principles of Heaven and the proper order of Earth, none deserve greater reverence than one’s parents; in the moral nature bestowed by Heaven and the enduring norms inherent in humanity, nothing takes precedence over filial piety. This arises entirely of itself: it is never something done through compulsion.

Thus our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty and established its succession, and posthumously conferred imperial status upon his ancestors. Extending this purpose, he composed the three compilations of the Great Pronouncements (Da Gao), elucidating the Five Constant Relationships and placing first the affection between father and son. Emperor Taizong Wen brought peace and order to the realm. Extending this purpose, he composed True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi), placing first the Emperor of Yu’s ability to bring his family into harmony through reverent vigilance. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang inherited the throne and preserved the achievements of his predecessors. Extending this purpose, he composed the Five Relationships (Wulun), placing first the principle that, within the family, fathers should act as fathers and sons as sons.

How great were the works of these three sages! How consummate were their intentions! All sought to make the filial piety of one person the filial piety of all under Heaven, and the filial piety of one family the filial piety of ten thousand generations. Though they lived in different ages from Shun and King Wu, did they not accord with them as perfectly as matching tallies?

Moreover, Shun fulfilled the way of serving his parents, and Gusou was brought to contentment; King Wu fulfilled the way of carrying forward his predecessors’ undertakings, and the royal enterprise was thereby accomplished. In the one case, he possessed great virtue and had the full means to enjoy and preserve honor and wealth; he received Heaven’s favor and …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
祿壽名位之兼得所以尊養乎親者備矣
一則追王先王而上祀乎先公制爲禮法
而遍及於天下所以尊崇乎親者隆矣夫
大舜武王虞周之大聖也以一誠而著大
孝達孝之稱以一孝而致雍熈太和之盛
聖德所極又何加焉自周而下若漢高祖
尊崇其父爲太公唐太宗尊崇其父爲太
上皇舉天下而奉一人尊養非不備也而
揆諸大舜之孝不同熈鴻號以示四海稱
===
號非不隆也而質諸武王之孝有間夫高
祖太宗漢唐之英主也儀文雖具初非躬
行心得之誠治效雖臻未免雜覇雜夷之
誚二君且然他何望焉恭惟
皇上繼
列聖之德踐
列聖之位盡愛敬而歡洽
兩宮崇
徽號而恩敷天下是以仁孝之著充塞乎兩間
punctuated:
祿壽名位之兼得，所以尊養乎親者備矣。一則追王先王，而上祀乎先公，制爲禮法，而遍及於天下，所以尊崇乎親者隆矣。夫大舜、武王，虞、周之大聖也，以一誠而著大孝、達孝之稱，以一孝而致雍熈太和之盛，聖德所極，又何加焉？自周而下，若漢高祖尊崇其父爲太公，唐太宗尊崇其父爲太上皇，舉天下而奉一人，尊養非不備也，而揆諸大舜之孝不同；熈鴻號以示四海，稱號非不隆也，而質諸武王之孝有間。夫高祖、太宗，漢、唐之英主也，儀文雖具，初非躬行心得之誠；治效雖臻，未免雜覇雜夷之誚。二君且然，他何望焉？

恭惟皇上繼列聖之德，踐列聖之位，盡愛敬而歡洽兩宮，崇徽號而恩敷天下，是以仁孝之著充塞乎兩間。
translation_en:
…with emoluments, longevity, renown, and rank all attained, everything needed to honor and nourish his parents was complete. The other posthumously conferred royal status upon the former kings and extended ancestral sacrifices back to the earlier lords, establishing ritual institutions that reached throughout the realm; thus the means of exalting his ancestors were magnificent. The great Shun and King Wu were the great sages of Yu and Zhou. Through undivided sincerity they earned their reputations for great filial piety and universally acknowledged filial piety; through filial piety alone they brought about flourishing concord and supreme harmony. What could be added to such consummate sagely virtue?

After the Zhou, rulers such as Gaozu of Han honored his father as Grand Sire, and Taizong of Tang honored his father as Retired Emperor. They devoted the resources of the entire realm to supporting one person: their provision of honor and sustenance was certainly complete, yet measured against the great Shun’s filial piety, it was not the same. They glorified lofty titles for all within the four seas to behold: these designations were certainly exalted, yet judged against King Wu’s filial piety, they fell short. Gaozu and Taizong were outstanding rulers of Han and Tang. Although their ceremonial forms were complete, these were never grounded in the sincerity of personal practice and inward understanding. Although their government achieved results, they could not escape the criticism that it mingled the ways of hegemons and barbarians. If even these two rulers were thus, what could one expect of others?

We reverently consider that Your Majesty has inherited the virtue of the successive sage emperors and ascended their throne. You express love and reverence to the fullest, bringing joy and harmony to the Two Palaces, and exalt their honorific titles, spreading beneficence throughout the realm. Thus the manifest brilliance of your benevolence and filial piety fills the space between Heaven and Earth…

translation_en:
…possessing emoluments, longevity, renown, and rank together, he had everything needed to honor and provide for his parents. The other posthumously conferred royal status upon the former kings and extended sacrifices back to the earlier lords, establishing these practices as ritual rules throughout the realm; thus the means of exalting his forebears were magnificent indeed. Although their ceremonial forms were complete, they lacked from the outset the sincerity that comes from personal practice and inward understanding. Although their government achieved results, they could not escape criticism for its admixture of hegemonic methods and non-Chinese customs. If even these two rulers were like this, what could one hope for from others?
We reverently reflect that Your Majesty has inherited the virtue of the successive sage emperors and ascended their throne. With the utmost love and reverence, you bring joy and harmony to the Two Palaces; by exalting their honorific titles, you spread your beneficence throughout the realm. Thus the manifest brilliance of your benevolence and filial piety fills the space between Heaven and Earth…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
德教之孚施及於四海匹夫匹婦必有息
風感神之異如阮卓劉平之輩卧氷泣笋
之祥如王祥孟宗之流者矣推而極之郊
焉而天神格廟焉而人鬼享以至九夷八
蠻之賓服鳥獸魚鼈之咸若何莫而非
皇上一心之誠之所致乎由是而觀
皇上之孝遠追虞周而無歉近法
祖宗而有光信足以為法於天下可傳於後世
漢唐諸君安能彷彿其萬一哉詩曰孝子
===
不匱永錫爾類傳曰至誠而不動者未之
有也謹拜首稽首以為
今日頌
第二問
宋澍
同考試官教諭謝 批大學一策正觀士子窮
經之學作者多掛一漏十條答詳明無踰此篇
同考試官學正陳 批善答所問必用心於本
領者
punctuated:
德教之孚，施及於四海。匹夫匹婦必有息風感神之異，如阮卓、劉平之輩；卧氷泣笋之祥，如王祥、孟宗之流者矣。推而極之，郊焉而天神格，廟焉而人鬼享，以至九夷八蠻之賓服、鳥獸魚鼈之咸若，何莫而非皇上一心之誠之所致乎？由是而觀，皇上之孝，遠追虞周而無歉，近法祖宗而有光，信足以為法於天下，可傳於後世。漢唐諸君安能彷彿其萬一哉？《詩》曰：「孝子不匱，永錫爾類。」《傳》曰：「至誠而不動者，未之有也。」謹拜首稽首，以為今日頌。
第二問
宋澍
同考試官教諭謝批：「大學一策，正觀士子窮經之學。作者多掛一漏十，條答詳明，無踰此篇。」
同考試官學正陳批：「善答所問，必用心於本領者。」
translation_en:
…the persuasive power of your moral teaching extends throughout the Four Seas. Among ordinary men and women there must surely be marvels of calming winds and moving spirits, such as those associated with Ruan Zhuo and Liu Ping, and auspicious wonders of lying upon ice and weeping for bamboo shoots, such as those associated with Wang Xiang and Meng Zong. Extending this to its fullest reach, the celestial spirits come to the suburban sacrifices, and the ancestral spirits receive the offerings in the ancestral temple. Even the submission of the Nine Yi and Eight Man peoples, and the harmonious flourishing of birds, beasts, fish, and turtles—what among these is not brought about by the sincerity of Your Majesty’s heart?
Viewed in this light, Your Majesty’s filial piety reaches back to match Yu and Zhou without falling short, and follows the more recent example of your imperial ancestors while adding to their glory. It can indeed serve as a model for all under Heaven and be handed down to later generations. How could the rulers of Han and Tang approximate even one ten-thousandth of it? The Book of Odes says: “The filial son is unfailing, forever bestowing blessings upon your kind.” The Commentary says: “There has never been one who possessed utmost sincerity yet failed to move others.” With reverent bows and my forehead to the ground, I offer this praise of the present day.
Second Question
Song Shu
Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: “This policy question on the Great Learning serves precisely to reveal the candidates’ learning in thoroughly investigating the Classics. Most writers mention one point while omitting ten. For detailed and clear answers to each point, no essay surpasses this one.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “He answers the questions well; he must be someone who has devoted his attention to the fundamentals.”

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曰致知格物是不探其端而驟語其次何
足以造道哉若夫釋明德而終帝典者所
以示淺深之序釋新民而先盤銘者所以
發新民之端切磋功易琢磨功難雖有學
問自脩之别而知行二者所當兼盡也聽
訟無異於人而自無訟可聽者盖聖人已
德既明而民德自新則得其本之明效也
程子有知至循理之論有談虎傷人之喻
此兩條者非言格物致知所當先而不可
===
後之意乎曰立誠意以格之曰入道莫如
敬曰涵養須用敬曰致知在所養又曰收
其心而不放此五條者非言涵養本原之
功以為格致之本乎道有善惡也非開其
知識之真則不能致其好惡之實故誠意
者必先致知焉心有體用也然一有自欺
之萌則不得其本然之正故正心者必先
誠意焉意誠而不能操存則身在於此而
心馳於彼故心有不在也心正而不能加
punctuated: 曰「致知格物」，是不探其端而驟語其次，何足以造道哉？若夫釋明德而終帝典者，所以示淺深之序；釋新民而先盤銘者，所以發新民之端。切磋功易，琢磨功難，雖有學問自脩之别，而知行二者所當兼盡也。聽訟無異於人，而自無訟可聽者，盖聖人已德既明，而民德自新，則得其本之明效也。程子有知至循理之論，有談虎傷人之喻，此兩條者，非言格物致知所當先而不可後之意乎？曰「立誠意以格之」，曰「入道莫如敬」，曰「涵養須用敬」，曰「致知在所養」，又曰「收其心而不放」，此五條者，非言涵養本原之功，以為格致之本乎？道有善惡也，非開其知識之真，則不能致其好惡之實，故誠意者必先致知焉。心有體用也，然一有自欺之萌，則不得其本然之正，故正心者必先誠意焉。意誠而不能操存，則身在於此而心馳於彼，故心有不在也。心正而不能加
translation_en:
…to speak of “extending knowledge and investigating things” in this way is to discuss the subsequent steps hastily without examining their starting point. How could this suffice to attain the Way? As for the explanation of illuminating bright virtue ending with the Canon of the Emperors, this shows the progression from the shallow to the profound; the explanation of renewing the people beginning with the inscription on the washbasin reveals the starting point of renewing the people. The work of cutting and filing is easy; that of chiseling and polishing is difficult. Although these distinguish learning and inquiry from self-cultivation, knowledge and action must both be pursued to the fullest. In hearing lawsuits, the sage is no different from others, yet naturally there are no lawsuits for him to hear. This is because, once the sage’s own virtue [?] has been illuminated, the people’s virtue renews itself: this is the manifest effect of grasping the root.

Master Cheng discusses knowledge reaching its utmost and following principle, and offers the analogy of speaking of a tiger injuring someone. Do these two passages not mean that investigating things and extending knowledge must come first and cannot be postponed? He says, “Establish sincerity of intention in order to investigate it”; “For entering the Way, nothing equals reverent attentiveness”; “Nurturing oneself requires reverent attentiveness”; “Extending knowledge depends on what one nurtures”; and also, “Gather in the mind and do not let it stray.” Do these five passages not speak of nurturing the fundamental source as the foundation for investigating things and extending knowledge?

The Way contains good and evil [?]. Unless one develops true understanding, one cannot bring one’s liking and disliking to genuine fulfillment. Thus, to make one’s intentions sincere, one must first extend one’s knowledge. The mind has both substance and function. Yet once even the germ of self-deception arises, it cannot retain its original rectitude. Thus, to rectify the mind, one must first make one’s intentions sincere. If one’s intentions are sincere but one cannot hold fast to and preserve the mind, the body will be here while the mind races elsewhere; hence the mind may be absent. If the mind is rectified but one cannot further apply…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭趙批縷析無遺可取
考試官教諭朱批末以敬字為指歸最佳
不有諸儒之說則大學之旨無以明於世
不究諸儒之意則大學之理無以得於心
此讀大學者所以必欲約其旨於章句而
詳其義於或問則充然有得而於脩己治
人之道無遺矣請申言之夫大學一書乃
垂世立教之大典進德脩業之本根學者
固不可以不講也聖經賢傳作於前朱子
===
章句明於後有所謂三綱領者焉有所謂
八條目者焉綱舉目張條分縷析固無容
議矣然或問一書又朱子集諸儒之說發
明章句未盡之意也聖遠言湮知之者能
有幾哉是故明德新民止至善三者不可
偏廢也如管仲不務明其明德佛老不屑
乎新民而王通不求止於至善果足以知
道乎格致誠正脩齊治平八者自有次第
也如韓子原道其言極於正心誠意而無
punctuated:
考試官教諭趙批：縷析無遺，可取。
考試官教諭朱批：末以敬字為指歸，最佳。
不有諸儒之說，則《大學》之旨無以明於世；不究諸儒之意，則《大學》之理無以得於心。此讀《大學》者所以必欲約其旨於《章句》，而詳其義於《或問》，則充然有得，而於脩己治人之道無遺矣。請申言之。夫《大學》一書，乃垂世立教之大典，進德脩業之本根，學者固不可以不講也。聖經賢傳作於前，朱子《章句》明於後，有所謂三綱領者焉，有所謂八條目者焉。綱舉目張，條分縷析，固無容議矣。然《或問》一書，又朱子集諸儒之說，發明《章句》未盡之意也。聖遠言湮，知之者能有幾哉？是故明德、新民、止至善，三者不可偏廢也。如管仲不務明其明德，佛老不屑乎新民，而王通不求止於至善，果足以知道乎？格、致、誠、正、脩、齊、治、平，八者自有次第也。如韓子《原道》，其言極於正心誠意，而無
translation_en:
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “A detailed analysis that leaves nothing out; worthy of acceptance.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “The conclusion takes reverent attentiveness as its guiding principle: excellent.”
Without the explanations of the Confucian scholars, the purport of the Great Learning could not be made clear to the world; without investigating their intentions, its principles could not be grasped in one's heart. Thus readers of the Great Learning must seek a concise account of its purport in the Commentary in Chapters and Sentences and a detailed explanation of its meaning in the Questions and Answers. They will then attain a full understanding, leaving nothing out of the Way of cultivating oneself and governing others. Allow me to elaborate.
The Great Learning is a great canonical work that establishes instruction for succeeding ages, and the foundation for advancing in virtue and cultivating one's undertakings. Students certainly cannot neglect its study. The sage's classic and the worthy's commentary were composed first; Master Zhu's Commentary in Chapters and Sentences subsequently elucidated them. There are what are called the Three Guiding Principles and what are called the Eight Steps. The guiding principles are raised and their particulars laid out, each item distinguished and each strand analyzed: there is surely no room for dispute. Yet in the Questions and Answers, Master Zhu also gathered the explanations of the Confucian scholars to illuminate meanings not fully treated in the Commentary in Chapters and Sentences. The sages are remote, and their words have fallen into obscurity: how many can understand them?
Thus the three principles—illuminating luminous virtue, renewing the people, and resting in the highest good—must not be selectively neglected. Guan Zhong did not devote himself to illuminating his luminous virtue; the Buddhists and Daoists disdained renewing the people; and Wang Tong did not seek to rest in the highest good. Could they truly be considered to understand the Way? The eight steps—investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, rectifying the heart, cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world—have their own proper sequence. For example, Master Han's Inquiry into the Way carries its discussion as far as rectifying the heart and making intentions sincere, but lacks…

不有諸儒之說，則大學之旨無以明於世；不究諸儒之意，則大學之理無以得於心。此讀大學者所以必欲約其旨於章句，而詳其義於或問，則充然有得，而於脩己治人之道無遺矣。請申言之。夫大學一書，乃垂世立教之大典，進德脩業之本根，學者固不可以不講也。聖經賢傳作於前，朱子章句明於後，有所謂三綱領者焉，有所謂八條目者焉。綱舉目張，條分縷析，固無容議矣。然或問一書，又朱子集諸儒之說，發明章句未盡之意也。聖遠言湮，知之者能有幾哉？是故明德、新民、止至善三者，不可偏廢也。如管仲不務明其明德，佛老不屑乎新民，而王通不求止於至善，果足以知道乎？格致誠正脩齊治平八者，自有次第也。如韓子原道，其言極於正心誠意，而無
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhao, an Instructor: “The analysis is meticulous and leaves nothing out; it merits acceptance.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, an Instructor: “The conclusion takes ‘reverent attentiveness’ as its guiding principle: excellent.”

Without the explanations of the Confucian scholars, the purport of the Great Learning could not be made clear to the world; without investigating their meaning, the principles of the Great Learning could not be grasped in the mind. This is why readers of the Great Learning must seek a concise account of its purport in the Commentary in Chapters and Sentences and a detailed explanation of its meaning in the Questions and Answers. They will then attain a full understanding, leaving nothing out of the Way of cultivating oneself and governing others. Allow me to elaborate.

The Great Learning is a great canon that establishes teachings to be handed down through the ages, and the foundation for advancing in virtue and cultivating one's undertakings. Students certainly cannot dispense with studying it. The classic of the sage and the commentary of the worthy were composed earlier; Master Zhu's Commentary in Chapters and Sentences elucidated them later. There are what are called the three guiding principles and what are called the eight steps. The guiding principles are raised and their particulars unfolded, each item distinguished and each thread analyzed: there is assuredly no room for objection. Yet the Questions and Answers is also a work in which Master Zhu collected the explanations of the Confucian scholars to elucidate meanings not fully explored in the Commentary in Chapters and Sentences. The sages are distant in time and their words obscured: how many can understand them?

Thus none of the three—illuminating luminous virtue, renewing the people, and resting in the highest good—may be neglected. Guan Zhong did not devote himself to illuminating his luminous virtue; the Buddhists and Daoists disdained renewing the people; and Wang Tong did not seek to rest in the highest good. Could they truly be considered to understand the Way? The eight steps—investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world—have their own proper sequence. For example, in Master Han's Inquiry into the Way, his discussion goes as far as rectifying the mind and making intentions sincere, yet lacks …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
察則好惡必陷於一偏故身有不脩也抑
豈特此哉仁讓之化積於一家貪戾之禍
起於一人即善必積而後成惡雖小而可
懼之戒也桃夭蓼蕭之言家人兄弟曹風
鳲鳩之言正是四國亦刑于寡妻至于兄
弟以御于家邦之意也孝弟慈固所以脩
身齊家而治國者也釋平天下復以為言
者蓋以三者人道之大端眾心之所同而
不能已耳何嫌於重覆哉自身而家而國
===
而天下均為推己及人之事也傳所以釋
之一事自為一說者亦以勢之遠邇事之
先後而所施有不同耳何名為異說哉至
於好惡以人而不以己義利以公而不以
私此絜矩二字平天下之要道也陸宣公
邦本民心之論呂晦叔小人聚斂之語非
得此章之旨而何小學以敬養其本原大
學以敬收其成功是敬之一字聖學之所
以成始而成終者也程子主一無適之言
punctuated: 察，則好惡必陷於一偏，故身有不脩也。抑豈特此哉？仁讓之化積於一家，貪戾之禍起於一人，即善必積而後成、惡雖小而可懼之戒也。《桃夭》《蓼蕭》之言家人兄弟，《曹風》《鳲鳩》之言正是四國，亦「刑于寡妻，至于兄弟，以御于家邦」之意也。孝弟慈，固所以脩身齊家而治國者也。釋平天下復以為言者，蓋以三者人道之大端，眾心之所同而不能已耳，何嫌於重覆哉？自身而家而國而天下，均為推己及人之事也。傳所以釋之一事自為一說者，亦以勢之遠邇、事之先後，而所施有不同耳，何名為異說哉？至於好惡以人而不以己，義利以公而不以私，此絜矩二字平天下之要道也。陸宣公邦本民心之論、呂晦叔小人聚斂之語，非得此章之旨而何？小學以敬養其本原，大學以敬收其成功，是敬之一字，聖學之所以成始而成終者也。程子主一無適之言
translation_en: …scrutiny, then likes and dislikes inevitably become one-sided, and thus the person remains uncultivated. Yet is this all? The transforming influence of benevolence and deference builds up within a single household, while the calamity of greed and perversity begins with a single person. This is precisely the warning that goodness must accumulate before it reaches fulfillment, whereas evil, however small, is to be feared. The references to family members and brothers in Peach Tree Tender and Tall Southernwood [?], and to “rectifying these four states” in The Cuckoo of the Airs of Cao, likewise convey the meaning of “setting an example for his wife, extending it to his brothers, and thereby governing his household and state.” Filial devotion, fraternal respect, and parental kindness are indeed the means of cultivating oneself, ordering the family, and governing the state. The explanation of bringing peace to all under Heaven mentions them again because these three are fundamental principles of human relationships, shared by all hearts and impossible to suppress. Why object to the repetition? From oneself to the family, to the state, and to all under Heaven, each involves extending to others what one understands through oneself. The commentary explains each matter separately merely because circumstances differ in their reach and affairs in their sequence, so that their application differs. Why call these divergent explanations? As for taking others rather than oneself as the basis for likes and dislikes, and taking the public rather than private interest as the basis for judging righteousness and profit: this is what the two characters jie ju, “measuring with the square,” mean—the essential way to bring peace to all under Heaven. Do not Lu Xuangong’s discussion of the people’s hearts as the foundation of the state and Lü Huishu’s remarks on petty men’s accumulation of wealth grasp the purport of this chapter? Elementary learning nourishes the roots through reverent attentiveness; advanced learning brings its achievement to completion through reverent attentiveness. Thus this single word, reverence, is how the learning of the sages fulfills both its beginning and its end. Master Cheng’s statement about concentrating on one thing without straying elsewhere…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
謝氏所謂惺惺法尹氏所謂收斂心身者
非知用力之方而何是則諸儒之說不一
也而推原聖賢之意則一或問之論有異
也而發明章句之義無異讀大學者舍此
不究而欲得於心難矣哉雖然大學之書
或問固所當知或問之中一敬尤所當重
盖敬者一心之主宰而萬事之本輿也能
敬則放心以收大本以立而是書之綱領
條目一以貫之而無疑矣愚生造詣未精
===
謬述以對惟執事進而教之
第三問
蔣曙
考試官教諭趙 批歷陳前代暨我
朝建儲之制甚悉且終篇之獻尤見忠懇佳士也
考試官教諭朱 批儲貳一策随問随答
得此於風簷寸晷之下亦難矣
儲君之繫於國也大矣而輔養之道當慎
于厥初焉盖養之不以其正則無以成儲
punctuated:
謝氏所謂惺惺法，尹氏所謂收斂心身者，非知用力之方而何？是則諸儒之說不一也，而推原聖賢之意則一；或問之論有異也，而發明章句之義無異。讀大學者，舍此不究而欲得於心，難矣哉！雖然，大學之書，或問固所當知；或問之中，一敬尤所當重。盖敬者，一心之主宰，而萬事之本輿也。能敬，則放心以收，大本以立，而是書之綱領條目，一以貫之而無疑矣。愚生造詣未精，謬述以對，惟執事進而教之。
第三問
蔣曙
考試官教諭趙批：歷陳前代暨我朝建儲之制甚悉，且終篇之獻尤見忠懇，佳士也。
考試官教諭朱批：儲貳一策，随問随答，得此於風簷寸晷之下，亦難矣。
儲君之繫於國也大矣，而輔養之道當慎于厥初焉。盖養之不以其正，則無以成儲
translation_en:
…what Master Xie called the method of maintaining alert awareness, and what Master Yin called gathering in the mind and person—do these not show knowledge of how to apply oneself? Thus, although the explanations of the various scholars differ, they are one in tracing the intentions of the sages and worthies to their source. Although the discussions in Questions and Answers differ, they do not differ in elucidating the meaning of the Chapters and Sentences. How difficult it would be for a reader of the Great Learning to neglect this inquiry yet seek to grasp its meaning in the heart! Nevertheless, in studying the Great Learning, one certainly ought to understand Questions and Answers; within Questions and Answers, the single principle of reverent attentiveness deserves particular emphasis. For reverent attentiveness governs the whole mind and is the foundation and support [?] of all affairs. If one can maintain it, the straying mind will be gathered in and the great foundation established; the guiding principles and detailed provisions of this book will then be threaded together by a single principle, leaving no doubt. My attainments, as an unworthy student, are not yet refined. I presumptuously set forth this reply, hoping that you will advance my understanding through your instruction.
Third Question
Jiang Shu
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: His detailed account of the institutions for establishing the heir apparent under former dynasties and our own is most thorough. Moreover, the proposals at the end of the essay particularly reveal his loyalty and sincerity. He is a fine scholar.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: This policy essay on the heir apparent answers each question in turn. To achieve this beneath the windswept eaves, within the brief time allotted, is indeed difficult.
The heir apparent is of great consequence to the state, and the means of guiding and nurturing him must be carefully considered from the very beginning. For if he is not nurtured in accordance with what is right, there will be no means of forming an heir apparent…

…What Master Xie called the method of keeping alert, and Master Yin called gathering in the mind and person—what are these if not an understanding of how to apply oneself? Thus, although the explanations of the various scholars differ, they agree in tracing the intentions of the sages and worthies to their source. Jiang Shu
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “He sets out in considerable detail the institutions for establishing an heir apparent under former dynasties and our own. Moreover, the proposals at the end particularly reveal his loyalty and earnestness. He is a worthy scholar.”

The heir apparent is of great consequence to the state [?], and the means of guiding and nurturing him must be attended to carefully from the very outset. For if he is not nurtured in what is correct, there will be no means of perfecting the heir apparent’s…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
君之善輔之不以其人則無以弘蒙養之
功養以正學輔以正人則德業有成而一
代之重器有所托矣此自古之明王曁我
朝之
列聖建儲之制謹始之道所以盡善盡美而為
有道之長也豈漢唐而下所可論哉請敷
陳之儲嗣天下之本也天命人心属焉宗
廟社稷係焉前有祖宗垂創之艱後有子
孫長久之計而教養輔翼之道誠不可不
===
早為之地也古者元子始生接以太宰而
嫡長之分已致隆於相接之儀負以卜士
而保受之禮不少忽於斯須之頃樂以修
內禮以修外而孩提有其教尊以師保弼
以丞疑而輔導有其人此固三王重儲嗣
之大畧也是故問安內豎文王盡世子禮
於王季也雖愛敬之心出於天性而涵養
薰陶之功焉可誣耶抗法伯禽周公示世
子法於成王也雖迂其身以善其君而左
punctuated:
君之善；輔之不以其人，則無以弘蒙養之功。養以正學，輔以正人，則德業有成，而一代之重器有所托矣。此自古之明王曁我朝之列聖建儲之制、謹始之道，所以盡善盡美而為有道之長也。豈漢唐而下所可論哉？請敷陳之。
儲嗣，天下之本也。天命人心属焉，宗廟社稷係焉。前有祖宗垂創之艱，後有子孫長久之計，而教養輔翼之道，誠不可不早為之地也。古者元子始生，接以太宰，而嫡長之分已致隆於相接之儀；負以卜士，而保受之禮不少忽於斯須之頃。樂以修內，禮以修外，而孩提有其教；尊以師保，弼以丞疑，而輔導有其人。此固三王重儲嗣之大畧也。是故問安內豎，文王盡世子禮於王季也。雖愛敬之心出於天性，而涵養薰陶之功焉可誣耶？抗法伯禽，周公示世子法於成王也。雖迂其身以善其君，而左
translation_en:
…the heir apparent’s goodness; if those who assist him are not the right people, there is no means of advancing the work of nurturing him in his formative years. Nurture him through correct learning and assist him with upright men, and his virtue and accomplishments will mature, giving the weighty charge of a dynasty someone to whom it can be entrusted. This is why the institutions for establishing an heir and the practice of taking care at the outset, observed by the enlightened kings of antiquity and the successive sage sovereigns of our dynasty, are perfect in every respect and foremost among those of rulers who possess the Way. How could the practices of the Han, Tang, and subsequent dynasties compare? Allow me to set this forth.
The heir is the foundation of all under Heaven. Heaven’s mandate and the people’s hearts converge upon him; the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain depend upon him. Behind him lie his ancestors’ arduous labors in founding the dynasty and handing it down; ahead lie plans for the enduring welfare of his descendants. Provision for his instruction, nurture, and assistance must therefore truly be made early. In antiquity, when the principal son was first born, the Grand Steward received him: the distinction accorded the eldest legitimate son was thus already exalted in the ceremony of reception. A divination officer [?] carried him, and the rites of safeguarding and receiving him were not neglected even for a moment. Music cultivated his inner character, and ritual cultivated his outward conduct, so that instruction began in infancy. Preceptors and guardians were accorded honor, and assistants and advisers supported him, so that suitable men provided his guidance. Such, in broad outline, was the importance the Three Kings attached to the heir. Thus, in asking the palace page about his father’s well-being, King Wen fulfilled toward Wang Ji the ritual duties of an heir. Although his affection and reverence arose from his innate nature, how could the contribution of nurture and formative instruction be denied? By enforcing the rules upon Bo Qin, the Duke of Zhou demonstrated to King Cheng the standards governing an heir. Although he took this indirect course to make his ruler good, yet those on his left …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
君之善輔之不以其人則無以弘蒙養之
功養以正學輔以正人則德業有成而一
代之重器有所托矣此自古之明王曁我
朝之
列聖建儲之制謹始之道所以盡善盡美而為
有道之長也豈漢唐而下所可論哉請敷
陳之儲嗣天下之本也天命人心属焉宗
廟社稷係焉前有祖宗垂創之艱後有子
孫長久之計而教養輔翼之道誠不可不
早為之地也古者元子始生接以太宰而
嫡長之分已致隆於相接之儀負以卜士
而保受之禮不少忽於斯須之頃樂以修
內禮以修外而孩提有其教尊以師保弼
以丞疑而輔導有其人此固三王重儲嗣
之大畧也是故問安內豎文王盡世子禮
於王季也雖愛敬之心出於天性而涵養
薰陶之功焉可誣耶抗法伯禽周公示世
子法於成王也雖迂其身以善其君而左
punctuated:
君之善，輔之不以其人，則無以弘蒙養之功。養以正學，輔以正人，則德業有成，而一代之重器有所托矣。此自古之明王曁我朝之列聖建儲之制、謹始之道，所以盡善盡美而為有道之長也。豈漢唐而下所可論哉？請敷陳之。
儲嗣，天下之本也。天命人心属焉，宗廟社稷係焉。前有祖宗垂創之艱，後有子孫長久之計，而教養輔翼之道，誠不可不早為之地也。古者，元子始生，接以太宰，而嫡長之分已致隆於相接之儀；負以卜士，而保受之禮不少忽於斯須之頃。樂以修內，禮以修外，而孩提有其教；尊以師保，弼以丞疑，而輔導有其人。此固三王重儲嗣之大畧也。是故問安內豎，文王盡世子禮於王季也。雖愛敬之心出於天性，而涵養薰陶之功焉可誣耶？抗法伯禽，周公示世子法於成王也。雖迂其身以善其君，而左
translation_en:
…the ruler’s goodness. If those appointed to assist him are unsuitable, there is no means of extending the work of nurturing him in childhood. Nurtured through correct learning and assisted by upright men, he will attain virtue and accomplishment, and the weighty charge of a dynasty will have someone to whom it can be entrusted. This is why the institutions for establishing an heir and the principle of taking care at the outset, observed by enlightened kings since antiquity and by the successive sage emperors of our dynasty, have achieved perfection in every respect and stand foremost among those of rulers who possess the Way. How could the Han, Tang, and subsequent dynasties be spoken of in the same terms? Allow me to explain at length.
The heir apparent is the foundation of all under Heaven. Heaven’s mandate and the people’s hearts rest upon him; the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain depend upon him. Behind him lie the hardships of the ancestors in founding and handing down the dynasty; ahead lie plans for the enduring future of their descendants. Preparations for his instruction, nurture, guidance, and support must therefore be made early. In antiquity, when the principal son was first born, the Grand Steward received him: the distinction accorded the eldest legitimate son was thus already exalted in the ceremony of reception. An officer selected by divination carried him: the rites for his protection and reception were not neglected even for an instant. Music cultivated his inner character, and ritual cultivated his outward conduct, so that he received instruction from infancy. Masters and guardians were honored, and assistants and advisers provided support, so that suitable people were available to guide him. These were indeed the broad principles by which the kings of the Three Dynasties attached importance to the heir apparent.
Thus, in asking the palace attendant about his father’s well-being, King Wen fully observed toward Wang Ji the ritual duties of an heir apparent. Although his love and reverence arose from his natural disposition, how could the contribution of sustained nurture and formative influence be denied? In holding Bo Qin to the prescribed standards, the Duke of Zhou demonstrated to King Cheng the rules governing an heir apparent. Although he took an indirect course through his own son to make his ruler good, yet in assisting …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
數君者儲貳之學非無所養也而擇術或
非其正儲貳之側非無所輔也而遴選或
非其人僚寀具員而無保傅之嚴講讀備
禮而無箴規之益肆君德所成或駮或純
治道所臻有得有失揆諸三代何可同日
而語哉仰惟我
朝
聖祖創業於前
列聖守成於後紀綱法度超越千古而於儲貳
===
之制尤惓惓焉
宫坊官屬選自儒林朝夕勸講本諸經術其
所以成就德器而正天下之本者盖有在
矣故百有餘年
聖德神功彌漫宇宙閎休偉烈照耀後先盖上
與三代明王媲休並美而陋歷代於下風
矣揆厥所自何莫而非蒙養中來耶矧我
皇上恭膺天眷甫建
青宫四海人心咸有攸屬自貽哲命兹其始
punctuated:
數君者，儲貳之學非無所養也，而擇術或非其正；儲貳之側非無所輔也，而遴選或非其人。僚寀具員，而無保傅之嚴；講讀備禮，而無箴規之益。肆君德所成或駮或純，治道所臻有得有失。揆諸三代，何可同日而語哉！
仰惟我朝，聖祖創業於前，列聖守成於後，紀綱法度超越千古，而於儲貳之制尤惓惓焉。宫坊官屬選自儒林，朝夕勸講本諸經術。其所以成就德器而正天下之本者，盖有在矣。故百有餘年，聖德神功彌漫宇宙，閎休偉烈照耀後先。盖上與三代明王媲休並美，而陋歷代於下風矣。揆厥所自，何莫而非蒙養中來耶？矧我皇上恭膺天眷，甫建青宫，四海人心咸有攸屬。自貽哲命，兹其始
translation_en:
…As for these several rulers, their education as heirs apparent did not lack cultivation, yet the methods chosen were sometimes improper; they did not lack assistance at their side as heirs apparent, yet those selected were sometimes unsuitable. The subordinate posts were fully staffed, but lacked the strictness of guardians and preceptors; lectures and readings observed all the formalities, but lacked the benefit of admonition and correction. Thus the ruler’s virtue, as formed, was sometimes mixed and sometimes pure, and the practice of government brought both successes and failures. Measured against the Three Dynasties, how could they be spoken of in the same breath?
We reverently reflect that, in our dynasty, the sagely founder established the enterprise, and the succeeding sage sovereigns preserved it. Its governing principles, laws, and institutions surpass those of all antiquity, and particular care has been devoted to the institutions concerning the heir apparent. Officials of the heir apparent’s household and secretariats are selected from the ranks of Confucian scholars; their morning and evening instruction rests on classical learning. There is thus a firm basis for bringing his virtue and capacity to maturity and rectifying the foundation of All under Heaven. Consequently, for more than a hundred years, sagely virtue and divine achievements have filled the universe, while vast blessings and mighty deeds have shone across successive generations. Looking back, these rival the glory and excellence of the enlightened kings of the Three Dynasties, leaving the intervening dynasties inferior by comparison. When we consider their source, what among them did not arise from nurture in childhood? Moreover, our present emperor, reverently receiving Heaven’s favor, has just established the heir apparent, and the hearts of all within the Four Seas now have someone upon whom to set their hopes. Securing for himself the mandate to rule wisely begins here…

text:

非其正儲貳之側非無所輔也而遴選或

translation_en:
As for those several rulers, their education as heirs apparent was not without cultivation, but the methods chosen were sometimes improper. They were not without assistance at their side as heirs apparent, but those selected were sometimes unsuitable. The full complement of officials was in place, yet lacked the rigor of protectors and preceptors; lectures and readings observed all the formalities, yet afforded none of the benefit of admonition and correction. Consequently, the imperial virtue thus formed was sometimes mixed and sometimes pure, and the governance achieved had both successes and failures. Measured against the Three Dynasties, how could they be spoken of in the same breath?
Reverently considering our dynasty, the sagely founding ancestor established its enterprise, and the succession of sage sovereigns thereafter preserved it. Its institutions, laws, and standards surpass those of all past ages, and particular care has been devoted to the arrangements for the heir apparent. Officials of the Eastern Palace and its administrative offices are selected from the ranks of Confucian scholars; their daily instruction and lectures are grounded in classical learning. Here, indeed, lies the means of perfecting the heir’s virtue and capacity and rectifying the foundation of the realm. Thus, for more than a hundred years, sagely virtue and divine accomplishments have filled the universe, and magnificent blessings and mighty achievements have shone across successive generations. They rival the glory and excellence of the enlightened kings of the Three Dynasties, leaving the intervening dynasties inferior by comparison. When we examine their source, what among these achievements did not arise from cultivation in childhood? Moreover, our emperor, reverently receiving Heaven’s favor, has just established the heir apparent, and the hearts of all within the Four Seas now have someone upon whom to rest their hopes. This marks the beginning of securing for himself the mandate of a wise ruler…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
矣則夫教養輔翼以衍億萬斯年之休者
端有望焉詩曰貽厥孫謀以燕翼子愚敢
以為
列聖頌書曰監于先王成憲其永無愆又敢以
為
今日獻
第四問
徐惟
同考試官教諭林批此策答者率多臆說
令人厭觀求如是篇之詳明斷制者可羨
考試官教諭趙批不拘問目不遺事實
方見作手
考試官教諭朱批足見該博之學
讀人求多聞之言則知學固貴於能博讀
誦詩三百之章則知學尤貴於能用盖能
博則有以為立政之本是其體也能用則
有以收所學之功是其用也有用而無體
固不足於政有體而無用亦何取於學哉
punctuated:
矣。則夫教養輔翼，以衍億萬斯年之休者，端有望焉。《詩》曰：「貽厥孫謀，以燕翼子。」愚敢以為列聖頌。《書》曰：「監于先王成憲，其永無愆。」又敢以為今日獻。
第四問
徐惟
同考試官教諭林批：此策答者率多臆說，令人厭觀。求如是篇之詳明斷制者，可羨。
考試官教諭趙批：不拘問目，不遺事實，方見作手。
考試官教諭朱批：足見該博之學。
讀「人求多聞」之言，則知學固貴於能博；讀「誦詩三百」之章，則知學尤貴於能用。盖能博，則有以為立政之本，是其體也；能用，則有以收所學之功，是其用也。有用而無體，固不足於政；有體而無用，亦何取於學哉？
translation_en:
… Thus there is indeed reason to hope that instruction, nurture, assistance, and guidance will extend these blessings for countless ages. The Book of Odes says: “Bequeath plans to his descendants, thereby bringing peace and support to his children.” I humbly venture to offer these words in praise of the successive sage emperors. The Book of Documents says: “Look to the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be free of error.” These words I also venture to offer to the present sovereign.
Fourth Policy Question
Xu Wei
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, School Instructor: Most who answered this policy question offered conjectural assertions that weary the reader. An essay as detailed, clear, and decisive in its judgments as this is admirable.
Comment by Examiner Zhao, School Instructor: Neither confined by the question’s individual points nor omitting the facts: here we truly see an accomplished writer.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, School Instructor: This amply demonstrates extensive learning.
Reading the words “people seek broad learning” [?], one understands that learning certainly prizes breadth; reading the passage “reciting the three hundred Odes,” one understands that learning prizes practical application still more. Breadth provides a foundation for establishing government: this is its substance. Practical application enables one to realize the fruits of what one has learned: this is its function. Function without substance is certainly inadequate for government; but with substance and no function, what value would learning have?

為
今日獻
第四問
徐淮
同考試官教諭林批此策答者率多臆說
===
令人厭觀求如是篇之詳明斷制者可羡
考試官教諭趙批不拘問目不遺事實
方見作手

第四問
徐淮

同考試官教諭林批：「此策答者率多臆說，令人厭觀。求如是篇之詳明斷制者，可羡。」

考試官教諭趙批：「不拘問目，不遺事實，方見作手。」

考試官教諭朱批：「足見該博之學。」

讀「人求多聞」之言，則知學固貴於能博；讀「誦詩三百」之章，則知學尤貴於能用。盖能博，則有以為立政之本，是其體也；能用，則有以收所學之功，是其用也。有用而無體，固不足於政；有體而無用，亦何取於學哉？
translation_en:
…Then there is indeed reason to hope that instruction, nurture, assistance, and support will extend these blessings for countless millions of years. The Book of Odes says: “He bequeathed plans to his descendants, thereby bringing peace and aid to his sons.” I venture, in my humble judgment, to offer this as praise of the successive sage emperors. The Book of Documents says: “Look to the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be without error.” I venture also to offer this to Your Majesty today.

Fourth Question
Xu Huai

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Most who answered this policy question indulged in conjecture, making their essays tiresome to read. An essay as detailed, clear, and decisive in its judgments as this is worthy of admiration.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Neither confined by the question’s particulars nor omitting the facts: here we see a skilled writer.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “This amply demonstrates broad and comprehensive learning.”

Reading the words ‘people seek to hear much’ [?], we recognize that learning certainly prizes breadth; reading the passage beginning ‘Recite the three hundred odes,’ we recognize that learning prizes still more the ability to put it to use. Breadth of learning provides a foundation for establishing government: this is its substance. The ability to apply it brings the benefits of what one has learned to fruition: this is its function. Function without substance is certainly inadequate for government; but with substance and no function, what value would learning have?

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
竊嘗考之書曰學古入官易曰君子多識
前言往行以畜其德則學不可以不博明
矣所以然者盖將舉此而措之於用耳若
伊尹誦詩讀書佐商以肇一代之基姬旦
多才多藝相周而垂百王之法學行兼該
體用具備卓乎不可尚已下此不能無優
劣之可論者焉姑以漢唐宋言之洛陽少
年論過伊管賈誼其才矣而治安一策實
救文帝之弊道明三代學際天人董仲舒
===
其儒矣而賢良三策切中武帝之心智於
子房而文則過辯如賈誼而術不疎陸敬
輿也而忠義足以弭奉天之難當時稱為
內相文起八代之衰道濟天下之溺韓昌
黎也而精誠足以馴鱷魚之暴潮陽號為
易治歐陽脩有名冠天下之文章而嘉祐
相業以救時行道為責司馬光有無所不
通之文學而元祐政治著旋乾轉坤之功
之數人者體既具矣用亦周焉譬之入陶
punctuated: 竊嘗考之，《書》曰：「學古入官。」《易》曰：「君子多識前言往行，以畜其德。」則學不可以不博明矣。所以然者，盖將舉此而措之於用耳。若伊尹誦詩讀書，佐商以肇一代之基；姬旦多才多藝，相周而垂百王之法：學行兼該，體用具備，卓乎不可尚已。下此不能無優劣之可論者焉。姑以漢唐宋言之，洛陽少年，論過伊管，賈誼其才矣，而治安一策，實救文帝之弊；道明三代，學際天人，董仲舒其儒矣，而賢良三策，切中武帝之心；智於子房而文則過，辯如賈誼而術不疎，陸敬輿也，而忠義足以弭奉天之難，當時稱為內相；文起八代之衰，道濟天下之溺，韓昌黎也，而精誠足以馴鱷魚之暴，潮陽號為易治；歐陽脩有名冠天下之文章，而嘉祐相業，以救時行道為責；司馬光有無所不通之文學，而元祐政治，著旋乾轉坤之功。之數人者，體既具矣，用亦周焉。譬之入陶
translation_en:
I have ventured to examine this. The Book of Documents says: “Study antiquity and enter office.” The Book of Changes says: “The gentleman acquaints himself widely with the words and deeds of the past, thereby nurturing his virtue.” It is thus clear that learning must be broad. The reason is simply that one intends to put this learning into practice. Yi Yin recited the Odes and read the Documents, assisting the Shang in laying the foundations of a dynasty. Ji Dan possessed many talents and accomplishments, assisting the Zhou and transmitting models for a hundred kings. Both embraced learning and conduct alike, fully possessing both substance and practical application. Their excellence could not be surpassed. Among those below them, however, relative merits necessarily remain open to discussion.

Let us speak provisionally of the Han, Tang, and Song. The young man of Luoyang, whose arguments surpassed those of Yi Yin and Guan Zhong, was the talented Jia Yi; his policy essay on good government and security truly addressed the failings of Emperor Wen’s rule. The scholar whose Way illuminated the Three Dynasties and whose learning reached between Heaven and humanity was Dong Zhongshu; his three policy responses in the examination for the worthy and good spoke directly to Emperor Wu’s concerns. Lu Jingyu possessed wisdom surpassing Zifang’s and excelled him in literary accomplishment; he was as eloquent as Jia Yi, yet his methods were free of impracticality. His loyalty and righteousness sufficed to quell the crisis at Fengtian, and contemporaries called him the “Inner Chief Councilor.” Han Changli revived literary writing after eight dynasties of decline, and through the Way rescued the world from drowning. His utter sincerity sufficed to tame the ferocity of crocodiles, and Chaoyang became known as easy to govern. Ouyang Xiu’s literary compositions were renowned above all others in the realm; in his work as chief councilor during the Jiayou era, he took remedying the troubles of the age and putting the Way into practice as his responsibility. Sima Guang’s literary learning encompassed everything; his administration during the Yuanyou era achieved the feat of turning Heaven and Earth around. These several men fully possessed the substance of learning, and their practical application of it was likewise comprehensive. To compare this to entering a pottery workshop [?]…

子房而文則過辯如賈誼而術不疎陸敬
輿也而忠義足以弭奉天之難當時稱為
內相文起八代之衰道濟天下之溺韓昌
黎也而精誠足以馴鱷魚之暴潮陽號為
易治歐陽脩有名冠天下之文章而嘉祐
相業以救時行道為責司馬光有無所不
通之文學而元祐政治著旋乾轉坤之功
之數人者體既具矣用亦周焉譬之入陶
punctuated: 竊嘗考之，《書》曰：「學古入官。」《易》曰：「君子多識前言往行，以畜其德。」則學不可以不博，明矣。所以然者，盖將舉此而措之於用耳。若伊尹誦詩讀書，佐商以肇一代之基；姬旦多才多藝，相周而垂百王之法。學行兼該，體用具備，卓乎不可尚已。下此，不能無優劣之可論者焉。姑以漢唐宋言之：洛陽少年，論過伊管，賈誼其才矣，而治安一策，實救文帝之弊；道明三代，學際天人，董仲舒其儒矣，而賢良三策，切中武帝之心；智於子房而文則過，辯如賈誼而術不疎，陸敬輿也，而忠義足以弭奉天之難，當時稱為內相；文起八代之衰，道濟天下之溺，韓昌黎也，而精誠足以馴鱷魚之暴，潮陽號為易治；歐陽脩有名冠天下之文章，而嘉祐相業，以救時行道為責；司馬光有無所不通之文學，而元祐政治，著旋乾轉坤之功。之數人者，體既具矣，用亦周焉。譬之入陶
translation_en:
I have ventured to examine this. The Book of Documents says, “Study antiquity and enter office.” The Book of Changes says, “The gentleman acquaints himself widely with the words and deeds of the past, thereby nourishing his virtue.” It is thus clear that learning must be broad. The reason is simply that one intends to bring all this learning into practical use. Yi Yin recited poetry and read the Documents, assisting the Shang in laying the foundations of a dynasty. Ji Dan possessed many talents and accomplishments, assisting the Zhou and bequeathing models for a hundred kings. Their learning and conduct embraced all things; both substance and practical application were complete. Their eminence could not be surpassed. Below them, there are inevitably relative strengths and weaknesses to discuss.
Let us take examples from the Han, Tang, and Song. The young man from Luoyang, whose arguments surpassed those of Yi Yin and Guan Zhong, was the talented Jia Yi; his policy essay on order and security truly remedied the failings of Emperor Wen’s government. The man whose Way illuminated the Three Dynasties and whose learning encompassed Heaven and humanity was the scholar Dong Zhongshu; his three policy responses in the examination for the Worthy and Good went straight to Emperor Wu’s heart. Comparable in wisdom to Zifang [?], yet surpassing him in literary ability, and as eloquent as Jia Yi, yet without his deficiencies in practical methods, was Lu Jingyu. His loyalty and righteousness sufficed to quell the crisis at Fengtian, and his contemporaries called him the “Inner Chief Councilor.” The man whose writing revived literature after eight dynasties of decline, and whose Way rescued the drowning world, was Han Changli. His profound sincerity sufficed to tame the ferocity of crocodiles, and Chaoyang gained a reputation for being easy to govern. Ouyang Xiu possessed literary accomplishments renowned above all others in the realm; in his work as chief councilor during the Jiayou era, he took rescuing his age and putting the Way into practice as his responsibility. Sima Guang possessed literary learning that left no subject unexplored; his governance during the Yuanyou era achieved the celebrated feat of turning Heaven and Earth around. These men possessed the substance in full, and their practical application was comprehensive. It is like entering Tao …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
朱之室隨取而隨足發扁鵲之厨隨施而
隨效博而能用一何偉歟至如緣飾儒術
公孫弘之辯論可取而懷倍約順旨之諼
言不顧行於論奚益博極群書揚雄之學
術可尚而有劇秦美新之作大節不謹於
術何工李太白之翰林風月學非不豪也
然黨永王而名節蔑聞其如政教何柳宗
元之瓊琚玉珮文非不美也然附叔文而
才猷靡邵其如治道何博學强記盧多遜
===
為當代名儒而數短趙普其致崖州之竄
亦宜也通今學古王安石固才高一世而
務行新法其壞熙寧之治非少也之數人
者學雖有餘政則不足譬之積囷廩之盛
不免於枵腹泛滄浪之深而乃以渴斃博
而無□何足稱哉乃若周勃重厚少文而
能誅吕安劉霍光不學亡術而能擁昭立
宣功之所建於博何預哉姚崇性好射獵
而以十事要說李德裕起自任子而以六
punctuated:
朱之室，隨取而隨足；發扁鵲之厨，隨施而隨效。博而能用，一何偉歟！
至如緣飾儒術，公孫弘之辯論可取，而懷倍約順旨之諼，言不顧行，於論奚益？博極群書，揚雄之學術可尚，而有《劇秦美新》之作，大節不謹，於術何工？李太白之翰林風月，學非不豪也，然黨永王而名節蔑聞，其如政教何？柳宗元之瓊琚玉珮，文非不美也，然附叔文而才猷靡邵，其如治道何？博學强記，盧多遜為當代名儒，而數短趙普，其致崖州之竄亦宜也。通今學古，王安石固才高一世，而務行新法，其壞熙寧之治非少也。之數人者，學雖有餘，政則不足。譬之積囷廩之盛，不免於枵腹；泛滄浪之深，而乃以渴斃。博而無□，何足稱哉！
乃若周勃重厚少文，而能誅吕安劉；霍光不學亡術，而能擁昭立宣。功之所建，於博何預哉？姚崇性好射獵，而以十事要說；李德裕起自任子，而以六
translation_en:
…the household of Tao Zhu, where whatever one takes is always sufficient; or opening Bian Que’s store of medicines, where every treatment proves effective. How magnificent it is to possess broad learning and be able to put it to use!
As for adorning oneself with Confucian learning, Gongsun Hong’s arguments were commendable, yet he harbored deceit, breaking agreements and accommodating the ruler’s wishes. His words took no account of his conduct: what benefit was there in his argumentation? Yang Xiong’s learning, encompassing a vast range of books, was admirable, yet he wrote Criticizing Qin and Praising Xin. Careless in matters of fundamental integrity, what excellence did he possess in his learning? Li Taibai’s wind-and-moon compositions in the Hanlin Academy certainly displayed splendid learning. Yet he sided with the Prince of Yong and won no reputation for integrity: what could he contribute to government and moral instruction? Liu Zongyuan’s writings, like precious jade ornaments, were certainly beautiful. Yet he attached himself to Shuwen, and his talents and counsels brought him no distinction [?]: what could he contribute to the way of government? Widely learned and possessed of a powerful memory, Lu Duoxun was a celebrated scholar of his age. Yet he repeatedly disparaged Zhao Pu; it was fitting that he should thereby bring upon himself banishment to Yazhou. Wang Anshi understood the present and studied antiquity, and his talents indeed surpassed those of his contemporaries. Yet he insisted on implementing the New Policies, doing no little damage to government during the Xining reign. These men possessed learning in abundance but fell short in governance. They were like someone with granaries filled to overflowing who nevertheless goes hungry, or someone sailing upon deep blue waters who nevertheless dies of thirst. What is praiseworthy about broad learning without □?
Then there was Zhou Bo, solid and grave in character but possessing little literary cultivation, who nevertheless destroyed the Lü clan and secured the Liu house. Huo Guang lacked learning and cultivated skills, yet he supported Emperor Zhao and enthroned Emperor Xuan. What did the achievements they established owe to broad learning? Yao Chong was by nature fond of archery and hunting, yet he presented ten matters as conditions in persuading the ruler; Li Deyu began his career through the privilege accorded to officials’ sons, yet with six…

punctuated: 朱之室，隨取而隨足；發扁鵲之厨，隨施而隨效。博而能用，一何偉歟！至如緣飾儒術，公孫弘之辯論可取，而懷倍約順旨之謾，言不顧行，於論奚益？博極群書，揚雄之學術可尚，而有《劇秦》《美新》之作，大節不謹，於術何工？李太白之翰林風月，學非不豪也，然黨永王而名節蔑聞，其如政教何？柳宗元之瓊琚玉珮，文非不美也，然附叔文而才猷靡邵，其如治道何？博學强記，盧多遜爲當代名儒，而數短趙普，其致崖州之竄亦宜也。通今學古，王安石固才高一世，而務行新法，其壞熈寧之治非少也。之數人者，學雖有餘，政則不足。譬之積囷廩之盛，不免於枵腹；泛滄浪之深，而乃以渴斃。博而無□，何足稱哉！乃若周勃重厚少文，而能誅吕安劉；霍光不學亡術，而能擁昭立宣。功之所建，於博何預哉？姚崇性好射獵，而以十事要說；李德裕起自任子，而以六
translation_en:
…Zhu’s household [?]: whatever is taken from it, there is always enough; open Bian Que’s medicine cupboard, and every remedy administered proves effective. How splendid it is to possess broad learning and be able to put it to use!

As for clothing arguments in Confucian learning, Gongsun Hong’s debating ability was commendable. Yet he harbored the deceitfulness of breaking agreements and accommodating the ruler’s wishes; his words took no account of his conduct. What benefit, then, was his argumentation? Yang Xiong’s learning, encompassing a vast range of books, was worthy of esteem. Yet he composed “Criticizing Qin” and “Praising Xin.” Failing to safeguard his integrity in great matters, what accomplishment did his learning represent? Li Taibai’s wind-and-moon writings in the Hanlin Academy certainly displayed magnificent learning. Yet he joined the Prince of Yong’s faction, and his reputation for integrity came to nothing. What could he contribute to government and moral instruction? Liu Zongyuan’s writings were certainly as beautiful as precious jade ornaments. Yet he attached himself to Shuwen, and his talents and plans failed to attain distinction [?]. What could he contribute to the way of governing?

Widely learned and endowed with a powerful memory, Lu Duoxun was a renowned scholar of his time. Yet he repeatedly disparaged Zhao Pu, and it was fitting that he should consequently be banished to Yazhou. Wang Anshi, versed in contemporary affairs and learned in antiquity, certainly possessed talents surpassing his contemporaries. Yet he insisted on implementing the New Policies, doing no little damage to the governance of the Xining reign. These men had learning in abundance but were deficient in government. They were like someone with granaries filled to overflowing who nevertheless goes hungry, or someone floating upon deep waters who nevertheless dies of thirst. What is praiseworthy about broad learning without □ [?]?

Consider, however, Zhou Bo: substantial in character and sparing in literary refinement, he nevertheless destroyed the Lü clan and secured the Liu ruling house. Huo Guang, unlearned and without scholarly attainments, nevertheless supported Emperor Zhao and enthroned Emperor Xuan. What did the achievements they established owe to broad learning? Yao Chong was by disposition fond of archery and hunting, yet he made his persuasive appeal through ten proposals. Li Deyu entered service through the privilege accorded to officials’ sons, yet with six…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
箴獻納業之所就何係於博哉東征西討
無不如意趙普開國之功可紀也即其所
學自論語之外無餘業焉澶淵請盟親扶
日轂寇準弭兵之力居多也求其所蘊於
張詠之誚不能免焉若此數人以學則無
淵源以政則有經濟是何也或天資之偶
合或才力之有餘故耳然考其終身不能
無議焉定亂者勃也械繫者亦勃也擁立
者光也啓禍者亦光也雖善應變僅濟小
===
康况又迎合成務乎雖善規諫未聞悟主
况又朋黨傾軋乎太平可致而金匱之誓
盟不可渝北門可托而朱能之天書不可
信使其學之有本安至是哉苟不究其始
終執此而曰學無益於政是猶見人之眇
焉能視而欲抉其目跛焉能行而欲刖其
足於理可乎比事而觀之則學而當博博
而當用斷斷乎其不可易矣抑說者又謂
天下之理同出一原若不取於博也殊不
punctuated: 箴獻納，業之所就何係於博哉？東征西討，無不如意，趙普開國之功可紀也。即其所學，自《論語》之外無餘業焉。澶淵請盟，親扶日轂，寇準弭兵之力居多也。求其所蘊，於張詠之誚不能免焉。若此數人，以學則無淵源，以政則有經濟，是何也？或天資之偶合，或才力之有餘故耳。然考其終身，不能無議焉。定亂者勃也，械繫者亦勃也；擁立者光也，啓禍者亦光也。雖善應變，僅濟小康，况又迎合成務乎？雖善規諫，未聞悟主，况又朋黨傾軋乎？太平可致，而金匱之誓盟不可渝；北門可托，而朱能之天書不可信。使其學之有本，安至是哉？苟不究其始終，執此而曰學無益於政，是猶見人之眇焉能視，而欲抉其目；跛焉能行，而欲刖其足，於理可乎？比事而觀之，則學而當博，博而當用，斷斷乎其不可易矣。抑說者又謂天下之理同出一原，若不取於博也，殊不
translation_en:
…admonitions submitted to the throne: how did his achievements depend on breadth of learning? Campaigning east and west, he succeeded in every undertaking: Zhao Pu’s contribution to founding the dynasty deserves commemoration. Yet as for his learning, beyond the Analects he had studied nothing else. When a covenant was sought at Chanyuan, Kou Zhun personally supported the imperial carriage and contributed greatly to ending hostilities. Yet when his store of learning was examined, he could not escape Zhang Yong’s mockery. These men lacked deep foundations in learning but possessed the ability to order the realm. Why was this? Simply because their natural gifts happened to suit the circumstances, or because their abilities were exceptional.

Yet if we examine their entire lives, they cannot escape criticism. It was Zhou Bo who quelled disorder, but also Zhou Bo who was put in fetters. It was Huo Guang who enthroned the ruler, but also Huo Guang who opened the way to calamity. Though adept at responding to changing circumstances, one achieved only a modest measure of peace—and what of his accomplishing affairs by accommodating others’ wishes? Though adept at admonition, another is not known to have brought his sovereign to understanding—and what of his involvement in factional strife? Peace could be achieved, yet the sworn covenant in the golden coffer could not be altered; the northern gate could be entrusted to him, yet Zhu Neng’s heavenly writings were not to be believed. Had their learning possessed firm foundations, how could they have come to this?

If, without examining their lives from beginning to end, one seizes upon these examples and declares that learning is of no benefit to government, it is like seeing that someone with impaired sight can still see and wishing to gouge out his eyes, or seeing that a lame person can still walk and wishing to cut off his feet. Could this accord with reason? Comparing these cases, we see that learning must be broad, and broad learning must be put to use: this is absolutely unalterable. Yet some argue further that all principles under Heaven issue from a single source, as though breadth of learning need not be sought. They utterly fail to…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
知泛應曲當用各不同學不博則不能守
約理不窮則不能力行君子其可以不博
哉古今事物萬有不齊固難致其博也誠
能近述諸今遠稽諸古事事而窮之物物
而格之則亦何患於不博哉愚生才慚樗
櫟學愧荒蕪以博不無望洋之嘆以用恐
有出位之思姑述所聞以復明問若究其
幼學壮行之志則自伊周之外未暇論焉
執事恕其狂瞽而教之幸甚
===
第五問
李鑾
同考試官訓導熊批處置此士兵民之事
甚善盖亦識時務之俊傑乎
考試官教諭趙批立法得人雖係常談
而治道之大要恐不出此
考試官教諭朱批篇終有題外意所識
可知
天下無不可為之事在為之者得其法天
punctuated:

第五問
李鑾

同考試官訓導熊批：「處置此士兵民之事甚善，盖亦識時務之俊傑乎！」

考試官教諭趙批：「立法得人，雖係常談，而治道之大要，恐不出此。」

考試官教諭朱批：「篇終有題外意，所識可知。」

天下無不可為之事，在為之者得其法。天
translation_en:
…know that responding broadly and fittingly to every particular circumstance requires different applications. Without breadth of learning, one cannot hold to the essentials; without fully investigating principles, one cannot earnestly put them into practice. Can the gentleman, then, dispense with breadth of learning? Affairs and things, ancient and modern, differ in myriad ways, so attaining such breadth is indeed difficult. Yet if one truly can draw on the present close at hand and examine antiquity far away, exhaustively investigating each affair and examining each thing, why worry about failing to attain breadth? I, an unworthy student, am ashamed that my talents are as useless as the ailanthus and oak, and that my learning is so neglected. As for breadth, I cannot help sighing like one gazing helplessly out upon the ocean; as for practical application, I fear my thoughts may stray beyond my station. I have merely related what I have heard in reply to your discerning question. If you inquire into my aspiration to learn in youth and act upon that learning in maturity, I have had no leisure to consider models other than Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. I would be most fortunate if you would pardon my rashness and blindness and instruct me.

Li Luan

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiong, Assistant Instructor: “His handling of these matters concerning scholars, soldiers, and commoners is excellent. Surely he too is an outstanding talent who understands the needs of the times!”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Establishing regulations and securing suitable men may be commonplace themes, but the essentials of the way of government probably extend no further than these.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The conclusion contains a meaning beyond the set topic; from this one can discern his understanding.”

There is nothing under Heaven that cannot be accomplished; it depends on those undertaking it finding the proper method. Heaven…

知泛應曲當用各不同學不博則不能守
約理不窮則不能力行君子其可以不博

能近述諸今遠稽諸古事事而窮之物物

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
下無不可救之弊在救之者得其人夫有
一事必有一法法非不善也而用法之非
其人故有不善耳苟得其人以之撫民而
民安以之勵兵而兵強何憂乎法之不立
事之不可為而弊之不可救哉執事發策
以廣右兵民之弊為問愚生含情憤激而
欲言之乆矣敢不悉心以對書曰民惟邦
本本固邦寧傳曰國之大事在祀與戎則
兵民二事有國家者不可不究心也况廣
===
右邇年以來民敝兵壞可忍而置於度外
乎以民言之則土曠人稀弱肉強食深山
大澤多占於夷類窮簷部屋畧存乎編氓
師旅興而民財已窮科差繁而民力已盡
誠有如執事之所慮也為今之計莫若竭
撫字之勤絕掊尅之害黎元之凋敝者寬
其征輸復其流亡而闢土地以居之夷類
之頑梗者殲其渠魁撫其餘黨而立保甲
以統之軍需預積使免推挽轉運之勞科
punctuated:
下無不可救之弊，在救之者得其人。夫有一事，必有一法。法非不善也，而用法之非其人，故有不善耳。苟得其人，以之撫民而民安，以之勵兵而兵強，何憂乎法之不立、事之不可為而弊之不可救哉？執事發策，以廣右兵民之弊為問，愚生含情憤激而欲言之乆矣，敢不悉心以對？《書》曰：「民惟邦本，本固邦寧。」《傳》曰：「國之大事，在祀與戎。」則兵民二事，有國家者不可不究心也。况廣右邇年以來，民敝兵壞，可忍而置於度外乎？

以民言之，則土曠人稀，弱肉強食，深山大澤多占於夷類，窮簷部屋畧存乎編氓。師旅興而民財已窮，科差繁而民力已盡，誠有如執事之所慮也。為今之計，莫若竭撫字之勤，絕掊尅之害。黎元之凋敝者，寬其征輸，復其流亡，而闢土地以居之；夷類之頑梗者，殲其渠魁，撫其餘黨，而立保甲以統之。軍需預積，使免推挽轉運之勞。科
translation_en:
…under Heaven there is no abuse that cannot be remedied, provided the right people are obtained to remedy it. For every undertaking there must be a method. It is not that the method is unsound; rather, those applying it are not the right people, and this alone produces unsatisfactory results. If the right people are obtained, employing them to care for the people will bring the people peace, and employing them to encourage the troops will make the troops strong. Why then worry that methods cannot be established, undertakings accomplished, or abuses remedied? You, sir, have set a policy question concerning the troubles of the troops and people of Guangyou. This humble student has long felt indignation and wished to speak of them. How could I dare not devote my whole mind to answering? The Book of Documents says: “The people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is firm, the state is at peace.” The Zuo Commentary says: “The great affairs of the state are sacrifice and warfare.” Thus, those who govern a state cannot fail to give thorough attention to the two matters of troops and people. All the more so in Guangyou, where in recent years the people have been impoverished and the military has deteriorated: can one bear to set these matters aside?

As for the people, the land is vast and the population sparse; the strong devour the weak. Deep mountains and great marshes are largely occupied by tribal peoples, while registered commoners barely subsist in wretched dwellings [?]. Military campaigns have exhausted the people's resources, and numerous levies and service obligations have depleted their strength. Matters are indeed as you fear, sir. The best course now is to exert every effort in caring for the people and to eliminate the harm of extortion. For the impoverished common people, ease their tax payments, bring back those who have fled, and open up land on which to settle them. For the recalcitrant tribal peoples, destroy their ringleaders, pacify their remaining followers, and establish the baojia system of mutual responsibility to organize them. Accumulate military supplies in advance, so that the people may be spared the toil of hauling and transporting them. As for levies…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
差裁省俾無隳突呌囂之嘆撫民之術豈
有外于此哉夫法既立矣而行之者在乎
守令之得人也誠使得人如谷永之守鬱
林以恩信招烏滸之人幾十餘萬栁宗元
之剌栁州以禮化致流逋之歸樂生興事
攝興安而有陶弼則勸浚靈渠以通餽餉
大為民利知梧州而有梁適則奏免折稅
以省轉運甚為民便有人而能撫民如此
則變惡為善轉危為安而民何憂於敞乎
===
以兵言之則行伍空虛武備廢弛剽掠起
於月餉之稍緩勞苦原於私役之無已寇
盜發而戍卒輙逃主将亡而麾下坐視誠
有如執事之所言也為今之計莫若精訓
練之方嚴名實之核給粮餉不失其時而
妄冒竊掠者雖強必誅公差操以節其力
而役占侵漁者雖貴必黜以守則時其簡
閱使絕逃竄之念以戰則嚴其號令俾奮
效死之心勵兵之計豈有出于此哉夫法
punctuated:
差裁省，俾無隳突呌囂之嘆。撫民之術，豈有外于此哉？夫法既立矣，而行之者在乎守令之得人也。誠使得人，如谷永之守鬱林，以恩信招烏滸之人幾十餘萬；栁宗元之剌栁州，以禮化致流逋之歸，樂生興事；攝興安而有陶弼，則勸浚靈渠以通餽餉，大為民利；知梧州而有梁適，則奏免折稅以省轉運，甚為民便。有人而能撫民如此，則變惡為善，轉危為安，而民何憂於敞乎？
以兵言之，則行伍空虛，武備廢弛，剽掠起於月餉之稍緩，勞苦原於私役之無已。寇盜發而戍卒輙逃，主将亡而麾下坐視，誠有如執事之所言也。為今之計，莫若精訓練之方，嚴名實之核，給粮餉不失其時，而妄冒竊掠者雖強必誅；公差操以節其力，而役占侵漁者雖貴必黜。以守，則時其簡閱，使絕逃竄之念；以戰，則嚴其號令，俾奮效死之心。勵兵之計，豈有出于此哉？夫法
translation_en:
…reduce service levies, so that the people have no cause to lament violent intrusion and clamorous harassment. Could the means of caring for the people extend beyond these measures? Once regulations have been established, their implementation depends upon securing suitable prefects and magistrates. If truly suitable men were appointed, they would be like Gu Yong, who, as governor of Yulin, attracted more than a hundred thousand Wuhu people [?] through kindness and trustworthiness; or Liu Zongyuan, who, as prefect of Liuzhou, transformed the people through ritual propriety, bringing displaced people and fugitives home to enjoy their livelihoods and pursue productive work. When Tao Bi served as acting magistrate of Xing'an, he encouraged dredging the Lingqu Canal to facilitate the transport of provisions, greatly benefiting the people. When Liang Shi administered Wuzhou, he memorialized requesting exemption from commuted taxes to reduce transport burdens, greatly easing the people's lives. With men capable of caring for the people in this way, bad conditions would become good and danger would give way to security. Why, then, should the people fear impoverishment [?]?
As for the troops, the ranks are depleted and military preparedness has fallen into neglect. Plundering begins when monthly pay is even slightly delayed, while hardship stems from unending private service. When bandits rise, garrison soldiers promptly flee; when their commander perishes, his subordinates stand idly by. Matters are indeed as you have said. The best course now is to refine methods of training and rigorously verify whether nominal strength matches actual strength. Grain and pay must be issued on time, and those who make fraudulent claims, steal, or plunder must be executed, however powerful they may be. Duty assignments and drills must be apportioned fairly to conserve the soldiers' strength, and those who appropriate soldiers for private service or exploit them must be dismissed, however exalted their rank. For defense, hold inspections and reviews at proper intervals, so that soldiers abandon any thought of desertion; for battle, enforce commands strictly, so that they summon the resolve to serve unto death. Could any plan for invigorating the troops go beyond these measures? Now, the regulations…

When bandits rise, the garrison soldiers promptly flee; when the commanding general dies, his subordinates stand by and watch. Matters are indeed as you have stated. The best course now is to refine methods of training, rigorously check actual conditions against the rolls, and issue grain and pay on time. Those who make fraudulent claims, steal, or plunder must be punished, however powerful they may be. Service assignments and drills should be administered fairly [?] to conserve the soldiers’ strength, while those who appropriate soldiers for private service or exploit them must be dismissed, however exalted their rank. For defense, conduct inspections and reviews at the proper times, eliminating thoughts of desertion; for battle, enforce commands strictly, inspiring the resolve to serve unto death. Could any plan for invigorating the troops surpass this? Now, the regulations…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
既立矣而行之者在乎將帥之得人也誠
使得人如王晙之都督桂州罷戍卒開屯
田以息轉漕之勞謝肇之經畧容管布威
令息忿爭而貽詔答之褒討儂賊而得狄
青則張燈饗士削平嶺南廣人為之磨崖
紀功守靜江而得馬墍則恩信結下戰死
踰時部將為之自焚無降有人而能勵兵
若此則恩威兼盡上下相親而兵何有於
壞耶是則民安係於守令兵强由於將帥
===
理固然也至於鼓舞轉移之機尤在乎當
道者何如耳誠使勸懲一出於公賞罰各
得其當則人心思奮事功有成而民安兵
强不期然而然矣管見區區未知執事以
為然否
punctuated: 既立矣，而行之者在乎將帥之得人也。誠使得人，如王晙之都督桂州，罷戍卒，開屯田，以息轉漕之勞；謝肇之經畧容管，布威令，息忿爭，而貽詔答之褒；討儂賊而得狄青，則張燈饗士，削平嶺南，廣人為之磨崖紀功；守靜江而得馬墍，則恩信結下，戰死踰時，部將為之自焚，無降。有人而能勵兵若此，則恩威兼盡，上下相親，而兵何有於壞耶？是則民安係於守令，兵强由於將帥，理固然也。至於鼓舞轉移之機，尤在乎當道者何如耳。誠使勸懲一出於公，賞罰各得其當，則人心思奮，事功有成，而民安兵强，不期然而然矣。管見區區，未知執事以為然否？
translation_en:
…once established, their implementation depends on securing the right men as commanders. If suitable men are indeed appointed, there are examples such as Wang Jun, who, as Area Commander of Guizhou, disbanded garrison troops and established military agricultural colonies to relieve the burden of transporting grain; and Xie Zhao, who, while administering military affairs in the Rong command area, promulgated authoritative orders and quelled bitter disputes, earning praise in an imperial rescript. When Di Qing was entrusted with suppressing the Nong rebels, he hung lanterns and feasted his soldiers, pacified Lingnan, and had his achievements commemorated by the people of Guangxi in an inscription carved into a cliff. When Ma Ji [?] was entrusted with defending Jingjiang, he bound his subordinates to him through kindness and trust; even some time after his death in battle, his subordinate commanders burned themselves to death for his sake, and none surrendered. With men capable of inspiring the troops in this way, both benevolence and authority are fully exercised, superiors and subordinates are bound by affection, and how could the army fall into decay? Thus the people's peace depends on prefects and magistrates, and military strength derives from commanders: this is indeed the natural principle.

As for the means of inspiring men and bringing about change, these depend above all on those in authority. If encouragement and discipline proceed entirely from impartiality, and rewards and punishments are each appropriate, people will aspire to exert themselves and undertakings will succeed. The people will then enjoy peace and the army will become strong without these results even having to be sought. These are merely my humble, limited views; I do not know whether you, sir, consider them sound.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
弘治壬子秋廣西鄉試列郡
士得其文中式者凡五十有
五人遂次第其氏名并彙集
其前列數人文為錄既成僉
謂堦當序其末簡竊惟天以
大道畀諸聖人聖人以大道
===
傳諸六經無非所以為民也
故易以前民用書以匡民德
詩以正民俗禮以節民性樂
以和民心春秋以嚴民防一
皆道之所寓惟明於道者而
後能加之民也自秦燔載籍
易以占春秋以史獲免樂竟
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序

弘治壬子秋，廣西鄉試列郡士，得其文中式者凡五十有五人。遂次第其氏名，并彙集其前列數人文為錄。既成，僉謂堦當序其末簡。竊惟天以大道畀諸聖人，聖人以大道傳諸六經，無非所以為民也。故易以前民用，書以匡民德，詩以正民俗，禮以節民性，樂以和民心，春秋以嚴民防，一皆道之所寓。惟明於道者，而後能加之民也。自秦燔載籍，易以占、春秋以史獲免，樂竟
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the renzi year of the Hongzhi reign (1492), Guangxi held its Provincial Examination for scholars from its various prefectures. Fifty-five men submitted compositions that met the requirements and passed. Their names were then arranged in order, and the compositions of several of the highest-ranking candidates were collected to form this record. Once it was completed, all agreed that I, Jie 堦, should write a postface for its closing pages.

I humbly reflect that Heaven bestowed the Great Way upon the sages, and the sages transmitted the Great Way through the Six Classics, all for the sake of the people. Thus, the Book of Changes guides the people’s practical activities; the Book of Documents rectifies their virtue; the Book of Odes corrects their customs; the Book of Rites regulates their dispositions; the Book of Music harmonizes their hearts; and the Spring and Autumn Annals makes strict the restraints governing their conduct. Each embodies the Way. Only those who understand the Way can then apply it to the people. When Qin burned the written records, the Book of Changes escaped because it concerned divination, and the Spring and Autumn Annals because it was history; the Book of Music ultimately…

Their names were then arranged in order, and essays by several of the highest-ranked candidates were collected to form this record.
