When the Qin burned the written records, the Changes escaped because it concerned divination, and the Spring and Autumn Annals because it was history; the Music ultimately…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
淪滅無傳書詩禮既熄而復
出禮有儀禮十七篇即古禮
經禮記多漢儒所作朱子以
為禮經之傳是也然禮經何
以不傳乎自宋王安石柄國
而廢之也然迄今數百年間
閭學士珍藏什襲在在有之
===
真若有神物護持之者禮經
豈終廢歟夫聖道之有六經
猶人身之有六腑一腑病則
諸腑弗寧人身日就危矣一
經廢則羣經無徵聖道幾於
蝕矣六經可多廢哉先正有
曰六經之道同歸禮樂之用
punctuated: 淪滅無傳。書、詩、禮既熄而復出。禮有《儀禮》十七篇，即古《禮經》。《禮記》多漢儒所作，朱子以為《禮經》之傳，是也。然《禮經》何以不傳乎？自宋王安石柄國而廢之也。然迄今數百年間，閭學士珍藏什襲，在在有之，真若有神物護持之者。《禮經》豈終廢歟？夫聖道之有六經，猶人身之有六腑。一腑病，則諸腑弗寧，人身日就危矣；一經廢，則羣經無徵，聖道幾於蝕矣。六經可多廢哉？先正有曰：「六經之道，同歸禮樂之用
translation_en:
…fell into oblivion and was no longer transmitted. The Documents, Odes, and Rites, after being extinguished, reappeared. Among the ritual texts are the seventeen chapters of the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili), which constitute the ancient Classic of Rites. The Record of Rites (Liji) was largely written by Han Confucian scholars. Master Zhu regarded it as a commentary on the Classic of Rites, and rightly so. But why did the Classic of Rites cease to be transmitted? Because Wang Anshi abolished its study when he held power under the Song. Yet throughout the several hundred years down to the present, scholars in local communities [?] have treasured it, wrapping it in many protective layers; copies are found everywhere. It truly seems as though supernatural beings have guarded it. Could the Classic of Rites ever be permanently abandoned?

The Way of the sages has the Six Classics just as the human body has its six hollow organs. If one organ becomes diseased, the others cannot remain at ease, and the body daily approaches peril. If one classic is abandoned, the other classics lose their corroborating evidence, and the Way of the sages comes close to being eroded. Can so many of the Six Classics be abandoned? A worthy predecessor said: “The Way of the Six Classics converges in the application of rites and music…

translation_en:

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
為急以禮視樂禮為尤急樂
已廢矣禮幸尚存顧在民間
經生造士所誦習者禮記而
已禮記雖未詳禮之節度而
亦足以發禮經之義程子嘗
謂其儘有格言則與羣經皆
不可不究心者諸士子以能
===
===
明易書詩春秋禮記見錄於
有司使或未究其極畫於半
途終亦必亡而已矣繼自今
鉤微剔賾根極領要瞭然大
道之指歸如有用我執此以
往民用前之民德匡之民俗
正之民防嚴之民性節且和
punctuated: 為急。」以禮視樂，禮為尤急。樂已廢矣，禮幸尚存。顧在民間，經生造士所誦習者，《禮記》而已。《禮記》雖未詳禮之節度，而亦足以發禮經之義。程子嘗謂其儘有格言，則與羣經皆不可不究心者。諸士子以能明《易》《書》《詩》《春秋》《禮記》，見錄於有司。使或未究其極，畫於半途，終亦必亡而已矣。繼自今，鉤微剔賾，根極領要，瞭然大道之指歸。如有用我，執此以往，民用前之，民德匡之，民俗正之，民防嚴之，民性節且和
translation_en:
…is urgent.” Comparing ritual with music, ritual is still more urgent. Music has already fallen into disuse; fortunately, ritual still survives. Yet among the people, what classical scholars and students under instruction recite and study is only the Record of Rites (Liji). Although the Record of Rites does not fully detail the prescribed forms and measures of ritual, it nevertheless suffices to elucidate the meaning of the ritual classic. Master Cheng once said that it contains many exemplary sayings; thus, like all the other classics, it must be studied with full attention.

You students have been selected by the responsible officials for your ability to understand the Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn Annals, and Record of Rites. If, however, you fail to investigate their utmost depths and stop halfway, in the end these too will inevitably be lost. Henceforth, draw out their subtleties, sift through their mysteries, probe their roots to the utmost, and grasp their essentials, so that you clearly understand the direction of the Great Way. Should someone employ you, take this understanding with you: advance the people’s practical undertakings [?], rectify their moral conduct, correct their customs, strengthen the restraints that guard them, and temper and harmonize their dispositions…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之斯不負天與聖人所以爲
民之意也若徒藉是以捷巍
科都高官咕咕自足而於民
生疾苦若罔攸聞甚至以不
道加之不獲罪於天與聖人

春秋具在若復儀禮爲經別
===
禮記爲傳訂之先正立之學
官使天下後世學者獲見五
經之全行當仰覩我
聖天子制作之盛
福建建寧府松溪縣儒學教
諭趙楷謹序
punctuated:
之，斯不負天與聖人所以爲民之意也。若徒藉是以捷巍科，都高官，咕咕自足，而於民生疾苦若罔攸聞，甚至以不道加之，不獲罪於天與聖人也者幾希！噫！樂廢矣，《易》《書》《詩》《春秋》具在。若復《儀禮》爲經，別《禮記》爲傳，訂之先正，立之學官，使天下後世學者獲見五經之全，行當仰覩我聖天子制作之盛。
福建建寧府松溪縣儒學教諭趙楷謹序。
translation_en:
…them. Only thus will one fulfill the intentions of Heaven and the sages toward the people. If one merely uses this learning to succeed in the highest examinations and occupy high office, smugly content with oneself [?], while seeming never to have heard of the hardships of the people’s lives, and even inflicting unprincipled treatment upon them, scarcely anyone could escape condemnation by Heaven and the sages!
Alas! The Classic of Music has been lost, but the Changes, Documents, Odes, and Spring and Autumn Annals all survive. If the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) were restored to the status of a classic, and the Record of Rites (Liji) separately designated as its commentary, this arrangement checked against the teachings of former worthies and established in the official schools, then scholars throughout the realm and in later generations could encounter the Five Classics in their entirety. We should then soon behold with reverence the splendor of our sagely Son of Heaven’s establishment of rites and institutions.
Preface respectfully written by Zhao Kai, Instructor of the Confucian School of Songxi County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之斯不負天與聖人所以爲
民之意也若徒藉是以捷巍
科都高官咕咕自足而於民
生疾苦若罔攸聞甚至以不
道加之不獲罪於天與聖人
也者幾希噫樂廢矣易書詩
春秋具在若復儀禮爲經別
===
禮記爲傳訂之先正立之學
官使天下後世學者獲見五
經之全行當仰覩我
聖天子制作之盛
福建建寧府松溪縣儒學教
諭趙堦謹序
punctuated:
之，斯不負天與聖人所以爲民之意也。若徒藉是以捷巍科、都高官，咕咕自足，而於民生疾苦若罔攸聞，甚至以不道加之，不獲罪於天與聖人也者幾希！噫！樂廢矣，《易》《書》《詩》《春秋》具在。若復《儀禮》爲經，別《禮記》爲傳，訂之先正，立之學官，使天下後世學者獲見五經之全，行當仰覩我聖天子制作之盛。
福建建寧府松溪縣儒學教諭趙堦謹序。
translation_en:
…it; only thus would one fulfill Heaven’s and the sages’ intentions for the people. If one merely uses this to attain distinction in the examinations and occupy high office, smugly content with oneself [?], while seeming to hear nothing of the hardships of the people’s livelihood, and even subjects them to unjust treatment, scarcely could one avoid incurring guilt before Heaven and the sages! Alas! The Classic of Music has been lost, but the Changes, Documents, Odes, and Spring and Autumn Annals all survive. If the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili) were restored to the status of a classic, the Record of Rites (Liji) distinguished as its commentary, this arrangement checked against the teachings of earlier worthies and established in the official schools, then scholars throughout the realm and in later generations could see the Five Classics in their entirety. We should then soon behold with reverence the splendor of our sagely Son of Heaven’s cultural and institutional achievements.
Preface respectfully written by Zhao Jie 趙堦, Instructor of the Confucian School of Songxi County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
維弘治壬子適
皇上在位之五年天下又當大比
之期總督兩廣右都御史閔
珪祗若
德意先期會巡按廣西監察御史
鄭惟桓朱文暨藩臬二司布
===
政使李孟暘黎福參政程廷珙
洪漢楊守隨參議吳昭按察
使傅希說副使周孟中陳寓
徐瑁僉事劉信黎鼎陳娃禮
聘麒與教諭趙堦司考校學
正陳珫教諭林光重謝澧訓
導熊縝余黙同考校于時總
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序

維弘治壬子，適皇上在位之五年，天下又當大比之期。總督兩廣右都御史閔珪祗若德意，先期會巡按廣西監察御史鄭惟桓、朱文暨藩臬二司布政使李孟暘、黎福，參政程廷珙、洪漢、楊守隨，參議吳昭，按察使傅希說，副使周孟中、陳寓、徐瑁，僉事劉信、黎鼎、陳娃，禮聘麒與教諭趙堦司考校，學正陳珫、教諭林光重、謝澧、訓導熊縝、余黙同考校。于時總
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the renzi year of the Hongzhi reign, the fifth year of His Majesty’s rule [1492], the time had again come for the triennial examinations throughout the empire. Min Gui, Supreme Commander of Guangdong and Guangxi and Right Censor-in-Chief, reverently following the imperial intentions, conferred in advance with Zheng Weihuan and Zhu Wen, Regional Inspectors serving as Investigating Censors in Guangxi, and with the officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions: Provincial Administration Commissioners Li Mengyang and Li Fu; Administration Vice Commissioners Cheng Tinggong, Hong Han, and Yang Shousui; Administration Assistant Commissioner Wu Zhao; Surveillance Commissioner Fu Xishuo; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhou Mengzhong, Chen Yu, and Xu Mao; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Liu Xin, Li Ding, and Chen Wa [?]. They formally invited Qi and County School Instructor Zhao Jie to serve as Examiners, and Department School Instructor Chen Chong, County School Instructors Lin Guangzhong and Xie Li, and Assistant Instructors Xiong Zhen and Yu Mo to serve as Associate Examiners. At that time, the chief …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
鎮太監王敬總兵伏羌伯毛
鋭同涖玆土武功既成文事
攸舉至期巡按監察御史祁
司員乃合孟中所提督之士
而覆閲之凡七百有竒鎖院
圍棘以就三試則福昭司提
調希説烓司監試而廷珙漢
===
信又皆贊襄防範於外與凡
中外百司皆遴選以充至於
秉公殫慮而始終監臨之者
寔御史祁司員也試已得中
式者五十有五人爰錄其氏
名并其文之合程度者以
獻麒謬忝校文宜序諸首竊謂
punctuated: 鎮太監王敬、總兵伏羌伯毛鋭同涖玆土，武功既成，文事攸舉。至期，巡按監察御史祁司員乃合孟中所提督之士而覆閲之，凡七百有竒。鎖院圍棘，以就三試，則福、昭司提調，希説、烓司監試，而廷珙、漢、信又皆贊襄防範於外。與凡中外百司，皆遴選以充。至於秉公殫慮而始終監臨之者，寔御史祁司員也。試已，得中式者五十有五人，爰錄其氏名，并其文之合程度者以獻。麒謬忝校文，宜序諸首，竊謂
translation_en:
…the eunuch Wang Jing, serving as Grand Defender, and Regional Commander Mao Rui, Earl of Fuqiang, jointly presided over this territory. With military achievements secured, literary endeavors were undertaken. At the appointed time, the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Qi Siyuan, assembled the scholars under Zhou Mengzhong’s supervision and examined them again. They numbered over seven hundred. The examination compound was locked and enclosed with thorn barriers for the three examination sessions. Li Fu and Wu Zhao served as Proctors; Fu Xishuo and Wei [?] supervised the examinations; and Cheng Tinggong, Hong Han, and Liu Xin all assisted with security outside. Personnel for the various offices inside and outside the compound were all carefully selected. It was Censor Qi Siyuan who, acting impartially and giving the matter his utmost attention, served as Supervising Official from beginning to end.

When the examination was completed, fifty-five men had qualified. Their names were accordingly recorded, together with those of their compositions that met the prescribed standards, for presentation to the throne. I, Qi, having undeservedly been entrusted with evaluating the compositions, ought to provide a preface at the beginning. I venture to observe that…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天地之化其開也有漸聖人
之化其成也亦有漸廣右去
京師萬里古百粤地也自秦
漢迄今更數千百年我
祖宗開基誕敷文德無遠弗届
列聖相承延及
皇上薫蒸融液聲敎益覃然後學
===
校之設詩書之化徧舉漸摩
殆駸駸然與中州齒而深山
大谷猶有怙終而迷復者何
哉譬之陰崖寒谷陽和之所
不及豈理然耶然觀泰伯逃
吴至德之聲漸被無窮子游
北學中國遂為聖門高弟常
punctuated: 天地之化，其開也有漸；聖人之化，其成也亦有漸。廣右去京師萬里，古百粤地也。自秦漢迄今，更數千百年。我祖宗開基，誕敷文德，無遠弗届。列聖相承，延及皇上，薫蒸融液，聲敎益覃。然後學校之設、詩書之化徧舉，漸摩殆駸駸然與中州齒。而深山大谷猶有怙終而迷復者，何哉？譬之陰崖寒谷，陽和之所不及，豈理然耶？然觀泰伯逃吴，至德之聲漸被無窮；子游北學中國，遂為聖門高弟。常
translation_en:
… The transforming work of Heaven and Earth unfolds gradually; the transforming work of the sages likewise reaches completion gradually. Guangyou lies ten thousand li from the capital and was anciently the land of the Hundred Yue. From the Qin and Han down to the present, thousands of years have elapsed. Our imperial ancestors founded the dynasty and broadly extended their civil virtue, reaching even the most distant places. Successive sage rulers carried on this work down to His Majesty, whose influence permeates and transforms, spreading the imperial teachings ever farther. Only then were schools established everywhere and the civilizing teachings of the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents universally promoted. Through gradual instruction and cultivation, the region has advanced steadily toward equality with the Central Plains. Yet in the deep mountains and great valleys there are still those who persist in wrongdoing to the end and lose their way back. Why is this? They resemble shaded cliffs and cold valleys unreached by the warmth of spring: could this be the natural order of things?
Yet consider how Taibo fled to Wu, where the renown of his consummate virtue spread gradually, with influence extending without end. Ziyou went north to study in the Central States and became an eminent disciple in the school of the Sage. Chang …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
衮廉閩親與諸生為主客之
禮閩人始知文學而歐陽詹
遂登龍虎榜吳與閩皆昔粤
地也自泰伯常衮之風化子
游歐陽詹之倡先遂為詩書
上國隱然海濱之鄒魯矣廣
右在宋時張栻出守靜江民
===
知向化流風餘韻至今猶存
馮京崛起慶遠解省廷對名
皆第一卒膺大拜史稱其有
中立不倚之操則風化之倡
先之未必無其人也詩書士
迨今亦且多矣獨其間頑悍
之習猶使人不能無憾焉者
punctuated: 衮廉閩，親與諸生為主客之禮，閩人始知文學，而歐陽詹遂登龍虎榜。吳與閩皆昔粤地也，自泰伯、常衮之風化，子游、歐陽詹之倡先，遂為詩書上國，隱然海濱之鄒魯矣。廣右在宋時，張栻出守靜江，民知向化，流風餘韻，至今猶存。馮京崛起慶遠，解、省、廷對，名皆第一，卒膺大拜。史稱其有中立不倚之操，則風化之、倡先之，未必無其人也。詩書士迨今亦且多矣，獨其間頑悍之習，猶使人不能無憾焉者，
translation_en:
…Gun [Chang Gun 常衮], serving as Surveillance Commissioner in Min, personally observed the courtesies of host and guest with the students. Only then did the people of Min come to appreciate literary learning, and Ouyang Zhan subsequently gained a place on the celebrated “Dragon and Tiger List” of successful examination candidates. Wu and Min were both formerly lands of Yue. Through the transforming influence of Taibo and Chang Gun, and the pioneering examples of Ziyou and Ouyang Zhan, they became eminent lands of the Odes and Documents, veritable coastal counterparts of Zou and Lu, the homelands of Mencius and Confucius.

In Guangyou, during the Song dynasty, Zhang Shi went out to serve as Prefect of Jingjiang, and the people learned to embrace moral transformation. The lingering influence of his example survives to this day. Feng Jing rose to prominence from Qingyuan, ranking first in the provincial and metropolitan examinations and the palace examination. He eventually received the grand appointment as Chief Councilor. The histories praise his integrity in standing firm in the middle way without partiality. Thus, this region has by no means lacked men to transform its customs and lead by example. By now, scholars versed in the Odes and Documents have also become numerous. Yet the persistence among them of stubborn and unruly habits still leaves one unable to feel entirely satisfied…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
豈以風化倡先之者吳閩則
肇自周唐之遠廣右僅啓於
有宋之近而其入人不能無
淺深之間也耶雖然以數與
時考之將必有裒然出而先
天下者矣諸士子果能脩於
身化於家推之鄉達之天下
===
由近而遠自易而難易異俗
而歸大同使我
聖朝之化如天之覆如地之載如
日月之照臨陰崖寒谷陽和
遍及頑悍之習罔有不率俾
不愧於同一古粵之區則人
必將稱之曰廣右有此人物
punctuated: 豈以風化倡先之者，吳閩則肇自周唐之遠，廣右僅啓於有宋之近，而其入人不能無淺深之間也耶？雖然，以數與時考之，將必有裒然出而先天下者矣。諸士子果能脩於身，化於家，推之鄉，達之天下，由近而遠，自易而難，易異俗而歸大同，使我聖朝之化，如天之覆，如地之載，如日月之照臨，陰崖寒谷，陽和遍及，頑悍之習，罔有不率，俾不愧於同一古粵之區，則人必將稱之曰：「廣右有此人物
translation_en: …Could it be because those who first promoted moral transformation in Wu and Min began as far back as the Zhou and Tang dynasties, whereas in Guangyou this began only as recently as the Song, so that its influence upon the people necessarily differs in depth? Even so, judging by the workings of destiny and the times, there will surely be those who emerge outstanding and take the lead throughout the realm. If you scholars can indeed cultivate yourselves, transform your households, extend this influence to your communities, and carry it throughout the realm—proceeding from near to far and from easy to difficult, changing divergent customs and bringing them into great concord—then you will make the transforming influence of our sagely dynasty like Heaven encompassing all, like Earth bearing all, and like the sun and moon shining upon all. Its springlike warmth will reach even shaded cliffs and cold valleys; those with stubborn and unruly habits will all submit to its guidance. Thus this region will have no cause for shame beside the other regions that once belonged to the same ancient Yue. People will then surely praise it, saying: “Guangyou has such men…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
如此無忝於古昔第一流人
物矣顧不偉歟諸士子幸相
與勉之
浙江衢州府龍游縣儒學教
諭朱麒謹序
punctuated:
如此，無忝於古昔第一流人物矣。顧不偉歟？諸士子幸相與勉之。
浙江衢州府龍游縣儒學教諭朱麒謹序。
translation_en:
…such as these, worthy of the foremost figures of antiquity. Would this not be magnificent? May you examination candidates encourage one another in this endeavor.
Preface respectfully written by Zhu Qi, Instructor in the Confucian School of Longyou County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
弘治五年廣西鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史祁司員〔宗規浙江山陰縣人戌戍進士〕
提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司右布政使黎福〔天與江西樂平縣人丙戌進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司左叅議吳昭〔守愚福建莆田縣人戊戌進士〕
監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使傅希說〔商佐山東武城縣人丙戌進士〕
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事陳烓〔文用福建閩縣人戌戍進士〕
===
考試官
浙江衢州府龍游縣儒學教諭朱麒〔汝祥福建懷安縣人丙午貢士〕
福建建寧府松溪縣儒學教諭趙堦〔文升浙江鄞縣人已酉貢士〕
同考試官
河南開封府睢州儒學學正陳珫〔廷珍湖廣漢陽縣人丙午貢士〕
浙江金華府武義縣儒學教諭林光重〔德輝福建莆田縣人丙午貢士〕
廣東潮州府饒平縣儒學教諭謝愷〔原仁福建莆田縣人已酉貢士〕
直隸鳳陽府壽州儒學訓導熊縝〔文密湖廣麻城縣人已酉貢士〕
江西廣信府儒學訓導余黙〔克容浙江龍游縣人已酉貢士〕
punctuated:
弘治五年廣西鄉試

監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史祁司員〔宗規，浙江山陰縣人，戌戍進士〕。

提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司右布政使黎福〔天與，江西樂平縣人，丙戌進士〕。
廣西等處承宣布政使司左叅議吳昭〔守愚，福建莆田縣人，戊戌進士〕。

監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使傅希說〔商佐，山東武城縣人，丙戌進士〕。
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事陳烓〔文用，福建閩縣人，戌戍進士〕。

考試官
浙江衢州府龍游縣儒學教諭朱麒〔汝祥，福建懷安縣人，丙午貢士〕。
福建建寧府松溪縣儒學教諭趙堦〔文升，浙江鄞縣人，已酉貢士〕。

同考試官
河南開封府睢州儒學學正陳珫〔廷珍，湖廣漢陽縣人，丙午貢士〕。
浙江金華府武義縣儒學教諭林光重〔德輝，福建莆田縣人，丙午貢士〕。
廣東潮州府饒平縣儒學教諭謝愷〔原仁，福建莆田縣人，已酉貢士〕。
直隸鳳陽府壽州儒學訓導熊縝〔文密，湖廣麻城縣人，已酉貢士〕。
江西廣信府儒學訓導余黙〔克容，浙江龍游縣人，已酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangxi Provincial Examination, Fifth Year of the Hongzhi Reign (1492)

Supervising Official
Qi Siyuan [?], Investigating Censor on an inspection tour of Guangxi, courtesy name Zonggui, was a native of Shanyin County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the year transcribed as 戌戍 [?].

Proctors
Li Fu, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangxi, courtesy name Tianyu, was a native of Leping County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.
Wu Zhao, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of Guangxi, courtesy name Shouyu, was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Examination Monitors
Fu Xishuo, Surveillance Commissioner of Guangxi, courtesy name Shangzuo, was a native of Wucheng County, Shandong, and a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.
Chen Wei, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Guangxi, courtesy name Wenyong, was a native of Min County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate of the year transcribed as 戌戍 [?].

Examiners
Zhu Qi, Instructor of the Confucian School of Longyou County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Ruxiang, was a native of Huai’an County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the bingwu year.
Zhao Jie, Instructor of the Confucian School of Songxi County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, courtesy name Wensheng, was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang, and a tribute scholar of the jiyou year [?, transcribed 已酉].

Associate Examiners

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
發憤忘食樂以忘憂
溥博如天淵泉如淵見而民莫不敬言而
民莫不信行而民莫不說
文王視民如傷望道而未之見武王不泄
邇不忘遠
易
大觀在上順而巽中正以觀天下
===
出可以守宗廟社稷以為祭主也
顯諸仁藏諸用
君子藏器於身待時而動何不利之有動
而不括是以出而有獲語成器而動
者也
書
詢于四岳闢四門明四目達四聰咨十有
二牧曰食哉惟時柔遠能邇惇德允
元而難任人
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

發憤忘食，樂以忘憂。

溥博如天，淵泉如淵。見而民莫不敬，言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。

文王視民如傷，望道而未之見。武王不泄邇，不忘遠。

易

大觀在上，順而巽，中正以觀天下。

出可以守宗廟社稷，以為祭主也。

顯諸仁，藏諸用。

君子藏器於身，待時而動，何不利之有？動而不括，是以出而有獲，語成器而動者也。

書

詢于四岳，闢四門，明四目，達四聰。咨十有二牧，曰：「食哉惟時！柔遠能邇，惇德允元，而難任人。」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

In his earnest striving he forgets to eat; in his joy he forgets his cares.

His breadth and vastness are like Heaven; his depth and inexhaustibility are like an abyss. When he appears, none among the people fail to respect him; when he speaks, none fail to trust him; when he acts, none fail to be pleased.

King Wen looked upon the people as though they were injured, and sought the Way as though he had yet to see it. King Wu did not slight those nearby or forget those far away.

Book of Changes

The great object of contemplation is above. Compliant and yielding, central and correct, he presents himself for the contemplation of all under Heaven.

On going forth, he can guard the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain, and serve as master of the sacrifices.

It is manifest in benevolence and concealed in its workings.

The gentleman keeps his capacities within himself and waits for the proper time to act. What could fail to be advantageous? When he acts, he is not constrained; thus, when he goes forth, he gains something. This speaks of one who acts only after his capacities are fully developed.

Book of Documents

He consulted the Four Mountains, opened the gates on all four sides, extended his vision in all four directions, and opened his hearing to all four quarters. He addressed the twelve regional governors, saying: “Food—see that it is provided in due season! Be gentle with those far away and kindly toward those nearby. Esteem virtue, trust the good, and keep deceitful men at a distance.”

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
三百里揆文教二百里奮武衛
月之從星則以風雨
天明畏弼我丕丕基
詩
赳赳武夫公侯腹心
我車既攻我馬既同四牡龐龐駕言徂東
赫赫明明王命卿士南仲大祖大師皇父
整我六師以脩我戎既敬既戒惠此
南國王謂尹氏命程伯休父左右陳
===
行戒我師旅率彼淮浦省此徐土不
留不處三事就緒
有飶其香邦家之光
春秋
元年 春王正月 天王使宰咺來歸惠
公仲子之賵〔隱公元年〕秋翬帥師 王
人子突救衛〔莊公六年〕季子來歸〔閔公元年〕
齊侯衛侯鄭伯來戰于郎〔桓公十年〕齊人衛
人鄭人盟于惡曹〔桓公十一年〕
punctuated:
三百里揆文教，二百里奮武衛。
月之從星，則以風雨。
天明畏，弼我丕丕基。

詩
赳赳武夫，公侯腹心。
我車既攻，我馬既同。四牡龐龐，駕言徂東。
赫赫明明，王命卿士：南仲大祖，大師皇父，整我六師，以脩我戎。既敬既戒，惠此南國。王謂尹氏：「命程伯休父，左右陳行，戒我師旅，率彼淮浦，省此徐土。不留不處，三事就緒。」
有飶其香，邦家之光。

春秋
元年，春，王正月。天王使宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵。〔隱公元年〕秋，翬帥師。王人子突救衛。〔莊公六年〕季子來歸。〔閔公元年〕齊侯、衛侯、鄭伯來戰于郎。〔桓公十年〕齊人、衛人、鄭人盟于惡曹。〔桓公十一年〕
translation_en:
Within three hundred li, attend to civil instruction; within the remaining two hundred li, exert military protection.
When the moon follows the stars, wind and rain result.
Heaven manifests its awe-inspiring power, assisting our great and enduring foundation.

Book of Odes
Valiant are the warriors, the trusted confidants of dukes and lords.
Our chariots have been made ready; our horses have been matched. The four stallions are mighty; we harness them and travel east.
Illustrious and resplendent, the king commands his high minister, the Grand Preceptor Huangfu, whose great ancestor was Nanzhong: “Set our six armies in order and prepare our forces. Be reverent and vigilant, and bring peace to these southern states.” The king tells the Yin officer: “Command Xiufu, Earl of Cheng, to array the ranks to left and right, put our troops on their guard, follow the banks of the Huai, and inspect this land of Xu. Neither linger nor tarry: bring the three undertakings into order.”
Rich is its fragrance, the glory of the state and ruling house.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In the first year, in spring, in the first month of the royal calendar. The Heavenly King sent Steward Xuan to bring funeral gifts for Duke Hui and Zhongzi. 〔First year of Duke Yin〕 In autumn, Hui led an army. Zitu, an officer of the king, came to the aid of Wei. 〔Sixth year of Duke Zhuang〕 Jizi returned. 〔First year of Duke Min〕 The Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Zheng came to wage battle at Lang. 〔Tenth year of Duke Huan〕 Men of Qi, Wei, and Zheng made a covenant at E’cao. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Huan〕

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
元年春王正月公即位〔文公元年〕
晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕
禮記
博聞强識而讓敦善行而不怠謂之君子
司徒脩六禮以節民性明七敎以興民德
齊八政以防淫一道德以同俗養耆
老以致孝恤孤獨以逮不足上賢以
崇德簡不肖以絀惡
古之聖人内之為尊外之為樂少之為貴
===
多之為美
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣
第貳場
論
孔子之道大而能博
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢諸儒講五經異同於石渠閣詔〔甘露三年〕
擬唐以魏徵為太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕
punctuated:
元年春，王正月，公即位。〔文公元年〕
晉陽處父帥師伐楚，以救江。〔文公三年〕

禮記
博聞强識而讓，敦善行而不怠，謂之君子。
司徒脩六禮以節民性，明七敎以興民德，齊八政以防淫，一道德以同俗，養耆老以致孝，恤孤獨以逮不足，上賢以崇德，簡不肖以絀惡。
古之聖人，内之為尊，外之為樂，少之為貴，多之為美。
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣。

第貳場
論
孔子之道大而能博。

詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢諸儒講五經異同於石渠閣詔。〔甘露三年〕
擬唐以魏徵為太子太師誥。〔貞觀十六年〕
translation_en:
In the first year, in spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke acceded to his position. 〔First year of Duke Wen.〕
Yang Chufu of Jin led an army to attack Chu in order to relieve Jiang. 〔Third year of Duke Wen.〕

Book of Rites
To be broadly learned and possessed of a strong memory, yet modest; to be earnest in good conduct and never slacken: this is what is called a gentleman.
The Minister of Education cultivates the six rites to regulate the people's dispositions, clarifies the seven teachings to promote their virtue, and orders the eight branches of government to prevent excess. He unifies moral principles to bring customs into accord, supports the aged to foster filial piety, cares for orphans and the solitary to aid those in want, honors the worthy to exalt virtue, and distinguishes the unworthy to suppress evil.
The sages of antiquity regarded inward observance as reverence and outward expression as joy; they esteemed fewness as precious and abundance as beautiful.
Only after attending court audiences do the feudal lords understand how to act as subjects.

Second Session
Discourse
The Way of Confucius is great and all-embracing.

Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One question from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict as if issued under the Han, directing the Confucian scholars to discuss agreements and differences concerning the Five Classics at the Shiqu Pavilion. 〔Third year of Ganlu.〕
Compose a proclamation as if issued under the Tang, appointing Wei Zheng Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. 〔Sixteenth year of Zhenguan.〕

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
擬立
皇太子正位東宮
賀表
判語〔五條〕
選用軍職
攬納稅粮
奏對失序
從征違期
干名犯義
===
第叄場
策〔五道〕
問帝王之德莫大於孝而其治天下亦莫
先於孝觀於帝舜以大孝而天下化武
王以達孝而下土式盖可見矣仰惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝御製大誥三編申明五常而首以
父子之親
太宗文皇帝御製孝順事實而首以虞書之克
punctuated:
擬立皇太子正位東宮賀表。

判語〔五條〕：選用軍職；攬納稅粮；奏對失序；從征違期；干名犯義。

第叄場
策〔五道〕
問：帝王之德，莫大於孝，而其治天下，亦莫先於孝。觀於帝舜以大孝而天下化，武王以達孝而下土式，盖可見矣。仰惟我朝太祖高皇帝御製《大誥》三編，申明五常，而首以父子之親；太宗文皇帝御製《孝順事實》，而首以《虞書》之「克
translation_en:
Compose a congratulatory memorial on the imagined occasion of the establishment of the Imperial Heir Apparent and his formal installation in the Eastern Palace.

Legal judgments〔five items〕: Selection and appointment of military officers; undertaking to remit tax grain on behalf of others; failure to observe proper order when responding to the throne; failure to meet the appointed deadline when joining a military expedition; violating hierarchical distinctions and moral obligations by bringing accusations against senior relatives.

Third Session
Policy questions〔five questions〕
Question: Among the virtues of emperors and kings, none is greater than filial piety; and in their governance of All under Heaven, nothing takes precedence over it. This can be seen in Emperor Shun, whose great filial piety transformed All under Heaven, and King Wu, whose consummate filial piety provided a model for the world below. Reverently considering our own dynasty: Emperor Taizu Gao personally composed the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements, elucidating the Five Constant Virtues and placing first the affection between father and son. Emperor Taizong Wen personally composed True Accounts of Filial Obedience, beginning with the words in the Book of Yu, “was able to…”

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諧齊栗
宣宗章皇帝御製五倫書而首以家人之父父
子子是其制作之盛足以為法於天下
可傳於後世
列聖之心蓋與舜武同一心也繼惟
皇上曩在春宮仁孝之聲聞于天下嗣登
大寶愛敬之誠洽于
重闈是其德教之至足以加于百姓刑于四海
皇上之心又與
===
列聖同一心也先儒論舜武之孝皆由庸行之
常推之以至其極而所謂極者莫大於
尊養之備稱號之隆而已然以尊養為
孝則後世之君尊養於其親者宜無不
備矣尊養果足以盡孝乎以稱號為孝
則後世之君稱號於其親者宜無不隆
矣稱號果足以盡孝乎夫大孝達孝皆
上聖事業也我
列聖之心既同乎舜武之心
punctuated: 諧齊栗。宣宗章皇帝御製《五倫書》，而首以《家人》之父父子子。是其制作之盛，足以為法於天下，可傳於後世。列聖之心，蓋與舜、武同一心也。繼惟皇上曩在春宮，仁孝之聲聞于天下；嗣登大寶，愛敬之誠洽于重闈。是其德教之至，足以加于百姓，刑于四海。皇上之心，又與列聖同一心也。先儒論舜、武之孝，皆由庸行之常，推之以至其極。而所謂極者，莫大於尊養之備、稱號之隆而已。然以尊養為孝，則後世之君尊養於其親者，宜無不備矣。尊養果足以盡孝乎？以稱號為孝，則後世之君稱號於其親者，宜無不隆矣。稱號果足以盡孝乎？夫大孝、達孝，皆上聖事業也。我列聖之心，既同乎舜、武之心，
translation_en:
… harmony, solemnity, and reverence. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang imperially composed the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), beginning with the statement in the Family hexagram that fathers should act as fathers and sons as sons. Such is the excellence of these writings that they can serve as models throughout the realm and be transmitted to later generations. The hearts of the successive sage emperors were indeed at one with those of Shun and King Wu.

We further reflect that, when His Majesty formerly resided in the Eastern Palace as heir apparent, his reputation for benevolence and filial devotion was known throughout the realm. Upon succeeding to the imperial throne, his sincere love and reverence suffused the inner palaces of his elders. Such is the perfection of his virtuous instruction that it can reach the common people and serve as a model throughout the Four Seas. His Majesty’s heart is likewise at one with those of the successive sage emperors.

Earlier Confucian scholars, discussing the filial piety of Shun and King Wu, held that both extended ordinary daily conduct to its utmost fulfillment. What they called its utmost fulfillment amounted to nothing greater than completeness in honoring and providing for one’s parents, and grandeur in the titles conferred upon them. Yet if honoring and providing for one’s parents constitutes filial piety, then surely later rulers should have been complete in every aspect of honoring and providing for their parents. Does honoring and providing for them truly suffice to fulfill filial piety? If conferring titles constitutes filial piety, then surely later rulers should have conferred titles of the greatest grandeur upon their parents. Does conferring titles truly suffice to fulfill filial piety? Great filial piety and universally acknowledged filial piety are both achievements of the highest sages. Since the hearts of our successive sage emperors were at one with those of Shun and King Wu …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇上之心又同乎
列聖之心而其為孝之極果安在乎夫孝也者
百行之本萬善之原可以動天地感鬼
神化强暴格鳥獸孚草木在匹夫尚然
况天子乎然則
皇上之孝由一念以充塞乎兩間皆諸士子耳
濡而目染必有能鋪張之者矣幸詳陳
以獻
問大學孔氏之遺書而初學入德之門也
===
朱子章句綱舉目張條分縷析無容議
矣然或問一書又所以發明章句未盡
之意學者類多忽而不講是以不能充
然有得今姑撮其大槩與二三子論之
明德新民止至善三綱領也世有不務
明德不屑新民而不求止至善者誰歟
格致誠正脩齊治平八條目也世有不
探其端而驟語其次者誰歟釋明德而
終帝典所言亦有序乎釋新民而先盤
punctuated:
皇上之心又同乎列聖之心，而其為孝之極果安在乎？夫孝也者，百行之本，萬善之原，可以動天地，感鬼神，化强暴，格鳥獸，孚草木。在匹夫尚然，况天子乎？然則皇上之孝，由一念以充塞乎兩間，皆諸士子耳濡而目染，必有能鋪張之者矣。幸詳陳以獻。
問：《大學》，孔氏之遺書，而初學入德之門也。朱子《章句》，綱舉目張，條分縷析，無容議矣。然《或問》一書，又所以發明《章句》未盡之意。學者類多忽而不講，是以不能充然有得。今姑撮其大槩，與二三子論之。明德、新民、止至善，三綱領也。世有不務明德、不屑新民，而不求止至善者，誰歟？格致誠正脩齊治平，八條目也。世有不探其端而驟語其次者，誰歟？釋明德而終《帝典》，所言亦有序乎？釋新民而先盤
translation_en:
…His Majesty’s heart likewise accords with the hearts of the successive sage emperors. Where, then, does the utmost perfection of his filial piety truly lie? Filial piety is the foundation of the hundred forms of conduct and the source of all goodness. It can move Heaven and Earth, stir ghosts and spirits, transform the violent, reach birds and beasts, and extend its influence even to plants and trees. If this holds even for an ordinary man, how much more so for the Son of Heaven? Thus His Majesty’s filial piety, extending from a single thought to fill the space between Heaven and Earth, is something all you examination candidates have absorbed through hearing and seeing. Surely some among you can expound it fully. Please set it forth in detail for presentation.
Question: The Great Learning is a surviving work of the school of Confucius and the gateway through which beginners enter into virtue. Master Zhu’s Chapters and Sentences sets out the main principles and their particulars, distinguishing each thread and analyzing every strand; it leaves no room for dispute. Yet his Questions and Answers further elucidates meanings not fully expressed in Chapters and Sentences. Students generally neglect this work and fail to study it, and consequently cannot attain a full understanding. Let us now select its main points for discussion with you.
Making bright virtue manifest, renewing the people, and resting in the highest good are the three guiding principles. Who are those in the world who do not strive to make bright virtue manifest, disdain renewing the people, and do not seek to rest in the highest good? Investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world are the eight items. Who are those in the world who fail to investigate their starting point yet hasten to speak of the subsequent stages? In explaining the manifestation of bright virtue, the discussion ends with the Canon of the Emperors: is there an order to what is said? In explaining the renewal of the people, why does it begin with the basin…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
銘所論果有義乎切磋琢磨於學問自
脩之功何所別聽訟無訟於明德新民
之義何所當有言格物致知所當先而
不可後者兩條可指明歟有言涵養本
原之功以為格物致知之本者五條可
歷數歟道有善惡也而誠意者何所先
心有體用也而正心者何所急且意誠
則心宜無不正矣何為有不在之語心
正則身宜無不脩矣何為有好惡之偏
===
仁讓言家貪戾言人而家與人果有別
乎首桃夭次蓼蕭終鳲鳩而三詩之序
亦有意乎至如孝弟慈三者釋齊家治
國既以為言矣而復見於治國平天下
之章不幾於重覆歟自身而家而國而
天下均為推己及人之事矣而釋傳者
一事自為一說若不能相通歟絜矩二
字平天下之要道也後人深得此章之
旨者誰耶敬之一字聖學之所以成始
punctuated: 銘，所論果有義乎？切磋琢磨，於學問自脩之功何所別？聽訟無訟，於明德新民之義何所當？有言格物致知所當先而不可後者，兩條可指明歟？有言涵養本原之功，以為格物致知之本者，五條可歷數歟？道有善惡也，而誠意者何所先？心有體用也，而正心者何所急？且意誠則心宜無不正矣，何為有不在之語？心正則身宜無不脩矣，何為有好惡之偏？仁讓言家，貪戾言人，而家與人果有別乎？首《桃夭》，次《蓼蕭》，終《鳲鳩》，而三詩之序亦有意乎？至如孝弟慈三者，釋齊家治國既以為言矣，而復見於治國平天下之章，不幾於重覆歟？自身而家而國而天下，均為推己及人之事矣，而釋傳者一事自為一說，若不能相通歟？絜矩二字，平天下之要道也，後人深得此章之旨者誰耶？敬之一字，聖學之所以成始
translation_en: …the basin inscription: does the discussion indeed have a significant purpose? How do cutting, filing, chiseling, and polishing differ in the work of learning and self-cultivation? How do hearing lawsuits and bringing it about that there are no lawsuits correspond to the principles of manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people? There are statements that investigating things and extending knowledge must come first and cannot be deferred: can you identify the two passages? There are statements concerning the work of nurturing the fundamental source as the foundation for investigating things and extending knowledge: can you enumerate the five passages? The Way has good and evil [?]; what, then, should take precedence in making the intentions sincere? The mind has substance and function; what, then, is most urgent in rectifying the mind? Moreover, once the intentions are sincere, the mind ought invariably to be rectified. Why, then, is there mention of its being absent? Once the mind is rectified, the person ought invariably to be cultivated. Why, then, are there biases in one's likes and dislikes? Benevolence and deference are spoken of in terms of the family, while greed and perversity are spoken of in terms of the individual: is there really a distinction between family and individual here? First comes “The Peach Tree Is Young and Tender” (Tao yao), next “The Tall Southernwood” (Liao xiao), and finally “The Cuckoo” (Shi jiu): does the sequence of these three poems also have a purpose? As for filial devotion, fraternal respect, and parental kindness, these three have already been discussed in explaining the regulation of the family and government of the state. Yet they appear again in the chapter on governing the state and bringing peace to all under Heaven. Does this not verge on repetition? From oneself to the family, to the state, and to all under Heaven, these are all matters of extending what is in oneself to others. Yet the commentator on the Commentary gives each matter a separate explanation, as though they could not be connected. Is that so? The two characters xie ju, ‘applying the measuring square,’ express the essential way to bring peace to all under Heaven. Who among later scholars deeply grasped the purport of this chapter? The single character jing, ‘reverence,’ is that by which the learning of the sages accomplishes its beginning…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而成終也後學能知用力之方者誰耶
凡此皆讀大學者之所當知而或問中
之所備載者也幸詳言之以觀窮經造
詣之學
問自古國家建立儲貳所以承宗廟之重
繫臣民之心事莫有大焉者也然易曰
蒙以養正聖功也書曰愼厥終惟其始
則教養輔翼之功尤當愼重於厥初焉
古者元子之生接以太牢負以卜士孩
===
提有教輔翼有人或問安於內竪或抗
法於魯公跡其德器治功之所成就卓
乎不可及已漢唐以来英君誼辟亦各
知所用心有委重二傅年甫十二輒通
論語崇尚儒學太子而下莫不受經其
人可指言歟有賜以帝範而極諫責之
羣臣導以師傅而每見必自先拜其人
可詳陳歟作書有法蓋有就學於資善
堂者矣而所輔之人何如師保賓客蓋
punctuated:
而成終也。後學能知用力之方者誰耶？凡此皆讀《大學》者之所當知，而《或問》中之所備載者也。幸詳言之，以觀窮經造詣之學。
問：自古國家建立儲貳，所以承宗廟之重、繫臣民之心，事莫有大焉者也。然《易》曰：「蒙以養正，聖功也。」《書》曰：「愼厥終，惟其始。」則教養輔翼之功，尤當愼重於厥初焉。古者元子之生，接以太牢，負以卜士；孩提有教，輔翼有人。或問安於內竪，或抗法於魯公。跡其德器、治功之所成就，卓乎不可及已。漢唐以来，英君誼辟亦各知所用心。有委重二傅，年甫十二輒通《論語》；崇尚儒學，太子而下莫不受經，其人可指言歟？有賜以《帝範》，而極諫責之羣臣；導以師傅，而每見必自先拜，其人可詳陳歟？作書有法，蓋有就學於資善堂者矣，而所輔之人何如？師保賓客，蓋
translation_en:
…and brings it to completion. Who among later students understood how to apply their efforts? All these are matters that readers of the Great Learning ought to know and that are fully treated in the Questions and Answers on the Great Learning. Please discuss them in detail, so that we may assess your scholarly attainment in thoroughly investigating the classics.
Question: Since antiquity, states have established heirs apparent to assume the weighty responsibility for the ancestral temples and secure the allegiance of officials and people. No matter is more important. Yet the Book of Changes says, “To nurture rectitude in the unenlightened is the work of a sage,” and the Book of Documents says, “To take care over the end, attend to the beginning.” Thus the work of educating, nurturing, assisting, and guiding an heir requires particular care at the outset. In antiquity, when the principal son was born, he was welcomed with a full sacrificial offering of an ox, a sheep, and a pig, and carried by an officer selected through divination. Instruction began in infancy, and men were appointed to assist and guide him. One inquired of a palace eunuch about his father's well-being; another upheld the rules before the Duke of Lu. When we trace their attainments in moral character, capacity, and the achievements of government, they stand so high as to be beyond reach. Since the Han and Tang, outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns have likewise understood where to direct their attention. One entrusted weighty responsibilities to two tutors, and at barely twelve years of age [the heir] already understood the Analects; another esteemed Confucian learning, so that everyone from the heir apparent down received instruction in the classics. Can you identify these men? One bestowed the Rules for Emperors (Difan) [on his heir] and charged his assembled officials with remonstrating to the utmost; another provided teachers and tutors to guide [his heir], and whenever he met them, invariably bowed first himself. Can you give a detailed account of these men? There were prescribed methods for writing, and there was indeed one who studied in the Zishan Hall; but what sort of person was the one being assisted? As for preceptors, guardians, and guest advisers, indeed…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
有處以耆舊老臣者矣而爲教之術安
在究其法意所存德業所就抑果有合
於古人否歟洪惟我
朝
列聖相承儲副之建
宮坊之制盖盡善而盡美矣然所以教之輔
之之道可述其一二乎較諸歷代亦果
有異同否乎諸士子豫養用世之學亦
必有見於此者矣願詳言之吾將以聞
===
于
上
問書曰學古入官易曰君子多識前言往
行以畜其德學固不可以不博也然考
諸往古驗其實用亦有不專於博者如
商周盛時賢才相望體用具備其人不
可尚已下此漢有論過伊管而治安一
策有救時弊學際天人而賢良三策切
中帝心固有可稱然亦有縁飾儒術而
punctuated:
有處以耆舊老臣者矣，而爲教之術安在？究其法意所存、德業所就，抑果有合於古人否歟？洪惟我朝列聖相承，儲副之建、宮坊之制，盖盡善而盡美矣。然所以教之輔之之道，可述其一二乎？較諸歷代，亦果有異同否乎？諸士子豫養用世之學，亦必有見於此者矣。願詳言之，吾將以聞于上。
問：書曰：「學古入官。」易曰：「君子多識前言往行，以畜其德。」學固不可以不博也。然考諸往古，驗其實用，亦有不專於博者。如商周盛時，賢才相望，體用具備，其人不可尚已。下此，漢有論過伊管，而治安一策有救時弊；學際天人，而賢良三策切中帝心，固有可稱。然亦有縁飾儒術而
translation_en:
…there were those who appointed venerable, longstanding ministers to these posts; but wherein lay their methods of instruction? Examining the intent underlying their arrangements and their achievements in virtue and accomplishment, did these indeed accord with those of the ancients? We reverently reflect that, in our dynasty, sage sovereigns have succeeded one another, and the establishment of the heir apparent and the organization of the Eastern Palace and its administrative offices have attained complete excellence and perfection. Yet could you describe some of the means by which the heir is instructed and assisted? Compared with successive dynasties, what similarities or differences are there? You candidates, cultivating in advance the learning needed for service in the world, must surely have insights into this matter. Please explain them fully; I shall report them to His Majesty.
Question: The Book of Documents says, “Study antiquity and enter office.” The Book of Changes says, “The gentleman acquaints himself widely with the words and deeds of the past, thereby nurturing his virtue.” Learning certainly must be broad. Yet if we examine antiquity and assess learning by its practical application, we also find cases in which breadth was not the sole consideration. In the flourishing ages of Shang and Zhou, worthy and talented men followed one another in succession, fully equipped in both substance and application; none could surpass them. Later, under the Han, there was one whose arguments surpassed those of Yi Yin and Guan Zhong, and whose single policy essay on order and security offered remedies for the troubles of his time; another whose learning encompassed Heaven and humanity, and whose three policy essays submitted in the examination for the worthy and good spoke directly to the emperor’s concerns. These certainly deserve praise. Yet there were also those who embellished their arguments with Confucian learning and…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曲學阿世博極羣書而劇秦美新至於
安社稷輔幼孤者乃在於少文不學之
人可歷指而言之歟唐有文過子房術
密賈誼而有内相之稱抵轢晉魏上軋
周漢而成潮陽之化固不可及然亦有
學比相如而名節蔑聞文學絕倫而才
猷靡邵至於陳十事獻六箴者乃出於
好獵任子之流可悉數而論之歟及宋
有文章名冠天下而著嘉祐之勳有文
===
學無所不通而致元祐之治學博之效
固有可見有如博學强記者疑可取也
而乃怙勢妬賢少習吏事者若可短也
而能定策開基何彼此之不同耶通今
學古者在所與也而乃變法誤國學術
不足者似可少也而能退敵弭兵何彼
此之有異耶夫以其博也而無益於治
以其不博也而有補於時則君子之學
果貴於博否乎雖然天下之理出於一
punctuated: 曲學阿世，博極羣書而劇秦美新，至於安社稷、輔幼孤者，乃在於少文不學之人，可歷指而言之歟？唐有文過子房、術密賈誼而有内相之稱，抵轢晉魏、上軋周漢而成潮陽之化，固不可及。然亦有學比相如而名節蔑聞，文學絕倫而才猷靡邵，至於陳十事、獻六箴者，乃出於好獵任子之流，可悉數而論之歟？及宋，有文章名冠天下而著嘉祐之勳，有文學無所不通而致元祐之治，學博之效，固有可見。有如博學强記者，疑可取也，而乃怙勢妬賢；少習吏事者，若可短也，而能定策開基，何彼此之不同耶？通今學古者，在所與也，而乃變法誤國；學術不足者，似可少也，而能退敵弭兵，何彼此之有異耶？夫以其博也而無益於治，以其不博也而有補於時，則君子之學果貴於博否乎？雖然，天下之理出於一
translation_en:
…distorted their learning to curry favor with their age, and ranged extensively through the collected writings yet condemned Qin and praised Xin. As for those who secured the altars of soil and grain and assisted young, orphaned rulers, they were instead men of little literary cultivation and no learning. Can you identify them individually and discuss them?

In the Tang, there was one whose literary ability surpassed Zifang’s and whose statecraft was more meticulous than Jia Yi’s, earning him the designation “Inner Grand Councilor”; and another whose writings eclipsed those of Jin and Wei and rivaled those of Zhou and Han, and who brought about the moral transformation of Chaoyang. These achievements were indeed beyond surpassing. Yet there were also those whose learning equaled Xiangru’s but whose reputation and integrity went unremarked, and those whose literary learning was peerless but whose talents and plans attained no distinction [?]. As for those who presented ten proposals or submitted six admonitions, they came instead from the ranks of men fond of hunting or appointed through hereditary privilege. Can you enumerate them all and discuss them?

Coming to the Song, there was one whose literary reputation ranked first in the realm and who performed distinguished service during the Jiayou era, and another whose literary learning encompassed everything and who brought about the good government of the Yuanyou era. The benefits of broad learning are certainly evident in these cases. A man of extensive learning and powerful memory might seem worthy of approval, yet he relied on powerful backing and envied the worthy. A man who had practiced administrative duties from youth might seem open to criticism, yet he was able to settle the succession and lay the dynasty’s foundations. Why were the two so different? A man versed in present affairs and learned in antiquity deserves our approval, yet he changed the laws and harmed the state. A man deficient in learning might seem deserving of scant regard, yet he was able to repel the enemy and bring warfare to an end. Why were the two so different?

If someone with broad learning contributes nothing to good government, while someone without it benefits his age, is breadth truly to be prized in the learning of a gentleman? Nevertheless, the principles of all under Heaven issue from a single…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
原而何以有取於博古今事物萬有不
齊而何以能致其博諸士子積學待用
有年請詳言之毋畧
問邦本固在於民國事莫大乎戎撫民勵
兵誠國家久安長治之策舍是非可以
言治也姑以廣西論之古號百粵之地
素為難治况邇年以来民敝兵壞莫此
為甚以民言則土曠人稀弱肉强食深
山大澤夷類十占八九窮簷部屋編氓
===
===
僅得二三師旅迭動其財已窮科差百
出其力已竭民敝若此司民牧者可忍
而不之究心哉兹欲祛除而撫摩之術
果安在以兵言則行伍空虛武備廢弛
粮餉稍緩剽掠遽及於省城勞苦窮年
役占無間於小大蠻寇肆暴而守卒逃
匿主将遇害而麾下坐視兵壞若此司
兵政者可忍而置諸度外哉兹欲飭治
而振起之計将安出夫法敝於今當稽
punctuated:
原，而何以有取於博？古今事物萬有不齊，而何以能致其博？諸士子積學待用有年，請詳言之，毋畧。

問：邦本固在於民，國事莫大乎戎。撫民勵兵，誠國家久安長治之策，舍是非可以言治也。姑以廣西論之，古號百粵之地，素為難治。况邇年以来，民敝兵壞，莫此為甚。以民言，則土曠人稀，弱肉强食；深山大澤，夷類十占八九；窮簷部屋，編氓僅得二三。師旅迭動，其財已窮；科差百出，其力已竭。民敝若此，司民牧者可忍而不之究心哉？兹欲祛除而撫摩之，術果安在？以兵言，則行伍空虛，武備廢弛；粮餉稍緩，剽掠遽及於省城；勞苦窮年，役占無間於小大；蠻寇肆暴，而守卒逃匿；主将遇害，而麾下坐視。兵壞若此，司兵政者可忍而置諸度外哉？兹欲飭治而振起之，計将安出？夫法敝於今，當稽
translation_en:
…source; why, then, should breadth of learning be valued? The affairs and things of past and present differ in countless ways; how can one attain comprehensive knowledge of them? You candidates have spent years accumulating learning while awaiting employment. Please explain this fully, omitting nothing.

Question: The foundation of the realm assuredly lies in its people, and no affair of state is greater than military affairs. Caring for the people and invigorating the troops are indeed the means of securing lasting peace and enduring good government for the state. Without these, one cannot speak of good government. Let us consider Guangxi. Anciently known as the land of the Hundred Yue, it has always been difficult to govern. Moreover, in recent years, nowhere has the exhaustion of the people and the deterioration of the troops been worse. As for the people, the land is extensive and sparsely populated, and the strong prey upon the weak. In the deep mountains and great marshes, indigenous peoples account for eight or nine out of ten; in humble dwellings [?], registered commoners number barely two or three. Repeated troop mobilizations have exhausted their wealth; levies and labor demands of every kind have drained their strength. With the people so exhausted, can those charged with governing them bear to give the matter no serious thought? If we now wish to remove these afflictions and care for the people, what methods can accomplish this? As for the troops, the ranks are depleted and military preparations neglected. At the slightest delay in provisions and pay, plundering immediately extends even to the provincial capital. Hardship and toil continue throughout the year, and the troops are appropriated for service by officials great and small alike. When indigenous raiders unleash violence, the garrison soldiers flee and hide; when their commanding general is killed, those under his command stand idly by. With the troops so deteriorated, can those responsible for military administration bear to leave the matter outside their consideration? If we now wish to restore discipline and revive the troops, what plan can we devise? When institutions have become defective in the present, we should investigate…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
諸古古之人有為鬱林太守而招降數
萬有為柳州刺史而流逋四歸有攝興
安而餽餉大為民利有知梧州而免稅
以為民便皆善於撫民者也果可施於
今乎有為桂州都督而息轉漕之勞有
為容管經畧使而貽詔答之榮有平邕
州之亂而廣人磨崖紀功有死靜江之
戰而部将自焚無降皆善於勵兵者也
果可用於今乎諸士子生長斯邦目擊
===
而心惟乆矣願為我陳之
punctuated: 諸古。古之人有為鬱林太守而招降數萬，有為柳州刺史而流逋四歸，有攝興安而餽餉大為民利，有知梧州而免稅以為民便，皆善於撫民者也。果可施於今乎？有為桂州都督而息轉漕之勞，有為容管經畧使而貽詔答之榮，有平邕州之亂而廣人磨崖紀功，有死靜江之戰而部将自焚無降，皆善於勵兵者也。果可用於今乎？諸士子生長斯邦，目擊而心惟乆矣，願為我陳之。
translation_en: …in antiquity. Among men of old, one served as Prefect of Yulin and induced tens of thousands to submit; one served as Prefect of Liuzhou, and displaced people and fugitives returned from all directions; one served as acting administrator of Xing'an, and his provision of military supplies greatly benefited the people; and one served as Prefect of Wuzhou and remitted taxes for the people's relief. All were adept at caring for the people. Can their methods indeed be applied today? One served as Area Commander of Guizhou and ended the burdens of grain transshipment; one served as Military Commissioner of Rongguan and earned the honor of an imperial reply; one quelled the rebellion in Yongzhou, and the people of Guang inscribed his achievements on a smoothed cliff face; and one died in the battle of Jingjiang, while his subordinate commanders burned themselves to death rather than surrender. All were adept at inspiring their troops. Can their methods indeed be employed today? You examination candidates were born and raised in this land; you have witnessed its circumstances and long pondered them. I ask you to set forth your views for me.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
發憤忘食樂以忘憂
黃犇
同考試官訓導余批題似易而難作者多
失之冗泛精緻者僅見此篇
考試官教諭趙批認理明措辭當可取
考試官教諭朱批簡明通暢可嘉
聖人自言其好學求之切而樂之深焉盖天下
===
之理必學之而後得也然則聖人未得而求之
切已得而樂之深其好學之篤爲何如哉想昔
吾夫子因子路不對葉公之問故告之以此若
謂吾之所以爲人無他惟篤於好學而已彼其
應事接物之間莫不各有本然一定之理方其
未有所得則理與我若有間也而憤可容已乎
殆必奮發激昂孳孳焉直欲求通夫此事之理
心一於是何食之暇計哉黽勉精進汲汲焉直
欲求達夫此物之理志有所在何食之暇念哉
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
發憤忘食，樂以忘憂。
黃犇

同考試官訓導余批：題似易而難，作者多失之冗泛，精緻者僅見此篇。
考試官教諭趙批：認理明，措辭當，可取。
考試官教諭朱批：簡明通暢，可嘉。

聖人自言其好學，求之切而樂之深焉。盖天下之理，必學之而後得也。然則聖人未得而求之切，已得而樂之深，其好學之篤爲何如哉？想昔吾夫子因子路不對葉公之問，故告之以此，若謂吾之所以爲人無他，惟篤於好學而已。彼其應事接物之間，莫不各有本然一定之理。方其未有所得，則理與我若有間也，而憤可容已乎？殆必奮發激昂，孳孳焉，直欲求通夫此事之理，心一於是，何食之暇計哉？黽勉精進，汲汲焉，直欲求達夫此物之理，志有所在，何食之暇念哉？
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“In his eagerness he forgets to eat; in his joy he forgets his cares.”
Huang Ben 黃犇

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: The topic appears easy but is difficult. Most writers fall into prolixity and vagueness; this is the only essay I have seen that is refined and precise.
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: Clear in its understanding of principle and apt in its wording; worthy of selection.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Concise, clear, fluent, and coherent; commendable.

The sage himself spoke of his love of learning: how earnestly he sought and how deeply he rejoiced in it. For the principles of all under Heaven can be apprehended only through learning. If, then, the sage sought so earnestly before apprehending them and rejoiced so deeply once he had apprehended them, how devoted must his love of learning have been!

Recall how our Master, because Zilu had not answered the Duke of She's question, instructed him with these words. It was as though he were saying: What makes me the person I am is nothing other than devotion to learning. In responding to affairs and engaging with things, each has its own inherent and fixed principle. Before I have apprehended it, there seems to be a separation between principle and myself. How, then, could my eager striving cease? Surely I must rouse myself with ardor and work unremittingly, intent only on comprehending the principle of this affair. With my mind wholly concentrated on it, what leisure have I to consider eating? Exerting myself diligently and advancing with urgency, I am intent only on grasping the principle of this thing. With my purpose thus engaged, what leisure have I to think of eating?

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
是何耶理無終窮不造其極自有不容於已者
耳及其既有所得則我與理若相契也而樂寧
有既乎殆見天君泰然靜與天游雖宮商相宣
不足以喻之矣外憂豈足以介于懷胷次悠然
動與天合雖律呂相和不足以方之矣外慮豈
足以動于内又何耶心無繫累獨得之妙自有
莫知其然者耳是則惟無憤也憤則自有以忘
乎食惟無樂也樂則自有以忘乎憂一憤一樂
循環代至吾之為人如斯而已矣抑觀聖人猶
===
天然天道有寒有暑而化工之妙以全聖人有
憤有樂而學問之功以備夫豈有所勉强於其
間哉乃若夫子之所自言一則曰好學二則曰
好學盖亦謙已誨人之意是不以既聖而自居
也然深味之則其全體至極純亦不已之妙有
非聖人不能及者亦在其中矣有志於希聖者
宜致思焉
溥博如天淵泉如淵見而民莫不敬言而
民莫不信行而民莫不說
punctuated:
是何耶？理無終窮，不造其極，自有不容於已者耳。及其既有所得，則我與理若相契也，而樂寧有既乎？殆見天君泰然，靜與天游，雖宮商相宣，不足以喻之矣，外憂豈足以介于懷？胷次悠然，動與天合，雖律呂相和，不足以方之矣，外慮豈足以動于内？又何耶？心無繫累，獨得之妙，自有莫知其然者耳。是則惟無憤也，憤則自有以忘乎食；惟無樂也，樂則自有以忘乎憂。一憤一樂，循環代至，吾之為人如斯而已矣。抑觀聖人猶天，然天道有寒有暑，而化工之妙以全；聖人有憤有樂，而學問之功以備。夫豈有所勉强於其間哉？乃若夫子之所自言，一則曰好學，二則曰好學，盖亦謙已誨人之意，是不以既聖而自居也。然深味之，則其全體至極、純亦不已之妙，有非聖人不能及者，亦在其中矣。有志於希聖者，宜致思焉。

溥博如天，淵泉如淵，見而民莫不敬，言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。
translation_en:
Why is this? Principle has no end or limit; until one reaches its utmost extent, one naturally cannot allow oneself to stop. Once one has attained understanding, however, the self and principle seem to accord with each other: how could joy ever come to an end? The mind, the ruler within, is at peace; in stillness it roams with Heaven. Even the answering notes of gong and shang cannot convey this joy. How could external sorrows intrude upon the heart? Within the breast all is serene; in activity one accords with Heaven. Even the harmony of the pitch pipes cannot compare with it. How could external concerns stir one within? Why, again, is this so? The mind is free of entanglements, and the subtle wonder of what one has personally apprehended naturally includes something whose workings no one can fathom. Thus, unless there is no ardent striving, striving naturally makes one forget food; unless there is no joy, joy naturally makes one forget sorrow. Striving and joy arrive in alternating cycles. This alone is the kind of person I am.

Consider, moreover, how the sage resembles Heaven. The Way of Heaven has cold and heat, through which the wondrous work of transformation is fulfilled; the sage has striving and joy, through which the work of learning is made complete. How could there be anything forced in this? As for the Master's own account of himself, he speaks of loving learning once, and then speaks of loving learning again. This surely expresses his intention to humble himself and instruct others: he does not claim the standing of one who has already become a sage. Yet if we ponder his words deeply, they also contain the wonder of his whole being reaching the utmost perfection, pure and unceasing—a state attainable only by a sage. Those intent on emulating sagehood should give this careful thought.

Vast and all-embracing like Heaven, a deep-flowing spring like the abyss: when he appears, none among the people fail to revere him; when he speaks, none fail to trust him; when he acts, none fail to be pleased.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
徐淮
同考試官教諭林批題本平易作者多不
精切此篇體認明白渾全是用錄出
考試官教諭趙批理明詞暢宜錄以式
後學
考試官教諭朱批體認精切必深於理
學者
中庸論至聖之德積於中也極其盛發於外也
當其可蓋有諸中必形諸外也孰謂聖德發見
===
之當其可不由於充積之極其盛者哉中庸三
十一章以小德川流言天道也且天下至聖聰
明睿知本於生知仁義禮智根於固有其積於
中固溥博淵泉而以時發見於外矣然豈止於
充積而已耶以溥博言之其大無外莫天若也
五者之德周遍廣闊一如天之大不可以限量
窺焉溥博而曰如天則充積之極其盛也可知
以淵泉言之其深無際莫淵若也五者之德靜
深有本一如淵之深不可以涯涘測焉淵泉而
punctuated:
徐淮

同考試官教諭林批：題本平易，作者多不精切。此篇體認明白渾全，是用錄出。

考試官教諭趙批：理明詞暢，宜錄以式後學。

考試官教諭朱批：體認精切，必深於理學者。

中庸論至聖之德，積於中也極其盛，發於外也當其可，蓋有諸中必形諸外也。孰謂聖德發見之當其可，不由於充積之極其盛者哉？中庸三十一章，以小德川流言天道也。且天下至聖，聰明睿知本於生知，仁義禮智根於固有，其積於中固溥博淵泉，而以時發見於外矣。然豈止於充積而已耶？以溥博言之，其大無外，莫天若也。五者之德，周遍廣闊，一如天之大，不可以限量窺焉。溥博而曰如天，則充積之極其盛也可知。以淵泉言之，其深無際，莫淵若也。五者之德，靜深有本，一如淵之深，不可以涯涘測焉。淵泉而
translation_en:
Xu Huai

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The topic is inherently straightforward, yet most writers fail to treat it with precision and relevance. This essay’s understanding is clear and fully integrated; for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: The principles are clear and the language flows freely. It should be included as a model for later students.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The understanding is precise and pertinent. The author must be deeply versed in the Learning of Principle.

In discussing the virtue of the utmost sage, the Doctrine of the Mean describes its accumulation within as reaching the fullest abundance, and its manifestation outwardly as perfectly appropriate. For what is possessed within must take form without. Who could say that the perfect appropriateness of sagely virtue’s manifestation does not arise from the fullest abundance of its accumulation? Chapter thirty-one of the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the Way of Heaven in terms of lesser virtues flowing like streams [?]. Now, in the utmost sage under Heaven, perceptiveness and sagacious understanding are based on knowledge possessed from birth, while benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom are rooted in what is inherently possessed. What accumulates within is indeed all-embracing and vast, deep and spring-like, and manifests itself outwardly at the proper times. Yet does it stop merely at accumulation? Speaking of its all-embracing vastness, nothing equals Heaven in being so great that nothing lies outside it. The five virtues extend everywhere in their breadth, just like the greatness of Heaven; they cannot be apprehended through finite measures. When this all-embracing vastness is described as “like Heaven,” we can recognize the fullest abundance of its accumulation. Speaking of its spring-like depth, nothing equals a deep pool in being unfathomably deep. The five virtues are still and deep, with a source, just like the depth of a pool; they cannot be measured by its banks and shores. As for its spring-like depth, and …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
曰如淵則充積之極其盛也可見夫聖德之盛
如此則其發於外者豈止於以時而已耶是故
見之於身則為德容動容周旋有以聳人之觀
瞻莫不敬之如神明矣形之於言則為德言渙
號宣布有以足人之聽聞莫不信之如蓍龜矣
施之於行則為德行政教覃敷足以感人之心
志而民又豈有不說乎夫聖德之發見而當其
可者如此非充積之盛曷克爾哉大抵莫強於
人心而可以德感莫柔於人心而不可以力服
===
聖人之德既極其盛則外有以正天下之觀内
有以通天下之志其敬信說服自有不期然而
然者矣抑豈止此哉聲名洋溢乎兩間尊親無
間於庶類德之所及直與天道脗合而為一焉
故曰配天
文王視民如傷望道而未之見武王不泄
邇不忘遠
宋澍
同考試官教諭謝批善形容文武憂勤惕
punctuated:
曰如淵，則充積之極，其盛也可見。夫聖德之盛如此，則其發於外者，豈止於以時而已耶？是故見之於身，則為德容，動容周旋，有以聳人之觀瞻，莫不敬之如神明矣；形之於言，則為德言，渙號宣布，有以足人之聽聞，莫不信之如蓍龜矣；施之於行，則為德行，政教覃敷，足以感人之心志，而民又豈有不說乎？夫聖德之發見而當其可者如此，非充積之盛，曷克爾哉？大抵莫強於人心，而可以德感；莫柔於人心，而不可以力服。聖人之德既極其盛，則外有以正天下之觀，内有以通天下之志，其敬信說服，自有不期然而然者矣。抑豈止此哉？聲名洋溢乎兩間，尊親無間於庶類，德之所及，直與天道脗合而為一焉。故曰配天。

文王視民如傷，望道而未之見；武王不泄邇，不忘遠。

宋澍

同考試官教諭謝批：善形容文武憂勤惕
translation_en:
…called “like an abyss,” the fullness of that accumulation, and its magnificence, can be seen. Since the sage’s virtue is so abundant, how could its outward expression amount merely to appearing at the proper time? Thus, when manifested in his person, it becomes a virtuous bearing: his movements and deportment inspire awe in those who behold him, and all revere him as they would a divine being. When expressed in speech, it becomes virtuous utterance: his proclamations are promulgated far and wide, fully satisfying those who hear them, and all trust him as they would the divining stalks and tortoise shells. When put into action, it becomes virtuous conduct: government and instruction spread broadly, moving people’s hearts and aspirations. How could the people fail to delight in him? Such is the manifestation of the sage’s virtue, always fitting the occasion. Without the abundance of its inward accumulation, how could this be achieved? In general, nothing is stronger than the human heart, yet virtue can move it; nothing is softer than the human heart, yet force cannot subdue it. Once the sage’s virtue reaches its fullest abundance, outwardly it sets right what all under Heaven behold, and inwardly it brings their aspirations into accord. Their reverence, trust, delight, and submission arise spontaneously, without being sought. But could it stop there? His fame fills the space between Heaven and Earth; all people alike honor and cherish him. The reach of his virtue accords perfectly with the Way of Heaven and becomes one with it. Hence the expression “matching Heaven.”

“King Wen regarded the people as though they were injured, and gazed toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it; King Wu did not slight those nearby or forget those far away.”

Song Shu

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: Skillfully portrays the anxious concern, diligence, and vigilance of Kings Wen and Wu…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
屬之意宛然在目可嘉可嘉
同考試官學正陳批題本正大作者皆蹈
襲陳言令人厭觀此篇融會傳註詞理俱到
真作手也是宜錄出
考試官教諭趙批文有發越可取
考試官教諭朱批詞理簡切佳作也
大賢舉二聖之事有不自足其所已足者有不
自忽其所易忽者蓋聖人之心一憂勤惕厲之
心也然則有周二聖之事雖若不同而此心寧
===
有異哉宜孟子並舉而言之也且夫當天下三
分有二之際而以服事殷者文王也文王之心
何心哉彼怙冒西土化行江漢民已安矣而文
也遹求厥寧遹觀厥成視咸和之民尚若瘡痍
之未瘳焉聰明齊聖徽柔懿恭道已至矣而文
也不顯亦臨無射亦保企精一之傳初若堂奧
之未窺焉謹怠荒於已治之餘加緝熈於既聖
之後可謂愛民深而求道切矣其不自足之心
為何如若夫纘太王王季文王之緒而遂有天
punctuated:
屬之意，宛然在目，可嘉可嘉。
同考試官學正陳批：題本正大，作者皆蹈襲陳言，令人厭觀。此篇融會傳註，詞理俱到，真作手也，是宜錄出。
考試官教諭趙批：文有發越，可取。
考試官教諭朱批：詞理簡切，佳作也。
大賢舉二聖之事，有不自足其所已足者，有不自忽其所易忽者。蓋聖人之心，一憂勤惕厲之心也。然則有周二聖之事雖若不同，而此心寧有異哉？宜孟子並舉而言之也。且夫當天下三分有二之際，而以服事殷者，文王也。文王之心何心哉？彼怙冒西土，化行江漢，民已安矣，而文也遹求厥寧，遹觀厥成，視咸和之民，尚若瘡痍之未瘳焉。聰明齊聖，徽柔懿恭，道已至矣，而文也不顯亦臨，無射亦保，企精一之傳，初若堂奧之未窺焉。謹怠荒於已治之餘，加緝熈於既聖之後，可謂愛民深而求道切矣。其不自足之心為何如？若夫纘太王、王季、文王之緒，而遂有天
translation_en:
…the sense of sustained vigilance is vividly before our eyes. Admirable, admirable!
Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor, comments: The topic itself is upright and grand, but writers all tread familiar paths and repeat stale expressions, making their work tiresome to read. This essay integrates the commentaries, achieving excellence in both expression and reasoning. Its author is truly an accomplished writer; it deserves to be included in the record.
Examiner Zhao, School Instructor, comments: The writing has expressive brilliance and merits selection.
Examiner Zhu, School Instructor, comments: Concise and apt in expression and reasoning—a fine composition.
The great worthy cites the deeds of two sages: one would not rest content with what was already sufficient; the other would not allow himself negligence in matters easily neglected. For the sage’s heart is wholly a heart of anxious diligence and vigilant self-discipline. Thus, although the deeds of the two sages of Zhou seem different, could their hearts have differed? It is fitting that Mengzi discusses them together. Now, the man who, even when he possessed two of the realm’s three parts, continued to serve Yin was King Wen. What kind of heart did King Wen possess? He sheltered and protected the western lands, and his transforming influence extended through the Jiang and Han regions. The people were already at peace; yet Wen still sought their tranquility and examined their accomplishments, regarding the people, though all lived in harmony, as if their wounds had not yet healed. Intelligent and perceptive, profoundly sagely, gracious and gentle, admirable and reverent, he had already attained the Way; yet Wen acted as though a higher presence watched over him even in unseen places, and maintained his devotion without weariness. He aspired to the transmitted teaching of refinement and single-mindedness, as though he had not yet glimpsed its innermost chambers. He guarded against indolence and neglect after good order had already been achieved, and further cultivated luminous virtue after he had already become a sage. Truly, his love for the people was profound and his pursuit of the Way earnest. How great was this heart that would never rest content! As for the one who continued the legacy of King Tai, Wang Ji, and King Wen, and ultimately came to possess all under Heaven…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
下者武王也武王之心何心哉彼邇者耳目之
所常接人易狎也武則聽微言如大政對僕御
如嚴賓初不以其邇而或泄焉遠者耳目之所
不及人易忘也武則視疎遠如左右慮千里於
几席初不以其遠而或遺焉存一敬於易泄之
時持一誠於易忘之頃可謂德之盛而仁之至
矣其不自忽之心又何如噫文武之事不同而
所以為憂勤惕厲則一此天理之所以常存而
人心之所以不死也歟抑不特此惡旨酒好善
===
言者禹此心也執中而立賢無方者湯此心也
思兼三王以施四事者周公亦此心也然文武
之聖上有以接禹湯之統下有以啓周公之傳
先後一揆父子一心此其所以開八百年之洪
基超二代而獨盛歟
易
出可以守宗廟社稷以為祭主也
黃鼒
同考試官訓導余批題本平易作者多不
punctuated:
下者，武王也。武王之心何心哉？彼邇者，耳目之所常接，人易狎也。武則聽微言如大政，對僕御如嚴賓，初不以其邇而或泄焉。遠者，耳目之所不及，人易忘也。武則視疎遠如左右，慮千里於几席，初不以其遠而或遺焉。存一敬於易泄之時，持一誠於易忘之頃，可謂德之盛而仁之至矣。其不自忽之心又何如？噫！文武之事不同，而所以為憂勤惕厲則一，此天理之所以常存，而人心之所以不死也歟？抑不特此，惡旨酒、好善言者，禹此心也；執中而立賢無方者，湯此心也；思兼三王以施四事者，周公亦此心也。然文武之聖，上有以接禹湯之統，下有以啓周公之傳。先後一揆，父子一心，此其所以開八百年之洪基，超二代而獨盛歟？
易
出可以守宗廟社稷，以為祭主也。
黃鼒
同考試官訓導余批：題本平易，作者多不
translation_en:
…was King Wu, who came to possess all under Heaven. What was King Wu’s heart like? People readily become overly familiar with those nearby, whom their eyes and ears constantly encounter. Yet Wu listened to modest words as though they concerned great affairs of government, and treated servants and charioteers as honored guests. He never allowed proximity to make him lax. Those far away lie beyond the reach of eyes and ears, and people readily forget them. Yet Wu regarded the distant as though they were at his side, and considered affairs a thousand li away while seated at his table. He never allowed distance to cause neglect. Maintaining reverence when laxity comes easily, and holding fast to sincerity when forgetfulness comes easily: this may indeed be called flourishing virtue and consummate benevolence. How great, then, was his refusal to grow careless!
Ah! The affairs of Wen and Wu differed, but their anxious diligence and vigilant self-discipline were one. Was this not why Heaven’s principle remained constantly present and the human heart did not become deadened? Nor was this true of them alone. Yu, who disliked fine wine and delighted in good words, had this heart; Tang, who held fast to the mean and appointed worthy men without restriction, had this heart; and the Duke of Zhou, who sought to combine the achievements of the Three Kings in carrying out four tasks, likewise had this heart. Yet the sagehood of Wen and Wu linked them above to the succession of Yu and Tang, and below opened the way for the tradition transmitted to the Duke of Zhou. Earlier and later rulers followed one standard; father and son shared one heart. Was this not how they laid the mighty foundation of eight hundred years, surpassing the two preceding dynasties in their exceptional flourishing?
Book of Changes
“On coming forth, he can guard the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain, and serve as master of the sacrifices.”
Huang Zi
