title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
原上文立說且分守宗社主祭作兩段殊失
本旨此作見理明措辭當宜録以為後學式
考試官教諭趙批說出長子之義可嘉
考試官教諭朱批簡明雄健宜冠本房
彖傳論儲君繼世足以承祀事之重焉盖儲君
天下本也自非震之長子曷克以繼世而承此
祀事之重也哉昔吾夫子傳震之彖至此推言
不喪匕鬯之義謂夫當震驚百里之時正驚遠
懼邇之日而震之長子恐懼為心而所執之匕
===
鬯不喪誠敬為念而所持之重器不失天命與
之人心歸之由是出而繼先世之統皇皇穆穆
于以宰制乎六合進而纘前人之緒赫赫明明
于以統御乎萬方彼宗廟之重未易守也今能
恐懼如此則可以守之而享祖宗於不已延國
祚於無疆而宗廟之神莫不依之而立矣豈不
可為宗廟之祭主乎社稷之大未易保也今能
誠敬如此則可以保之而享神明於无窮壯基
圖於不拔而社稷之神莫不由之而安矣豈不
punctuated:
原上文立說，且分守宗社、主祭作兩段，殊失本旨。此作見理明，措辭當，宜録以為後學式。
考試官教諭趙批：說出長子之義，可嘉。
考試官教諭朱批：簡明雄健，宜冠本房。
彖傳論儲君繼世，足以承祀事之重焉。盖儲君，天下本也。自非震之長子，曷克以繼世而承此祀事之重也哉？昔吾夫子傳震之彖，至此推言不喪匕鬯之義，謂夫當震驚百里之時，正驚遠懼邇之日，而震之長子恐懼為心，而所執之匕鬯不喪；誠敬為念，而所持之重器不失。天命與之，人心歸之。由是出而繼先世之統，皇皇穆穆，于以宰制乎六合；進而纘前人之緒，赫赫明明，于以統御乎萬方。彼宗廟之重，未易守也。今能恐懼如此，則可以守之，而享祖宗於不已，延國祚於無疆，而宗廟之神莫不依之而立矣。豈不可為宗廟之祭主乎？社稷之大，未易保也。今能誠敬如此，則可以保之，而享神明於无窮，壯基圖於不拔，而社稷之神莫不由之而安矣。豈不
translation_en:
…base their arguments on the preceding text; moreover, they divide guarding the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain and presiding over sacrifices into two separate sections, seriously missing the original meaning. This composition understands the principle clearly and expresses it aptly. It should be recorded as a model for later students.
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “It brings out the significance of the eldest son. Commendable.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Concise and clear, vigorous and forceful. It deserves first place among the scripts in this examination section.”
The Commentary on the Judgments discusses how the heir apparent, on succeeding to the throne, is fully capable of bearing the weighty responsibility of sacrificial service. The heir apparent is the foundation of all under Heaven. Unless he is the eldest son represented by Zhen, how can he succeed to the throne and bear this weighty sacrificial responsibility? When our Master Confucius composed his commentary on the judgment of Zhen, at this point he elaborated the meaning of “not losing the sacrificial ladle and aromatic wine.” He meant that when thunder startles people for a hundred li, frightening those far away and alarming those nearby, the eldest son represented by Zhen keeps apprehensive awe in his heart and does not lose the sacrificial ladle and aromatic wine he holds. With sincerity and reverence in his thoughts, he does not let slip the precious ritual vessels in his keeping. Heaven’s Mandate is bestowed upon him, and the people’s hearts turn to him. Thus he comes forth to succeed to the rule of his forebears, august and solemn, to govern the six directions; he advances to continue his predecessors’ work, illustrious and radiant, to rule the myriad regions.
The weighty charge of the ancestral temple is no easy thing to safeguard. Yet, capable of such apprehensive awe, he can safeguard it, offering sacrifices to his ancestors without cease and extending the dynasty’s allotted span without limit. All the spirits of the ancestral temple depend upon him for their enduring establishment. Can he not serve as the presiding sacrificer of the ancestral temple? The great charge of the altars of soil and grain is no easy thing to preserve. Yet, capable of such sincerity and reverence, he can preserve it, offering sacrifices to the spirits without end and making the foundations of dynastic rule unshakable. All the spirits of the altars of soil and grain thereby find repose. Can he not…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
可爲社稷之祭主乎吁極敬懼之心承祀事之
重震之長子其優於負荷也歟大抵莫爲之前
雖美弗彰莫爲之後雖盛弗傳君子創業垂統
固有光於家國矣不有儲君出而繼之則宗社
孰爲之守而祀事孰爲之主乎然則震之長子
其殆光前而裕後者歟
顯諸仁藏諸用
許紀
同考試官訓導余批本義顯藏二字作表
===
裏說場中多襲陳言體認不切令人厭觀是
篇發明顯仁藏用深得本旨宜錄
考試官教諭趙批辭達而已此篇庶乎
考試官教諭朱批發明顯藏二字得旨
著於外者造化之功斂於內者機緘之妙一道
之所寓也夫仁乃造化之功用乃機緘之妙也
然而所以顯之藏之何莫非斯道之所寓哉大
傳聖人論一陰一陽之道至此謂夫天地之間
莫非陰陽陰陽之道无非動靜是故自道之動
punctuated:
可爲社稷之祭主乎？吁！極敬懼之心，承祀事之重，震之長子，其優於負荷也歟！大抵莫爲之前，雖美弗彰；莫爲之後，雖盛弗傳。君子創業垂統，固有光於家國矣。不有儲君出而繼之，則宗社孰爲之守，而祀事孰爲之主乎？然則震之長子，其殆光前而裕後者歟！
顯諸仁，藏諸用。
許紀
同考試官訓導余批：本義顯藏二字作表裏說，場中多襲陳言，體認不切，令人厭觀。是篇發明顯仁藏用，深得本旨，宜錄。
考試官教諭趙批：辭達而已，此篇庶乎！
考試官教諭朱批：發明顯藏二字，得旨。
著於外者，造化之功；斂於內者，機緘之妙：一道之所寓也。夫仁乃造化之功，用乃機緘之妙也。然而所以顯之藏之，何莫非斯道之所寓哉？大傳聖人論一陰一陽之道，至此謂夫天地之間，莫非陰陽；陰陽之道，无非動靜。是故自道之動
translation_en:
…could he not serve as master of the sacrifices to the gods of soil and grain? Ah! With the utmost reverence and apprehension, he bears the weighty responsibility of sacrificial service. Is not the eldest son represented by Zhen especially well fitted to shoulder this burden? In general, without someone to precede him, even excellence cannot become manifest; without someone to follow him, even flourishing achievement cannot be transmitted. The noble man who establishes an enterprise and hands down its succession certainly brings glory to his house and state. Yet unless an heir apparent comes forward to succeed him, who will safeguard the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain, and who will preside over the sacrifices? Thus, is not the eldest son represented by Zhen one who brings glory to his predecessors and leaves abundance to his successors?
Manifest in benevolence, concealed in its functioning.
Xu Ji
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, an Assistant Instructor: The Original Meaning explains the two words “manifest” and “concealed” in terms of the outer and the inner. Many candidates here merely repeat conventional phrases, without grasping their meaning precisely, making their work tiresome to read. This essay elucidates manifestation in benevolence and concealment in functioning, thoroughly grasping the essential meaning. It merits inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Zhao, an Instructor: “Words need only convey the meaning.” This essay comes close to that!
Comment by Examiner Zhu, an Instructor: Its elucidation of the two words “manifest” and “concealed” captures their purport.
What becomes apparent externally is the achievement of creation and transformation; what is gathered within is the subtle working of its hidden mechanism. Both are where the single Way resides. Benevolence is the achievement of creation and transformation, while functioning is the subtle working of the hidden mechanism. Yet how could that which makes them manifest or concealed be anything other than a dwelling place of this Way? In the Great Commentary, the sage discusses the Way of alternating yin and yang. At this point, he means that between Heaven and Earth there is nothing other than yin and yang, and that the Way of yin and yang consists entirely in movement and stillness. Thus, considering the movement of the Way…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而行乎陽者言之則爲顯諸仁焉蓋必自内而
外自裏而表續生意於幾息之餘著貞性於幾
泯之後勾者萌甲者拆煥乎品物之咸章卵者
形胎者息蔚乎庶類之咸美凡其流動充滿而
不可掩者何莫非此造化之功乎此顯諸仁所
以爲用之迹德之發也自道之靜而具於陰者
言之則爲藏諸用焉蓋必自外而内由表而裏
歸已續之生意於中固既著之貞性於内脆者
堅華者實充然性命之各正大成大小成小□
===
然大和之保合凡其凝靜收斂而不可見者何
莫非此機緘之妙乎此藏諸用所以爲仁之心
業之本也吁一顯一藏而顯微無間曰仁曰用
而體用一源斯道運行於天地間曷嘗一息之
或停哉大抵此章論道之體用皆不外乎陰陽
也上文曰繼之者善成之者性蓋以賦受言此
曰顯諸仁藏諸用鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂蓋
以表裏言皆兼人物而通論之也若以流行不
息言之則繼而成成而復繼顯而藏藏而復顯
punctuated:
而行乎陽者言之，則爲顯諸仁焉。蓋必自内而外，自裏而表，續生意於幾息之餘，著貞性於幾泯之後。勾者萌，甲者拆，煥乎品物之咸章；卵者形，胎者息，蔚乎庶類之咸美。凡其流動充滿而不可掩者，何莫非此造化之功乎？此顯諸仁所以爲用之迹、德之發也。自道之靜而具於陰者言之，則爲藏諸用焉。蓋必自外而内，由表而裏，歸已續之生意於中，固既著之貞性於内。脆者堅，華者實，充然性命之各正；大成大，小成小，□然大和之保合。凡其凝靜收斂而不可見者，何莫非此機緘之妙乎？此藏諸用所以爲仁之心、業之本也。
吁！一顯一藏，而顯微無間；曰仁曰用，而體用一源。斯道運行於天地間，曷嘗一息之或停哉？大抵此章論道之體用，皆不外乎陰陽也。上文曰：「繼之者善，成之者性。」蓋以賦受言。此曰：「顯諸仁，藏諸用，鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂。」蓋以表裏言，皆兼人物而通論之也。若以流行不息言之，則繼而成，成而復繼，顯而藏，藏而復顯。
translation_en:
…and proceeds through yang, it is said to be “manifested in benevolence.” For it necessarily moves from within to without, from the interior to the exterior, renewing the impulse of life after it has almost ceased and manifesting the enduring nature after it has nearly vanished. Curled shoots sprout, seed coats split, and the myriad things become brilliantly manifest. Those born from eggs take shape, those borne in wombs grow, and the many kinds of beings flourish in all their beauty. Whatever flows forth and fills everything, so that it cannot be concealed—how could any of this fail to be the achievement of creative transformation? This is why “manifested in benevolence” constitutes the traces of functioning and the expression of inherent power. Speaking of the Way in its stillness, embodied in yin, it is said to be “concealed in functioning.” For it necessarily moves from without to within, from the exterior to the interior, returning the renewed impulse of life to the center and securing within the enduring nature already manifested. What is tender becomes firm; what flowers bears fruit. Each being’s nature and allotted life attain their proper fulfillment. The great fulfill themselves as great, the small as small, and the Supreme Harmony is preserved and united [preceding character illegible]. Whatever becomes still and gathered inward, so that it cannot be seen—how could any of this fail to be the subtle working of the hidden mechanism? This is why “concealed in functioning” constitutes the heart of benevolence and the foundation of achievement.
Ah! Now manifest, now concealed, yet there is no separation between the apparent and the subtle. Called benevolence or called functioning, substance and function have a single source. As this Way moves between Heaven and Earth, when has it ever stopped for even a single breath? Broadly speaking, this chapter’s discussion of the Way’s substance and function never goes beyond yin and yang. The preceding passage says: “What continues it is goodness; what brings it to completion is nature.” This speaks in terms of bestowal and reception. Here it says: “It is manifested in benevolence and concealed in functioning; it animates the myriad things without sharing the sage’s concerns.” This speaks in terms of exterior and interior. Both passages discuss human beings and other things together in general terms. If we speak of its ceaseless flowing operation, then continuation leads to completion, completion leads back to continuation, manifestation leads to concealment, and concealment leads back to manifestation…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
循環无端一生生而无窮矣故下文又曰生生
之謂易聖人之言各有攸當讀易者此又不可
不知
書
三百里揆文教二百里奮武衛
龍竒
同考試官教諭林批作此題者多不以禹
制服為重獨此得之且一結尤佳宜録以冠
本房
===
考試官教諭趙批文簡意足録之
考試官教諭朱批詞能達意可取
內治用乎文外治用乎武此聖人定綏服之制
也盖地有內外而治有文武勢固然也禹定綏
服而分為二等者如此其嚴華夏之辨何如哉
且夫水土既平法制斯定侯服之外有綏服焉
內取王城千里外取荒服千里以五百里之地
介乎內外之間聖人制治方畧能無異耶是故
內三百里密邇侯甸而安中國之治在所重也
punctuated:
循環无端，一生生而无窮矣。故下文又曰：「生生之謂易。」聖人之言，各有攸當，讀易者此又不可不知。

書
三百里揆文教，二百里奮武衛。
龍竒

同考試官教諭林批：「作此題者，多不以禹制服為重，獨此得之，且一結尤佳，宜録以冠本房。」
考試官教諭趙批：「文簡意足，録之。」
考試官教諭朱批：「詞能達意，可取。」

內治用乎文，外治用乎武，此聖人定綏服之制也。盖地有內外，而治有文武，勢固然也。禹定綏服而分為二等者如此，其嚴華夏之辨何如哉！且夫水土既平，法制斯定，侯服之外有綏服焉。內取王城千里，外取荒服千里，以五百里之地介乎內外之間，聖人制治方畧能無異耶？是故內三百里密邇侯甸，而安中國之治在所重也。
translation_en:
…cycling without beginning or end, a single process of generation and regeneration without limit. Thus the passage below also says: “Generation and regeneration are what is called change.” Each statement of the sage has its particular application; this, too, readers of the Book of Changes must understand.

Book of Documents
“For three hundred li, regulate civil instruction; for two hundred li, exert military defense.”
Long Qi

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Most who write on this topic fail to give due weight to Yu’s establishment of the service zones. This answer alone grasps it. Moreover, its conclusion is especially fine. It should be selected to head the selections from this examining room.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “The writing is concise and the meaning fully expressed. Select it.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The language conveys the meaning effectively. It merits selection.”

Civil means are employed in governing the interior, and military means in governing the exterior: this was the sage’s arrangement in establishing the Pacification Zone. Territory has its inner and outer divisions, and government its civil and military methods; the circumstances naturally require this. Such was Yu’s division of the Pacification Zone into two sections when he established it. How strictly he maintained the distinction marking off Hua-Xia, the civilized realm!

Once the waters and lands had been brought into order, laws and institutions were established. Beyond the Lords’ Zone lay the Pacification Zone. Inward lay the thousand li of the royal domain; outward lay the thousand li extending to the Wilderness Zone. With a territory five hundred li wide interposed between interior and exterior, could the sage’s methods of government be without differences? Thus the inner three hundred li closely adjoined the Lords’ and Royal Domains, and particular weight was placed upon government that secured the central lands.…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
禹於是而有揆文教之制焉揆之何如殆必學
校立焉人倫明焉而施為有其序五典敷焉民
則和焉而詳畧有其宜勞來匡直之政恒修禮
義仁讓之化有漸則所以治乎内者於是矣外
二百里聯屬要荒而安邊疆之治在所急也禹
於是而有奮武衛之制焉奮之何如殆必修車
馬也備器械也而嚴禦戎之具比什伍也時簡
教也而精練兵之方王靈布昭於遐服武備保
障乎群黎則所以治乎外者於是矣吁文武之
===
治既異華夏之辨自嚴聖人經理之周密有如
是哉雖然文武並用國家長久之道也史臣叙
禹定服似乃岐而二之何歟盖聖人之治各有
所主内治非無武也而以文為主外治非無文
也而以武為主初非各一其用而有所遺也其
視後世彼此偏廢卒以貽窮兵黷武之譏致夷
狄侵陵之患者詎可同日語哉此其制治之微
意讀者自當於書法之外求焉
天明畏弼我丕丕基
punctuated:
禹於是而有揆文教之制焉。揆之何如？殆必學校立焉，人倫明焉，而施為有其序；五典敷焉，民則和焉，而詳畧有其宜；勞來匡直之政恒修，禮義仁讓之化有漸，則所以治乎内者於是矣。外二百里，聯屬要荒，而安邊疆之治在所急也。禹於是而有奮武衛之制焉。奮之何如？殆必修車馬也，備器械也，而嚴禦戎之具；比什伍也，時簡教也，而精練兵之方。王靈布昭於遐服，武備保障乎群黎，則所以治乎外者於是矣。吁！文武之治既異，華夏之辨自嚴，聖人經理之周密有如是哉！雖然，文武並用，國家長久之道也。史臣叙禹定服，似乃岐而二之，何歟？盖聖人之治，各有所主。内治非無武也，而以文為主；外治非無文也，而以武為主。初非各一其用而有所遺也。其視後世彼此偏廢，卒以貽窮兵黷武之譏、致夷狄侵陵之患者，詎可同日語哉？此其制治之微意，讀者自當於書法之外求焉。

天明畏，弼我丕丕基。
translation_en:
…Yu accordingly established a system for ordering civil instruction there. How was this ordering carried out? Surely schools were established and human relationships clarified, so that measures were implemented in their proper sequence; the teachings governing the five relationships were disseminated and the people brought into harmony, with appropriate degrees of detail and simplicity. Policies to comfort the hardworking, encourage the people, and correct and rectify them were constantly maintained; transformation through ritual propriety, righteousness, benevolence, and deference proceeded gradually. Such were the means of governing the inner area.

The outer two hundred li adjoined the Yao and Huang zones, where securing the frontier was the urgent task of government. Yu accordingly established a system for strengthening military defenses there. How was this strengthening carried out? Surely chariots and horses were put in order and weapons and equipment prepared, making rigorous provision for resisting hostile incursions; men were organized into units of ten and five, and periodically inspected and trained, perfecting the methods of training troops. Royal majesty shone forth throughout the distant zones, and military preparations protected the common people. Such were the means of governing the outer area.

Ah! Once civil and military government were differentiated, the distinction marking off the civilized Xia realm naturally became strict. How thorough and meticulous was the sage’s ordering of affairs! Nevertheless, employing civil and military means together is the way to secure the state’s longevity. Why, then, does the court historian’s account of Yu’s establishment of the zones of service seem to divide them into two separate courses? In the sage’s government, each area had its own principal emphasis. Government of the inner area did not lack military measures, but gave priority to civil measures; government of the outer area did not lack civil measures, but gave priority to military measures. It was never a matter of using only one in each area and leaving something neglected. How could this be spoken of in the same breath as later ages, when one or the other was neglected, ultimately inviting criticism for exhausting military resources in reckless warfare or bringing the calamity of incursions and encroachment by the Yi and Di peoples? This is the subtle intent behind his system of government; readers should seek it beyond the manner in which the account is written.

Heaven, manifest and awe-inspiring, supports our exceedingly great foundation.

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
徐淮
同考試官教諭林批天明畏主今日卜吉
而言作者往往將預告之卜混講此篇體認
真切詞理俱優故錄之
考試官教諭趙批詞膽理明可嘉
考試官教諭朱批說出成王諭臣之意
宛然
賢王原天命之可畏實天眷之所存以見卜之
不可違也夫卜伐有殷而吉是明命可畏而天
===
眷周之意有在也成王原此以示邦君御事則
卜之不可違者可見矣且王之意若曰國有大
事當稽于天天有明命一寓於卜則卜之所在
天命之所在也彼夫往伐武庚蓋嘗求之卜矣
而朕卜有并吉之祥是上帝討罪之意昭告於
鑽灼之間凛乎其無赦可畏孰加焉徂征四國
我嘗决之龜矣而三龜有并吉之兆是上天禍
淫之命顯示於墨食之頃赫然其不僭可畏孰
甚焉然天之意果安在哉誠以今日之歷數即
punctuated:
徐淮

同考試官教諭林批：「天明畏，主今日卜吉而言。作者往往將預告之卜混講，此篇體認真切，詞理俱優，故錄之。」

考試官教諭趙批：「詞膽理明，可嘉。」

考試官教諭朱批：「說出成王諭臣之意，宛然。」

賢王原天命之可畏，實天眷之所存，以見卜之不可違也。夫卜伐有殷而吉，是明命可畏，而天眷周之意有在也。成王原此以示邦君御事，則卜之不可違者可見矣。且王之意若曰：「國有大事，當稽于天。天有明命，一寓於卜，則卜之所在，天命之所在也。彼夫往伐武庚，蓋嘗求之卜矣，而朕卜有并吉之祥，是上帝討罪之意，昭告於鑽灼之間，凛乎其無赦，可畏孰加焉？徂征四國，我嘗决之龜矣，而三龜有并吉之兆，是上天禍淫之命，顯示於墨食之頃，赫然其不僭，可畏孰甚焉？然天之意果安在哉？誠以今日之歷數即
translation_en:
Xu Huai

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “‘Heaven’s manifest awesomeness’ refers principally to the auspicious divination made on this occasion. Writers often confuse it with the earlier divination that gave advance notice. This essay grasps the meaning accurately and thoroughly, and excels in both expression and reasoning; hence its inclusion.”

Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “Bold diction [?] and clear reasoning: commendable.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “It vividly conveys King Cheng’s intent in instructing his ministers.”

The worthy king traced the awesomeness of Heaven’s mandate to its source and established where Heaven’s favor lay, thereby showing that the divination could not be contravened. The auspicious result of divining about an attack on Yin meant that Heaven’s manifest mandate was awesome, and that Heaven’s intention to favor Zhou had its purpose. King Cheng explained this to the lords of the states and the officers conducting affairs, making clear why the divination could not be contravened. The king’s meaning was as though he said:

“When the state has a great undertaking, it must consult Heaven. Heaven has a manifest mandate, expressed entirely through divination; thus, where the divination points, there Heaven’s mandate lies. As for going forth to attack Wu Geng, I have already sought guidance through divination. My divinations yielded uniformly auspicious signs: the intention of the Lord on High to punish guilt was clearly proclaimed through the drilling and scorching of the shells. Sternly admitting no pardon, what could surpass it in awesomeness? For the expedition against the four states, I have already sought a decision from the tortoise shells. All three tortoises yielded auspicious omens: High Heaven’s decree to bring calamity upon the wicked was revealed as the cracks consumed the ink marks. Majestic and unerring, what could be more awesome? Yet where, indeed, does Heaven’s intention lie? Truly, it is because the dynastic succession allotted to us today is precisely …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
武王之歷數基莫有大焉者也苟武庚不靖丕
基不幾於危乎兹盖使我肅將天威戡彼禍亂
于以奠安宗社而綿歷數於無疆也棐弼成我
之丕基而何今日之五服即武王之五服業莫
有大焉者也苟四國靡寧王業不幾於衰乎兹
盖使我奉行天討推彼敗亡于以指定疆土而
嗣五服於無窮也棐輔成我之大業而何夫天
之眷周驗諸卜而可見我之伐殷質諸天而無
疑爾邦君御事何乃欲違卜而勿征乎抑考武
===
王集大統而有天下凡以順天而應人也不期
而會者八百國人心從周可知矣夫何一傳而
至成王蠢爾四國乃敢動摇其間豈不以三監
有隙實有以啓之耶是以成王上原天命下憫
人窮而反覆終始乎卜之一言盖所以斷天下
之疑定天下之業而求匹休於前人也卒致罪
人黜服而為繼世之令主也宜哉
詩
赳赳武夫公侯腹心
punctuated:
武王之歷數，基莫有大焉者也。苟武庚不靖，丕基不幾於危乎？兹盖使我肅將天威，戡彼禍亂，于以奠安宗社，而綿歷數於無疆也。棐弼成我之丕基而何？今日之五服，即武王之五服，業莫有大焉者也。苟四國靡寧，王業不幾於衰乎？兹盖使我奉行天討，推彼敗亡，于以指定疆土，而嗣五服於無窮也。棐輔成我之大業而何？夫天之眷周，驗諸卜而可見；我之伐殷，質諸天而無疑。爾邦君御事，何乃欲違卜而勿征乎？抑考武王集大統而有天下，凡以順天而應人也。不期而會者八百國，人心從周可知矣。夫何一傳而至成王，蠢爾四國，乃敢動摇其間？豈不以三監有隙，實有以啓之耶？是以成王上原天命，下憫人窮，而反覆終始乎卜之一言，盖所以斷天下之疑，定天下之業，而求匹休於前人也。卒致罪人黜服，而為繼世之令主也，宜哉！

詩

赳赳武夫，公侯腹心。
translation_en:
…the dynastic allotment of King Wu: no foundation could be greater. If Wu Geng were not pacified, would this great foundation not be in danger? Heaven is thus surely directing me reverently to wield its might and quell that turmoil, thereby securing the ancestral temples and altars of state and perpetuating our dynastic allotment without limit. What could this be but Heaven’s aid in completing my great foundation? The five domains of submission today are those of King Wu: no undertaking could be greater. If the four states were not at peace, would the royal enterprise not approach decline? Heaven is thus surely directing me to carry out its punishment and bring about their defeat and destruction [?], thereby settling the boundaries of our territory and perpetuating our possession of the five domains without end. What could this be but Heaven’s aid in completing my great undertaking? Heaven’s favor toward Zhou can be seen by examining the divinations; my attack upon Yin, tested against Heaven’s will, admits of no doubt. Why, then, do you, rulers of states and officers conducting affairs, wish to defy the divinations and refrain from campaigning?

Now consider how King Wu assumed the supreme succession and possessed all under Heaven: it was entirely through obeying Heaven and responding to the people. Eight hundred states assembled without prior arrangement; from this we can know that the people’s hearts followed Zhou. How was it, then, that after only one succession, when the throne passed to King Cheng, those unruly four states dared to stir up turmoil? Was it not because discord among the Three Supervisors had indeed opened the way for them? Thus King Cheng looked upward to the source of Heaven’s mandate and downward with compassion upon the people’s distress. From beginning to end he returned repeatedly to the single matter of divination, seeking thereby to resolve the doubts of all under Heaven, secure the empire’s enterprise, and equal his predecessor’s glory. In the end, he brought the guilty to submission through punishment and became an excellent ruler who inherited the throne. How fitting!

Book of Odes

“Valiant are the warriors, the trusted confidants of dukes and lords.”

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
宋澍
同考試官教諭謝批題本冠冕塲中臆說
紛紛多以赳赳作才甚戾本旨此篇不惑衆
見察理詳明蓋嘗用心於詩者高薦何忝
同考試官學正陳批作此題者不泛則畧
求其認理精切措詞溫厚無踰此篇健羨健羨
考試官教諭趙批詞理豐贍
考試官教諭朱批以才立說得旨
詩人美武勇之賤者而同體於貴者此其才之
===
可用也夫以武勇野人而與公侯同心德則人
才之盛可見矣非蒙聖化其能然乎昔文王化
行俗美賢才衆多雖罝兎之野人而其才之可
用猶如此故詩人因其所事而美之及此意謂
當岐周興王之始適賢才輩出之時彼其肅肅
以罝兎者一田野之民耳設罝之間但見其如
熊如羆而有以振果敢之氣其武何赳赳也罝
兎於中林者一獵者之儔耳施罝之頃惟見其
如虎如貔而有以奮强壯之威其勇何赳赳也
punctuated:
宋澍。
同考試官教諭謝批：題本冠冕，塲中臆說紛紛，多以赳赳作才，甚戾本旨。此篇不惑衆見，察理詳明，蓋嘗用心於詩者，高薦何忝！
同考試官學正陳批：作此題者，不泛則畧。求其認理精切、措詞溫厚，無踰此篇。健羨，健羨！
考試官教諭趙批：詞理豐贍。
考試官教諭朱批：以才立說，得旨。
詩人美武勇之賤者而同體於貴者，此其才之可用也。夫以武勇野人而與公侯同心德，則人才之盛可見矣。非蒙聖化，其能然乎？昔文王化行俗美，賢才衆多，雖罝兎之野人，而其才之可用猶如此，故詩人因其所事而美之及此。意謂當岐周興王之始，適賢才輩出之時，彼其肅肅以罝兎者，一田野之民耳。設罝之間，但見其如熊如羆，而有以振果敢之氣，其武何赳赳也！罝兎於中林者，一獵者之儔耳。施罝之頃，惟見其如虎如貔，而有以奮强壯之威，其勇何赳赳也！
translation_en:
Song Shu.
Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: “The topic itself is dignified, yet conjectural interpretations abound among the examination candidates. Many take ‘martial’ to mean talent, greatly departing from the original purport. This essay is not misled by prevailing views; its examination of principle is detailed and clear. Its author has evidently devoted attention to the Book of Odes. What cause for embarrassment could there be in recommending it highly?”
Associate Examiner Chen, School Director, comments: “Those who write on this topic are either diffuse or cursory. For precise and penetrating understanding of principle and a gentle, generous choice of words, no essay surpasses this one. Admirable indeed, admirable indeed!”
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “Rich and ample in both expression and reasoning.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “By grounding its argument in talent, it grasps the purport.”
The poet praises men of martial courage who, though lowly, form one body with the exalted: this shows that their talents can be put to use. When rustic men of martial courage share the hearts and virtue of dukes and marquises, the abundance of talent becomes apparent. Could this be so unless they had received the transforming influence of a sage? Formerly, when King Wen’s transforming influence spread, customs were admirable and worthy men of talent were numerous. Even rustic men who set nets for rabbits possessed talents as serviceable as these. Thus the poet, taking their occupation as his starting point, extended his praise to this point. His meaning is that, at the beginning of Zhou’s rise to kingship at Qi, worthy men of talent were emerging in succession. Those who solemnly set nets for rabbits were merely people of the fields. Yet as they set their nets, one saw them like bears and great brown bears, displaying a resolute and daring spirit. How martial their prowess! Those who netted rabbits in the woodland were merely members of the hunting fraternity. Yet as they laid their nets, one saw them like tigers and fierce beasts, displaying the might of their strength. How martial their courage!

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
是武夫也沐聖德於綱紀之中沾神化於振作
之下其可用之才不與公侯同心德乎是故人
雖微也才則公侯之貴如輔相朝廷之政公侯
為國武夫亦為國其心與之同焉心之同者才
之同也豈特好仇而已哉事雖小也才則公侯
之大如參贊國家之務公侯為民武夫亦為民
其德與之同焉德之同者才之同也豈特善匹
而已哉吁野人有可用之才如此而文王德化
之盛因可見矣大抵天下之事有所為者必有
===
所益故勤於菑田者則以自養樂於植材者則
以自庇况善於作人者豈不得人以為用哉詩
人稱文王之作人則曰勉勉我王綱紀四方稱
文王之得人則曰濟濟多士文王以寧如此詩
之武夫則亦在其綱紀之中者矣易曰雲從龍
風從虎聖人作而萬物覩其文王之謂歟
赫赫明明王命卿士南仲大祖大師皇父
整我六師以脩我戎既敬既戒惠此南國
王謂尹氏命程伯休父左右陳行戒我師
punctuated:
是武夫也，沐聖德於綱紀之中，沾神化於振作之下，其可用之才不與公侯同心德乎？是故人雖微也，才則公侯之貴。如輔相朝廷之政，公侯為國，武夫亦為國，其心與之同焉。心之同者，才之同也，豈特好仇而已哉？事雖小也，才則公侯之大。如參贊國家之務，公侯為民，武夫亦為民，其德與之同焉。德之同者，才之同也，豈特善匹而已哉？吁！野人有可用之才如此，而文王德化之盛因可見矣。大抵天下之事，有所為者必有所益。故勤於菑田者，則以自養；樂於植材者，則以自庇。况善於作人者，豈不得人以為用哉？詩人稱文王之作人，則曰：「勉勉我王，綱紀四方。」稱文王之得人，則曰：「濟濟多士，文王以寧。」如此詩之武夫，則亦在其綱紀之中者矣。《易》曰：「雲從龍，風從虎，聖人作而萬物覩。」其文王之謂歟？

赫赫明明，王命卿士，南仲大祖，大師皇父：「整我六師，以脩我戎。既敬既戒，惠此南國。」王謂尹氏：「命程伯休父，左右陳行，戒我師
translation_en:
These martial men, bathed in the sage’s virtue within the order he established and touched by his wondrous transforming influence as he roused them to action—do they not, in their serviceable abilities, share the purpose and virtue of dukes and marquises? Thus, although their station is humble, their abilities possess the worth of dukes and marquises. In assisting with the government of the court, for example, dukes and marquises serve the state, and martial men likewise serve the state: their purpose is the same. Sharing the same purpose means sharing the same abilities. How could they be merely good companions? Although their tasks are small, their abilities possess the greatness of dukes and marquises. In helping to manage the affairs of the state, for example, dukes and marquises act for the people, and martial men likewise act for the people: their virtue is the same. Sharing the same virtue means sharing the same abilities. How could they be merely good partners? Ah! That men of the countryside possessed such serviceable abilities reveals the flourishing power of King Wen’s moral transformation. Generally, in the affairs of the world, whatever one undertakes must yield some benefit. Thus, those who diligently reclaim fields thereby provide themselves with sustenance; those who delight in planting timber thereby provide themselves with shelter. How much more must one who excels at nurturing men obtain men whose talents he can employ! Praising King Wen’s nurturing of men, the poet says: “Unremitting was our king; he ordered the four quarters.” Praising King Wen’s acquisition of worthy men, he says: “Numerous were the worthy officers; through them King Wen enjoyed tranquillity.” The martial men in this poem, too, were among those encompassed by his ordering influence. The Book of Changes says: “Clouds follow the dragon; winds follow the tiger. The sage arises, and all things behold him.” Does this not refer to King Wen?

Majestic and illustrious, the king commanded his high minister, the Grand Preceptor Huangfu, whose great ancestor was Nanzhong: “Set our six armies in order, and put our military affairs in readiness. Be reverent and vigilant, and bring peace to these southern lands.” The king said to the Yin officer: “Command Chengbo Xiufu to array the ranks on the left and right, and admonish our army …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
旅率彼淮浦省此徐土不留不處三事就
緒
陳堯道
同考試官教諭謝批見理明白行文條暢
宜置優列
同考試官學正陳批此題宣王自將以征
不庭命皇父休父治其軍事場中作者往往
認理不真立說穿鑿惟晚得此作理明詞順
非精於葩經者不能也宜錄出
===
考試官教諭趙批作大雅義當齊莊嚴
重此作得之
考試官教諭朱批斂繁就簡可佳
王者自將以伐遠既親命世臣以治其事復傳
命大臣以副其事盖軍事至重不可忽也今王
者既親命世臣以治之而又傳命大臣以副之
慎重其事也為何如哉昔宣王自將以伐淮北
之夷詩人作此以美之謂夫吾王當徐方不庭
之時動萬乘自將之舉故玉音渙發赫赫明明
punctuated:
旅，率彼淮浦，省此徐土，不留不處，三事就緒。
陳堯道。
同考試官教諭謝批：見理明白，行文條暢，宜置優列。
同考試官學正陳批：此題宣王自將以征不庭，命皇父、休父治其軍事。場中作者往往認理不真，立說穿鑿。惟晚得此作，理明詞順，非精於葩經者不能也，宜錄出。
考試官教諭趙批：作《大雅》義，當齊莊嚴重，此作得之。
考試官教諭朱批：斂繁就簡，可佳。
王者自將以伐遠，既親命世臣以治其事，復傳命大臣以副其事，盖軍事至重，不可忽也。今王者既親命世臣以治之，而又傳命大臣以副之，慎重其事也為何如哉！昔宣王自將以伐淮北之夷，詩人作此以美之。謂夫吾王當徐方不庭之時，動萬乘自將之舉，故玉音渙發，赫赫明明
translation_en:
…the troops; lead them along the banks of the Huai, inspect this land of Xu. Neither linger nor tarry; bring the three tasks to completion.

Chen Yaodao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: His understanding of the principles is clear, and his writing is coherent and fluent. This should be placed among the superior papers.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor (xuezheng): This topic concerns King Xuan’s personally commanding a campaign against those who would not acknowledge his court, and his ordering Huangfu and Xiufu to manage its military affairs. Writers in the examination hall frequently misunderstood the principles and advanced strained interpretations. Only late did we obtain this composition, whose reasoning is clear and whose language flows smoothly. No one without a thorough mastery of the Classic of Poetry could have achieved this. It should be transcribed for inclusion in the record.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: An exposition on the Greater Odes should be dignified, solemn, and weighty. This composition achieves that.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: It reduces complexity to simplicity. Commendable.

When a king personally commands a campaign against distant peoples, he first directly orders a hereditary minister to manage its affairs, then has orders conveyed to a high minister to assist in them. Military affairs are of the utmost importance and must not be neglected. Now, since the king has both directly ordered a hereditary minister to manage them and had orders conveyed to a high minister to assist, how great is the care with which he treats this undertaking!

Formerly, King Xuan personally commanded a campaign against the Yi peoples north of the Huai, and the poet composed this ode to praise him. Its meaning is that, when the region of Xu would not acknowledge the royal court, our king, sovereign of ten thousand chariots, undertook to command the campaign himself. Thus his royal words issued forth, awe-inspiring and manifestly clear…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而命卿士之謂南仲爲大祖兼大師而字皇父
者盖以文事武備而籌策素習也命之何如整
我從行之六軍而上下同心脩我敵愾之戎事
而器械精好師嚴器備而有制勝之勢所以然
者淮夷爲患南國爲之不寧當旣敬旣戒執訊
獲醜而惠此南方之國無擾攘之患焉有嚴有
翼聲罪致討而安此南土之人無侵凌之害焉
夫軍旅之事旣有大師以治之可無司馬以副
之乎於是王命以𠅘肅如絲如綸而詔尹氏策命
===
程伯休父而授以司馬之職者盖以料敵制勝
而計出萬全也命之何如使之左右陳行而無
愆於六步七步之法戒我師旅而無爽於六伐
七伐之律循彼淮浦而省徐州之土所以然者
師之久處農事爲之荒廢當式遄其歸無久留
於彼令三事得以就緒而俶載南畝也早畢其
事不久處於外令三農得以就業而有事西疇
也吁王者行師命臣分任其事如此則成自將
之功也可必矣雖然宣王之服淮夷豈特分命
punctuated: 而命卿士之謂南仲爲大祖、兼大師而字皇父者，盖以文事武備而籌策素習也。命之何如？整我從行之六軍，而上下同心；脩我敵愾之戎事，而器械精好。師嚴器備，而有制勝之勢。所以然者，淮夷爲患，南國爲之不寧。當旣敬旣戒，執訊獲醜，而惠此南方之國，無擾攘之患焉；有嚴有翼，聲罪致討，而安此南土之人，無侵凌之害焉。夫軍旅之事，旣有大師以治之，可無司馬以副之乎？於是王命以𠅘肅，如絲如綸，而詔尹氏策命程伯休父，而授以司馬之職者，盖以料敵制勝而計出萬全也。命之何如？使之左右陳行，而無愆於六步七步之法；戒我師旅，而無爽於六伐七伐之律；循彼淮浦，而省徐州之土。所以然者，師之久處，農事爲之荒廢。當式遄其歸，無久留於彼，令三事得以就緒，而俶載南畝也；早畢其事，不久處於外，令三農得以就業，而有事西疇也。吁！王者行師，命臣分任其事如此，則成自將之功也可必矣。雖然，宣王之服淮夷，豈特分命
translation_en:
…and he commanded the high minister who took Nanzhong as his great ancestor, concurrently held the office of Grand Preceptor, and bore the courtesy name Huangfu. This was because he was thoroughly versed in civil affairs, military preparations, and strategic planning. What did the king command him to do? To put in order the six armies accompanying him, so that superiors and subordinates would act with one mind; and to prepare the military measures for confronting the enemy, ensuring that weapons and equipment were excellent. With disciplined troops and equipment ready, they would be positioned to secure victory. The reason was that the Huai Yi were causing trouble, depriving the southern states of peace. He must be both vigilant and watchful, seize prisoners for interrogation and capture the enemy host, thus benefiting these southern states and freeing them from turmoil. With stern discipline and circumspection, he must proclaim the enemy’s offenses and carry out a punitive expedition, thus bringing security to the people of the southern lands and freeing them from aggression.

Since the Grand Preceptor already directed military affairs, could there be no Minister of War to assist him? Accordingly, the king’s commands were solemn [?], like silk threads and thick cords, and he ordered the Yin minister formally to appoint Chengbo Xiufu and confer upon him the office of Minister of War. This was because he could assess the enemy and secure victory, devising plans that left nothing to chance. What did the king command him to do? To arrange the ranks on the left and right without departing from the rule of advancing six or seven paces; to admonish our troops without violating the rule of striking six or seven times; and to follow the banks of the Huai and inspect the lands of Xuzhou. The reason was that a prolonged military presence would cause farming to fall into neglect. He must therefore hasten his return and not linger there, allowing the three kinds of work to proceed in order and cultivation to begin in the southern fields. He must finish his task promptly and not remain long abroad, allowing the farmers of the three kinds of land to resume their occupations and work in the western fields.

Ah! When a king leads an expedition and assigns his ministers their respective responsibilities in this way, success in his personal command can surely be assured. Nevertheless, was King Xuan’s subjugation of the Huai Yi due merely to his separately commanding…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
二臣指授方畧之得其宜而已盖由推赤心以
置其腹中耳故卒章曰王猶允塞徐方既來徐
方既同天子之功不然書何以曰至誠感神矧
茲有苗後之治夷者可以鑒夫
春秋
齊侯衞侯鄭伯來戰于郎〔桓公十年〕齊人衞
人鄭人盟于惡曹〔桓公十一年〕
季鑾
同考試官訓導熊批題目平易作者浮泛
===
不切惟此篇一本傳意而文足以發之殆行
空天馬自不羣也錄之
考試官教諭趙批融會傳註成文可取
考試官教諭朱批有斷制
列國兵舉於逞忿春秋既著其罪信講於固黨
春秋尤示其責此于郎書爵以來戰為罪惡曹
書盟以奪爵為貶觀春秋之書法而三國之罪
自見矣且魯桓非義得國而甞結援於諸侯齊
鄭投間濟私而因納交於我魯今何為而有郎
punctuated:
二臣，指授方畧之得其宜而已，盖由推赤心以置其腹中耳。故卒章曰：「王猶允塞，徐方既來。徐方既同，天子之功。」不然，《書》何以曰：「至誠感神，矧茲有苗。」後之治夷者，可以鑒夫！

春秋

齊侯、衞侯、鄭伯來戰于郎。〔桓公十年〕齊人、衞人、鄭人盟于惡曹。〔桓公十一年〕

季鑾

同考試官訓導熊批：「題目平易，作者浮泛不切。惟此篇一本傳意，而文足以發之，殆行空天馬，自不羣也。錄之。」

考試官教諭趙批：「融會傳註，成文可取。」

考試官教諭朱批：「有斷制。」

列國兵舉於逞忿，《春秋》既著其罪；信講於固黨，《春秋》尤示其責。此于郎書爵，以來戰為罪；惡曹書盟，以奪爵為貶。觀《春秋》之書法，而三國之罪自見矣。且魯桓非義得國，而甞結援於諸侯；齊鄭投間濟私，而因納交於我魯。今何為而有郎
translation_en:
…the two ministers and appropriately instructing them in strategy? Rather, it was because he offered them his utterly sincere heart, placing it within their very breasts. Thus the final stanza says: “The king’s counsels were truly sound; the people of Xu have come in submission. The people of Xu are now united: this is the Son of Heaven’s achievement.” Otherwise, why would the Book of Documents say: “Utmost sincerity moves the spirits; how much more these Miao”? Those who govern the non-Chinese peoples in later ages may take this as a lesson!

Spring and Autumn Annals

“The Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Zheng came to wage battle at Lang.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Huan〕 “Men of Qi, Wei, and Zheng covenanted at E’cao.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Huan〕

Ji Luan

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiong, Assistant Instructor: “The topic is straightforward, but writers have treated it superficially and missed the point. This essay alone is grounded throughout in the meaning of the commentary, and its prose adequately brings that meaning out. Like a heavenly horse coursing through the sky, it stands apart from the crowd. Selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “It integrates the commentaries and annotations into an essay worthy of selection.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “It shows decisive judgment.”

When the states raised troops to vent their anger, the Spring and Autumn Annals clearly recorded their guilt; when they pledged good faith to consolidate their faction, the Spring and Autumn Annals showed their culpability still more pointedly. Thus, in the entry concerning Lang, it records their noble ranks and treats their coming to wage battle as their offense; at E’cao, it records their covenant and expresses censure by stripping them of their ranks. Examining the wording of the Spring and Autumn Annals, the guilt of the three states becomes evident of itself. Now Duke Huan of Lu had acquired his state unrighteously and had sought support among the feudal lords. Qi and Zheng seized an opening to advance their private interests and consequently established friendly relations with our state of Lu. Why, then, was there now a military expedition at Lang…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之師乎盖鄭忽因救齊之有功怒魯以周班而
後已故要齊衛之兵特戰于郎之地聲威大奮
勢云强矣初非誅暴禁亂之舉甲胄長驅忿固
泄矣寧免悖道縱欲之譏夫兵凶戰危聖人所
慎也使其以道興師而伸討逆之義尚有可言
乃以私忿小怨親帥其師而戰于魯境尚為知
類也哉故春秋紀兵以受伐者為主此特列齊
衛鄭之爵而以來戰書者是主三國而罪之也
夫戰郎之師既□而怒魯之氣當舒又何為而
===
有惡曹之盟乎盖三君既思啟釁於魯恐其尚
懷報復之心即惡曹而為盟植私黨以自固詔
於鬼神惟圖以仇魯也而懲忿窒慾之義罔聞
誓於牲歃惟務以樹黨也而處已息爭之道安
在夫盟以長亂聖人所惡也使其講信脩睦以
公天下為事猶有可取顧乃私相要誓謀以敵
人而愈陷於惡尚為知義也哉故微者盟會不
志於春秋此盟實齊衛鄭之君而以人書者是
微三國而貶之也吁惡曹之三人即戰郎之三
punctuated: 之師乎？盖鄭忽因救齊之有功，怒魯以周班而後已，故要齊衛之兵，特戰于郎之地，聲威大奮，勢云强矣。初非誅暴禁亂之舉，甲胄長驅，忿固泄矣，寧免悖道縱欲之譏？夫兵凶戰危，聖人所慎也。使其以道興師，而伸討逆之義，尚有可言；乃以私忿小怨，親帥其師而戰于魯境，尚為知類也哉？故《春秋》紀兵，以受伐者為主。此特列齊衛鄭之爵，而以來戰書者，是主三國而罪之也。夫戰郎之師既□，而怒魯之氣當舒，又何為而有惡曹之盟乎？盖三君既思啟釁於魯，恐其尚懷報復之心，即惡曹而為盟，植私黨以自固。詔於鬼神，惟圖以仇魯也，而懲忿窒慾之義罔聞；誓於牲歃，惟務以樹黨也，而處已息爭之道安在？夫盟以長亂，聖人所惡也。使其講信脩睦，以公天下為事，猶有可取；顧乃私相要誓，謀以敵人，而愈陷於惡，尚為知義也哉？故微者盟會，不志於《春秋》。此盟實齊衛鄭之君，而以人書者，是微三國而貶之也。吁！惡曹之三人，即戰郎之三
translation_en:
…the military expedition at Lang? Hu of Zheng, having earned merit by rescuing Qi, resented Lu for placing him behind others according to the precedence established by Zhou. He therefore enlisted the troops of Qi and Wei expressly to fight at Lang. Their military prestige rose greatly, and their power could indeed be called formidable. Yet this was never an undertaking to punish violence and suppress disorder. Advancing far in armor, they certainly vented their anger; but could they escape the reproach of defying the Way and indulging their desires? Arms are inauspicious and warfare perilous: these are matters about which the sage is cautious. Had they raised troops in accordance with the Way and upheld the righteousness of punishing rebellion, something might still have been said in their defense. Instead, out of private anger and petty resentment, they personally led their armies to fight within Lu’s borders. Could they still be called capable of discerning proper distinctions? Thus, when recording military affairs, the Spring and Autumn Annals normally takes the state under attack as its principal subject. Here, however, it specifically lists the ranks of the rulers of Qi, Wei, and Zheng and records that they “came to do battle.” This makes the three states the principal subjects and condemns them.

Once the expedition that fought at Lang had [illegible character; ?], their anger toward Lu should have subsided. Why, then, was there also the covenant at E Cao? Having sought to provoke hostilities with Lu, the three rulers feared that Lu might still harbor thoughts of revenge. They therefore proceeded to E Cao and made a covenant, establishing a private alliance to secure themselves. In their declarations to the spirits, they sought only to act as enemies of Lu; nothing was heard of the principle of restraining anger and curbing desire. In swearing their oath and tasting the sacrificial blood, they strove only to build their faction. Where was the proper way of conducting themselves and ending contention? Covenants that foster disorder are what the sage detests. Had they cultivated good faith and harmonious relations, taking impartial concern for all under Heaven as their task, there would still have been something commendable. Instead, they privately bound one another by oaths and plotted to oppose others, sinking ever deeper into wrongdoing. Could they still be called people who understood righteousness? Thus, covenants and meetings of persons of low standing are not recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Those who made this covenant were actually the rulers of Qi, Wei, and Zheng, yet they are recorded merely as “men.” This reduces the standing of the three states and censures them. Ah! The three “men” at E Cao were precisely the three…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
君也一戰一盟而均失於義一爵一人而各致
其誅春秋之意夫豈苟然哉大抵春秋孔子之
刑書也褒善貶惡錙銖不爽隨事立義其變無
窮一人之身俄而進退焉豈特於此見之哉前
伐山戎書齊人後獻戎捷書齊侯則知伐戎者
即齊侯也上之會蜀書公子嬰齊下之盟蜀書
楚人則知盟蜀者即嬰齊也比事求之春秋懲
惡之義思過半矣先儒謂通於春秋然後能權
天下之事信哉
===
晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕
歐一清
同考試官訓導熊 批此題自有明傳易於
遣詞作者率多遺之惟此篇組織傳註發明
用兵之法筆勢雄偉讀之令人起敬
考試官教諭趙 批發明傳意殆無餘蘊
考試官教諭朱 批此篇深得本旨佳作也
伯國失恤患之道春秋紀用兵之法夫用兵貴
乎得宜也處父救江有愧於人多矣春秋得不
punctuated:
君也。一戰一盟，而均失於義；一爵一人，而各致其誅。春秋之意，夫豈苟然哉？大抵春秋，孔子之刑書也，褒善貶惡，錙銖不爽；隨事立義，其變無窮。一人之身，俄而進退焉，豈特於此見之哉？前伐山戎書齊人，後獻戎捷書齊侯，則知伐戎者即齊侯也。上之會蜀書公子嬰齊，下之盟蜀書楚人，則知盟蜀者即嬰齊也。比事求之，春秋懲惡之義，思過半矣。先儒謂通於春秋，然後能權天下之事，信哉！

晉陽處父帥師伐楚以救江〔文公三年〕
歐一清

同考試官訓導熊批：此題自有明傳，易於遣詞，作者率多遺之。惟此篇組織傳註，發明用兵之法，筆勢雄偉，讀之令人起敬。

考試官教諭趙批：發明傳意，殆無餘蘊。

考試官教諭朱批：此篇深得本旨，佳作也。

伯國失恤患之道，春秋紀用兵之法。夫用兵貴乎得宜也，處父救江，有愧於人多矣。春秋得不
translation_en:
…rulers. In the battle and in the covenant alike, they departed from righteousness; whether designated by noble rank or merely as “men,” each received his due condemnation. Could the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals possibly be arbitrary? In essence, the Spring and Autumn Annals is Confucius’s book of punishments. It praises good and censures evil without the slightest error; it establishes judgments appropriate to events, with inexhaustible variation. The same person may be elevated or degraded in rapid succession: is this the only place where we see it? In the earlier attack on the Shanrong, the text says “men of Qi”; in the later presentation of the spoils of victory over the Rong, it says “the Marquis of Qi.” Thus we know that the one who attacked the Rong was the Marquis of Qi himself. In the earlier meeting at Shu, it says “Prince Yingqi”; in the subsequent covenant at Shu, it says “men of Chu.” Thus we know that the one who covenanted at Shu was Yingqi himself. By comparing events and seeking their meaning, one has already gone more than halfway toward understanding the principles by which the Spring and Autumn Annals chastises evil. Earlier scholars said that only after comprehending the Spring and Autumn Annals could one weigh the affairs of the world. How true!

“Yang Chufu of Jin led an army to attack Chu in order to rescue Jiang.” 〔Third year of Duke Wen〕
Ou Yiqing

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiong, Assistant Instructor: “This topic has a clear explanation in the commentary, making it easy to formulate an answer, yet most writers neglect it. This essay alone weaves together the commentary and annotations to elucidate the methods of employing troops. Its writing has grandeur and vigor; reading it inspires respect.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “It elucidates the meaning of the commentary, leaving virtually nothing unexplored.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “This essay thoroughly grasps the essential purport. It is an excellent work.”

The hegemonic state failed in its duty to relieve distress; the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded the proper method of employing troops. In employing troops, what matters is acting appropriately. In rescuing Jiang, Chufu fell far short of others. Could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
致意於書法間哉昔者楚窺晋政挑釁圍江處
父先事而伐楚欲其引兵以自救其謀未為失
也胡為不足於春秋而書以耶盖嘗考諸經矣
楚始伐鄭齊桓合召陵之師而鄭患自弭又嘗
圍宋晋文角城濮之戰而宋禍以紓今江國小
而弱楚人圍之必不待舉國甲兵之衆以勢易
為力也楚當是時負覆載不容之罪以義所當
討也使晋襄果能謀如桓文命齊秦諸兵以剪
其羽翼率曲沃大衆直擣其腹心伸我王法問
===
彼悖逆楚必震恐而江圍自解矣豈不得用兵
之法哉何乃君怠臣昏計不出此獨遣處父之
孤軍遠攻陸梁之强國友邦未見其從征元惡
不聞其致討意者晋人於此豈誠心於伐楚哉
特恐失諸侯之好而姑以塞其責耳是以門于
方城而建旗未旆一遇息公而卷甲遂還一矢
莫加於楚秋毫無補於江既不如召陵之盟有
以服其心又不如城濮之戰有以聾其氣楚益
猖獗江竟滅亡晋實為之也善用兵者果如是
punctuated: 致意於書法間哉？昔者楚窺晋政，挑釁圍江，處父先事而伐楚，欲其引兵以自救，其謀未為失也。胡為不足於春秋，而書「以」耶？盖嘗考諸經矣：楚始伐鄭，齊桓合召陵之師，而鄭患自弭；又嘗圍宋，晋文角城濮之戰，而宋禍以紓。今江國小而弱，楚人圍之，必不待舉國甲兵之衆，以勢易為力也。楚當是時，負覆載不容之罪，以義所當討也。使晋襄果能謀如桓文，命齊秦諸兵以剪其羽翼，率曲沃大衆直擣其腹心，伸我王法，問彼悖逆，楚必震恐，而江圍自解矣。豈不得用兵之法哉？何乃君怠臣昏，計不出此，獨遣處父之孤軍，遠攻陸梁之强國？友邦未見其從征，元惡不聞其致討。意者晋人於此，豈誠心於伐楚哉？特恐失諸侯之好，而姑以塞其責耳。是以門于方城，而建旗未旆；一遇息公，而卷甲遂還。一矢莫加於楚，秋毫無補於江。既不如召陵之盟有以服其心，又不如城濮之戰有以聾其氣。楚益猖獗，江竟滅亡，晋實為之也。善用兵者果如是
translation_en:
…give particular attention to its manner of recording the event? Formerly, Chu watched for weaknesses in Jin’s government, provoked hostilities, and besieged Jiang. Chufu anticipated events by attacking Chu, intending to make it withdraw its troops to defend itself. His plan was not in itself mistaken. Why, then, did it fall short of the standards of the Spring and Autumn Annals, which recorded the event using the word yi, “in order to”?

I have examined this in the Classic. When Chu first attacked Zheng, Duke Huan of Qi assembled the army at Shaoling, and the danger to Zheng subsided of itself. When Chu later besieged Song, Duke Wen of Jin fought the battle of Chengpu, and Song’s calamity was thereby relieved. Now Jiang was a small and weak state. Chu certainly did not need to mobilize its entire armed forces to besiege it, since its superior position made the task easy. At this time, Chu bore guilt that neither Heaven nor Earth could tolerate, and righteousness demanded its punishment. Had Duke Xiang of Jin truly been able to devise plans like those of Dukes Huan and Wen, he could have ordered the troops of Qi, Qin, and the other states to clip Chu’s wings, and led the great host of Quwo straight against its heartland, upholding our royal law and calling Chu to account for its defiance. Chu would surely have trembled with fear, and the siege of Jiang would have lifted of itself. Would this not have accorded with the proper methods of warfare?

Why, then, were the ruler negligent and his ministers benighted, unable to devise such a plan, sending only Chufu’s isolated force to attack a powerful and unruly state far away? No friendly states were seen joining the expedition, nor was the chief offender heard to have received punishment. One wonders: were the men of Jin truly intent on attacking Chu? They merely feared losing the friendship of the feudal lords and acted perfunctorily to discharge their responsibility. Thus they reached the gates of Fangcheng and raised their banners, but had yet to unfurl them; upon encountering the Duke of Xi, they rolled up their armor and returned. Not a single arrow struck Chu, and not the slightest assistance reached Jiang. Their action neither subdued Chu’s heart, as the covenant of Shaoling had done, nor broke its spirit [?], as the battle of Chengpu had done. Chu became still more rampant, and Jiang was ultimately destroyed. Jin was truly responsible for this. Do those skilled in warfare really act in this way…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
乎故春秋於侵伐多不言所事此特書伐楚以
救江傳云以者不以者也言救江雖善而所以
救之者非其道矣其紀用兵之法為何如哉嗟
夫王風不競荆蠻暴橫其為患於中國久矣然
中國加兵於楚者僅有三處父救江有伐楚之
名而無討楚之實晋定召陵有伐楚之勢而僅
為侵楚之陋所謂彼善於此者其惟齊桓召陵
之師乎管仲相桓屈完受盟固其所也噫賢如
管仲乃能相君而成安攘之績彼處父者何以
===
為哉
禮記
司徒脩六禮以節民性明七教以興民德
齊八政以防淫一道德以同俗養耆老以
致孝恤孤獨以逮不足上賢以崇德簡不
肖以絀惡
蔣曙
考試官教諭趙批詞暢理明可取
考試官教諭朱批題本正大而組織傳
punctuated:
乎？故《春秋》於侵伐多不言所事，此特書「伐楚以救江」。傳云：「以者，不以者也。」言救江雖善，而所以救之者非其道矣。其紀用兵之法為何如哉？嗟夫！王風不競，荆蠻暴橫，其為患於中國久矣。然中國加兵於楚者僅有三：處父救江，有伐楚之名而無討楚之實；晋定召陵，有伐楚之勢而僅為侵楚之陋。所謂彼善於此者，其惟齊桓召陵之師乎？管仲相桓，屈完受盟，固其所也。噫！賢如管仲，乃能相君而成安攘之績，彼處父者何以為哉？
禮記
司徒脩六禮以節民性，明七教以興民德，齊八政以防淫，一道德以同俗，養耆老以致孝，恤孤獨以逮不足，上賢以崇德，簡不肖以絀惡。
蔣曙
考試官教諭趙批：「詞暢理明，可取。」
考試官教諭朱批：「題本正大，而組織傳
translation_en:
…could this be how one skilled in warfare acts? Thus, in recording incursions and punitive expeditions, the Spring and Autumn Annals usually does not state their purpose. Here alone it expressly records: “Attacked Chu in order to rescue Jiang.” The commentary says: “‘In order to’ means that the purpose was not fulfilled.” This means that although rescuing Jiang was good, the means used to rescue it were improper. How, then, does this record set forth the proper methods of warfare? Alas! The influence of the royal house had waned, and the barbarians of Jing acted violently and willfully. They had long afflicted the Central States. Yet there were only three occasions on which the Central States took up arms against Chu. Chufu’s rescue of Jiang bore the name of an attack on Chu but lacked the substance of a punitive expedition. Duke Ding of Jin’s undertaking at Shaoling had the outward force of an attack on Chu but amounted merely to a paltry incursion. As for what is called “one being better than another,” surely this applies to Duke Huan of Qi’s campaign at Shaoling! Guan Zhong assisted Duke Huan, and Qu Wan accepted the covenant: this was indeed the fitting outcome. Ah! Only someone as worthy as Guan Zhong could assist his ruler in achieving security at home and repelling threats from abroad. What could that Chufu accomplish?
Record of Rites
The Minister of Education cultivates the six rites to regulate the people’s dispositions, clarifies the seven teachings to foster their virtue, coordinates the eight measures of government to guard against excess, and unifies the Way and virtue to bring uniformity to customs. He cares for the aged to promote filial piety, relieves orphans and the solitary so that aid reaches those in need, exalts the worthy to honor virtue, and distinguishes the unworthy to reject evil.
Jiang Shu

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
註措詞莊重無如此篇是用錄出
大臣於鄉學必詳其教民取士之法也蓋教民
取士鄉學之政令也大臣於此烏可不詳其法
而總其政令哉且夫先王立鄉學之教必設大
司徒以總其政令然其教民取士之法當何如
哉彼民性非禮節之則易以流必脩冠昏喪祭
鄉相見之六禮以節民性使不至於流焉民德
非教興之則易以廢必明父子兄弟夫婦君臣
長幼朋友賓客之七教以興民德使不至於廢
===
焉八政不齊則亦禮教之害又必齊其飲食衣
服事為異別度量數制之八政以防民淫所以
使之無過行也道德異尚則其體不一又必一
其人所共由之道衆所同得之德以同民俗所
以使之無異習也六十曰耆七十曰老養耆老以
享食之禮則推愛親之心於是為至矣無父曰
孤無子曰獨恤孤獨以常餼之養則損有餘之
心無所不及矣至於能帥教而才德穎出者為
賢於賢者上之則命鄉論秀或升於司徒而名
punctuated:
註，措詞莊重，無如此篇，是用錄出。

大臣於鄉學，必詳其教民取士之法也。蓋教民取士，鄉學之政令也。大臣於此，烏可不詳其法而總其政令哉？且夫先王立鄉學之教，必設大司徒以總其政令，然其教民取士之法當何如哉？彼民性非禮節之，則易以流，必脩冠、昏、喪、祭、鄉、相見之六禮，以節民性，使不至於流焉。民德非教興之，則易以廢，必明父子、兄弟、夫婦、君臣、長幼、朋友、賓客之七教，以興民德，使不至於廢焉。八政不齊，則亦禮教之害，又必齊其飲、食、衣、服、事為、異別、度量、數制之八政，以防民淫，所以使之無過行也。道德異尚，則其體不一，又必一其人所共由之道、衆所同得之德，以同民俗，所以使之無異習也。六十曰耆，七十曰老，養耆老以享食之禮，則推愛親之心於是為至矣。無父曰孤，無子曰獨，恤孤獨以常餼之養，則損有餘之心無所不及矣。至於能帥教而才德穎出者為賢，於賢者上之，則命鄉論秀，或升於司徒而名
translation_en:
…the commentaries; its wording is dignified. No other essay equals this one, and it has therefore been selected for inclusion.

In overseeing the district schools, a high minister must thoroughly understand the methods of instructing the people and selecting worthy men. For instructing the people and selecting worthy men constitute the administrative business of the district schools. How could a high minister fail to understand these methods thoroughly and oversee their administration? When the former kings established instruction in the district schools, they necessarily appointed a Minister of Education to oversee its administration. But what should the methods of instructing the people and selecting worthy men be?

Unless ritual restrains the people's dispositions, they readily go astray. One must therefore cultivate the six rites—capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice, district drinking ceremonies, and formal meetings—to regulate the people's dispositions and keep them from going astray. Unless instruction fosters the people's virtue, it readily falls into neglect. One must therefore clarify the seven teachings governing fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers, husbands and wives, rulers and ministers, elders and juniors, friends, and hosts and guests, so as to foster the people's virtue and prevent its neglect.

If the eight regulations are not made uniform, this too harms ritual instruction. One must therefore bring into conformity the eight regulations concerning drinking, eating, clothing, attire, undertakings, distinctions, weights and measures, and numerical standards, to guard against the people's excesses and keep them from improper conduct. If people esteem different ways and virtues, the community lacks unity. One must therefore unify the Way that all people follow and the virtue that all share, thereby making popular customs uniform and preventing divergent practices.

Those of sixty are called seniors, and those of seventy elders. Supporting seniors and elders through the rites of feasting and feeding extends to the utmost the affection one bears one's own parents. Those without fathers are called orphans, and those without children are called the solitary. Caring for orphans and the solitary through regular provisions extends everywhere the intention to give from one's surplus.

Those who follow the teachings and stand out in talent and virtue are deemed worthy. To advance the worthy, the districts are ordered to assess their outstanding men; some are promoted to the Minister of Education and designated…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
選士或升於國學而名俊士其崇德也可見不
帥教而無善可録者為不肖於不肖者簡之則
命鄉習禮或移郊遂以示其不變或屏遠方而
示以不齒其絀惡也可知噫教民取士之法其
詳如此非大司徒總其政令孰能然哉雖然此
特鄉學教民取士之法耳下章有曰樂正崇四
術立四教順先王詩書禮樂以造士至於大樂
正論造士之秀者以告于王而升之司馬曰進
士此又言國學教國子民俊及取賢才之法也
===
蓋古者鄉學教庶人國學教國子及庶人之俊
而皆升其秀者而爵禄之此所以人無不學野
無遺賢治隆俗美而為王道之成也歟
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣
藍貴
考試官教諭趙 批簡明
考試官教諭朱 批辭理俱到發明武王
大教之意殆盡録之
聖王始制尊君之禮群臣自效尊君之誠夫禮
punctuated:
選士，或升於國學而名俊士，其崇德也可見。不帥教而無善可録者為不肖，於不肖者簡之，則命鄉習禮，或移郊遂以示其不變，或屏遠方而示以不齒，其絀惡也可知。噫！教民取士之法，其詳如此，非大司徒總其政令，孰能然哉？雖然，此特鄉學教民取士之法耳。下章有曰：「樂正崇四術，立四教，順先王詩書禮樂以造士。」至於大樂正論造士之秀者，以告于王，而升之司馬，曰進士，此又言國學教國子、民俊及取賢才之法也。
蓋古者鄉學教庶人，國學教國子及庶人之俊，而皆升其秀者而爵禄之。此所以人無不學，野無遺賢，治隆俗美，而為王道之成也歟？
朝覲然後諸侯知所以臣
藍貴
考試官教諭趙批：「簡明。」
考試官教諭朱批：「辭理俱到，發明武王大教之意殆盡，録之。」
聖王始制尊君之禮，群臣自效尊君之誠。夫禮
translation_en:
…“Selected Scholars”; others are advanced to the state school and designated “Outstanding Scholars.” His honoring of virtue is thus evident. Those who do not follow the teachings and have no goodness worth recording are deemed unworthy. He distinguishes these unworthy men, ordering them to practice ritual in the local community; some are transferred to the suburban and outer rural districts to mark their failure to reform, while others are banished to distant regions to show that they are excluded from the community. His rejection of wickedness can thus be understood. Ah! The methods for educating the people and selecting scholars were so detailed: who could have achieved this had the Minister of Education not coordinated their administration? Nevertheless, these are only the methods by which the local schools educated the people and selected scholars. The following chapter says: “The Director of Music gives prominence to the four arts and establishes the four teachings, following the former kings’ Poetry, Documents, Rites, and Music to train scholars.” It goes on to describe how the Grand Director of Music assesses the outstanding men among the scholars so trained, reports them to the king, and advances them to the Minister of War, calling them “Advanced Scholars” (jinshi). This, in turn, describes the state school’s methods for educating the sons of the nobility and outstanding men from among the people, and for selecting worthy talent.
In antiquity, the local schools taught commoners, while the state school taught the sons of the nobility and outstanding commoners. Both advanced their most excellent students and granted them rank and emoluments. Was this not why no one went untaught and no worthy man remained overlooked in the countryside, why government flourished and customs were admirable, and why the Kingly Way was brought to fulfillment?
“Only after attending court audiences do the regional lords understand how to act as subjects.”
Lan Gui
Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Concise and clear.”
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished. It elucidates almost exhaustively the intent of King Wu’s great teaching. Include it.”
The sage king first established the rites for honoring the ruler; his assembled ministers, for their part, demonstrated their sincerity in honoring him. Now, as for ritual …

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
莫尊於朝覲也然則群臣知自效其尊君之誠
者豈無所由來哉樂記論武王克商之後武功
告成而文教之誕敷封賞既行而禮制之當舉
彼其春見曰朝諸侯敬君之大禮也武王即位
之初遂制為朝禮以嚴上下之分所謂天子當
宁而立諸公東面諸侯西面之禮於是乎定矣
秋見曰覲諸侯尊君之大典也武王踐祚之始
即制為覲禮以明君臣之義所謂天子當依而
立諸侯北面而見之禮於是乎舉矣夫朝覲之
===
禮既有定制由是析圭儋爵而為公為侯者非
一臣也今則莫不再拜稽首於冕旒之前功罪
舉焉黜陟行焉而知所以臣者一天冠地屨之
截然也尊君之誠容有已乎分茅胙土而曰伯
曰子男者非一國也今則靡不對揚休命於阼
陛之下賞罰明焉予奪加焉而知所以臣者一
山高澤卑之自如也敬君之心容有間乎此朝
覲所以為大禮武王所以為大教也歟抑論武
王當商家之季興牧野之師救民於水火之中
punctuated: 莫尊於朝覲也。然則群臣知自效其尊君之誠者，豈無所由來哉？樂記論武王克商之後，武功告成，而文教之誕敷；封賞既行，而禮制之當舉。彼其春見曰朝，諸侯敬君之大禮也。武王即位之初，遂制為朝禮，以嚴上下之分，所謂天子當宁而立，諸公東面、諸侯西面之禮，於是乎定矣。秋見曰覲，諸侯尊君之大典也。武王踐祚之始，即制為覲禮，以明君臣之義，所謂天子當依而立，諸侯北面而見之禮，於是乎舉矣。夫朝覲之禮既有定制，由是析圭儋爵而為公為侯者，非一臣也。今則莫不再拜稽首於冕旒之前，功罪舉焉，黜陟行焉，而知所以臣者一，天冠地屨之截然也，尊君之誠容有已乎？分茅胙土而曰伯、曰子男者，非一國也。今則靡不對揚休命於阼陛之下，賞罰明焉，予奪加焉，而知所以臣者一，山高澤卑之自如也，敬君之心容有間乎？此朝覲所以為大禮，武王所以為大教也歟？抑論武王當商家之季，興牧野之師，救民於水火之中，
translation_en:
…none is more exalted than the court audiences. If so, could the assembled ministers’ understanding that they should themselves express their sincere reverence for their ruler have arisen without a cause? The Record of Music describes how, after King Wu conquered Shang, his military achievements were complete and civil instruction was widely disseminated; enfeoffments and rewards had been bestowed, and ritual institutions were due to be established. An audience in spring was called chao: this was the great rite through which the feudal lords showed respect for their ruler. At the beginning of his reign, King Wu accordingly instituted the spring audience rite to make strict the distinction between superior and inferior. Thus was established the prescribed ceremony in which the Son of Heaven stood in the courtyard gateway, with the dukes facing east and the marquises facing west. An audience in autumn was called jin: this was the great ceremony through which the feudal lords honored their ruler. At the outset of his accession, King Wu instituted the autumn audience rite to clarify the proper relationship between ruler and minister. Thus was put into practice the prescribed ceremony in which the Son of Heaven stood before the ceremonial screen and the feudal lords faced north to appear before him.

Once fixed regulations existed for these audiences, the ministers who received jade tablets and bore noble rank as dukes and marquises were many. Now all bowed twice and knocked their heads to the ground before the sovereign in his pendant-adorned crown. Their merits and offenses were brought forward, and demotions and promotions were carried out. They were united in understanding how to serve as ministers: the distinction was as sharp as that between Heaven above, like a cap, and Earth below, like shoes. Could their sincere reverence for their ruler ever cease? The states whose rulers received grants of thatch and land and were styled earls, viscounts, and barons were many. Now all acknowledged and extolled the gracious commands below the eastern steps of the throne hall. Rewards and punishments were made clear, and grants and deprivations were imposed. They were united in understanding how to serve as ministers: the relationship was as natural as mountains being high and marshes low. Could their respect for their ruler ever lapse? Is this not why the court audiences constituted great rites, and why King Wu made them a great means of instruction?

Furthermore, consider how King Wu, in the last days of the Shang house, raised the army that fought at Muye and rescued the people from water and fire…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
撥亂而歸之正大教之舉豈止此哉觀其習射
以貍首騶虞為節諸侯以裨冕搢笏為容明堂
耕籍養老之禮以次而行皆以一天下之制度
新天下之觀聽所以周道四達而禮樂交通也
孔子語賓牟賈武樂之遲而又久者其以此夫
第貳場
論
孔子之道大而能博
徐淮
===
同考試官教諭林批作者多於大博二字
分別不精理明詞暢者僅見是篇宜錄
考試官教諭趙批議論疊出詞理渾成
非筆端有造化者安能辦此
考試官教諭朱批論有抑揚有歸宿且
辭氣春容真佳士也
舉斯道之全體而獨歸於聖人善言聖人
者也夫道原于天而畀于人本至大而且
博也顧見之小者自失其大局於偏者自
punctuated:
撥亂而歸之正，大教之舉豈止此哉？觀其習射，以貍首、騶虞為節，諸侯以裨冕搢笏為容，明堂、耕籍、養老之禮以次而行，皆以一天下之制度，新天下之觀聽，所以周道四達而禮樂交通也。孔子語賓牟賈武樂之遲而又久者，其以此夫！

第貳場

論

孔子之道大而能博

徐淮

同考試官教諭林批：作者多於大博二字分別不精，理明詞暢者僅見是篇，宜錄。

考試官教諭趙批：議論疊出，詞理渾成，非筆端有造化者，安能辦此？

考試官教諭朱批：論有抑揚，有歸宿，且辭氣春容，真佳士也。

舉斯道之全體而獨歸於聖人，善言聖人者也。夫道原于天而畀于人，本至大而且博也。顧見之小者自失其大，局於偏者自
translation_en:
…He quelled disorder and restored right order. Surely his measures for providing great instruction extended beyond this! Consider how, in archery practice, the songs “The Wildcat’s Head” (Li shou) and “The Zouyu” (Zou yu) set the rhythm; how the regional lords presented themselves in ceremonial robes and caps, with their audience tablets tucked into their sashes; and how the rites of the Hall of Enlightenment, the ploughing of the ritual field, and the honoring of the aged were performed in due sequence. All these served to unify the institutions of the realm and renew what its people saw and heard. Thus the Way of Zhou reached in every direction, and rites and music circulated throughout. Was this not why Confucius, speaking to Binmou Jia, explained the delays and prolonged duration of the music of the Wu dance?

Second Session

Discourse

“The Way of Confucius Is Great and All-Embracing”

Xu Huai

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Most writers fail to distinguish precisely between the two words “great” and “all-embracing.” This is the only essay I have seen whose reasoning is clear and whose expression flows freely. It should be included in the record.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: Arguments unfold one after another, while expression and reasoning form an organic whole. How could anyone accomplish this without a creative power at the tip of his brush?

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The discourse has restraint and emphasis and reaches a definite conclusion. Moreover, its language and tone have the ease and warmth of spring. Truly an outstanding scholar!

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
狹其博而道之全體虧矣然則大以該其
博博以成其大舉全體而咸備於一身不
於聖人之歸而誰歸哉是其一理純全渾
淪而無外萬善畢具該貫而無遺無惑乎
門弟子不能徧觀而盡識也韓愈氏有見
于此而獨言之可謂善言聖人者矣請畢
其說天地生物而厚於人天地生人而厚
於聖人人也者道之寓也聖人者人之至
而斯道所由以傳者也然群聖相承至孔
===
子而獨盛聖道相傳至孔子而獨全道全
於孔子則其集群聖之大成而既大且博
也固宜且孔子之道何道也堯舜禹湯文
武周公之道也亦天下古今所共由之道
也然知之而不能有有之而不能咸者衆
矣道之全體惡乎備彼夷之清尹之任惠
之和幾于大矣而所就各倚於一偏何有
於博聃之禮弘之樂郯之官似乎博矣而
所知各局於一善何有於大下此則愈小
punctuated: 狹其博，而道之全體虧矣。然則大以該其博，博以成其大，舉全體而咸備於一身，不於聖人之歸而誰歸哉？是其一理純全，渾淪而無外；萬善畢具，該貫而無遺。無惑乎門弟子不能徧觀而盡識也。韓愈氏有見于此而獨言之，可謂善言聖人者矣。請畢其說。天地生物而厚於人，天地生人而厚於聖人。人也者，道之寓也；聖人者，人之至，而斯道所由以傳者也。然群聖相承，至孔子而獨盛；聖道相傳，至孔子而獨全。道全於孔子，則其集群聖之大成而既大且博也，固宜。且孔子之道何道也？堯舜禹湯文武周公之道也，亦天下古今所共由之道也。然知之而不能有，有之而不能咸者衆矣，道之全體惡乎備？彼夷之清、尹之任、惠之和，幾于大矣，而所就各倚於一偏，何有於博？聃之禮、弘之樂、郯之官，似乎博矣，而所知各局於一善，何有於大？下此則愈小
translation_en:
…narrow its breadth, and thus impair the Way in its entirety. Greatness, then, encompasses its breadth, and breadth completes its greatness. If the embodiment of its entirety, fully present in a single person, is not attributed to the sage, to whom could it be attributed? In him, the single principle is pure and complete, an undivided whole with nothing outside it; every goodness is fully present, comprehensively embraced with nothing omitted. It is no wonder that his disciples could not survey it in all its aspects and comprehend it completely. Han Yu perceived this and gave it particular expression: he may indeed be called one who spoke well of the sage. Allow me to explain this fully.

Heaven and Earth bring forth living things, but endow human beings most generously; they bring forth human beings, but endow sages most generously. Human beings are where the Way resides; sages are the highest perfection of humanity and those through whom this Way is transmitted. Yet, as the sages succeeded one another, only with Kongzi did their achievement reach its fullest flowering; as the Way of the sages was handed down, only with Kongzi did it attain completeness. Since the Way was complete in Kongzi, it was surely fitting that he brought together the consummate achievements of all the sages and was both great and broad in scope. And what Way was Kongzi’s Way? It was the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and Zhou Gong, and also the Way followed in common by all under Heaven, past and present.

Yet many know it without being able to embody it, or embody it without being able to encompass it all. In whom, then, is the Way present in its entirety? The purity of Bo Yi, the responsibility assumed by Yi Yin, and the harmony of Liuxia Hui approached greatness; yet each attained only one aspect. How could they possess breadth? Lao Dan’s knowledge of ritual, Chang Hong’s of music, and the Viscount of Tan’s of official institutions seem broad; yet each person’s knowledge was confined to a single excellence. How could they possess greatness? Below these, attainments become ever smaller…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
愈狹初不足以企吾道之彷彿其視所謂
大者博者何物耶學者欲識斯道之全曷
不於孔子而觀之乎是故仁義禮智其性
也而一由於天縱親義序别信其用也而
一出於安行仰之彌高鑽之彌堅何窮盡
也瞻之在前忽焉在後何方體也語其所
至渾然如元氣流行而諸子之清之任之
和直道中之一端耳曾足以方其大耶古
今事變貫徹於敏求之餘物理精粗昭融
===
於默識之表釣弋獵較事至微也而無乎
不能乘田委吏職至卑也而無乎不稱究
其所有充然如萬象森列而諸子之禮之
樂之官僅道中之一藝耳曾足以擬其博
耶譬諸天輕清在上穹然其形也而日月
行焉星辰繫焉舉萬物而無不覆譬諸地
重濁在下隤然其質也而華岳峙焉河海
振焉舉萬物而無不載聖人之道天地之
道也知天地則知聖人矣是則非大無以
punctuated: 愈狹，初不足以企吾道之彷彿，其視所謂大者博者何物耶？學者欲識斯道之全，曷不於孔子而觀之乎？是故仁義禮智，其性也，而一由於天縱；親義序别信，其用也，而一出於安行。仰之彌高，鑽之彌堅，何窮盡也？瞻之在前，忽焉在後，何方體也？語其所至，渾然如元氣流行，而諸子之清之任之和，直道中之一端耳，曾足以方其大耶？古今事變，貫徹於敏求之餘；物理精粗，昭融於默識之表。釣弋獵較，事至微也，而無乎不能；乘田委吏，職至卑也，而無乎不稱。究其所有，充然如萬象森列，而諸子之禮之樂之官，僅道中之一藝耳，曾足以擬其博耶？譬諸天，輕清在上，穹然其形也，而日月行焉，星辰繫焉，舉萬物而無不覆；譬諸地，重濁在下，隤然其質也，而華岳峙焉，河海振焉，舉萬物而無不載。聖人之道，天地之道也，知天地則知聖人矣。是則非大無以
translation_en: …and ever narrower, wholly insufficient even to approach a semblance of our Way. What could they amount to when measured against what is called great and broad? If students wish to understand this Way in its entirety, why do they not look to Confucius? Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom constituted his nature, all bestowed by Heaven; affection, righteousness, order, distinction, and trustworthiness constituted its practical expression, all proceeding from effortless conduct. Looking up, one finds it ever higher; boring into it, one finds it ever harder. How could it be exhausted? One sees it ahead, and suddenly it is behind. What fixed location or form could it have? Speaking of his attainment, it was an integrated whole, like the primal vital force flowing everywhere. The purity, responsibility, and harmony of the other masters were merely single aspects of the Way: could they possibly equal its greatness? The events and changes of past and present were thoroughly comprehended through his diligent inquiry, with capacity to spare; the principles of things, both fine and coarse, were luminously understood beyond what he silently retained. Fishing with a line, shooting birds with a corded arrow, and competing in the hunt were exceedingly minor activities, yet there was none he could not perform. Keeper of livestock and granary clerk were exceedingly humble offices, yet in neither did he fail to discharge his duties fittingly. Examining all that he possessed, one finds it abundant, like the myriad phenomena arrayed in profusion. The other masters’ knowledge of ritual, music, and offices amounted merely to individual arts within the Way: could these possibly match its breadth? Compare it to Heaven: light and clear above, vaulted in form, with sun and moon moving through it and stars fastened to it, it covers every one of the myriad things. Compare it to Earth: heavy and turbid below, settled in substance, with Mount Hua and the other great peaks towering upon it and rivers and seas surging through it, it bears every one of the myriad things. The Way of the sage is the Way of Heaven and Earth. To understand Heaven and Earth is to understand the sage. Thus, without greatness there would be no means to…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
該乎博而大者博之所寓也非博無以成
其大而博者大之所包也具其大而不遺
於博孔子之道如之何其可及乎夷考當
時七十之徒相與受學亦皆得其性之所
近如淵騫之德行予賜之言語初非無所
得也而各一其善由求之政事游夏之文
學亦非無所得也而各一其長何也道大
而博不能徧觀而盡識也及門之徒尚然
則夫授受於列國源遠而末益分者可知
===
矣宜乎百有餘歲之後僅一孟軻氏上接
其傳而得其宗也噫至哉孔子之道乎其
備全體而獨盛亘古今而一人者乎愈也後
孟軻而生乃復遠窺而特稱之謂非善言
聖人者能之歟抑愈於此既稱夫子之道
而謂得其傳者在於軻矣至於原道復歷
叙列聖相傳之統而歎軻死不得其傳焉
其意豈不以軻之所自任者自期耶惜其
志雖有在而大道未聞閎中肆外之文尚
punctuated:
該乎博，而大者博之所寓也；非博無以成其大，而博者大之所包也。具其大而不遺於博，孔子之道如之何其可及乎？夷考當時，七十之徒相與受學，亦皆得其性之所近。如淵騫之德行、予賜之言語，初非無所得也，而各一其善；由求之政事、游夏之文學，亦非無所得也，而各一其長。何也？道大而博，不能徧觀而盡識也。及門之徒尚然，則夫授受於列國，源遠而末益分者，可知矣。宜乎百有餘歲之後，僅一孟軻氏上接其傳而得其宗也。
噫！至哉，孔子之道乎！其備全體而獨盛，亘古今而一人者乎！愈也後孟軻而生，乃復遠窺而特稱之，謂非善言聖人者能之歟？抑愈於此既稱夫子之道，而謂得其傳者在於軻矣。至於《原道》，復歷叙列聖相傳之統，而歎軻死不得其傳焉。其意豈不以軻之所自任者自期耶？惜其志雖有在，而大道未聞，閎中肆外之文尚
translation_en:
…encompass its breadth; greatness is that in which breadth resides. Without breadth, its greatness cannot be perfected; breadth is what greatness embraces. Possessing such greatness while omitting nothing of its breadth, how could Confucius’s Way possibly be equaled? Examining the circumstances of his time, we find that the seventy disciples who studied together under him each attained what accorded with his own disposition. Thus Yan Yuan and Min Ziqian excelled in virtuous conduct, and Zai Yu and Zigong in speech. It was certainly not that they had attained nothing, but each excelled in one particular respect. Zilu and Ran Qiu excelled in government, and Ziyou and Zixia in literary learning. They too had certainly attained something, but each had his particular strength. Why was this? The Way was so great and broad that they could not survey it in its entirety and comprehend it completely. If even those who studied directly under him were like this, we can readily understand how, as it was taught and received throughout the various states, its branches became increasingly divided as they grew more distant from their source. Little wonder that, more than a hundred years later, only Meng Ke reached back to inherit its transmission and grasp its essential purport.
Ah, how consummate is Confucius’s Way! Was he not uniquely preeminent in embodying its entirety, a figure without equal throughout past and present? Han Yu, born after Meng Ke, nevertheless discerned it across the intervening ages and singled it out for praise. Could anyone who was not adept at speaking of the sage have done this? Moreover, here Han Yu both praised the Master’s Way and stated that it was Meng Ke who received its transmission. In On the Way (Yuan dao), he further recounted the succession through which the sages transmitted it, and lamented that, after Meng Ke died, no one received that transmission. Did he not thereby aspire to take upon himself the responsibility that Meng Ke had assumed? It is regrettable that, although he had this aspiration, he had not apprehended the Great Way; his writing, ample in its inner substance and expansive in its outward expression, still…

title: 弘治五年廣西鄉試錄
text:
未敢上擬夫子之所謂傳者而況於其大
乎雖然道具於心者也道有顯晦而心無
存亡又安知千載之下不有以心感心而
契此道之傳者哉
表

皇太子正位東宮

同考試官教諭謝批駢驪有則
同考試官學正陳批詞氣渾厚而忠愛之
心見於言外可謂善
頌禱者矣
考試官教諭趙批表有忠悃之誠非區
區騁浮詞者
考試官教諭朱批得體
弘治五年三月初八日伏遇
皇上冊立
punctuated:
未敢上擬夫子之所謂傳者，而況於其大乎？雖然，道具於心者也。道有顯晦，而心無存亡，又安知千載之下不有以心感心而契此道之傳者哉？

弘治五年三月初八日，伏遇皇上冊立
translation_en:
…he did not yet dare compare himself to those whom the Master called transmitters, much less to the greatness of the Master himself. Nevertheless, the Way is fully present in the mind. The Way may be manifest or obscured, but the mind neither comes into existence nor passes away. How, then, can we know that a thousand years hence there will not be someone whose mind responds to another mind and thereby accords with the transmission of this Way?
